items.title: How lexical knowledge becomes decision evidence: Distributional representations and frequency modulate drift in lexical decision.
items.abstract: How does lexical knowledge enter the decision process? We develop a framework that links distributional lexical representations to the evidence accumulation process, allowing explicit tests of how lexical information contributes to decision evidence in lexical decision. Words and nonwords are represented with word embeddings (FastText or BERT) and passed through a compact classifier; its outputs are mapped to accumulator drift rates with an additional term capturing the independent influence of lexical frequency. The resulting models were fitted to choice and response time data from the English Lexicon Project Across the factorial model set, racing diffusion variants outperformed the corresponding ballistic race variants, and adding explicit lexical frequency improved predictive fit. The best-supported factorial specification also provided better predictive fit than its corresponding benchmark. The primary FastText-racing diffusion model (RDM) was then evaluated using probabilities from a locked stimulus-disjoint classifier holdout. Within the tested RDM specifications, assigning lexical frequency to word-channel drift gave better predictive performance than the matched response-bias and common-caution alternatives. In a separate comparison that held the frequency route fixed, the tested drift mapping of classifier-derived lexical support outperformed a response-bias mapping. These findings support a drift-based account in which distributional lexical information and frequency contribute to the quality of evidence accumulated during lexical decision.

items.title: Individual and environmental predictors of math anxiety in primary school children.
items.abstract: Previous meta-analyses have indicated that math anxiety (MA) is weakly to moderately and negatively related to math achievement, yet relatively few studies have simultaneously examined a range of predictors of MA and the proportion of variance in MA explained by these predictors. We investigated individual and environmental predictors of MA using multilevel regression models based on data from 166 fourth-grade primary school children in Poland. We tested four models, sequentially introducing sociodemographic factors (gender, age), math domain-specific variables (math achievement, intellectual helplessness in math), domain-general affective factors (general and test anxiety), domain-general cognitive variables (fluid intelligence, working memory), and family-related factors (mothers' home numeracy activities, MA, and education), while controlling for school as a fixed effect and including class as a random effect. Test anxiety was a stable predictor of MA across successive regression models. Intellectual helplessness in math and fluid intelligence were associated with MA in some models, but these predictors were not stable across successive models. The fixed effects, including school, explained approximately 58-63% of the variance in MA, while differences between classes accounted for only 1.4-2.4% of the variance. These findings underscore the need to consider both individual and environmental factors when developing interventions aimed at reducing MA and fostering a supportive learning environment.

items.title: The Dutch compulsory care act: Long-term compulsory care before and after mental health law reform.
items.abstract: To assess whether the Dutch Compulsory Care Act (Wvggz, 2020) altered long-term compulsory care pathways compared to the former Special Admissions Act (BOPZ,1994). We compared routinely registered long-term authorization cases pre-reform (2015-2018) with care authorization cases post-reform (2021-2024), excluding the transition years 2019 and 2020. Outcomes included prevalence and duration, inpatient and outpatient exposure, seclusion events and hours, and compulsory medication (inpatient and outpatient). Involuntary treatment authorisations and patient numbers decreased (2646 to 1833; 831 to 661), while median duration increased (117 to 145 days). Seclusion declined sharply (746 to 64 events; 62,195 to 1943 h). Compulsory medication increased, including newly registered outpatient medication (79 to 1181 inpatient events; 0 to 529 outpatient events). Diagnostic composition also changed: organic mental disorders, substance use disorders, schizophrenia-spectrum disorders, intellectual disability and somatic comorbidity were more frequently recorded in the post-reform period, whereas neurotic/stress-related/somatoform and personality disorders were less represented. After the implementation of the Wvggz, seclusion decreased dramatically, while compulsory medication became more prominent within fewer but longer long-term care pathways. Fewer patients were subject to long-term involuntary treatment, and the diagnostic case mix differed between periods. The observational design cannot determine the extent to which these changes are attributable to the law, case mix, COVID-19 or other concurrent changes in practice.

items.title: Visual learning through auditory reactivation during wakefulness and sleep.
items.abstract: Visual learning, like other kinds of learning, has classically been attributed to intensive, active training; however, whether it can be achieved via effortless, passive reactivation remains unresolved. Here, we triggered targeted reactivation using auditory tones that had acquired contextual meaning through preceding visual-auditory associative learning. Re-exposure to learned tones improved subsequent visual performance during both wakefulness and slow-wave sleep. Wake reactivation matched training in both improvement and improvement per trial, whereas sleep reactivation surpassed both wake reactivation and training. By contrast, re-exposure to unlearned tones impaired performance only during slow-wave sleep. Reactivation-induced improvement and impairment were strictly orientation- and location-specific and were associated with a convergent auditory-visual coupling pathway. Beyond this shared pathway, auditory reactivation during wakefulness and sleep unfolded through distinct coupling architectures linking sensory and higher-order cortical regions. Collectively, our findings establish auditory reactivation as a highly efficient route to visual learning, identify sleep as its most potent state, and reveal a double-edged, state-dependent neuroplastic architecture.

items.title: Probabilistic neural code for subjective value and metacognition in human cortex.
items.abstract: Subjective value underlies many everyday decisions, yet the neural representations supporting these valuations are inherently noisy and subject to uncertainty. Whether humans have metacognitive access to this uncertainty and how this access is supported neurally remain unclear. Here, we provide converging behavioral and neural evidence that subjective value is represented probabilistically in the human brain. Behaviorally, participants' uncertainty reports tracked trial-by-trial fluctuations in valuation. Neurally, we decoded probability distributions over value from functional magnetic resonance imaging activity in ventromedial prefrontal and orbitofrontal cortex, and superior parietal lobe and intraparietal sulcus. Decoded neural uncertainty predicted behaviorally reported uncertainty across trial, item, and individual levels. Moreover, predicting behavioral uncertainty required modeling the covariance structure of population noise. These findings indicate that neural populations jointly encode value and uncertainty, extending probabilistic population coding from perception, working memory to subjective value, and providing a neural basis for metacognitive access to uncertainty in value-based decisions.

items.title: Chemosensory and somatosensory profiles in craniofacial pain: A comparison of chronic rhinosinusitis and migraine.
items.abstract: Migraine (MIG) and chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) serve as critical models for studying how distinct pathological processes, such as central sensitization and peripheral inflammation, remodel the human trigeminal system. This study compared the chemosensory and somatosensory profiles of these conditions to characterize their unique sensory signatures. Sixty-eight participants (30 MIG, 18 CRS, and 20 healthy participants) completed chemosensory assessments involving olfactory and intranasal trigeminal function; quantitative sensory testing of electrical and mechanical detection and pain thresholds; and questionnaires on allodynia and mental health. Group comparisons were performed using generalized linear mixed models controlling for age and sex, while multinomial logistic regressions identified key differential predictors. Results showed that CRS was primarily characterized by reduced chemosensory function, with significantly lower Sniffin' Sticks scores and lower trigeminal lateralization scores (among female participants) compared to MIG and healthy participants. In contrast, MIG patients exhibited preserved chemosensory perception but a relatively hypersensitive somatosensory profile, with lower electrical detection thresholds across both trigeminal and extra-trigeminal sites, and higher allodynia scores than CRS or healthy groups. These findings suggest that while both conditions involve trigeminal pathway, their sensory profiles are distinct. The chemosensory loss observed in CRS is consistent with a predominantly peripheral mechanism, whereas the preserved chemosensory function and generalized hypersensitivity observed in MIG are consistent with central sensitization. This research highlights how distinct chronic craniofacial pain conditions uniquely remodel human perception. Future studies with larger and more age- and sex-balanced cohorts are needed to confirm the findings.

items.title: Daily Temporal Associations of Negative Muscle Talk With Body Appreciation, Relaxation, and Anxiety Among Medical and Nursing Students: A 10-Day Diary Study.
items.abstract: Negative muscle talk (NMT) is usually framed as negative body-related communication, yet common NMT expressions may simultaneously convey dissatisfaction with the present body, aspiration toward a desired future self, and interpersonal or self-presentational meanings. These different features suggest that NMT may be followed by distinct short-term psychological processes. We therefore examined two theory-grounded exploratory temporal sequences linking daily NMT with anxiety through body appreciation or relaxation among medical and nursing students. A 10-consecutive-day daily diary study was conducted among 966 Chinese medical and nursing students (289 males, 677 females; Mage = 19.93 years), who contributed 5510 completed diary assessments. Bayesian dynamic structural equation modeling (DSEM) estimated person-specific random cross-lagged paths from NMT at t - 2 to body appreciation or relaxation at t - 1 and from each candidate intermediate variable to anxiety at t. A higher-compliance sensitivity analysis was conducted among participants who completed at least five diary assessments. In the primary relaxation model, higher NMT predicted greater subsequent relaxation (b = 0.074, 95% BCI [0.024, 0.123]), and greater relaxation predicted lower later anxiety (b = -0.177, 95% BCI [-0.285, -0.073]); however, the random indirect effect included zero (b = -0.029, 95% BCI [-0.081, 0.024]). The hypothesized population-average body-appreciation sequence was not supported. NMT predicted greater subsequent relaxation, which was subsequently associated with lower anxiety, revealing a more complex short-term pattern between NMT and psychological well-being than traditionally assumed. These associations may vary across individuals and interpersonal contexts, highlighting the importance of directly assessing the motives, meanings, and social settings in which NMT occurs.

items.title: Connection, belonging, and agency: A qualitative study of stateless community spaces and the mental wellbeing of stateless people.
items.abstract: Statelessness, affecting an estimated fifteen million people globally, has significant mental health impacts. Largely excluded from formal provision, stateless people often turn to community spaces, delivered by and for stateless people for purposes such as advocacy, legal assistance, education, or community connection. Although previous research suggests these spaces benefit the mental wellbeing of stateless people, few studies explore this topic. This study explores the mental wellbeing experiences of organisers and members of stateless community spaces and examines barriers and facilitators to running them effectively. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with twelve people with lived experience of statelessness who had participated in or organised these spaces. Data was analysed using thematic analysis. Three themes emerged: Personal Journeys in Community Spaces; Making It Work; and Navigating Challenging Systems. Results demonstrated that community spaces represent a vital tool in supporting stateless people's mental wellbeing by offering experiences of connection, belonging, and agency systematically denied to stateless people in wider society. Participants identified stateless leadership and practical support, such as legal and financial assistance, as essential to effective community spaces. Mental health support was usually offered indirectly by community spaces rather than through explicit provision, and while participants valued the wellbeing benefits of these spaces, they felt more dedicated mental health support was needed for both members and organisers. Community spaces were shown to be operating without adequate funding and in challenging political environments, often at considerable personal cost to organisers. Lack of funding forced trade-offs regarding which activities to prioritise, making further mental health provision challenging. Increased sustained funding is urgently needed for stateless community spaces to maintain existing activities and to develop mental health support.

items.title: Mapping nonordinary experiences in a representative German sample: Phenomenology, prevalence and links to self-transcendence.
items.abstract: This study investigated the prevalence, phenomenology, and potential transformative significance of nonordinary experiences in a representative German sample. Across cultures and historical periods, such experiences have been widely reported and often culturally valued. To assess these phenomena, the study employed the Inventory of Nonordinary Experiences (INOE; Taves et al., 2023), a phenomenologically grounded instrument that focuses on subjective experiential qualities rather than explanatory frameworks. The INOE was administered alongside two validated measures: the Questionnaire on the Phenomenology of Exceptional Experiences (PExE-II), which assesses frequency and types of anomalous experiences, and the Inventory of Secular/Spiritual Wakefulness (WAKE-16), which measures positive self-transformation. Data from 440 participants revealed that nonordinary experiences are widely distributed. Exceptionally strong emotional experiences (e.g., awe, love, loss) were most frequently reported, while explicitly anomalous phenomena (e.g., telepathy, sensed presences) were less common but still notable, with prevalence rates of 10-30%. Correlational analyses showed positive associations between INOE domains and PExE-II dimensions, suggesting that experiences more common in the population also tend to occur more frequently within individuals. In structural equation modelling, the INOE emerged as a significant positive predictor of the WAKE-16, indicating an association between nonordinary experiences and self-transcendent personality development. Overall, the findings support the perspective that nonordinary experiences constitute a widespread and meaningful aspect of human experience.

items.title: The clickbait paradox: Why sensationalist styling damages trustworthy content most.
items.abstract: In an increasingly digital media environment, social media platforms have become central to how individuals access news. However, these platforms also facilitate the rapid spread of misinformation, often presented in stylistically persuasive formats such as clickbait. Understanding how both the style and accuracy of online content influence user responses is critical for addressing the psychological mechanisms underlying misinformation engagement. In the current study, we examined how article style (clickbait vs. non-clickbait) and content accuracy (true vs. false) affect user engagement metrics (liking, commenting, sharing) and perceptions of veracity (truthfulness and credibility). In an online within-subjects experiment, a sample of 203 adults rated a series of mock social media posts varying systematically in style and accuracy. Participants also completed validated measures of news media literacy and susceptibility to misinformation to assess the contribution of individual differences. Across all engagement measures, participants reported a low likelihood of interacting with posts, particularly those in a clickbait style. Posts containing false information elicited reduced engagement, although this effect did not extend to sharing behaviour. Perceived truthfulness and credibility were significantly lower for posts with clickbait features and false content. Notably, the detrimental effect of clickbait was more pronounced for posts that were factually accurate, suggesting that stylistic cues may especially undermine trustworthy information. Individual differences moderated these effects: participants with lower news media literacy were more likely to perceive clickbait posts as credible, while those more susceptible to misinformation were more likely to view false posts as truthful. News media literacy also moderated the effect of article style on engagement, with the reduction in engagement toward clickbait-style posts concentrated among more literate participants. These findings underscore the role of stylistic cues in shaping perceived veracity and highlight the importance of psychological traits in susceptibility to misinformation. The results suggest that interventions addressing both media literacy and content presentation may be effective in mitigating the spread and influence of misinformation on social media.

items.title: Systematic review of quantitative studies exploring links between mindfulness, mental health, and social media use.
items.abstract: There is growing interest in inter-individual differences linked to risk and resilience in the associations between social media use and mental health. Here, we systematically reviewed empirical studies exploring links between mindfulness, social media use, and mental health, in order to explore the possibility that mindfulness plays a protective role. Systematic searches of PsychInfo, Medline, and Web of Science databases were run from database inception to January 2026. Forty-three studies met criteria for inclusion. Mindfulness was modelled variably as an independent variable, dependent variable, mediator, and moderator. Overwhelmingly, results linked mindfulness to better mental health and more beneficial patterns of social media use, and mediated/ moderated associations between the two in a protective manner where tested. Existing studies were limited by a predominance of cross-sectional designs, a paucity of research in non-'WEIRD' samples, and a bias towards younger population samples. The findings support the role of mindfulness as a potential protective factor in the association between social media and mental health, but highlight a need for longitudinal and experimental research to unpick underlying directions of causality, and examine the clinical utility of mindfulness as a modifiable trait.

items.title: "When the Images You Are Seeing Are Not Your Life": Autistic Adults' Autobiographical Memories of Media Consumed in Adolescence.
items.abstract: Recent research has investigated how autistic youth select the media they consume and what they gain from those experiences. However, the influence of media on autistic adolescents' identity development is not well understood. We explored how autistic individuals perceive and internalize media they consumed as adolescents, particularly representations of pain and suffering. Eighteen autistic adults (aged 18-43 years) were interviewed and asked about formative memories of the media they consumed during adolescence, with a focus on character representations of autism and neurodevelopmental disabilities, how it informed their experiences of pain and suffering, and how they believed these portrayals should be changed. We developed four themes with reflexive thematic analysis: (1) painful playback of media stereotypes; (2) "it's nice to know you're not the only one": the pain of exclusion; (3) finding perspective on the pain of masking; and (4) escape from pain: adventuring into imagined worlds and community. Participants described how their identities developed within a historical context of media that lacked authentic and diverse autistic representation and how media reinforced the pain of invalidation they experienced in their social environments. In response, participants critiqued and reimagined popular media to create stories they needed to support their developing identities. Findings underscore how media representations of autism and neurodiversity could be both stigmatizing and a needed outlet for comfort and information. In the absence of affirmation and belonging in their lives, autistic individuals critiqued, rewrote, and reimagined popular media to create the stories they needed to support their developing identities.

items.title: LSC-lex: a lexical database of Catalan Sign Language.
items.abstract: This article presents Lengua de Signos Española (LSC)-lex, the largest lexical database of Catalan Sign Language (LSC) to date, comprising 56,381 annotated tokens and providing objective measures of lexical frequency. Subjective frequency ratings were also collected for a subset of lexical signs. Objective frequency was positively, although weakly, correlated with subjective frequency ratings. Despite the limitations inherent to relatively small sign language corpora, LSC-lex provides language-specific psycholinguistic indices for investigating LSC processing, acquisition, and structure.

items.title: Creating in the between: An account of healing through clinical hypnosis .
items.abstract: This is an in-depth first-person description of transformation within hypnosis psychotherapy, told through a series of vignettes from the therapeutic work. I'm using the word "transformation" to denote the process whereby memories held by dissociation in the unconscious move into waking consciousness. The effect of this kind of transformation is to free up psychic energy; allow for the emergence of new ways of perceiving, thinking, and feeling; and to relieve suffering. The article includes a selective chronology of formative events that led me to seek this form of therapy. Essential to the therapy is the process of two women - therapist and patient - co-creating an unshakable, safe, trustworthy relational environment. I am a practicing clinician, and as such bring a range of perspectives; I write as patient, psychiatrist, neuroscientist, observer, and explorer.

items.title: Culturally and Linguistically Diverse Clients' Perspectives on Barriers to Telehealth Mental Health Interventions: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Migration is a challenging experience that impacts immigrants' well-being. The aim of this systematic review was to ascertain the perspectives of culturally and linguistically diverse individuals, including Indigenous populations about mental health interventions via telehealth to facilitate the delivery of culturally appropriate services and improve engagement and intervention efficacy. A review of the current literature published in English was carried out across four electronic databases in psychology, health, and social sciences collected through ProQuest, Google Scholar, PubMed, and Informit with no time restrictions. The perspectives of 4125 of CALD clients are represented within the 24 included studies retrieved across the four databases. Key themes comprised: Individual Level, Provider Level, and System Level. These three major themes comprised of 14 sub-themes. Key barriers on the Individual Level included the low levels of technological literacy, compounded by financial difficulties as clients are unable to access these technologies. Key Provider Level concerns included poor intervention design and language barriers. Clients preferred to engage in interventions in their own language and struggled with poor intervention design such as the layout, format, and characteristics of the telehealth intervention. Key System Level issues included cultural factors that were not considered by organisations and providers. As such, the proliferation of telehealth across the world suggests that mental health systems and providers must adapt to culturally and linguistically diverse clients that require support. Recommendations for systemic changes, training, and practice are discussed.

items.title: Religiosity and Superstition in Regularly Exercising Young Adults in Hungary: Structural Validation of a Brief Sports Superstition Attitude Scale.
items.abstract: Superstition and religiosity are often studied together, but research shows these are related yet distinct belief systems. Religiousness involves a persistent sense of meaning and transcendence. In contrast, superstition involves situational irrational beliefs used to cope with uncertainty. This cross-sectional online study, conducted in Hungary, examined the structural validity of a short version of the Sports Superstition Attitude Scale (SSAS). It aimed to unveil the strength of the relationships among superstition, religiosity, biological sex, and exercise habits. Young physically active adults, aged 18-30 years (N = 549; 97.6% in Hungary), completed the SSAS, the Multidimensional Inventory for Religious/Spiritual Well-Being (MI-RSWB 12), and questions on exercise history, weekly frequency, form of exercise, and competition status. Confirmatory factor analysis supported a unidimensional six-item SSAS with good model fit (CFI = .98, SRMR = .03) and reliability (ω = .87). Associations between superstition and religion measures were small (|r| = .09-.24), positive for general religiosity and connectedness and negative for forgiveness and hope. Exploratory factor and network analyses showed superstition as distinct from religiousness, hope, forgiveness, and connectedness. Women reported higher superstition and connectedness than men, but no other sex differences emerged. Hierarchical regressions controlling for age and sex showed that exercise characteristics explained at most 2.2% of the variance in any belief measure. Overall, superstition differs from religiousness, and although superstition is common in sport, this study found weak associations between exercise and both superstition and religiousness among young, physically active adults in Hungary.

items.title: Assessing the Effectiveness of the KiVa Anti-bullying Program in Belgium: a Cluster Quasi-experimental Trial Testing Dosage Effects.
items.abstract: This study assessed the effectiveness of KiVa, one of the most extensively studied anti-bullying programs, using a quasi-experimental design, in French-speaking Belgium. It also examined KiVa's hypothesized mechanisms, including students' affective empathy, anti-bullying attitudes, classroom injunctive anti-bullying norm and descriptive defending norm, and aggregated perceptions of teachers' active reactions to bullying. In addition, we examined associations between class-level implementation dosage and outcomes. Regardless of dosage, the program was not associated with changes in victimization or any of the hypothesized mediators. However, students in classes with higher level of KiVa implementation reported lower bullying perpetration compared to those in control classes (d = .19). This effect did not remain statistically significant after Bonferroni correction for multiple testing. These findings highlight the need for further research on the mechanisms underlying reductions in bullying to deepen our understanding of effective prevention strategies. They also underscore variability in implementation within schools and the importance of accounting for class-level dosage when evaluating anti-bullying programs.

items.title: Integrating Multiple Informants' Reports about Adolescents' Safety Behaviors.
items.abstract: Adolescents who experience social anxiety frequently avoid unfamiliar social situations. When socially anxious adolescents encounter anxiety-provoking situations they cannot avoid (e.g., school projects, family gatherings), they might manage their distress via subtle avoidance strategies (i.e., safety behaviors), such as avoiding eye contact, remaining silent, and speaking in short sentences. Safety behaviors can temporarily relieve distress, but their use may raise risks for impairing interpersonal functioning and slowing treatment responses. Further, safety behaviors are triggered by the contexts in which anxiety manifests. Validly assessing these behaviors requires data from informants who observe adolescents within clinically relevant contexts. Within these contexts, various informants can provide psychometrically sound reports about adolescents' safety behaviors, and yet recent work highlights that (a) these reports commonly disagree and (b) the disagreements contain valid data about safety behaviors. We therefore require validity studies that test approaches to integrating multi-informant data about adolescents' safety behaviors. In a preregistered study of a mixed community/clinical sample of 134 adolescents, we took an integrated approach to assessing safety behaviors that capitalizes on the unique and common variance produced by multiple informants' reports. Integrated scores from this approach yielded moderate-to-large-magnitude relations when predicting adolescents' behavior within anxiety-provoking social situations. Further, integrated scores designed to reference context-specific safety behaviors uniquely predicted both adolescents' social skills within anxiety-provoking situations and an estimate of how anxious adolescents and their interaction partners were in these situations. Among adolescents, assessing safety behaviors requires strategies for integrating multi-informant data that capture the contexts in which these behaviors manifest.

items.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and bone fragility: pathophysiological links between liver and skeletal metabolism.
items.abstract: Osteoporosis and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) pose substantial global health burdens. Osteoporosis is characterized by reduced bone mineral density (BMD) and microarchitectural deterioration, leading to increased fracture risk, whereas MASLD encompasses a spectrum ranging from simple steatosis to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. The prevalence of both conditions has risen markedly, in parallel with the global increase in obesity, insulin resistance, and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Emerging evidence suggests a potential pathophysiological link between MASLD and osteoporosis, highlighting the existence of a liver-bone axis. Shared mechanisms, including chronic low-grade inflammation, insulin resistance, adipokine imbalance, oxidative stress, vitamin D deficiency, and alterations in cytokine and osteokine signaling, may contribute to bone loss in patients with MASLD (Fig. 1). In particular, pro-inflammatory mediators and molecular pathways implicated in MASLD progression may disrupt the balance between bone formation and resorption, thereby promoting skeletal fragility. Several observational studies and meta-analyses have reported an association between MASLD and adverse skeletal outcomes, including higher odds of osteoporosis or osteoporotic fractures (OR = 1.17, 95% CI 1.04-1.31), increased risks of osteoporosis (RR = 1.28, 95% CI 1.08-1.52) and fractures (RR = 1.17, 95% CI 1.00-1.37), as well as lower BMD; however, findings are not entirely consistent across populations and disease stages. Herein, we aim to summarize current evidence regarding the association between MASLD and osteoporosis and to explore the underlying pathogenetic mechanisms linking these two conditions. A better understanding of the liver-bone crosstalk may facilitate early identification of high-risk individuals and support the development of integrated therapeutic strategies targeting both hepatic and skeletal health.

items.title: Update on Purging Disorder.
items.abstract: This review covers recent research on purging disorder. We aim to provide a comprehensive summary of what purging disorder is, whom it affects, why it occurs, and what can be done. Purging disorder is defined by recurrent self-induced vomiting and/or misuse of laxatives, diuretics, or other medications to influence weight or shape in the absence of binge eating. It shows evidence of clinical significance and distinctiveness, including predictive validity. The disorder persists over time, affects individuals in all demographic groups, with higher prevalence in women and underrepresented sexual/gender groups, and is associated with medical complications and significant impairment across life domains. Recent advances in research on purging disorder solidify its status as a serious mental illness. However, it is poorly understood outside eating disorder specialty care. More work is needed in research, policy, and practice to care for people impacted by this disorder.

items.title: Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) Attitudes, Self-Efficacy, and Prescription Practices Among Physicians in Sao Paulo, Brazil: Insights for Optimizing PrEP Service Delivery.
items.abstract: Brazil is well-known for its longstanding public policies for HIV prevention; however, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) uptake remains suboptimal in the country. Expanding PrEP uptake depends on physicians' attitudes, prescription self-efficacy, and practices. Thus, our study investigated the prevalence of positive attitudes toward PrEP, prescription self-efficacy, and PrEP prescription practices, as well as the factors associated with these outcomes among physicians in Sao Paulo, Brazil. A self-administered cross-sectional survey was conducted online among 283 physicians in Sao Paulo, Brazil, between July 2024 and January 2025. We used bivariate and multivariable logistic regression to examine associations between sociodemographic and other characteristics and the outcome variables (i.e., attitudes, self-efficacy, and prescription practices), with multiple imputations for missing data. Participants' mean age was 33.6 years (standard deviation = 4.7 years). Most participants were White (82.5%) and female (69.8%), and only 15.2% specialized in infectious diseases. Most (87.7%) participants held positive attitudes toward PrEP, while less than one-third (31.3%) reported high prescription self-efficacy, and only 21.5% had prescribed PrEP. Participants with an Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Queer, or Other (LGBQ+) sexual orientation were more likely to have positive attitudes toward PrEP [adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 10.08, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.83-55.53], high PrEP prescription self-efficacy (aOR: 9.89, 95% CI: 4.66-21.00), and a past prescription for PrEP (aOR: 4.08, 95% CI: 1.66-10.02). In addition, infectious disease specialists were more likely to have high PrEP prescription self-efficacy (aOR: 108.51, 95% CI: 28.23-417.01) and a past PrEP prescription (aOR: 48.85, 95% CI: 18.62-128.10). Conversely, participants assigned male at birth were less likely to have positive attitudes toward PrEP (aOR: 0.34, 95% CI: 0.14-0.83). Physicians in Sao Paulo, Brazil, held positive attitudes toward PrEP but exhibited low self-efficacy and low prescription rates. Our results emphasize the need for tailored training programs to enhance prescription self-efficacy and increase PrEP prescribing among noninfectious disease specialists and primary care physicians in Sao Paulo, Brazil.

items.title: General Population's and Clinicians' Perspectives on the Expansion of Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing: A Scoping Literature Review.
items.abstract: Technological advances in non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) have enabled screening beyond the common trisomies, including rare autosomal trisomies, subchromosomal aberrations, microdeletion/duplication syndromes, and selected monogenic disorders. Consequently, clinical, ethical, and social questions have emerged regarding the appropriate scope and implementation of expanded NIPT. This scoping review systematically mapped the perspectives on expanded NIPT of primary stakeholders-general population and healthcare professionals (HCPs). Five electronic databases were searched from inception to October 2nd 2024. 40 studies met the inclusion criteria, including 24 studies involving general population and 16 involving HCPs. Overall, attitudes toward expanded NIPT were generally positive but varied according to the characteristics of the conditions screened. Support was highest for severe, childhood-onset disorders and lower for conditions with uncertain prognosis, variable expressivity, reduced penetrance, or adult-onset disorders. General population primarily emphasized access to information, reproductive autonomy, and preparedness, whereas HCPs focused on clinical validity, interpretation of results, counseling challenges, and implementation considerations. Common concerns included uncertain findings, increased counseling complexity, ethical implications of broader testing, and equitable access to screening. These findings suggest that future expansion of NIPT requires careful balancing of informational benefits, clinical utility, counseling needs, and ethical considerations to support responsible implementation in prenatal care.

items.title: Likelihood of Care Seeking for Miscarriage and Abortion in Restricted and Protected States After the Dobbs Decision.
items.abstract: This study evaluates self-reported likelihood of seeking care for contraception, miscarriage, and abortion in a restricted and protected state, post-Dobbs. A convenience sample of participants presenting to ambulatory OBGYN clinics in South Carolina (SC) and Massachusetts (MA) completed surveys from June 2024 to January 2025. The outcome of interest is reduced likelihood of seeking care for miscarriage, abortion, or contraception post-Dobbs. We generated descriptive and comparative analyses with Stata. Surveys were completed by 201 respondents (n = 101 SC, n = 100 MA). Compared to participants from Massachusetts, those from South Carolina had higher odds of reporting a reduced likelihood of seeking miscarriage care (OR: 5.29, 95% CI: 1.82, 15.40) and abortion care (OR: 4.59, 95% CI: 2.14, 9.84) from ObGyn providers. Even in Massachusetts, approximately one-quarter of participants reported reduced likelihood of seeking miscarriage care from Planned Parenthood, a public health clinic, or the emergency department. Participants from South Carolina had higher odds of reporting reduced likelihood of seeking abortion medication (OR: 2.50, 95% CI: 1.31, 4.81) and emergency contraception (OR: 2.50, 95% CI: 1.23, 5.10) from in-person pharmacies. Roughly one-third of participants in both states reported a reduced likelihood of seeking all medications from online pharmacies. While most pronounced in the restricted state, participants in both policy settings reported reduced likelihood of seeking not just abortion care, but miscarriage care as well. Reduced likelihood of seeking medication for contraception, miscarriage management, and abortion from online pharmacies impacts participants in both settings. The findings can guide clinicians, public health leaders, and policy-makers.

items.title: Reframing Person-Centred Care as a Safety Critical Practice in the Digital Era-A Discursive Paper.
items.abstract: This discursive paper argues that person-centred fundamental care is not separate from, or secondary to, safety-critical care; it is a safety-critical nursing practice. A discursive paper. The Fundamental of Care Framework was used as a conceptual lens to purposively identify relevant conceptual and empirical literature for discussion. PubMed and CINAHL databases were searched for papers and supplemented by citation searching and reference list checking. Sources were interpreted iteratively in relation to the nurse-patient relationship, the integration of physical, psychosocial and relational care needs and the context in which care is delivered. Similarities, differences and tensions were compared to develop a transparent, conceptually informed argument rather than a comprehensive evidence synthesis. Three connected areas: fundamental care as skilled and safety-critical nursing practice; the capacity of digital technology to support or disrupt fundamental care; and the implications for nursing education, leadership, policy and healthcare systems. Considered through the lens of the Fundamentals of Care Framework, digital technologies may strengthen safety when they support relational engagement, integrated care and professional judgement, but may undermine it when they redirect attention towards documentation, alerts and task completion. Digital technologies offer important opportunities to support nursing care, but their contribution to safety depends on how they are designed, implemented and used. Applying the Fundamentals of Care Framework demonstrates that technology should support the nurse-patient relationship, the integration of physical, psychosocial and relational care needs and the context required for safe care. Recognising person-centred fundamental care as skilled and safety-critical is therefore essential to ensure that digital innovation strengthens rather than displaces relational engagement, professional judgement and integrated care. Person-centred fundamental care should be recognised as skilled, safety-critical nursing practice. Nurses, educators, leaders and policymakers should ensure that digital systems support the nurse-patient relationship, integrate care needs and facilitate the organisational conditions required for safe care. Further research should examine how different technologies and clinical contexts affect nurses' relational, observational and interpretive work, particularly for patients at greater risk of missed care. The Fundamentals of Care Framework was used to examine how digital technologies may enable or disrupt the relational, integrated and contextual dimensions of fundamental care. It demonstrates that technology should be evaluated not only by its efficiency or capacity to record activity, but by whether it supports the nursing practices through which risks are recognised, care needs are integrated and harm is prevented. The paper identifies implications for nursing education, leadership, policy, research and digital system design. There was no patient or public contribution to this discursive paper.

items.title: Safe and inclusive spaces in co-produced research: co-creating a practical guide.
items.abstract: Co-produced research requires meaningful collaboration amongst Indigenous people, patients/people with lived and living experience, researchers, and others who ultimately use research knowledge. Despite good intentions, traditional academic environments, structures, and hierarchies where research is done can create unintentional barriers and make meaningful collaboration among partners difficult. Few resources integrate trauma-informed care; Indigenous ways of knowing, being and doing; and, anti-oppression frameworks specifically for the practical demands of co-produced, patient- and community-engaged health research meetings and events. To address this gap, the Brain-Heart Interconnectome co-produced a practical, living resource called Tips to Create Safe Spaces. Drawing from trauma-informed care; patient engagement principles; Indigenous ways of knowing, being, and doing; and anti-oppression frameworks, our team collaboratively developed actionable guidance organized across three stages of research meetings and events: planning, conducting, and debriefing. The resulting guidance emphasizes important practices such as proactively offering accommodations (rather than placing the burden on individuals to request them), using facilitation practices that dismantle hierarchies to create multiple pathways for participation, co-designing meetings and materials with partners from the outset, and collecting feedback in ways that are safe and that demonstrably inform future practices. Creating safe spaces is an ongoing process that requires humility and sustained commitment. Research teams are encouraged to adopt and adapt this guidance, commit to ongoing learning, and treat the creation of safe spaces as a ongoing practice rather than a one-time effort. When all team members feel genuinely supported and valued, co-produced research becomes more rigorous, relevant, and capable of driving meaningful change.

items.title: Effective targeting of pediatric bone sarcoma cells by engineered CAR.HER2 T-cells.
items.abstract: Pediatric and adolescent osteosarcoma (OS) and Ewing's sarcoma (EWS) are highly aggressive malignancies associated with poor outcomes in the relapsed or metastatic setting, where survival rates remain below 20-30% despite intensive multimodal therapy. The transmembrane tyrosine-kinase receptor HER2 is expressed in a substantial proportion of OS and EWS; however, current HER2-directed antibody-based therapies show limited efficacy, likely due to the low antigen expression in these tumors. HER2 expression was evaluated by flow-cytometry on adult and pediatric tumor cell lines, as well as in biopsy tissues from pediatric sarcoma patients. We generated two third-generation CAR.HER2 constructs carrying ΔCD19 as both a tracking marker and safety switch to improve the safety profile. Retroviral vectors, (4D5)CAR.HER2 and (2C4)CAR.HER2, incorporate trastuzumab- or pertuzumab-derived single-chain variable fragments (scFvs), respectively, which linker was optimized through structural bioinformatic. These scFvs are coupled to the CD28 and 4-1BB costimulatory domains and the CD3ζ signaling domains, to promote robust T-cell activation and persistence. The antitumor activity of CAR.HER2 T-cells was assessed in vitro and in vivo against HER2 + OS and EWS tumors. HER2 expression was detected in 87% of tumor cell lines and in 38.5% of OS and 36.8% of EWS patient samples. Both CAR.HER2 T-cells exhibited strong CAR expression and comparable immunophenotypic profiles, following T-cell transduction. In 2D/3D in vitro models, CAR.HER2 T-cells showed potent cytotoxic activity against HER2-high OS and HER2-low EWS cells, including trastuzumab-deruxtecan (T-DXd)-resistant tumor cell lines. In in vivo models, both CAR.HER2 T-cells achieved complete regression in HER2-high OS xenografts, while in HER2-low EWS xenograft model only (4D5)CAR.HER2 T-cells induced full tumor eradication, whereas (2C4)CAR.HER2 T-cells delayed tumor progression without achieving full tumor elimination. Xenoreactivity associated with CAR.HER2 T-cell expansion was successfully controlled via ΔCD19 activation using an anti CD19/CD3 T-cell engager, enabling selective CAR T-cell depletion and toxicity resolution. Overall, (4D5)CAR.HER2 T-cells demonstrated superior antitumor activity, persistence, and functional fitness, achieving rapid tumor clearance in HER2-low pediatric sarcoma models. The integrated ΔCD19 safety switch induce a prompt CAR T-cell elimination. These findings support the clinical translation of high-affinity-(4D5)CAR.HER2 T-cells and suggest broader applicability of this design for targeting HER2-low tumors and overcoming resistance to HER2-immunotherapy.

items.title: Preventing congenital syphilis: a review of maternal screening.
items.abstract: Congenital syphilis remains one of the most preventable causes of stillbirth, neonatal mortality, and infant morbidity worldwide. Despite inexpensive diagnostic tests and effective treatment, surveillance indicates a resurgence of maternal and congenital syphilis. Untreated maternal infection can result in miscarriage, stillbirth, prematurity, neonatal death, or severe congenital disease. In 2022, the World Health Organization estimated 700,000 congenital syphilis cases worldwide, resulting in nearly 390,000 adverse pregnancy outcomes, including fetal and neonatal deaths and infants born with clinical disease. Implementation failures across the prevention cascade continue to undermine global elimination efforts. Surveillance data demonstrate concerning increases in high-income countries, including the United States, Canada, and Australia, while substantial disparities persist among Indigenous and marginalised populations. Congenital syphilis prevention relies on timely antenatal screening, early diagnosis, and prompt treatment with benzathine penicillin. However, prevention failures, including limited access to antenatal care, missed screening opportunities, delayed treatment, and inadequate partner management, continue to drive transmission despite the availability of diagnostics and treatment. The COVID-19 pandemic further exposed vulnerabilities in maternal health services, widening existing prevention gaps and weakening surveillance systems. Conversely, successful elimination initiatives demonstrate that congenital syphilis is preventable when screening, treatment, surveillance, and health-system implementation are effectively integrated. Strengthening antenatal screening programmes, expanding access to rapid point-of-care diagnostics, implementing repeat screening where appropriate, and reinforcing integrated surveillance systems should therefore remain global priorities. Ultimately, eliminating congenital syphilis is not a technological but an implementation challenge requiring sustained political commitment, equitable access to maternal healthcare, and coordinated public health action.

items.title: Sexual Health and Intentions to Use Anabolic-Androgenic Steroids Among Boys and Men.
items.abstract: Although anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) use is linked to sexual health issues, including difficulties, no studies have examined how sexual health issues relate to intentions to use AAS. Therefore, this study sought to explore the relationship between sexual health and intentions to use AAS. Data from 1515 boys and young men who had never used AAS from The Study of Boys and Men were analyzed. Multiple linear regression analyses were used to determine the associations between lifetime sexual intercourse, eight indicators of sexual difficulties, and the use of sexual performance-enhancement supplements or drugs, and intentions to use AAS. Findings revealed significant associations across all variables, with the exception of one form of sexual difficulty. Of the sexual difficulties, feeling no excitement or arousal during sex (B = 2.24, 95% CI 1.25, 2.34), lack of enjoyment in having sex (B = 1.67, 95% CI 0.74, 2.60), and having trouble getting or keeping an erection (B = 1.57, 95% CI 0.64, 2.50) were most strongly associated with greater intentions to use AAS. Evaluating intentions to utilize AAS and offering evidence-based treatments for sexual difficulties may be essential in diminishing the initiation of AAS use.

items.title: Barriers to Bridges: Leveraging a Multidisciplinary Collaborative Care Model to Innovate Recruitment to Retention Pathways in School Mental Health.
items.abstract: Behavioral health workforce shortages limit efforts to address the growing youth mental health crisis, particularly in rural and underserved communities. The Multidisciplinary Pathways to Recruit, Train, and Retain School Mental Health Providers in Iowa (MPath) project was developed to address these shortages through a multidisciplinary workforce development model grounded in the Collaborative Care framework. This paper describes the MPath model and presents findings from a 4-year mixed-methods program evaluation. Data sources include administrative records, participant surveys, professional development evaluations, post-graduation surveys, and exit interviews from 48 scholars enrolled across three cohorts, with 21 graduates, 20 active scholars, and 7 withdrawals. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, with qualitative data analyzed through iterative coding and constant comparison. Findings indicate high levels of scholar satisfaction, particularly regarding financial support, mentoring, professional development, and practicum experiences. More than 90% of scholars reported that the program prepared them for their future careers, and professional development activities were associated with perceived gains in behavioral health knowledge and skills. Approximately 71% of graduates were employed at graduation, and most are working in positions aligned with their training and serving high-need schools or communities. Qualitative findings highlighted the importance of tuition assistance, multidisciplinary collaboration, and experiential learning. Results underscore the influence of broader policy and funding environments on workforce development efforts. Implications are discussed for strengthening behavioral health workforce pipelines through ecosystem-level investments in scholars, supervisors, partnerships, and training infrastructure.

items.title: Breviscapine Attenuates Manganese-Induced Renal Injury and Associated Redox and Iron Imbalances in Mice.
items.abstract: Manganese (Mn) is an essential trace element, but excessive exposure can cause systemic toxicity. The kidney is involved in metal handling and excretion, yet the molecular features of Mn-induced renal injury and potential interventions remain unclear. This study evaluated whether breviscapine (Bre) attenuates subacute Mn-induced renal injury in mice and examined its association with oxidative stress, iron dyshomeostasis, and ferroptosis-related molecular alterations. Male C57BL/6 mice were first exposed to different doses of MnCl₂·4 H₂O for 30 consecutive days to establish a dose-response model. A second experiment including control, Mn, Bre, and Mn + Bre groups was performed to assess the protective effect of Bre. Serum Mn concentrations were measured only in the Mn dose experiment; renal Mn concentrations were not measured in either experiment. Relative serum creatinine (Scr) levels, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), renal histopathology, malondialdehyde (MDA), glutathione (GSH), Fe²⁺, and ferroptosis-related molecular markers were also assessed. Mn exposure increased serum Mn concentrations, relative serum Scr levels, and serum BUN levels, and induced renal tubular injury. Mn also increased renal MDA and Fe²⁺ levels, decreased GSH content, reduced renal NRF2, SLC7A11, and GPX4 protein abundance, upregulated DMT1 and TFR1, and enhanced ACSL4-positive fluorescence signals. Bre treatment reduced Mn-induced renal dysfunction and histopathological injury. It also partially reversed oxidative stress, iron dyshomeostasis, and ferroptosis-related molecular alterations. These findings suggest a potential protective effect of Bre against subacute Mn-induced renal injury, with accompanying improvements in redox and iron-related measures.

items.title: Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease.
items.abstract: Although coronary artery disease (CAD) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci, most variants lie in non-coding regions, obscuring the causal gene programmes and cell types driving disease1,2. Here we performed single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility in human coronary arteries from 44 people to construct a genome-wide single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map. We identified 11,269 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) across principal vascular cell types, including CAD-associated caQTLs in smooth muscle cells (SMCs). Using dynamic single-cell caQTL modelling3, we show that variant effects on chromatin vary across SMC states. For example, rs658956 -mediated suppression of the FGGY-DT enhancer through disruption of an AP-1 motif is amplified as SMCs transition towards a fibromyocyte fate. We next performed genome-wide high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) in 15 human coronary arteries, showing that rs4887091 in the ADAMTS7 CAD locus has allele-dependent effects on CCCTC-binding factor occupancy and loop strength. Integrating Hi-C, Hi-C with chromatin immunoprecipitation and in vitro clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats interference (CRISPRi) nominated AMOTL2 as a distal SMC-specific CAD gene whose loss promotes proliferation and suppresses contractile identity. Finally, arrayed Perturb-seq of GWAS-nominated enhancers converged on extracellular matrix remodelling as a core SMC disease programme. Together, these findings provide a framework for mapping non-coding GWAS variants to cell types, chromatin states and gene programmes in human disease.

items.title: Biotin intake and mental health: findings from a large population-based cohort and biological insights from hippocampal and gut-brain pathways.
items.abstract: The relationship between biotin and mental health remains largely unexplored. Leveraging data from the UK Biobank prospective cohort, we found that dietary biotin intake in the second quartile was associated with a 15% lower risk of major depressive disorder, while intake in the third quartile was associated with a 14% lower risk of anxiety disorder, compared with the lowest quartile. Furthermore, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses revealed nonlinear associations between dietary biotin intake and both outcomes, with the lowest risks of incidence observed at biotin intake levels of approximately 40-50 μg. Neuroimaging analyses further revealed positive associations between dietary biotin intake and fractional anisotropy in the cingulum-hippocampus tract, suggesting a potential link between biotin intake and white matter microstructure in a pathway involved in emotional regulation. We then examined the effects of a 9-week biotin intervention in mice and observed changes consistent with two potential pathways: a hippocampus-related pathway involving enhanced protein biotinylation, reduced neuronal nitric oxide synthase (nNOS) expression, and increased brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) expression, and a gut-brain axis pathway characterized by greater microbial diversity and an increased relative abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila, which was positively associated with brain 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) levels. These findings provide complementary biological evidence that may help explain the observed association between dietary biotin intake and mental health.

items.title: Predictive uncertainty representations in clinical AI shape physicians' advice uptake, accuracy, and trust.
items.abstract: Machine-learning-based clinical decision support is entering routine care, but its value depends on whether clinicians can judge when to follow its advice and when to override it. Evidence suggests this judgment is often poorly calibrated in both directions. Whether displaying a model's predictive uncertainty helps physicians integrate advice more selectively is unclear. In a preregistered, randomized vignette experiment, 227 physicians produced 1,802 sepsis risk assessments. Physicians gave an initial risk estimate, saw advice from a machine-learning system, and revised their estimate. They were randomized to see a risk score alone, or the score together with one of two visual representations of predictive uncertainty: icon arrays with uncertainty bands, or quantile dotplots. Outcomes were advice uptake, accuracy of the revised risk estimate, and trust. Here we show that both uncertainty representations increase advice uptake relative to the risk score alone, by 23% and 21%, and that the gap between correct and incorrect advice is descriptively about twice as large. Uptake of incorrect advice is not reliably reduced. Both formats improve the accuracy of revised risk estimates, with the larger effect for quantile dotplots, but only icon arrays increase trust. Physicians describe uncertainty as actionable only where they can tell why it is elevated. Displaying predictive uncertainty changes how physicians integrate machine-learning advice, but the representation format determines whether the benefit appears mainly as accuracy or trust. The effect is partial: uncertainty representations support recognizing reliable advice more than rejecting unreliable advice.

items.title: Local Decoherence of Stress Anisotropy Triggers Solitary Cell Escape From Epithelial Collectives.
items.abstract: Epithelial tissues can transition between cohesive sheets and discrete migratory individuals, a bifurcation that underlies morphogenesis and cancer dissemination. Here we identify stress anisotropy, the directional imbalance between radial and circumferential stresses within the monolayer, as a physical order parameter governing this transition. Using traction force microscopy and monolayer stress microscopy, we construct spatiotemporal maps of the stress tensor during epithelial expansion and uncover that the collective-to-solitary transition is preceded by a local loss of stress anisotropy, rather than by a change in force magnitude. At prospective dissemination sites, anisotropic stress initially develops with protrusion but subsequently collapses before overt cell escape, whereas it remains sustained in collective fingers. We further show that P-cadherin stabilizes this anisotropic stress state, maintaining mechanical coherence and cohesive motion. Its depletion disrupts stress anisotropy and increases solitary cell escape. These findings identify local decoherence of stress anisotropy as a mechanical transition preceding solitary escape and implicate P-cadherin in maintaining the stress coherence that favors collective fingering, establishing stress anisotropy as a central organizing principle in epithelial tissue mechanics.

items.title: Tumor Membrane-Coated Biogenic Ausome Nanovaccine Reprograms the Metastatic Liver Niche of Colorectal Cancer for Potent Prophylactic and Therapeutic Immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) remains a major clinical challenge, partly due to its immunosuppressive microenvironment, which limits responses to conventional immunotherapies. Conventional cancer nanovaccines may face challenges related to limited adjuvant signaling breadth and insufficient antigen coverage in heterogeneous tumors. Herein, we report a biohybrid nanovaccine (FnM-Vax) engineered by repurposing the tumor-colonizing bacterium Fusobacterium nucleatum as a living biofactory to synthesize immunostructurally active gold nanoparticles (AusomeFn) with a functional corona of bacterial biomolecules. Coating these AusomeFn cores with MC38-derived tumor cell membranes generates a self-adjuvanting nanovaccine that combines a broad repertoire of tumor-associated membrane antigens with bacteria-derived immunostimulatory components. Transcriptomic profiling revealed coordinated changes in Toll-like receptor- and NOD-like receptor-associated signaling pathways in DCs, accompanied by enhanced DC maturation and immunostimulatory responses. After intravenous administration, DiD-labeled FnM-Vax displayed organ-dependent distribution and association with multiple antigen-presenting and myeloid-cell populations. In murine CRLM models, early FnM-Vax administration suppressed metastatic progression, whereas therapeutic administration was associated with enhanced CD8+ T-cell and NK-cell-associated immune responses and reduced regulatory T-cell frequencies in the metastatic microenvironment. Sequential treatment with oxaliplatin and FnM-Vax further enhanced antitumor efficacy and was associated with positive enrichment of PPAR signaling and changes in fatty acid oxidation-related gene and protein expression.

items.title: Prevalence and outcomes of bloodstream infections caused by multidrug-resistant bacteria in the emergency department: results from a prospective multicentre study.
items.abstract: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) are a major cause of sepsis and septic shock cases presenting to the Emergency Department (ED). The aim of the present study was to determine the prevalence of multidrug-resistant organisms (MDRO) among patients presenting to the ED with BSI, to identify factors associated, and describe their impact on clinical outcomes. We conducted an observational prospective multicentre study, involving 7 centres, including all adult patients admitted between January 2025 and October 2025 with a confirmed BSI. Primary outcome was to determine the prevalence of BSIs caused by MDROs and the factors associated with MDROs BSI. We included 210 patients with a confirmed BSI: the origin of BSI was the urinary tract in 44.3% of subjects; Gram-negative bacteria accounted for 68.6% of cases, mainly Enterobacterales (60.9%). A MDRO was isolated in 56 (29.2%) of the 192 patients with available susceptibility data. The presence of a urinary catheter was the only independent predictor of MDRO BSI (OR 3.423, 95% CI 1.522-7.695; p = 0.003). Overall, 28-day and 7-day mortality and clinical response rate were 34.2%, 10.3% and 46.1%, respectively. A higher baseline SOFA score was independently associated with 28-day mortality (OR 1.379, 95% CI 1.009-1.885; p = 0.044), whereas infectious disease consultation resulted as a protective factor (OR 0.137, 95% CI 0.021-0.901; p = 0.039). Nearly one-third of BSIs diagnosed in the ED were caused by MDROs. Knowledge of local resistance epidemiology and early identification of patients at increased risk of MDRO infections are essential to optimize empirical antibiotic therapy and improve clinical outcomes.

items.title: Harmonising cardiovascular risk classification across prediction functions using population percentiles: The ORESTES study.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevention strategies use risk prediction functions to classify individuals into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk categories. Currently recommended thresholds allocate markedly different proportions of the population to these categories across functions. We aimed to develop a percentile-based approach for deriving population-calibrated cut-off points across models and to replicate the approach in an independent cohort. We analysed 437,733 participants aged 45-74 years from a population-based cohort in Catalonia, Spain (PADRIS), and replicated findings in 644,989 participants from other Spanish regions (BIFAP). CVD risk was estimated using Framingham, REGICOR, FRESCO, SCORE2, CUORE, and the AHA Pooled Cohort Equation. For each function, percentile-based cut-off points corresponding approximately to the lower 65%, middle 20%, and upper 15% of the population risk distribution were derived, as an example. We compared population classification, event incidence, and illustrative numbers needed to treat (NNT). During a median follow-up of 9.6 years in PADRIS (4.2 million person-years), 10-year incidence was 4.7% for CVD. Guideline-recommended thresholds produced substantial heterogeneity in population classification, with 12-29% of individuals classified as high risk by functions. Despite these differences, discrimination was broadly similar across models. Percentile-based thresholds harmonised category distributions across risk functions, with similar illustrative NNT estimates. Findings were replicated in BIFAP. Commonly used CAD and CVD risk functions classify substantially different proportions of the population into intermediate- and high-risk categories. A percentile-based population approach may harmonise relative risk categorisation across models without modifying the underlying continuous risk estimates.

items.title: Modified LRINEC score incorporating bullae and band-form neutrophils for differentiating necrotizing fasciitis from severe cellulitis.
items.abstract: Necrotizing fasciitis (NF) is a rapidly progressive, life-threatening condition that is often difficult to distinguish from severe cellulitis because of overlapping early clinical features. Although the Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis (LRINEC) score was developed for early diagnosis, its performance has been inconsistent across validation studies. We aimed to identify additional predictors from common clinical and laboratory indicators, develop a modified LRINEC (m-LRINEC) score, and validate its diagnostic performance. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with NF or severe cellulitis at a tertiary center. NF cases from 2007 to 2017 were identified using ICD-9/10 codes and confirmed by operative or pathological findings. Severe cellulitis controls were selected using standardized SSTI severity criteria and systemic inflammatory response syndrome criteria. An independent cohort from 2018 to 2022 was used for validation. Variables significant in univariate analysis were entered into stepwise logistic regression to construct the m-LRINEC score. The derivation cohort comprised 103 patients with NF and 152 with severe cellulitis. Stepwise logistic regression identified three predictors of NF: LRINEC score, bullae formation, and band-form neutrophils. The m-LRINEC (LRINEC score + 4 points for bullae + 7 points for band forms) score outperformed the original score, with AUROCs of 0.805 vs. 0.635 in the derivation cohort and 0.954 vs. 0.867 in the validation cohort. Klebsiella pneumoniae and Staphylococcus aureus were the predominant pathogens in monomicrobial NF. The m-LRINEC score improves diagnostic performance and may facilitate recognition and management of NF.

items.title: Prenatal exposure to drug treatment for attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder and risk of neurodevelopmental disorders: Scandinavian multinational cohort study.
items.abstract: To assess whether prenatal exposure to drug treatment for attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) increases the risk of neurodevelopmental disorders in children. Population based cohort study. Nationwide register data on births, dispensed drugs, and specialist healthcare diagnoses from Denmark, Norway, and Sweden. 3 643 376 children born in 2000-21 followed up for a median 9 years after birth in Sweden and 10 years in Norway and Denmark. Prenatal exposure, defined as ≥1 filled prescription for ADHD drug treatment anytime during pregnancy or in the second/third trimester (≥98 days after the last menstrual period). Analyses were also done for monotherapy with methylphenidate, amphetamines, and atomoxetine. Unexposed pregnancies had no filled prescriptions for ADHD drugs during pregnancy. Neurodevelopmental disorders (any, subgroups, and individual disorders), identified on the basis of inpatient and outpatient diagnoses in specialist healthcare. Propensity score overlap weighted Cox proportional hazards regression was used to estimate adjusted (weighted) hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Data from Denmark were analysed separately, and results were pooled using random effects meta-analysis. 7595 (0.2%) children were prenatally exposed to any ADHD drug (5230 methylphenidate, 1510 amphetamines, 553 atomoxetine only). About one third (n=2389) were exposed in the second/third trimester. After control for confounders, neither any nor second/third trimester exposure to ADHD drugs overall or by drug type was associated with increased risk of any neurodevelopmental disorder (weighted hazard ratio 1.05, 95% confidence interval 0.98 to 1.12), behavioural and emotional disorders (1.04, 0.97 to 1.12), or disorders of psychological and intellectual development (1.06, 0.96 to 1.18). Some elevated hazard ratios for infrequent outcomes were observed but not consistently identified across analyses. This multinational cohort study found no increased risk of childhood neurodevelopmental disorders associated with prenatal exposure to ADHD drugs. These findings strengthen existing evidence and can assist pregnant people and clinicians in weighing the benefits and risks of such treatment during pregnancy.

items.title: Preconception antidepressant use in fathers and risk of metabolic disorders in offspring: Danish population based cohort study.
items.abstract: To investigate the associations between paternal antidepressant use during spermatogenesis and risk of metabolic disorders in offspring. Nationwide population based cohort study. Danish national registers. 1 365 887 liveborn singleton infants in Denmark from 2000 to 2023, followed from birth until 31 December 2023, death, emigration, or first occurrence of outcome, whichever came first. Metabolic disorders in offspring, including type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, and overweight or obesity, were identified from hospital and prescription records. Offspring of fathers who took antidepressants during spermatogenesis (three months before pregnancy) were compared with those of fathers who did not take antidepressants during this period and fathers who used antidepressants only during pregnancy to further account for underlying paternal mental health conditions. Associations between paternal antidepressant use and metabolic disorders, collectively and individually, were estimated as propensity score weighted hazard ratios using Cox regression. 23 572 (1.7%) offspring were born to fathers who used antidepressants during spermatogenesis. During a mean follow-up of 12.1 years (standard deviation 7.0 years), 18 353 (1.3%) offspring were diagnosed with a metabolic disorder, including 364 whose fathers used antidepressants during spermatogenesis and 17 989 whose fathers did not use antidepressants during this period (1.39 v 1.11 events per 1000 person years, respectively). Offspring whose fathers used antidepressants during spermatogenesis had a slightly higher risk of developing metabolic disorders (weighted hazard ratio 1.20, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.04 to 1.38) compared with offspring who were unexposed. The associations varied by specific metabolic outcomes, with weighted hazard ratios ranging from 0.81 (95% CI 0.45 to 1.47) for hypercholesterolaemia to 1.64 (95% CI 1.21 to 2.22) for hypertension. However, when compared with offspring of fathers who took antidepressants during the pregnancy period only, no increased risk was found of any metabolic disorders (0.75, 95% CI 0.58 to 0.98) or of specific metabolic disorders. The slightly increased risk of metabolic disorders in offspring of fathers using antidepressants during spermatogenesis was probably attributable to underlying paternal mental health disorders. These findings offer reassurance for men treated with antidepressants before pregnancy.

items.title: [Obesity disease management program for adults: an empirical-ethical analysis].
items.abstract: Obesity poses major challenges to the German healthcare system due to its high prevalence. To date, no standardised model of routine care has been established. In 2023, the structural framework for a Disease Management Program (DMP) for obesity was adopted; however, nationwide contractual implementation has yet to be achieved. Ethical reflection on DMPs remains an underexplored area of research. A retrospective analysis was conducted on 20 semi-structured interviews with participants in a weight reduction programme to identify and critically reflect on requirements for a DMP. The interviews were transcribed, pseudonymised, and coded using qualitative data analysis software. Data were analysed by means of qualitative content analysis. Ethical mid-level principles (relational autonomy, care, and justice) were applied within the framework of empirical ethics to interpret the data and derive normative conclusions for healthcare practice. The findings indicate that, due to the lack of structured care pathways, participants are largely left to manage their obesity on their own and often try numerous diets, mostly without achieving sustainable success. In addition, some individuals are unable to participate in an appropriate structured programme because of limited financial or time resources, as reimbursement policies among statutory health insurance providers are inconsistent. Participants also frequently reported experiences of weight-related stigma and emphasised the importance of social support provided by peer groups. From an ethical perspective, a DMP for obesity should not primarily be understood as an instrument for behavioural control or cost containment, but rather as a normative framework for shaping equitable and patient-centred care. An ethically robust obesity DMP should actively promote patient autonomy, provide holistic and compassionate care, and reduce rather than reinforce structural inequalities. Achieving these aims requires clearer allocation of responsibilities and stronger interprofessional collaboration. Moreover, the findings suggest that an obesity DMP should be embedded within broader societal efforts to promote health and prevent obesity.

items.title: The association between prenatal exposure to metals and food allergy in children.
items.abstract: Food allergy is a global health concern. Prenatal exposure to heavy metals has been associated with immune dysregulation and may influence child food allergy (CFA) risk. We investigated associations between prenatal metals (non-essential and essential) and CFA. This study included 555 mother-child pairs in New York City from the PRogramming of Intergenerational Stress Mechanisms (PRISM) cohort, a prospective pregnancy cohort. Prenatal levels of antimony, arsenic, aluminum, copper, cadmium, lead, manganese, and zinc were measured in urine samples collected mid-pregnancy. Child food allergy was reported by mothers from ages two to thirty-four months. Individual and mixture associations were examined using multivariable logistic and weighted quantile sum (WQS) regressions, respectively, adjusting for maternal race/ethnicity, age, educational attainment, prenatal urinary creatinine level, gestational age at sample collection, and child sex. Women were predominantly Black (55%) and Non-Black Hispanic (39%). Child food allergy prevalence was 19%. In individual multivariable adjusted models, CFA was associated with manganese (OR=1.29 per doubling of exposure, 95%CI: 1.12-1.51) and aluminum (OR=1.27, 95%CI:1.07-1.53) concentrations, and marginally associated with antimony (OR=1.25, 95%CI: 0.98-1.60) and lead (OR=1.15, 95%CI: 0.97-1.37) concentrations. In WQS models for an overall mixture effect, a decile increase in the mixture was associated with increased odds of CFA in the overall sample (OR=1.19 , 95%CI: 1.06-1.35), driven primarily by manganese, antimony and aluminum. In sex-stratified WQS analyses, a decile increase in the mixture was associated with increased CFA (OR=1.31, 95%CI: 1.07-1.62) in male children compared to non-significant increase (OR = 1.10, 95%CI: 0.94-1.29) in females. Prenatal metal exposures were positively associated with parent-reported CFA, particularly among males.
