items.title: Oral microbiome signatures were associated with per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and circulating cardiometabolic biomarkers.
items.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widespread environmental contaminants linked to cardiometabolic health, yet the role of the oral microbiome remains unexplored. We examined associations between PFAS exposure, oral microbiome, and circulating cardiometabolic biomarkers. In 381 adults from the Chicago Multiethnic Prevention and Surveillance Study (COMPASS), we measured five serum PFAS (PFOA, br-PFOS, n-PFOS, n-PFHxS, ∑PFOS). The oral microbiome was profiled in saliva. We used ANCOM-BC2 to identify PFAS-associated taxa (FDR<0.05) and constructed PFAS-oral microbiome indices. Associations of these indices with oral microbiome composition and six cardiometabolic biomarkers (ghrelin, resistin, leptin, C-peptide, CK-MB, MCP-1) were evaluated. PFAS exposure was significantly associated with 42 taxa. Positive associations were predominantly observed with obligate anaerobes linked to periodontitis (e.g., Sphaerochaeta, Fretibacterium), while inverse associations were observed for facultative anaerobes and beneficial genera (e.g., Bifidobacterium, Butyrivibrio). Single PFAS compounds and individual taxa showed few associations with oral microbiome diversity or cardiometabolic biomarkers. In contrast, PFAS-oral microbiome indices were significantly associated with alpha diversity and explained significant variation in beta diversity (R2=4.7%-7.0%, all p-value < 0.001). The PFOA-oral microbiome index was positively associated with MCP-1, and the n-PFHxS-oral microbiome index was inversely associated with C-peptide. PFAS exposure is associated with oral microbiome signatures characterized by obligate anaerobes and periodontitis-related taxa, alongside lower abundance of beneficial bacteria. PFAS-microbiome indices were associated with inflammatory and metabolic biomarkers, suggesting that the oral microbiome may be involved in the pathways linking PFAS exposure to cardiometabolic health. Longitudinal studies are needed to confirm causality.

items.title: Self-administered hormonal contraception use and screening bimanual pelvic examinations: associations in an employer-sponsored insurance claims database.
items.abstract: We sought to test our hypothesis that the prevalence of screening pelvic examinations at preventive care visits was higher for users of self-administered hormonal contraception (SAHC) compared to non-users of SAHC. We identified females ages 15 to 54 enrolled in a large, employer-sponsored insurance claims database and used prescription fills around an index preventive care visit to classify them as non-users, recent users, ongoing users, or new users of SAHC. We compared each user group to SAHC non-users, balanced covariates using inverse probability of treatment weights, and calculated the relative prevalence of screening pelvic examinations, i.e., those that occurred in the absence of a coded medical indication, on index visit for each SAHC user group compared to non-users. At the index preventive care visits, the crude prevalence of screening pelvic exams was 43.9% for SAHC non-users, 54.5% for recent, 60.3% for ongoing, and 63.7% for new SAHC users. The weighted relative prevalence of screening pelvic exams was 1.21 among ongoing SAHC users vs. non-users (95% confidence interval, CI, 1.20-1.21), 1.19 among new vs. non-users (95% CI 1.19-1.20), and 1.14 among recent vs. non-users (95% CI 1.14-1.14). Individuals classified as recent, ongoing, or new SAHC users at the time of a preventive care visit experienced a higher prevalence of screening pelvic exams at that visit compared to non-users of SAHC. Future work is needed to examine the potential barrier that screening pelvic exams pose to SAHC use and strategies to de-implement the practice of performing them when prescribing or caring for SAHC users.

items.title: Displaced Knowledge: Abortion-related False Information, Legal Ambiguity, and Grassroots Resistance in Post-Dobbs Texas.
items.abstract: The purpose of this study was to examine how false information about abortion is experienced, navigated, and resisted by those supporting abortion access in Texas following the U.S. Supreme Court's decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization. We conducted a secondary thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with 15 grassroots abortion activists recruited through purposive and snowball sampling between November 2023 and April 2024. Guided by a reproductive justice perspective, we examined activists' experiences with abortion-related false information, including its perceived sources, impacts, and organizational responses. Activists described barriers to accessing accurate abortion information, including fragmented digital platforms, limited Spanish-language resources, and misleading information from crisis pregnancy centers. Participants reported that legal uncertainty contributed to fear and self-censorship, with healthcare providers, educational institutions, and community partners increasingly reluctant to share abortion-related information. In response, activists relied on trusted community networks, developed educational materials, directed individuals to vetted abortion resources, and organized campaigns to expose misleading practices at crisis pregnancy centers. In restrictive policy environments, abortion information is not eliminated but displaced from formal clinical systems into informal networks, disproportionately burdening marginalized communities. In response, activists described information-sharing through trusted community networks, vetted resources, and community education. Restrictive abortion policy environments may affect not only access to abortion care but also pathways to accurate reproductive health information. Activists' reliance on trusted community networks highlights opportunities for healthcare systems to strengthen connections with community-based information pathways.

items.title: Exclusion of patients experiencing homelessness from Canadian linked health administrative data research: A critical investigation.
items.abstract: In Canada, health administrative research typically includes encounters linked through a valid health card number (HCN), which serves as proof of public insurance coverage. Patients experiencing homelessness (PEH) often lack valid HCNs, which can lead to exclusion and bias. We compared invalid HCN in emergency department (ED) visits between PEH and people not experiencing homelessness (PNEH). This population-level study included ED visits in jurisdictions with complete reporting (Ontario, Alberta, and Yukon) from April 1, 2022, to March 31, 2023. PEH were identified using ICD-10-CA codes Z59.0 and Z59.1. The primary outcome was invalid HCN. Differences between PEH and PNEH were estimated using adjusted incidence rate ratios (aIRR) from Poisson generalized linear models with robust variance. Subgroup aIRRs were compared with the overall aIRR using ratios of IRRs (RIRR) with 95% confidence intervals from seemingly unrelated estimation. Among 100,082 PEH and 6,838,899 PNEH visits, PEH were over three times more likely to have invalid HCN (9.0% vs. 2.2%; aIRR 3.38 [95% CI 3.31-3.45]). PEH-PNEH differences were significantly above average for visits covered through provincial or territorial healthcare plans (RIRR 2.66 [2.55-2.71]), ages 40-59 (RIRR 1.31 [1.26-1.35]) ages 60+ (RIRR 2.54 [2.39-2.71]), and circulatory (RIRR 1.51 [1.26-1.81]), respiratory (RIRR 1.26 [1.12-1.42]) and digestive system visits (RIRR 1.18 [1.02-1.36]). They were significantly below average for mental and behavioural disorders (RIRR 0.83 [0.80-0.86]) and injuries affecting specific body regions (RIRR 0.85 [0.80-0.91]). Restricting to visits with valid HCNs overestimated disparities for substance use and cold-related injuries, but the net effect on estimates using all visits was modest. PEH health encounters are disproportionately and non-randomly excluded from administrative data research linked using HCN. Non-random exclusion could result in biased disparity estimates. Health administrative data infrastructure reliant on health card identifiers should consider implementing more inclusive linkage approaches.

items.title: Adipocyte lipolysis associates with long-term development of hyperlipidaemia.
items.abstract: Adipocyte functions (cellularity, lipid breakdown and synthesis) associate with simultaneous presence of elevated circulating lipid levels. This study examined if such features also relate to future development of hyperlipidaemia. Between 1988-2016 we investigated 1004 Swedish individuals with biochemical/anthropometric examinations, a health questionnaire, and abdominal subcutaneous adipocyte size, basal and stimulated lipolysis (triglyceride breakdown), and adipose insulin resistance (Adipo-IR, fasting serum levels of insulin times fatty acids). All individuals were contacted again 2018-22 for a repeated health survey (17 years in mean observation time). A response was obtained from 280 participants, whereof 210 individuals did not haveout hyperlipidaemia at baseline and follow-up and 44 developed a hyperlipidaemia diagnosis at follow-up. These groups were compared by unpaired t-test and logistic regression, while considering the influence of relevant co-factors. Of all functional features, only the basal (spontaneous) adipocyte lipolysis rate (log10 µmoles of glycerol release per number of adipocytes) independently associated with development of hyperlipidaemia over time. The basal lipolysis rate was about 45 % increased (p = 0.0002) in those developing hyperlipidaemia. This relationship with hyperlipidaemia development was independent of sex, age, body mass index, initial lipid levels, waist-to-hip ratio, bariatric surgery, observation time, insulin resistance, body weight changes over time , smoking, physical activity or simultaneous presence of type 2 diabetes. The basal rate of fat cell lipolysis associates with future development of hyperlipidaemia even following adjustment for pertinent co-factors.

items.title: HELZ2 knockdown alleviates hepatic steatosis and reduces inflammatory responses in mice.
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) involves hepatic steatosis, metabolic dysfunction and inflammation. HELZ2 has been linked to hepatic lipid metabolism and immune transcription, but its role in MAFLD remains unclear. Peripheral-blood whole-transcriptome sequencing was performed in eight patients with MAFLD and eight healthy controls. Candidate genes were examined by RT-qPCR in an independent cohort. We studied HELZ2 in HFD-fed mice via AAV8-mediated knockdown and in a public human liver RNA-sequencing cohort. HELZ2 was nominally upregulated in the discovery cohort but lost significance after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (log2FC = 0.677; nominal P = 0.00475; adjusted P = 0.999). It had the highest discovery-cohort AUC (0.922) and was the only prioritized gene significantly increased in validation. Peripheral-blood HELZ2 strongly correlated with clinical parameters of MAFLD, including BMI, liver enzymes, and lipid profiles. In an independent liver cohort (GSE135251), HELZ2 expression was higher in the fatty liver disease group (median ratio, 1.42; two-sided Wilcoxon P = 0.000709). HFD feeding increased hepatic HELZ2 expression, TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB-associated signaling, circulating cytokines, and CD86/iNOS, while reducing Arg1/CD206. HELZ2 knockdown reduced hepatic lipid accumulation, steatosis, and serum ALT/AST, with minimal body-weight effects, and reversed the pathway-associated readouts, circulating cytokines, and tissue-marker changes. HELZ2 is associated with MAFLD, and its knockdown alleviated hepatic steatosis and liver injury in HFD-fed mice. These improvements were accompanied by reduced inflammatory responses and TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB-associated signaling, together with altered M1/M2-associated tissue-marker expression. The findings do not establish a direct HELZ2-TLR interaction or macrophage-specific polarization effects; the underlying molecular mechanism remains unresolved.

items.title: Differential Cardio-Cerebrovascular Health Implications of PM 2.5 Oxidative Potential Metrics: DTTm versus DTTv in a large Chinese Adult Population.
items.abstract: Existing studies have shown that fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is associated with an increased risk of cardio-cerebrovascular diseases (CCVD), while the oxidative potential of PM2.5 (OPP) has emerged as a toxicity-relevant metric. However, epidemiological evidence linking OPP exposure to CCVD remains limited. This study examined the association between OPP exposure and CCVD among 788,472 adults in the Pearl River Delta region of Guangdong Province, China, and compared the associations of the two OPP metrics (DTTm and DTTv). CCVD outcomes were self-reported physician-diagnosed conditions including coronary heart disease and cerebrovascular diseases. Participants were assigned OPP exposures based on geocoded residential addresses using spatial-temporal exposure models. Associations were estimated using spatial generalized linear mixed models that adjusted for potential confounders. Each interquartile range (IQR) increase in OPP exposure was associated with higher odds of overall CCVD (OR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.10-1.13 for DTTm; OR = 1.03, 95% CI: 1.02-1.05 for DTTv). Similar patterns were observed for coronary heart disease (OR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.17-1.20 for DTTm; OR = 1.07, 95% CI: 1.05-1.09 for DTTv). Overall, associations were numerically larger for DTTm than for DTTv across CCVD outcomes. Furthermore, associations of DTTm with CCVD were larger in magnitude among participants aged <65 years, those with higher education and income, non-smokers, regular exercisers, and individuals with normal weight, whereas no clear or significant subgroup differences were observed for DTTv except for age, education and income. These findings support further investigation of OPP as a complementary metric to PM2.5 mass concentration in epidemiological studies of CCVD. However, given the cross-sectional study design, causal inferences cannot be made, and prospective studies are needed to confirm these associations and clarify the potential health effects of OPP.

items.title: Enhanced Protection by Fluoride Varnish with Nano-Sized Sodium Trimetaphosphate Against Enamel Erosive Wear: An In Situ Study.
items.abstract: To assess the effects of fluoride varnishes containing micrometric or nano-sized sodium trimetaphosphate (TMPmicro or TMPnano, respectively) on erosive tooth wear (ETW) in situ. In this randomized, double-blind, crossover study, 14 participants wore palatal devices containing bovine enamel blocks (n=4/device), which received each of the four varnish treatments in separate experimental periods: Placebo (Pla - without F/TMP); 5% NaF (5NaF); 5NaF + 5% TMPmicro (5-TMPmicro); and 5NaF + 5% TMPnano (5-TMPnano). After 6 h of intraoral exposure and varnish removal, the blocks underwent four daily erosive challenges ex vivo for five days (ERO, 0.05 M citric acid, pH 3.2, 90 s), while two blocks were additionally subjected to abrasion by brushing (ERO+ABR). Profilometry, surface hardness (SH), cross-sectional hardness (ΔKHN) and computed X-ray micro tomography (gHAp × cm⁻³ × µm) were performed. Data were analyzed using two-way repeated-measures ANOVA and Holm-Sidak's test (p<0.05). ETW, integrated mineral loss and depth of mineral loss of the remaining eroded enamel showed a consistent treatment ranking under both conditions, with the greatest protection observed for 5-TMPnano, followed by 5-TMPmicro, 5NaF, and Pla. Compared with 5NaF, ETW was reduced by 20-22% with 5-TMPmicro and 40-50% with 5-TMPnano under ERO and ERO+ABR. A similar pattern was observed for hardness in depth (ΔKHN at 5-30 µm from the enamel surface), except between 5-TMPmicro and 5-TMPnano. Compared with 5NaF, SH loss was significantly lower for both TMP-containing varnishes under ERO, but only for 5-TMPnano under ERO+ABR. F varnish supplemented with TMP significantly reduced ETW in situ, and nano-sized TMP provided additional protection. The addition of TMP to 5% NaF varnishes, especially as nanoparticles, may enhance their protective effect against enamel erosive wear.

items.title: Survival of root canal-treated teeth during a 15-year observation period in public dental service: A register-based study.
items.abstract: Regardless of the increasing numbers of studies investigating outcomes of non-surgical root canal treatment (nsRCT), it is important to explore long-term survival of root canal-treated teeth (RCTT) in clinical practice. This study aimed to assess survival of RCTT in public dental service (PDS) in a 15-year observation period, and to evaluate the impact of patient-, tooth-, and operator-related factors on tooth survival. This retrospective register-based study was conducted by using data obtained from electronic patient records of the PDS of the City of Helsinki. Altogether 84 320 non-surgically RCTT between 2002 and 2016 were included in the study. Survival of the RCTT was assessed with Kaplan-Meier estimator and Cox regression model. Cumulative survival rates after primary nsRCT in a five-, 10- and 15-year observation period were 91.1%, 82.8% and 77.2%, respectively. Hazard of tooth extraction was highest in older age groups, and for molar teeth. Teeth restored with indirect restorations had over 50% lower hazard of tooth extraction compared to those restored with direct restorations. Placement of coronal restoration after 12 months of root canal filling was found to decrease the likelihood of tooth survival. The cumulative survival rates of RCTT in the PDS were similar to those reported in previous studies elsewhere. Higher age and molars were risk factors for tooth extraction. Placement of indirect restoration was associated with higher likelihood of tooth survival, supporting its consideration as part of the coronal restorative management of RCTT. Confounding factors such as treatment history and restorability of the tooth and caries risk of the patient should be taken into account in future studies. Long-term tooth survival rates after endodontic treatments can be acceptable in routine clinical practice where most of the treatments are performed by general dentists. Tooth survival was associated with factors related to restorative treatment highlighting its importance in retention of root canal-treated teeth.

items.title: Requirements under external constraint: infection prevention and control in field hospitals.
items.abstract: Field hospitals must maintain baseline infection prevention and control (IPC) when access to external services and resources is restricted. This analysis examines how external constraint changes the fulfilment of established IPC requirements, not the requirements themselves. WHO Standard Precautions provided the international baseline, supported by NATO doctrine on routine IPC in medical treatment facilities. Eleven precautions were expressed as functional target states and mapped to dependencies on Infrastructure, Material, Human, Organization and Assurance. Typical external fulfilment pathways were identified, and consequences of constraining supply, removal, processing, space and specialist capacity were examined. Constraint shifts fulfilment onto the organic system. Across the precautions examined, consequences of this shift could be described using three recurring, non-exclusive dynamics: depletion of finite inputs, accumulation of outputs that cannot leave the system, and saturation of finite organic capacity. IPC capability cannot be inferred from nominal configuration alone; fulfilment pathways must be made explicit before constraint produces failure.

items.title: Immunogenicity and safety of a live-attenuated varicella vaccine in healthy individuals aged ≥13 years in China: a phase 3, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, non-inferiority trial.
items.abstract: This phase 3, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled, non-inferiority trial compared test and control varicella vaccines (VarVs) in healthy participants aged ≥13 years without prior varicella vaccination or disease. Conducted at a single center in China (July 2023-March 2024), 1,600 eligible participants were stratified by age (13-17 vs. ≥18 years) and randomized 1:1:1:1 to receive test or control VarV on 0- and 4-week or 0- and 8-week schedule. Primary endpoints were seroconversion rate (SR) difference and geometric mean titer (GMT) ratio at 42 days post-full immunization. Non-inferiority required the lower bound of two-sided 95% CI for SR difference >-5.00% and for GMT ratio >0.67. Primary safety endpoint was incidence of adverse reaction (AR) within 28 days after either dose. In per-protocol population (n =1,444), test VarV was non-inferior to control VarV for SR (difference 3.97%, 95% CI 0.75%, 7.18%) and GMT (ratio 1.20, 95% CI 1.09, 1.33). Local ARs were higher with test VarV, including injection-site pain (7.01% vs. 3.63%), erythema (3.00% vs. 1.13%), swelling (2.88% vs. 0.75%), and induration (2.88% vs. 0.25%), all mild to moderate. Serious adverse events were balanced (0.88% each), with no deaths or sequelae. Test VarV demonstrated non-inferior immunogenicity and acceptable safety. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR) Identifier: ChiCTR2500098374 (Retrospectively registered-March 6, 2025). Available from https://www.chictr.org.cn. items.title: Impact of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist Treatment on Post-Operative Atrial Fibrillation.
items.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists have demonstrated cardiovascular benefits with anti-inflammatory and anti-arrhythmic properties. This study aimed to evaluate the association of GLP-1 use with postoperative atrial fibrillation and mortality in patients undergoing cardiac surgery. This was a retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery from 2010 to 2025. Patients were stratified into GLP-1 users and non-users. Patients with a history of atrial fibrillation (AF), concurrent MAZE procedure, and prior cardioversions or ablations were excluded. The primary outcome was incidence of new onset postoperative AF within 30 days. Secondary outcomes included AF-related readmissions and all-cause mortality. Multivariable adjusted regression models were used to compare POAF incidence and time-to-event secondary outcomes. A total of 8,672 patients were included. The 411 GLP-1 users were younger with higher BMI and HbA1c and were more likely to have diabetes compared to non-users (all p<0.001). After multivariable adjustment, GLP-1 users demonstrated a significantly lower incidence of postoperative AF compared to non-users (29.0% vs. 34.6%, RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.71-0.99, p=0.038). AF-related readmission in GLP-1 users were 1.2% at 1 year and 3.5% at 5 years, compared to 2.9% and 6.5% in non-users, respectively (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.30-1.13, p=0.111). One- and five-year mortality was similar between groups (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.67-1.25, p=0.561). In this large real-world cohort, GLP-1 agonist use was associated with significant reduction of new onset postoperative AF and trended towards lower AF related readmissions. These findings support further investigation of GLP-1s in perioperative cardiac surgery.

items.title: Evolution of cardiovascular risk scores in type 2 diabetes: Insights from the USA, the UK, and China.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D), and cardiovascular risk scores increasingly inform preventive strategies and treatment decisions. However, these scores have been developed across diverse populations, regions, and time periods using heterogeneous methodological approaches, raising questions about their comparability, transportability, and applicability in diabetes care. We provide an up-to-date synthesis of cardiovascular risk scores relevant to T2D in the USA, the UK, and China, drawing on reviews, guideline documents, and targeted literature searches across these settings and relevant regional or global contexts. Models were compared across 20 methodological and implementation domains. A total of 56 cardiovascular risk score entries were identified, including 31 classified as general-population models and 25 as T2D-specific models. These models differed substantially in derivation populations, predictor composition, outcome definitions, prediction horizons, validation patterns, and implementation characteristics, while T2D-specific models more frequently included diabetes-related predictors such as glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), diabetes duration, albuminuria, and renal function. Descriptive evidence based largely on indirect cross-study comparisons did not establish a consistent performance advantage for either category. Marked regional variation may reflect differences in epidemiology, healthcare systems, data infrastructure, and guideline traditions, which could influence model development, recalibration, and clinical use. Cardiovascular risk prediction has gradually moved towards larger datasets, richer predictor information, broader cardiovascular outcomes, greater emphasis on validation, and more accessible implementation formats. Overall, cardiovascular risk scores in T2D show substantial heterogeneity, and no single model is optimal across all settings. Selection of cardiovascular risk scores in T2D patients should place emphasis on population-specific validation, calibration, alignment of the predicted outcome and prediction horizon with the clinical decision, predictor availability, and implementation feasibility, rather than model category alone. Local recalibration and periodic performance reassessment may be particularly relevant when absolute risk estimates inform threshold-based preventive treatment decisions. (300 /300 words).

items.title: Prevalence and Correlates of Appearance- and Performance-Enhancing Drugs and Substances Use among a Population-Based Sample of Canadians: A Cross-Sectional Survey, 2026.
items.abstract: To estimate the prevalence and sociodemographic correlates of appearance- and performance-enhancing drugs and substances (APEDS), including legal supplements and illicit drugs, among Canadians. Data were from 4,017 Canadians who participated in a cross-sectional, population-based survey administered by Mental Health Research Canada. Lifetime and current use of six APEDS (protein drinks/powders, creatine, pre-workout drinks/powders, anabolic-androgenic steroids [AAS], injectable/oral peptides, and other hormone-like or muscle-building drugs) without a medical prescription were assessed. Prevalence of APEDS use was determined among the overall sample, and by age, gender, and race/ethnicity. Six separate logistic regression models were estimated to determine the sociodemographic associations with lifetime use of each APEDS. Use of protein drinks/powders was most prevalent amongst Canadians (35.2% lifetime; 13.2% current). Lifetime AAS, peptide, and other hormone-like drug use each approximated 5%. Lifetime use of all APEDS was highest among 16-29-year-olds. Cisgender men had higher odds than cisgender women of using creatine, pre-workout drinks/powders, AAS, peptides, and other hormone-like drugs. In this population-based Canadian sample, legal APEDS were commonly used, and illicit APEDS were used by a smaller but non-trivial minority, particularly younger adults, cisgender men, participants identifying with a racial or ethnic minority group, and those engaged in muscle-building exercise.

items.title: Validation and Establishment of the Contrast Volume Prediction Model: For Optimizing Renal Efficiency in EVAR (the FORE-EVAR calculator).
items.abstract: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) is a preventable complication associated with iodinated contrast volume during endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR). We previously published a prediction model "For Optimizing Renal Efficiency in EVAR" (FORE-EVAR) which utilizes 13 patient-specific variables to generate a recommended contrast-volume threshold to prevent CA-AKI after EVAR. This study evaluates FORE-EVAR against machine-learning models and establishes FORE-EVAR's user-interface for general use. Eight machine-learning algorithms were applied to a 49,417-patient Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) EVAR cohort (2003-July 2024). Following comparison of FORE-EVAR with machine-learning models, an updated VQI EVAR dataset (August 2024-October 2025) of 7,112 new patients was used for temporal validation. Using split-sample approach (80% training; 20% validation) of the 49,417-patient dataset, FORE-EVAR demonstrated a strong AUC=0.753 (comparable to machine-learning models [range=0.712-0.759]) with similar performance across other predictive metrics. Importantly, FORE-EVAR requires input of 13 patient variables which is significantly less than the 50+ variables required by machine-learning models. The comparable prediction metrics and simplicity of variables support FORE-EVAR as a practical candidate for clinical implementation. Temporal validation with the 7,112-patient dataset showed AUC=0.706, emphasizing FORE-EVAR's predictability across cohorts. FORE-EVAR's user-interface provides three personalized outputs: CA-AKI risk category (Low, Moderate, High, or Very High); a recommended contrast volume threshold; and predicted CA-AKI risk at fixed volumes of 50mL and 100mL for procedural guidance. FORE-EVAR is a validated prediction tool which provides valuable patient-specific contrast-volume recommendations. Prospective studies are needed to evaluate FORE-EVAR's impact on intraoperative contrast volume and incidence of CA-AKI.

items.title: Eating practices and associated occupational and health factors among teachers in a Brazilian state public-school system.
items.abstract: To assess eating practices according to the Dietary Guidelines for the Brazilian Population and associated factors among basic education teachers in the state public-school system of Montes Claros, Minas Gerais, Brazil. In this cross-sectional study, 1907 teachers completed an online questionnaire in October-December 2021. Eating practices were assessed using a validated 24-item scale; associations were examined using Poisson regression with robust variance. Eating practices were adequate in 50.9%, required modification in 38.7%, and were inadequate in 10.4%. Higher prevalence of practices requiring modification or classified as inadequate was associated with male sex (1.14; 1.03-1.27), working ≥40 h/week (1.15; 1.01-1.31), suspected common mental disorder (1.52; 1.35-1.72), poor or very poor sleep quality (1.23; 1.10-1.37), and being sedentary or irregularly active (1.30; 1.16-1.45); age ≥ 44 years was associated with lower prevalence (0.87; 0.80-0.96). Estimates are adjusted prevalence ratios with 95% confidence intervals. These findings highlight occupational, psychosocial, and behavioral factors that may be relevant to workplace health-promotion strategies aimed at supporting healthier eating practices among teachers.

items.title: Evidence translation and community engagement within US cancer centers.
items.abstract: The National Cancer Institute requires cancer centers to maintain Community Outreach and Engagement components (COEs) that bridge research and community priorities to support evidence translation. Limited information exists on how COEs implement evidence-based interventions (EBIs) with community partners. We describe how COEs translate evidence into practice and promising community engagement practices. We conducted semi-structured interviews in 2021 with COE leaders at 38 NCI-designated US cancer centers. EBIs were categorized along a community engagement continuum, and cross-cutting themes and highly-engaged practices were identified. Transcripts were double-coded and analyzed using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research. COEs implemented a wide range of EBIs at varying levels of community engagement. Implementation was shaped by community- and data-driven priority setting, leadership support, staffing constraints, and sustainability challenges. Highly-engaged EBIs involved community partners in identification, adapting materials, training faculty/staff on community engagement, and participating in evaluation and data analysis. They were most common among COEs with strong leadership support and dedicated funding. Findings suggest well-supported COEs enabled more highly engaged EBI implementation. Institutional commitment and meaningful community partnership roles are important considerations for COEs seeking to embed community engagement throughout implementation and enhance reach and effectiveness of EBIs to reduce cancer disparities.

items.title: AI-Assisted PROTAC Design for Cancer Therapy: An Evidence-to-Decision Framework for Designer, Connector and Predictor Roles.
items.abstract: AI methods are used in proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC) discovery for candidate generation, ternary-complex modelling and property prediction. These tasks are organised here into Designer, Connector and Predictor roles to examine how computational outputs can inform experimental decisions in cancer drug discovery. Published studies connect selected computationally generated compounds to biological testing and show how new measurements can inform chemical optimisation and property-model refinement. Case studies of linker modifications and PKMYT1 stereoisomers illustrate discrepancies between binding and cellular degradation. Further preclinical and clinical findings show why target depletion must be interpreted alongside pathway suppression, tissue exposure and tolerability. The analysis identifies measurements that could distinguish competing explanations and guide changes to candidate chemistry, structural hypotheses, prediction models or experimental conditions. Predictive performance depends on chemical and biological context, so validation needs to reflect the compounds, targets and endpoints encountered in the intended application. Exposure-response models can help interpret pharmacological findings when supported by relevant tissue and pathway measurements. Clinical outcomes are also distinguished from evidence of AI involvement in individual candidates. Current evidence supports specific connections between computation and experiment. Prospective comparisons are needed to determine whether coordinating these methods improves candidate selection and pharmacological outcomes.

items.title: Multivariate genome-wide association study of cardiometabolic diseases reveals shared genetic architecture and enhances risk prediction through integrated polygenic and proteomic risk scores.
items.abstract: Cardiometabolic diseases (CMD) are interconnected, but their shared and domain-specific genetic architecture and the value of integrating genetic and proteomic information for risk prediction remain unclear. We applied LD score regression, factor analyses, and genomic structural equation modeling to genome-wide association summary statistics for seven CMD components in European-ancestry cohorts. We performed multivariate genome-wide association analysis, functional annotation, tissue and cell-type enrichment, gene prioritization, and pathway analysis. Polygenic risk scores (PRS) were evaluated in 310,708 UK Biobank participants, and proteomic risk scores (ProRS) were developed and tested in a proteomics subset of 33,253 participants. A hierarchical model identified cardiac (coronary artery disease and heart failure), vascular (stroke and hypertension), and metabolic (body mass index, type 2 diabetes, and triglyceride-to-HDL cholesterol ratio) factors underlying a higher-order CMD factor. We identified 328 independent CMD-associated variants, including 15 novel variants, and prioritized 297 high-confidence CMD genes. Heritability was enriched in brain regions, adipose tissue, and gastrointestinal mucosa. Participants in the highest versus lowest CMD-PRS decile had 2.82-fold higher CMD risk. ProRS outperformed PRS for CMD prediction (AUC, 0.740 versus 0.681), while the combined model achieved an AUC of 0.741. Participants with high PRS and high ProRS had the greatest risk (HR, 2.51; 95% CI, 2.29-2.75). CMD reflects shared genetic liability with distinguishable cardiac, vascular, and metabolic components. Plasma proteomics adds predictive information to inherited risk and may improve risk stratification, although external validation and a parsimonious protein panel are required before clinical implementation.

items.title: Wider social determinants of the presentation and outcomes of patients enrolled in small abdominal aortic aneurysm surveillance.
items.abstract: Elective repair offers better outcomes than urgent repair for patients in small abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) surveillance who reach treatment thresholds, or treatment being declined due to surgical risk. Internationally, socioeconomically deprived, ethnic minority, and rural populations receive fewer guideline recommended surgical procedures. In Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ), Māori face barriers to timely surgical access. This multicentre, observational analysis of prospectively collected AAA surveillance data (2002 - 2019) examined disparities in AAA stage at diagnosis and elective repair by socioeconomic deprivation, ethnicity, and distance to vascular services. Patients with incidentally detected AAAs were grouped by socioeconomic deprivation, ethnicity (Māori/non-Māori), and travel time to vascular services. Outcomes included age and AAA diameter at diagnosis, and elective repair rates. Cumulative incidence functions estimated 36 month probability of elective repair, with cause specific Cox regression adjusted for comorbidities. 1 684 patients were eligible for analysis. Patients in highly deprived areas were diagnosed younger, but higher deprivation was associated with lower elective repair rates (hazard ratio [HR] 0.85, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.75 - 0.98; p = .02). Māori were diagnosed younger (68.7 vs. 73.4 years; p < .001) yet had lower elective repair rates for medium (≥ 45 mm) AAAs in univariable analysis (36 month probability 0.27 vs. 0.54; p = .04) and multivariable analysis controlling for covariates (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.29 - 0.86; p = .01) despite reaching treatment thresholds at least as often. Rural location was not associated with repair rates. Socioeconomic and ethnic inequities in outcomes of small AAA surveillance exist in NZ. Patients in more deprived areas had lower elective repair rates. Māori received fewer elective repairs despite equivalent or greater clinical need, likely reflecting higher comorbidity burden and operative risk. Earlier diagnosis, improved access to specialist care, including national AAA screening, enhanced risk factor management, and strengthened primary care access may reduce inequity. Socioeconomic, ethnic, and geographical factors should inform equitable screening and service delivery.

items.title: Intraoperative Blood Pressure Targeting in Noncardiac Surgery: A Bayesian Random-effects Meta-analysis of Randomized Trials.
items.abstract: Background Whether protocolized intraoperative arterial pressure-targeting strategies provide incremental benefit beyond contemporary usual care remains uncertain. The authors performed a Bayesian meta-analysis of randomized trials in major noncardiac surgery. Methods MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to January 5, 2026, with additional literature surveillance through June 29, 2026. Randomized trials comparing protocolized intraoperative arterial pressure-targeting strategies with usual care or lower-pressure approaches were included. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were acute kidney injury (AKI) and myocardial injury after noncardiac surgery (MINS). Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis was prespecified as the primary analytical framework, with confirmatory frequentist analyses. Results Fifteen randomized trials met the inclusion criteria. Mortality (13 trials) remained centered around an odds ratio (OR) of 1.00 (frequentist OR, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.83 to 1.21; Bayesian median OR, 1.00; 95% credible interval [CrI], 0.73 to 1.38), with wide Bayesian prediction intervals (OR, 0.56 to1.78). AKI (14 trials) showed the most favorable estimates (frequentist OR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.73 to 1.03; Bayesian median OR, 0.88; 95% CrI, 0.70 to 1.05), but estimates remained compatible with no clinically important benefit, heterogeneity was moderate, and leave-one-out analyses, excluding each trial in turn, showed sensitivity to individual trial exclusion. MINS (eight trials) likewise remained compatible with no treatment effect (frequentist OR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.93 to 1.15; Bayesian median OR, 1.05; 95% CrI, 0.90 to 1.26). Exploratory analyses suggested that any potential renal benefit may depend on the broader hemodynamic context in which arterial pressure targets are implemented. Conclusions Protocolized intraoperative arterial pressure-targeting strategies did not demonstrate a consistent incremental benefit over contemporary usual care in major noncardiac surgery. Mortality and MINS remained compatible with no treatment effect. Although AKI showed the most favorable estimates, the evidence remained uncertain, was sensitive to individual trial exclusion, and should be interpreted cautiously.

items.title: Beneath the glass ceiling: an examination of gender disparities in Canadian medical education leadership.
items.abstract: This study aims to assess gender representation in leadership and academic ranks within Canadian universities and affiliated medical schools during 2020-2021, and describe scholarly productivity by inferred gender. This cross-sectional study identified 1,163 faculty leaders across 17 medical schools and parent universities. Public records, NamSor-inferred gender and Scopus bibliometrics were analysed using contingency tables, Cramér's V and exploratory unadjusted odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. Productivity comparisons were descriptive. Gender was associated with leadership category among 1,110 tabulated leaders (χ2(3) = 24.49, p < 0.001; V = 0.149) and academic rank among 823 leaders (χ2(2) = 16.39, p < 0.001; V = 0.141). Women comprised 30.1% of department heads and 36.1% of full professors. Women had lower odds than men of holding department-head versus other listed leadership roles (OR = 0.46, 95% CI 0.33-0.64) and full versus assistant/associate professorships (OR = 0.54, 95% CI 0.40-0.73). Mean bibliometric measures were higher among men. These historical data cannot establish current representation or causal mechanisms. Gender inference, differing analytic denominators, unmeasured confounding and unaddressed institutional clustering limit interpretation. Updated longitudinal studies, interviews and validated surveys are needed. This national analysis examines gender representation in leadership, academic rank and scholarly productivity across Canadian universities and their affiliated medical schools.

items.title: AGNFormer. I: Reconstruction of active galactic nucleus spectra using a probabilistic transformer model
items.abstract: When analysing spectroscopic data to extract physical properties, emphasis is often placed on small portions of a spectrum (e.g. ionisation diagnostic diagrams, broad Hβ or Mg ii emission lines, etc.), potentially discarding a wealth of useful information. We explore how an uncertainty-aware transformer-based architecture can leverage information embedded across the entire observed optical spectra of active galactic nuclei (AGNs), focussing on the algorithm's ability to predict unseen or masked parts of luminous AGN spectra, providing a direct probe of the learnable correlations between AGN continua and broad lines. We introduce AGNFormer -1 $; missing halves), inputting rest-frame spectral fluxes and uncertainties across the entire redshift range of the SDSS DR16 Quasar Catalogue. We evaluate the performance of the model on both full (no S/N limit) and high-quality (S/N $> 10) spectral samples using the negative-log likelihood and via comparisons with existing ̧iv and łyman reconstruction algorithms. The model successfully reconstructs unseen AGN broad lines up to an error floor of ≈2-6% of the flux at S/N ≈ 40, while the predictive power for larger unseen halves diminishes with distance from the cut-off wavelength of the input spectrum. Predictions faithfully reproduce the broad AGN spectral diversity across the entire optical and UV quasi-stellar object (QSO) main sequence parameter spaces, including both Gaussian and Lorentzian profile regimes, complexes, and narrow emission lines. The performance is found to be similar or better compared to previous spectral reconstruction algorithms. The high precision of the broad-line region reconstruction demonstrates that the method successfully aggregates information across the spectrum and highlights how the AGN continuum as well as weaker lines and complexes have the potential to assist astronomers in the extraction of the entire wealth of information embedded in AGN spectra. 's underlying model could be a valuable tool for processing the spectra of many other classes of astrophysical objects. AGNFormer

items.title: Euclid. XI. A two-point correlation approach to diagnosing star-related systematics in the spectroscopic survey
items.abstract: The Euclid spectroscopic survey will measure galaxy clustering with unprecedented precision, which demands stringent control over observational and instrumental systematics. Among these, star-related effects may contaminate the spectroscopic images through photometric persistence and through imperfect masking of stellar images. We characterized the imprint of star-related effects in the spectroscopic exposures and quantified their impact on galaxy clustering analyses. If these effects produce characteristic angular features, they can be identified and characterized in the data, thereby enabling an assessment of their impact on cosmological measurements. We used angular and spatial auto- and cross-correlation statistics to quantify these effects. For the galaxies we used mock spectroscopic catalogues extracted from EuclidLargeMocks. We focused on a 330 region of the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS). For the stars, we considered the real Gaia and star catalogues in the same area. To simulate photometric persistence, we implemented a simplified detector-level model calibrated on spectroscopic measurements and modulated the strength of the effect to introduce varying fractions of `interlopers' into the mock galaxy catalogues. For the stellar mask, we modelled potential inconsistencies between the mask used to remove regions around stars in the data and the mask applied to the random catalogue used to quantify the survey selection function. We measured the star--star, galaxy--galaxy, and star--galaxy angular correlation functions using the Landy--Szalay estimator and quantified deviations from the expected null star–galaxy correlation with a dedicated metric. Finally, we evaluated the impact of these systematics on large scales using the 3D two-point correlation function (2PCF). Our results show that photometric persistence produces a characteristic feature in the star--galaxy angular cross-correlation at scales of order 100 consistent with the scale set by the Euclid dithering pattern and grism dispersion geometry. It also induces a spurious, positive cross-correlation signal that remains approximately constant in amplitude up to 1^̧irc. We find that star–galaxy cross-correlation analysis is a sensitive tool for detecting residual persistence and is capable of revealing spurious contamination levels as low as 10% in a Data Release 1-like spectroscopic catalogue. In contrast, mismatches in stellar masking produce strong small-scale angular signatures but do not significantly impact the large-scale 2PCF under realistic EWS conditions.

items.title: P2D - A Two-Dimensional Multi-Spacecraft Solar Wind Persistence Model
items.abstract: The background solar wind is a key component in space weather forecasting, as it contains geoeffective high-speed streams and provides the medium through which coronal mass ejections propagate and evolve in interplanetary space. Due to the solar rotation and the slow evolution of large-scale solar wind structures, solar wind properties exhibit an autocorrelation with a period of roughly 27 days, particularly at solar minimum. We made use of this property to develop a solar wind persistence model with input from multiple spacecraft (Solar Orbiter, Parker Solar Probe, STEREO-A, STEREO-B and the OMNI database). The model ballistically propagates in-situ data from the position of their measurement radially away from the Sun, as well as longitudinally with the solar rotation rate, producing 2D maps of solar wind parameters. These can be extracted at any point in the heliosphere for a solar wind reconstruction. From Earth’s perspective, the reconstruction performs with an MAE of 65.41 km~s$^{-1}$ and 3.51 $cm^{-3}$ for speed and density, respectively. During high-speed streams, the peak hit rate is 50\% and 48\% for speed and density. It performs best during times when there are spacecraft located between Earth and Lagrange point L5. During these times, the mean absolute error of the predicted solar wind velocity decreases by roughly 35\% in comparison to the benchmark 27-day persistence model. Therefore, future L5 missions like Vigil are expected to provide a robust basis for reliable persistence forecasts.

items.title: The ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST Survey: Investigating the role of interstellar dust, gas, and stars in high-z galaxies at kiloparsec scales
items.abstract: A comprehensive understanding of galaxy evolution requires a detailed analysis of gas and dust, including their distribution and evolution within galaxies. In this work, we analyse spatially resolved (∼,1-2,kpc) rest-frame C ii and dust continuum ALMA observations together with JWST/NIRSpec IFU data of a sample of six massive galaxies at z,∼,4-5. We focus on deriving and comparing the spatial distributions of atomic and molecular gas masses, dust and stellar masses, star formation rates (SFR), and metallicity. The oxygen abundance maps have median values in the range of 12+log(O/H),sim8.1-8.3 with variations of the order of 1,dex within the same galaxy. In four galaxies of our sample, the oxygen abundance shows a minimum at the peak of the Hα emission and an enhancement in the outer parts. The calibration used in this study to estimate the atomic gas mass in our galaxies seems to overestimate the atomic gas mass surface densities by up to one to two orders of magnitude. However, a calibration based on a spatially resolved C ii conversion factor gives a more robust estimation of the total gas mass. The dust-to-gas surface mass density ratio varies between łog Σ_ ̊m dust /Σ_ ̊m gas =-2.2 ^ +0.24 _ -0.19 and łogΣ_ ̊m dust /Σ_ ̊m gas =-2.69^ +0.21 _ -0.16 , while the dust-to-stellar surface mass density ratio ranges from łogΣ_ ̊m dust /Σ_ ̊m star =-2.01^ +0.13 _ -0.12 to łogΣ_ ̊m dust /Σ_ ̊m star =-2.91^ +0.13 _ -0.13 . A detailed analysis of the dust-to-stellar surface mass density ratio and the gas mass fraction versus metallicity revealed that galaxies exhibiting signatures of strong outflows have a lower dust-to-stellar surface mass density ratio and lower gas mass fractions than the galaxies with no outflow signatures. While the latter is consistent with these galaxies ejecting part of their gas reservoir to the circumgalactic medium, the low dust-to-stellar surface mass density ratios also suggest that part of the dust content is expelled outside the galaxy, which reinforces previous theoretical suggestions of dust removal by stellar feedback or radiation pressure to explain the high UV luminosities in galaxies at very high redshifts. Some galaxies of our sample have almost an order of magnitude higher ratios of dust-to-gas and dust-to-stellar surface mass density than galaxies in the local Universe, suggesting that a large dust reservoir has been built up already at timescales of sim1,Gyr in these galaxies.

items.title: Surveying for close binaries among lithium-rich giants
items.abstract: The existence of low-mass giants with high lithium (Li) abundances poses a challenge to our understanding of post-main sequence stellar structure and evolution. Li-rich giants are preferentially found in the red clump (RC) rather than on the first-ascent red giant branch (RGB). One of the scenarios proposed to explain this Li enrichment involves tidal interaction with a close binary companion, which, if dominant, predicts an enhanced binary fraction among Li-rich giants relative to Li-normal ones. We aim to test the binary interaction scenario for the origin of Li-rich giants by using multi-epoch radial velocities (RVs) in order to measure the close binary fraction of a statistically robust sample of Li-rich giants. The surveyed sample contains both RC and RGB targets, which allows us to examine potential differences in the binary fraction as a function of evolutionary stage. We monitored 70 giants (40 RC and 30 RGB) using the ESPRESSO spectrograph, 57 (32 RC and 25 RGB) of which already had four or more visits over a ∼7-month baseline. The analysis presented here is based on these latter targets. We first used a criterion based on surface gravity and the maximum observed RV difference within our data in order to discard RV variations attributable to intrinsic stellar jitter. For the targets with RV variation larger than this threshold, we performed Monte Carlo simulations over a grid of companion mass and orbital period, to estimate the probability that the observed RV variation is due to a stellar (P_SB) or substellar (P_SS) companion. After removing targets consistent with stellar jitter, 11 (34 ± 8%) RC and eight (32 ± 9%) RGB stars remained as binary candidates or stars with a companion. Of these, three targets (16 ± 8% of the filtered sample) are confirmed stellar binaries. The distributions of P_SB and P_SS are statistically indistinguishable between the RC and RGB samples. We find no evidence in our current data for a binary fraction for Li-rich giants (in either evolutionary stage) larger than that expected for a regular Li-normal population, which suggests that binary interaction is unlikely to be the dominant mechanism driving Li enrichment in this sample. Extending the RV baseline to probe longer orbital periods will be important to continue exploring the plausibility of this scenario.

items.title: The Pristine survey. XXIX. Data Release 2: Photometric metallicities for 15 millions stars down to G∼ 20.3
items.abstract: Tailored narrowband photometric observations are an efficient way to measure the metallicity of Milky Way stars. The Pristine survey has been mapping the northern sky since 2015 using narrowband CaHK photometry obtained with the MegaCam imager on the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope (CFHT). The Pristine Data Release 1 (DR1) provided a high-precision absolute calibration of the survey observed before October 2022 using Gaia DR3 XP synthetic photometry, yielding photometric metallicities over ∼6500 deg2$, but was limited in depth to the availability of Gaia spectro-photometry ($G łesssim 17.65). We present the Pristine Data Release 2 (DR2) that includes all Pristine observations until January 2025, corresponding to an additional 1500,deg2$ of coverage, and including all faint sources down to $G This release aims to exploit the full depth of the Pristine observations to uncover the faint metal-poor halo. We process all images observed from the start of the survey in March 2015 through to January 2025 following the methodology presented in DR1. The core of the calibration utilizes the subset of bright stars with Gaia synthetic CaHK_ neural network. We then derive photometric metallicities using the established Pristine (CaHK, G, G_ magnitudes to train the PhotCalib ̊m BP , G_ ̊m RP ) to FeH model. The resulting catalog covers approximately ∼ 8000 deg 2 and provides photometric metallicities for 15 million FGK stars, which show good agreement with recently published independent Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) metallicities. With its increased coverage and access to a significantly fainter regime compared to DR1, DR2 significantly increases the volume of the survey. We report more than 200,000 and 6500 very and extremely metal-poor star candidates, respectively.

items.title: Forward model of the Gaia DR3 selection function
items.abstract: The completeness of an astronomical catalogue depends on its selection function, which is a combination of the observing strategy, instrumental characteristics, and intrinsic properties of the sources being observed. This is particularly complex for Gaia, whose non-uniform scanning law and onboard prioritisation of bright sources in dense areas make its selection function vary strongly with celestial position and source brightness. We estimate the source catalogue selection function across the whole sky and over the full magnitude range, using only data from the Gaia catalogue and knowledge of the nominal scanning law as provided by the Gaia Observation Forecast Tool. 3 We developed a hierarchical Bayesian model that estimates the number of times Gaia scanned each celestial position jointly with the source detection efficiency, and fitted it via Markov chain Monte Carlo to the 1,806,196,447 sources in 3 with reported celestial positions, G magnitudes, and astrometric matched transit counts. 3 is essentially complete for G ∈ (5,19.5) in the on-sky median. After that, the completeness decreases with magnitude according to the scanning law pattern combined with the imprint of crowded regions. The completeness is also lower at the very bright end of the survey, consistent with the known limitations on Gaia observations of bright stars. We find an unexpected completeness increase beyond G ∼ 21, which we conclude is an artefact caused by extended sources, as confirmed by cross-matching against Euclid's Q1 catalogue. Our approach builds on previous efforts that use the understanding of the Gaia survey strategy to model the survey selection function. Our model does not rely on a precise knowledge of the Gaia scanning law, making it more robust, while retaining the capability of deriving an all-sky selection function without the need to extrapolate from limited external surveys providing `ground truth'. Treating the scanning law as part of the inference process, and anchoring it to all sources of all magnitudes on a fine-grained grid on the sky, removes the need for an explicit crowding correction. The resulting selection function, valid everywhere where Gaia data are available, is released as part of the GaiaUnlimited Python package. 3

items.title: Constraining dust properties along the minor axis of Andromeda
items.abstract: Previous studies of dust emission in the Andromeda galaxy (M31) based primarily on Herschel data have reported inconsistent radial trends in the dust emissivity index (β), partly due to limited wavelength coverage and the degeneracy between dust temperature (T_̊m dust) and β. We aim to improve the constraints of β determinations and obtain the spatial surface density and temperature distributions at giant molecular cloud scales in M31 by extending the spectral coverage into the millimeter regime and by quantifying the impact of wavelength coverage on the T_̊m dust–β degeneracy. We present the 1.15 mm continuum emission along the minor axis of M31 with the 30 m telescope of the Institut de radioastronomie millimétrique (IRAM). The map has an angular resolution of 11.6'', corresponding to approximately 40 pc at the distance of M31. We used these data with Herschel and 450 and 850 μm maps from the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope to perform pixel-by-pixel single-component modified blackbody fitting. Including the 850 μm and 1.15 mm data helps reduce the T_̊m dust–β degeneracy and yields an average emissivity index of β ≈ 1.8, which is systematically lower than values derived from far-infrared–only analyses. Radial analysis shows higher β values in the 5 kpc ring compared to the 10 kpc ring. The elevated β values in the inner 5 kpc may be linked to changes in dust composition, potentially associated with enhanced starlight heating in this region. Millimeter wavelength coverage is important for improving β constraints in M31. The lower β values inferred from the 250--1150 μm spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting suggest possible variations in dust emissivity and highlight the importance of sampling the long-wavelength SED slope in nearby galaxies.

items.title: Impact of the large-scale environment on the baryonic scaling relations of disc galaxies: Insights from the GASP survey
items.abstract: The Tully--Fisher relation (TFR) and the specific angular momentum--mass relation (SAMR) link the baryonic content of a disc to its kinematics and dynamics. Hence, these scaling relations should bear the imprints of any process removing baryons or altering their kinematics, such as those acting in clusters of galaxies. We tested this scenario using the MUSE survey `GAs Stripping Phenomena in galaxies' (GASP), which targets field, group, and cluster members at z ≈ 0.05 and various stages of ram pressure stripping. For the 81 discs with favourable inclinations, we measured the distribution and kinematics of stars and ionised gas and their specific angular momenta. Within their scatter, the stellar and baryonic relations show no significant dependence on the large-scale environment. The TFRs have slopes of α ≈ 3.6 and ≈ 3.5 for any kinematic tracer, and the SAMRs have α ≈ 0.65--0.75, as predicted by tidal torque theory. The same holds for the ten S0-S0/as in our sample, consistent with the `faded spiral' formation scenario. Only the gas SAMR shows an environmental signature, with ram pressure stripped galaxies lying ≈ 0.16 dex below unperturbed ones. This offset is mostly due to their enhanced star formation rate and thus higher gas mass when inferred through the Schmidt-Kennicutt law rather than to kinematic perturbations or disc truncation. Our results suggest that within the area probed by MUSE (łesssim6 disc scale lengths), these discs have preserved the angular momentum acquired at formation not only from cluster processes and pre-processing in filaments but also from mergers and ejective feedback acting in any environment.

items.title: Mitigating variance shrinkage in multitask galaxy property inference from imaging data via statistical manifold alignment
items.abstract: Inferring photometric redshifts (z) and key stellar population properties (łog(M_*/ _⊙), D_n 4000, and mathrm M H δ_A) directly from multiband imaging is increasingly critical for spectroscopically limited large surveys such as LSST and CSST. However, conventional pointwise loss functions (e.g., mean squared error or Huber loss) employed in deep neural networks often induce ``variance shrinkage''---a regression-to-the-mean effect that contracts predicted variances, distorts nonlinear physical manifolds (such as bimodal distributions), and truncates heavy-tailed populations. Here, we present ViTMultiTask, a vision transformer framework that incorporates a multiscale maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss to enforce higher-order joint distribution alignment in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. Trained on 83,846 galaxies from Subaru HSC five-band (g,r,i,z,y) imaging cross-matched with DESI Data Release 1 Bright Galaxy Survey spectra, the model achieves high point-estimate precision on an independent test set of 5,000 galaxies: σ_ NMAD = 0.020 for z, 0.169, for łog(M_*/ _⊙), 0.073 for D_n 4000, and 1.185, δ_A. Ablation experiments demonstrate that incorporating the MMD loss effectively mitigates variance shrinkage and more accurately reproduces the observed spectroscopic parameter distributions (including bimodal structures and heavy tails), while maintaining point-estimate accuracy statistically consistent with the baseline (with RMSE changes łe 3.5%) and catastrophic outlier rates fully comparable to the baseline. This kernel-based manifold alignment offers a statistically grounded and practical paradigm for comprehensive galaxy property inference in the deep imaging era. M for mathrm H

items.title: Inferring accretion bursts in intermediate-mass protostars from asteroseismic imprints
items.abstract: During star formation, objects may gain the majority of their final mass through regular and intense bursts of mass accretion. For burst events of the FU Orionis-type (FUor), accretion rates can climb as high as 10^ -3 in short windows of time, amounting to just a few percent of the main accretion phase. Some bursters had not been observed in the preceding quiescent stage, making their classification as FUors difficult. To study the occurrence of such events observationally, signatures of the current accretion bursts and tracers of recent bursts are crucial. In this work, we investigate the potential to identify current accretion bursts and detect recent bursts in protostars and pre-main sequence (pre-MS) stars of intermediate mass using asteroseismology. The aim is to characterize theoretical period-spacing diagrams of pre-MS gravity-mode (g-mode) pulsators that have undergone accretion bursts. We used the stellar structure and evolution code to evolve stellar models from the protostellar seed phase of 0.01 MESA and 1.5 ̊sun up to 4.0 with a constant accretion rate of 10^ -6 A single accretion burst was initialized during the accretion phase. The stellar oscillation code GYRE was employed to compute the resulting asteroseismic properties of the models. Accretion bursts of up to 10^ -3 are sufficient to cause the convective cores of the models to recede, leaving behind a chemical trace that is manifested in the form of quasi-periodic dips in the g-mode period spacing. This effect is strongest during the outburst, but also lingers for up to 475 years before the convective core is re-established and the dips are gone. Our experiment shows that a single accretion burst leaves an imprint in the deep interiors of protostars and pre-MS stars of intermediate mass and that this imprint can be captured with asteroseismology. Well-resolved g-mode pulsations of young stellar objects may therefore help identify current and recent accretion bursts. Our results are most conclusive for burst magnitudes greater than 1 -4 corresponding to FUor-type bursts.

items.title: The long-period central star of the planetary nebula MPAJ1508-6455
items.abstract: A significant fraction of planetary nebulae have been shown to host short-period binary central stars, but longer-period central stars are scarcer. We characterise the central star of the planetary nebula MPAJ1508-6455, which has previously been claimed to be an intermediate-period binary with a period of approximately 12 days. We studied archival and catalogue photometry to probe the previously reported photometric variability and binary spectral energy distribution. We used long-term high-resolution spectroscopic monitoring to measure the radial velocity curves of the two components of the central binary, and to derive their atmospheric parameters. We also undertook kinematical and chemical abundance analyses of the nebula itself. The orbital period of the central binary of exceeds five years and is highly eccentric. The binary comprises a relatively low-temperature sdO-type central star and a spun-up K-type giant companion. The Kiel mass of the central star is approximately half the dynamical mass derived from the radial velocities. While the systemic velocity and inclination of the nebula are consistent with the radial velocities of the binary, its abundance pattern adds support for a lower-mass progenitor that did not experience hot bottom burning (and is thus more consistent with the Kiel mass than the mass derived from the radial velocities). To the best of our knowledge, the central star of is only the fourth planetary nebula central star to have a spectroscopically confirmed orbital period longer than one year.

items.title: OmniAct: One Policy, One Million Embodiments
items.abstract: A single policy that controls diverse robots must not only transfer task knowledge across embodiments, but also adapt its behavior to each robot's capabilities. Existing approaches facilitate transfer through shared action representations, but these representations do not necessarily capture how differences in robot morphology should shape manipulation strategies. We introduce OmniAct, a cross-embodiment manipulation policy that conditions directly on each robot's kinematics in a specific scene to produce embodiment-specific behavior. This kinematic graph represents the robot's joint positions, motion axes, and connectivity to its visual observation, allowing the policy to account for how its embodiment related to objects and surfaces in the scene. A flow-matching policy predicts relative joint motions for each node, enabling control across robots with different degrees of freedom and kinematic configurations. To learn how physical structure shapes behavior at scale, we procedurally design and filter one million physically feasible robot embodiments; next, we develop algorithms to generate robot trajectories in simulation for all embodiments; finally, we train across diverse simulated manipulation tasks. On 2,000 embodiment-scene-held-out evaluation episodes, OmniAct achieves 63.0% success, compared to 17.8% for pi 0.5 and 57.9% for the strongest baseline; on the task families GPT-6 Astra was evaluated on, it achieves 64.7% against GPT-6 Astra's 41.1%. On a previously unseen real-world robot, it achieves nearly twice the success rate of the next best method, MolmoAct2. Beyond task success, we observe that OmniAct learns distinct manipulation strategies that exploit the capabilities and accommodate the limitations of different morphologies. items.title: MetaFORGE: A Meta-Learning Framework for Harness Optimization in Automated Code Generation for Parallel Computing
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate parallel programs, but their correctness and performance depend strongly on the instructions that guide generation. We present \textsc{MetaFORGE}, an execution-grounded meta-learning framework that iteratively optimizes persistent natural-language skill specifications for MPI C code generation. \textsc{MetaFORGE} combines correctness testing, compiler diagnostics, static-analysis findings, runtime measurements, and rank-level load-imbalance profiles into a scalar reward that drives textual-gradient refinement, while an external memory distills and retrieves reward-supported optimization knowledge across runs. Across six MPI tasks and three workload sizes, \textsc{MetaFORGE} improves static-analysis quality, runtime, and load balance relative to zero-shot generation and generally exceeds the evaluated \textsc{TextGrad} iterative baseline. A model-matched refinement ablation shows that the MetaFORGE advantage persists when its refinement model is reduced to \texttt{gpt-4o}. An expanded retrieval ablation across all 18 task--workload configurations shows consistent runtime benefit and broad static-analysis and load-balance benefit from retrieved context. Leakage-controlled held-out and zero-update experiments further provide evidence that optimization knowledge persists in both the transferred skill and external memory under the evaluated protocol.

items.title: Draft Calibration for Speculative Decoding: Accelerating LLM Serving by Matching Draft and Target Distributions
items.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) inference by employing a lightweight draft model to propose draft tokens and allowing the target model to verify the new tokens in parallel to improve inference-time compute utilization. The speedup relies on the acceptance probability of draft tokens in target verification, which is directly related to the gap $\|p-q\|_1$ between the target distribution $p$ and the draft distribution $q$. In this paper, we study draft calibration of speculative decoding to improve the speedup of speculative decoding, where we employ post-hoc methods to calibrate the draft distribution to mitigate the distribution gap. We observe that though current community open-source draft models may learn the top candidate token correctly, they are generally underconfident compared to the target model, suggesting a consistent distribution mismatch. To mitigate the effect of this mismatch on the acceptance rate of the draft models, we try various post-hoc calibration methods, including standard temperature scaling and token-wise calibration. Our results suggest that a standard temperature scaling applied to the draft distribution improves the acceptance length by up to approximately 10\% with almost no additional cost across different tasks. Throughput analysis further verifies that this improvement in serving efficiency. Analysis of more general calibration methods reveals further potential room for improvement.

items.title: Temporal Conditioning for Human Behavioral Cloning in Chess
items.abstract: Behavioral cloning models in chess typically predict human moves from board states while ignoring temporal inputs such as the remaining clock. However, time pressure is a major determinant of human decision-making quality, and temporal state is a missing dimension of human behavioral modeling. This paper introduces a time-aware transformer that extends a Chessformer-style architecture with learned temporal conditioning tokens encoding player clock state, time control, and recent tempo, together with behavioral heads for thinking time and resignation. The model is trained on large-scale online chess data and evaluated against time-agnostic baselines and the state of the art. Results show that temporal conditioning yields modest overall accuracy improvements but substantially stronger gains under time pressure. Beyond move choice, it also produces more accurate thinking-time and resignation predictions. More importantly, the model better matches human move-quality degradation in critical time regimes, reducing the systematic over-strength observed in time-agnostic behavioral cloning models. These results suggest that temporal state is a previously underutilized but important signal for human behavioral cloning in chess.

items.title: Delegent: A Multi-Agent Harness That Reduces Cost without Sacrificing Performance
items.abstract: Agents built on frontier language models are expensive. At every step, the frontier model re-reads its entire context and executes every subtask regardless of its difficulty. This paper explores the simple thesis that much of this cost can be removed by delegating easy subtasks to a small language model, or SLM, that runs on hardware one already owns. To test it, we build Delegent, a simple and effective agent harness built on Claude Code, in which the frontier model stays in charge of every task but hands focused subtasks, such as investigating code, running tests, and searching a corpus, to SLM subagents. Existing approaches such as cascades and model routers usually choose which model executes the entire task, whereas in Delegent, the frontier model always leads the execution and delegates easy subtasks to the SLM. No router or model is trained, so either model can be swapped freely. With the help of a 27B FP8 SLM, Delegent reduces the frontier cost of long-horizon coding by 67% and of agentic search by 59%, with no loss in task performance, and even a 2B SLM that fits on a laptop reduces the coding cost by 66%. The savings grow with the legwork that the frontier model would otherwise do itself, and a short instruction, which leaves the main coding tasks to the frontier model, accounts for most of the saving and keeps the 2B SLM from losing tasks. items.title: EventDiffusion: Learning Native Event Stream Distribution from Videos
items.abstract: Event cameras capture asynchronous brightness changes at high temporal resolution, but scarce recordings constrain data-driven research. Sparse RGB observations cannot uniquely determine intervening events since identical frames may correspond to streams with different activity, polarities, and timing. Existing simulators largely rely on prescribed sensor dynamics and estimated brightness trajectories, whose assumptions limit the diversity and fidelity of plausible event streams. We introduce EventDiffusion, a hierarchical generative framework that directly learns the conditional distribution of native asynchronous event streams from real recordings. EventDiffusion decomposes generation into three probabilistic processes: Event Activity Diffusion (EAD) learns stochastic discrete event counts; Event Spatial Allocation (ESA) distributes these counts to individual pixels while preserving cardinality; and Event Timing Diffusion (ETD) learns continuous asynchronous timestamp distributions. We also introduce CEFS, an event-stream realism metric combining event activity and polarity with multiscale space-time structure and temporal fidelity. Across all datasets, EventDiffusion achieves double the accuracy of SOTA methods and demonstrates robustness across different cameras at any resolution.

items.title: AIChipBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Automated AI Accelerator Design
items.abstract: A language-model decoder carries state between decoding steps, and in hardware a wrong state update can leave the current token correct and corrupt the output several tokens later, so a design can pass output tests and still be wrong. AIChipBench asks what LLM coding agents need to build such hardware correctly. Agents implement quantized Qwen3.5, Gemma 3, Gemma 4, and Llama 3.2 decoders in synthesizable register-transfer-level (RTL) code against an executable integer reference that specifies the outputs and the stored state at every decoding step. They debug against public tests under fixed budgets; their frozen designs are graded on held-out token sequences, resets, memory stalls, and synthesis, and a second track asks them to speed up a correct design at nearly fixed area. Across 9,136 attempts by four coding agents, the difficulty lies in stored state. Feedback that points to the first state mismatch raises acceptance over output-only feedback in all 12 agent--task cells of a matched study, by 25.0 to 46.9 percentage points, and halves the agent-hours per accepted design. Regraded on new sequences and conditions, 45 of 69 accepted designs fail within the 32 steps their tests required. More than a third of attempts to speed up a correct design end without one. An overall score ranks Sol 5.6 and Fable 5.1 above Astra 6 and Opus 5.5, and both halves of the instances give this order in all 200 random splits. Hardware agents therefore need debugging feedback that exposes stored state, and their benchmarks need final tests well beyond the development cases.
