items.title: Expanding the Reach of Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Insomnia: National Dissemination of Sleep Education to Provisional Psychologists.
items.abstract: Cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is the gold-standard treatment for insomnia; however, it is rarely taught in graduate psychology pathways, which limits its reach. Guided by the RE-AIM framework, this study evaluated the reach and effectiveness of a sleep and CBT-I education workshop for provisional psychologists in Australia. In 2024, the Australasian Sleep Association offered a free, online sleep workshop to all provisional psychologists nationally studying a graduate psychology pathway (e.g., Master's, Doctorate or completing an internship pathway), with registrants compared to the total number of provisional psychologists registered with the Psychology Board of Australia. Pre-post assessments measured sleep and CBT-I knowledge, self-efficacy to manage sleep disturbances and participants' sleep health. Results indicated that the workshop reached 10.3% of all provisional psychologists in Australia in 2024 (n = 819). Significant improvements were observed in attendees' sleep and CBT-I knowledge, self-efficacy in managing sleep disturbances, and personal sleep health (all p's < 0.001). Satisfaction ratings for the workshop overall were very positive, with 88% rating the workshop as Very Good or Excellent. This study demonstrates that a free, online sleep education workshop can reach a substantial proportion of provisional psychologists in Australia and effectively improve their CBT-I knowledge, self-efficacy to manage sleep disturbances, and sleep health. However, continued and expanded sleep education efforts are needed to improve the dissemination of CBT-I into psychological practice and improve mental health outcomes.

items.title: An exploratory mixed methods program evaluation of adult Mental Health First Aid on a college campus.
items.abstract: Objective Mental health issues among college-aged individuals are rising. Gatekeeper programs like Mental Health First Aid (MHFA) may play a critical role in meeting needs. This study builds on prior work, exploring how MHFA was implemented on a university campus and how outcomes, such as MHFA knowledge and skill retention, changed over time. Participants Quantitative analyses included 126 MHFA-trained individuals, and 22 interviewees. Methods Utilizing mixed-methods, this study aimed to evaluate whether training gains were maintained across two time points, 3- and 6-months post-training. Individual interviews explored training experiences. Results MHFA knowledge and self-efficacy generally remained stable over time. Skill utilization increased between follow-up surveys. Evidence suggests that participants found it slightly easier over time to have a supportive conversation with someone experiencing a substance use crisis. Conclusion College settings should increase access to gatekeeper trainings like MHFA to increase mental health literacy, knowledge, confidence, and skills for community support.

items.title: Relational effects of sexual abuse disclosure: perspectives of victims, offenders, and confidants.
items.abstract: Background: Sexual abuse is a complex public health concern and is often perpetrated by someone known to the victim, frequently within an intrafamilial context, which complicates disclosure. Although previous research suggests that disclosure occurs in a social context, the perspectives of victims, offenders, and confidants on the relational effects of disclosure remain poorly understood. Objective: This study aimed to explore and compare the ways in which relationships among victims, offenders, and confidants changed after disclosure of sexual abuse from all three perspectives. Method: This study employed a cross-sectional, multi-perspective qualitative design. Victims, offenders and confidants answered closed- and open-ended questions in an online questionnaire developed for this study. The total sample ( N = 93) comprised three subgroups: victims ( n = 50), offenders ( n = 7), and confidants ( n = 36). 73% of all participants referred to the disclosure of intrafamilial abuse. Participants in each subgroup were recruited independently and were asked to describe post-disclosure changes in their relationships within their independent relational triad. Data from the open-ended questions were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results: Several overlapping themes were found across the three subgroups: (1) internalization of blame; (2) spectrum of alienation; and (3) longing for recognition and openness. These themes revealed the interconnected nature of emotions and experiences across relationship triads as well as perspectives unique to each of the three subgroups. Conclusions: The disclosure of sexual abuse mostly affected the relationships between victim, offender, and confidant negatively or ambivalently, often resulting in alienation, communicative tension and a disrupted family system. The findings point to the value of adopting a systemic framework when working with affected families that recognizes the interdependence of family members' responses, while prioritizing the victim's safety.

items.title: Growth disturbance following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with or without lateral extra-articular procedures in skeletally immature patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Purpose To evaluate the incidence of growth-related complications after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) combined with lateral extra-articular procedures (LEAP) in skeletally immature patients. It was hypothesized that adding a LEAP would not be associated with a relevant increase in growth-related complications. Methods A PRISMA-based systematic search of PubMed, MEDLINE, Scopus and Google Scholar was performed through November 2025. Studies (Levels I-IV) reporting radiographically assessed growth disturbances after ACLR combined with LEAP in skeletally immature patients and with a follow-up of ≥24 months were included. Growth disturbance was defined as limb length discrepancy (LLD) ≥ 10 mm and/or coronal plane angular difference ≥5° versus the contralateral limb. Methodological quality was assessed using the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies (MINORS). When comparative data were available, pooled risk ratios (RRs) were calculated. Results Thirteen studies were included, comprising 436 patients: 334/436 (77%) underwent ACLR + LEAP, and 102/436 (23%) underwent isolated ACLR. The overall methodological quality assessed by MINORS was moderate (mean score: 13, range: 10-17). Overall, growth disturbance occurred in 8 of 436 patients (1.8%). LLD occurred in 4/334 patients after ACLR + LEAP (1.2%; mean 12 ± 2 mm) and in 2/102 patients after isolated ACLR (1.9%; quantitative data not reported). Valgus deformity occurred in 2/334 patients after ACLR + LEAP (0.6%) and in 1/102 patients after isolated ACLR (0.9%). No varus deformity was reported. Meta-analysis was feasible only for valgus deformity (2 studies; 21 ACLR + LEAP vs. 37 isolated ACLR), showing no significant difference between groups (RR = 1.56 [95% CI = 0.35-6.90]; p = 0.56; I 2 = 66%). Conclusion Although the comparative analysis was underpowered by the low number of events, adding a LEAP to ACLR showed no statistically significant difference in growth-related complications compared to isolated ACLR in skeletally immature patients. Level of evidence Level IV.

items.title: Increased Task Precision Demands Disproportionately Reduce Paretic Arm Choice After Right-Hemisphere Stroke.
items.abstract: Background Individuals with right cerebrovascular accidents (RCVAs) use their contralesional paretic arm less than those with left cerebrovascular accidents (LCVAs). However, the contribution of task precision demands to this disparity remains unclear. Objective To examine effects of arm choice and performance under increased task precision demands in RCVA compared to LCVA and their relation to daily paretic arm use. Methods Eighteen individuals with chronic unilateral stroke (8 LCVA and 10 RCVA) with similar motor impairment and 9 age-matched neurotypical controls performed a planar reaching task, choosing either arm to reach randomly presented targets. Target size was manipulated to test whether movement precision demands influenced arm choice. Paretic arm use in daily life was measured with bilateral accelerometers over 5 consecutive days. Reaction time to left and right targets was recorded to examine lateralized attention effects on paretic arm performance. Lease absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used to identify whether measures of motor and attentional capacity predicted paretic arm use. Results The RCVA group showed significantly fewer paretic arm reaches and more nonparetic arm midline crosses than controls. Target size influenced paretic arm choice in RCVA, but not in LCVA and controls. Both motor performance and attention measures predicted paretic arm choice. Finally, arm choice during small target conditions predicted daily arm use measured with accelerometry. Conclusions Greater task-precision demands amplify paretic arm nonuse after RCVA, suggesting that hemisphere of lesion moderates the effect of precision demand on paretic arm choice. Motor and attentional deficits, together with nonpreference-paresis concordance may contribute to heightened nonuse.

items.title: Representational drift in the gustatory brainstem.
items.abstract: The parabrachial nucleus of the pons (PbN) is a hub in the central pathway for taste in non-primate mammals. To account for the neural representation of taste stimuli in the PbN, the labeled line theory has played a dominant role. In this conceptualization, each of the basic taste qualities is encoded by separate groups of neurons, identified by the stimulus that evokes the most vigorous or "best" response. A tacit assumption of this theory is that the stimulus selectivity of these groups of neurons is reliable and stable over time. Here, using one photon calcium imaging, we recorded PbN responses to liquid taste stimuli to test this assumption. Female rats were prepared for calcium imaging by surgical implantation of a GRIN lens. PbN activity was imaged during multiple sessions spanning up to 112 days while animals licked various tastants in an experimental chamber. In general, PbN cells responded to more than one taste quality. While response profiles of individual PbN cells shifted over days/weeks, across-unit patterns differentiating taste quality remained relatively stable, a phenomenon analogous to representational drift found in sensory cortices. Collectively, these results challenge the labeled line conceptualization of taste representation in the PbN and support a role for dynamic population coding in maintaining perceptual stability.

items.title: Beyond Human Helpers: Young People's Help-Seeking in the Era of Chatbots.
items.abstract: BackgroundChildren and young people are increasingly using artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots for mental health support, particularly when barriers limit access to traditional services. Although these systems are often perceived as accessible, immediate and non-judgemental, there is limited understanding of how they function within the complex developmental context of adolescence. Chatbots may simulate empathy and validation without possessing clinical judgement or contextual awareness, raising questions about safety, reliability and their influence on help-seeking behaviours.MethodThis commentary adopts an interdisciplinary perspective, integrating insights from clinical psychology, philosophy and machine learning. It draws on emerging evidence, conceptual analysis and approaches to AI safety evaluation.ResultsChatbot failures are most likely to occur in ambiguous or high-risk situations, where systems may provide misplaced reassurance, inappropriate validation or fail to recognise the need for escalation. Current evaluations often prioritise engagement and acceptability, overlooking clinically important risks. Young people need support to recognise the limitations of AI-generated advice and respond critically when systems operate beyond their competence.ConclusionsRigorous interdisciplinary frameworks are required to evaluate chatbot safety and effectiveness. Researchers should prioritise clinically meaningful outcomes, transparency and accountability, while ensuring responsibility for safe use is addressed as a collective ethical and public health concern.

items.title: Blunted No-Go P3 predicts faster increases in disordered eating symptoms in early adolescence: A four-wave longitudinal study.
items.abstract: In Canada, about 1.7 million individuals experience an eating disorder at any given time. Early adolescence is a high-risk period for the onset of disordered eating attitudes and behaviors, which may persist into adulthood and predict negative outcomes. Identifying mechanisms associated with the development of eating pathology is therefore important for early risk identification and intervention. One such risk factor is inhibitory control (IC)-the ability to suppress a prepotent response to support goal-directed behavior. However, most research linking IC to eating pathology has been cross-sectional and has relied on self-report or behavioral measures of IC. This study examined whether the No-Go P3, an ERP correlate of IC, predicted changes in disordered eating symptoms over two years during early adolescence. A group of 115 healthy early adolescents (66 girls; Mean/SD age at baseline = 10.94/1.18 years; 87.5% White, 3.6% Asian, 8.9% more than one race) completed an EEG Go/No-Go task at baseline and reported on their eating problems across four assessments. Multilevel growth models demonstrated that youth with a smaller baseline No-Go P3, which might indicate inefficient recruitment of IC-related neural resources, showed faster increases in disordered eating symptoms over time. No association was found for commission errors of IC.

items.title: Switch it up!: Variability in emotion supports children's word learning.
items.abstract: Children learn words in emotionally rich contexts, yet emotional variability has rarely been considered as a factor shaping word learning. The present study examined whether variability in emotional context affects children's initial mapping of novel words. Four-year-old children (N = 96; 48 male and 48 female) learned novel words in a storybook with each word presented in one, two, or four distinct emotional contexts. Children showed the strongest learning when words were encountered across four emotional contexts, indicating a benefit of high emotional variability for early word learning (ηp2=.08). These findings demonstrate that variability in emotional context, despite being unrelated to word meanings themselves, can support word learning. By extending prior work on contextual variability, the results highlight emotional input as an important and previously overlooked dimension of children's learning environments and underscore the interconnected nature of emotion and cognition.

items.title: RSV prevention after nirsevimab: what Europe has learned-and what it has not.
items.abstract: Europe moved within two seasons from selective respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prophylaxis for a small high-risk group to population-based strategies capable of protecting most infants. We aimed to examine the European experience with RSV prevention after nirsevimab introduction, and identify key lessons regarding implementation, programme performance, comparative evaluation, and remaining evidence gaps. Studies evaluating RSV prevention after nirsevimab introduction in Europe were searched. Evidence was mapped according to implementation strategies, effectiveness outcomes, healthcare impact, safety, resistance, and emerging research questions. Real-world studies from Europe consistently reported considerable reductions in RSV hospitalisation and intensive-care admission following nirsevimab implementation. Heterogeneity in programme design and delivery suggests that product effectiveness is only one determinant of impact: programme characteristics like administration timing, catch-up strategies, coverage, maternity-versus-community delivery, and the age distribution of baseline burden influence observed outcomes. Second-season evidence distinguishes limited residual individual protection from a persisting cumulative two-season benefit. Maternal RSVpreF vaccination is highly effective when administered sufficiently before delivery, although cross-strategy comparisons remain vulnerable to timing and selection bias. Safety findings remain reassuring; resistance-associated substitutions are detectable but have not undermined population-level effectiveness. The recent introduction of clesrovimab further expands preventive options. Conclusion Europe has answered whether universal infant RSV prevention can reduce severe disease burden but not yet standardised how programmes are compared. The next phase should move from product advocacy to programme science: one primary strategy for most infants, explicit rescue indications, linked immunisation-outcome-genomic surveillance, common estimands and transparent measurement of equity and opportunity cost. What is known • Long-acting monoclonal antibodies and maternal RSVpreF vaccination prevent severe RSV disease in early infancy. What is new • The European lesson is not a universal product ranking: delivery architecture, catch-up and the interval between maternal vaccination and birth determine population impact. • Second-season policy requires estimand discipline: limited residual effectiveness can coexist with substantial cumulative two-season benefit and no rebound.

items.title: Early Adolescent Romantic Experiences and Psychosocial Stress in Sexual Minority and Heterosexual Youth.
items.abstract: Sexual minority youth are at greater risk for negative psychosocial outcomes starting in early adolescence. We examined early romantic involvement as a risk or protective factor for sexual minority youth compared to heterosexual youth. This study examined associations among youth romantic experiences, sexual orientation, and psychosocial stress from early (age 12) to middle (age 15) adolescence (N = 392; n = 348 heterosexual youth, n = 44 sexual minority youth). Although heterosexual and sexual minority youth had similar levels of early romantic experiences, early adolescent romantic experiences were uniquely associated with poorer concurrent and subsequent psychiatric symptoms and psychosocial outcomes among sexual minority youth; however, romantic experience in middle adolescence was not associated with concurrent increased psychological stress for sexual minority youth. Early adolescent, but not middle adolescent, romantic experiences are associated with heightened negative psychosocial outcomes among sexual minority youth. Timing of romantic involvement may determine whether romantic experiences are a risk or protective factor for this population.

items.title: Pharmacogenomic diversity at tuberculosis-treatment loci across African populations: phased haplotypes, regulatory architecture and NAT2 acetylator inference
items.abstract: Background: Tuberculosis imposes a major public-health burden in Africa, while variation in isoniazid and rifampicin disposition creates opportunities for improved pharmacotherapy. The population architecture of extended, phased pharmacogenomic backgrounds remains less well characterized than individual marker frequencies. Methods: We analyzed high-coverage, phased GRCh38 genomes from 661 unrelated individuals sampled from five continental-African and two African-diaspora populations at NAT2, SLCO1B1, CES2, HLA-B, NR1I2 and UGT1A1. We integrated frequency differentiation, reduced phased signatures, linkage disequilibrium, functional annotation and NAT2 core-allele inference with individual-clustered permutation tests. Results: The six loci contributed 17,223 annotated variant records and 276 entries in a capped frequency-differentiation register. Exact NAT2 core-definition matching was achieved for 1,321/1,322 chromosomes (99.92%), and determinate genotype-inferred acetylator categories for 620/661 individuals (93.80%). Among the sampled continental-African populations, 35-site noncore background distributions differed within NAT2 *5 (BH-adjusted q=0.000100), *4 (q=0.024733) and *6 (q=0.000350) groups. Distinct phased and linkage architectures also characterized transporter, hydrolysis, regulatory and HLA-B genomic regions. Conclusion: African population-associated variation extends beyond commonly used pharmacogenetic allele definitions. The observed NAT2 backgrounds and complementary locus signatures provide a foundation for targeted molecular studies and prospective pharmacokinetic validation that could inform future population-responsive TB treatment research.

items.title: Association between Social Media Exposure and Self-Medication Practices: Public Health Implications in Punjab, Pakistan
items.abstract: Background: Social media has become an important source of health information, including information about medicines. Exposure to medicine-related content may affect decisions to use medicines without professional consultation. Objective: To describe self-medication practices and social-media exposure among adults in Punjab, Pakistan, and explore associations between self-medication frequency and demographic, social-media-use, and attitudinal factors. Methods: A cross-sectional analytical survey was conducted among adults aged 18-60 years in Punjab between March and May 2026. The final analytic sample comprised 280 participants. A bilingual (Urdu/English) questionnaire assessed demographics, social-media use and health-content exposure, self-medication in the preceding six months, medicine categories, and attitudes. The questionnaire was reviewed by two clinical experts and piloted among 30 participants. Descriptive analyses, chi-square tests, and multinomial logistic regression were reported using IBM SPSS Statistics; significance was set at alpha = 0.05. Results: Self-medication frequency was reported as Rarely by 117 participants (41.8%), Frequently by 130 (46.4%), and More Often by 33 (11.8%). Fever medicines were reported by 179 participants (63.9%) and gastrointestinal medicines by 96 (34.3%); multiple-response medicine categories were not mutually exclusive. Instagram was the most frequently selected social-media platform. Advertisement recall differed across self-medication frequency groups (chi-square (22) = 35.28, p = .036). Belief that medicines shown in advertisements/posts were safe was associated with self-medication frequency (chi-square (4) = 14.26, p = .007), while perceived risk was not (chi-square (4) = 1.587, p = .811). The multinomial model's overall test was not statistically significant (chi-square (40) = 54.07, p = .068; Nagelkerke R2 = .205). Likelihood-ratio tests identified associations for daily social-media-use duration (chi-square (2) = 13.085, p = .001), age group (chi-square (6) = 14.930, p = .021), and perceived advertisement safety (chi-square (4) = 10.899, p = .028). Conclusion: Self-medication was commonly reported in this sample. Some social-media-use and advertising-attitude variables were associated with self-medication frequency, but the overall regression model was not statistically significant and the cross-sectional design cannot establish causality. Findings should be interpreted cautiously given the sample composition and reported data limitations.

items.title: Evaluating WGS-based methods as an in silico replacement of phage typing for historical continuity and host association in Salmonella Typhimurium
items.abstract: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium (STm) poses a significant burden on public health worldwide. The Anderson phage typing scheme has historically supported surveillance, outbreak investigations and source attribution through associations between phage types and animal hosts. However, limitations inherent to the scheme have led to the gradual replacement of phage typing by whole-genome sequencing (WGS)-based methods. In this study, we applied statistical and machine learning approaches to 1,329 high-quality STm whole-genome sequences to compare phage typing with hierarchical clustering of core-genome multilocus sequence typing (HierCC) and the single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) address. We observed low congruence (< 0.60) between phage typing and WGS-based approaches. Nevertheless, a random forest model using WGS-based subtypes as features was able to predict all phage types with high specificity (≥ 0.94) and at least 80% recall for 10 of the 24 analysed phage types. These included phage types of human and veterinary epidemiological importance, including DT193, DT104, DT2, DT40, DT56, DT9, and DT99. We then assessed whether WGS-based subtyping methods could replace the host-association feature of phage typing. At higher distance thresholds (≥ 100) WGS-based subtyping methods were more informative of animal host species and displayed stronger host-associations than phage types for 11 of the 12 animal hosts, with significantly stronger associations for ducks, finches, and pigs (all p < 0.05). Thus, despite low congruence between phage types and WGS-based subtypes, our random forest model accurately predicted several epidemiologically important phage types, including those important to public health and veterinary surveillance, supporting its potential as an in silico alternative for those phage types. Finally, our findings suggest HierCC and SNP address methods can capture the host-association information historically derived from phage typing.

items.title: Employing the expertise of people with lived experience and other stakeholders in big data projects: Consultation methodology in a mental health research study
items.abstract: Patient and public involvement and engagement (PPIE) in health research is a cornerstone of good research practice. In this paper, we report on three different approaches to consultation for the purpose of clarifying aspects of big data usage in mental health science. The three case studies reported offer examples of different methodologies; illustrate how those methodologies were put into practice; and critically reflect on the role of consultation as a PPIE activity. The consultations used lived experience perspectives to obtain further insight into participant survey responses, clinicians’ interpretation of data from electronic health records, and relationship-building to shape ongoing research activities across a programme of research. All three case studies can be described in terms of solving existing challenges of big “messy” data by working with people with lived experience and mental health professional stakeholders on their interpretation through small-scale qualitative methodologies. We conclude with reflections on consultation as a valuable and flexible tool that creates space for new interpretations and understanding of mental health issues and their treatment.

items.title: Phytochemical and In Silico Evaluation of the Antimalarial Potential of Tecomella undulata through Molecular Docking and ADMET Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Plasmodium is the most prevalent infectious disease and a significant worldwide public health problem, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions. Most of the clinical drugs are plant-originated products. Traditionally, therapeutic shrubs have been utilized to treat a wide range of illnesses and are regarded as important sources of therapeutic chemicals. That’s why medicinal plants Tecomella undulata were chosen for this study because of their historic usage in folk medicine and their therapeutic significance. Firstly, plant compounds were extracted from the PubChem database, and their ADMET and drug-likeness pharmaceutics were analyzed with the help of the Swiss ADME (https://www.swissadme.ch/) tool. Compounds that met Lipinski’s rules were shortlisted for further molecular docking examination. Molecular docking of selected compounds was performed against three important Plasmodium falciparum proteins, FP-2, FP-3, and Plm-2. 2D and 3D conformations of best binding interactions were prepared with the help of the Discovery Studio visualizer. Among all the selected compounds, Dehydrotectol showed the best binding energy score of -10.3 kcal/mol with both the target proteins and could be a promising bioagent for the treatment of malaria.

items.title: Prussian blue nanozyme-based colorimetric biosensor for rapid visual quantification of β-galactosidase-positive foodborne bacteria in bottled water and milk
items.abstract: Abstract Infections caused by foodborne pathogens pose a serious challenge to global public health. Conventional detection approaches suffer from inherent drawbacks, e.g., time-consuming, operationally complex, high-cost, and instrument-dependent. Thus, to develop a rapid, sensitive, convenient, and cost-effective novel visual sensor for bacterial detection remains an urgent need. Herein, we rationally designed a novel sensing strategy based on β-galactosidase-positive bacteria (β-gal) can interact with a peroxidase-like nanomaterials, i.e., Prussian blue nanoparticles (PB NPs). The PB NPs-based β-galactosidase detection approach enables highly specific recognition toward β-galactosidase-positive bacteria with the linear range from 8 × 10 1 to 8 × 10 7 CFU/mL (R 2 = 0.9984). Generally, PB NPs firstly catalyze H 2 O 2 -mediated oxidation of colorless 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) and yield a blue signal (oxidized TMB, ox-TMB). Upon the trigger of target bacteria, p-aminophenyl-β-D-galactopyranoside (PAPG) is subsequently hydrolyzed into reductive p-aminophenol (PAP), which suppresses ox-TMB, i.e., the blue signal is negatively correlated with the bacterial concentration. The turnaround time from sample generation to measurement has been reduced by half. The novel approach achieves real-time and sensitive detection for β-galactosidase-positive bacteria flora, showing excellent feasibility, robustness, and great potential for practical applications.

items.title: Integrated Group Antenatal Care Model: Development of a Brazilian Group Antenatal Care Programme Using Plan–Do–Study–Act Cycles
items.abstract: Abstract Background Group antenatal care (ANC-G) has emerged as an innovative model to improve the quality of antenatal care (ANC) by integrating clinical assessment, health education and psychosocial support. Although evidence supporting its effectiveness is growing, its implementation within public health systems, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, remains limited. Objective To describe the development, implementation and structure of an ANC-G programme. Methods This quality improvement report, prepared in accordance with the SQUIRE 2.0 guidelines, describes a programme implemented in a teaching hospital in Brazil. The programme was developed through iterative Plan–Do–Study–Act (PDSA) cycles during a pilot randomised study; the comparative outcomes of that study are not reported in this manuscript. Group sessions were scheduled according to participants’ gestational age, with one session in the postpartum period and 10 at the recommended timing for routine antenatal/postpartum care. All sessions were delivered by a multidisciplinary team. Results The programme comprised 11 structured group sessions, each lasting approximately 2 hours, involving 8–12 pregnant women, and facilitated by obstetric nurses, with participation from obstetricians, psychologists, a physical educator, nursing students, obstetrics resident and invited professionals, including nutritionists, physiotherapists and social workers. The model integrated all clinical/obstetric assessment with group-based health education, physical activity and psychosocial support. Topics addressed throughout the programme included nutrition, immunisation, physical activity, warning signs, infection prevention, mental health, gender-based violence, reproductive planning, birth preparedness, breastfeeding, newborn care, women’s rights and postpartum adaptation. The sessions incorporated participatory educational strategies, including group discussions, simulations, practical demonstrations, games, artistic activities, reflective writing and peer learning. The PDSA process enabled the development of a structured, contextually adapted programme and generated detailed documentation of programme content, implementation procedures, educational strategies and professional roles. Conclusions This study provides a comprehensive description of a structured ANC-G programme implemented in a university hospital. The programme offers a replicable framework for integrating clinical, educational, and psychosocial components of ANC and may inform future implementation and scale-up within public health systems. Trial registration: Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (ReBEC), RBR-8xcjmf; UTN U1111-1243-6241. Registered on 26 February 2020.

items.title: A Robust Evaluation of Low-Dose CT Reconstruction Through Generative and Discriminative Models
items.abstract: Abstract Low-dose CT (LDCT) reconstruction is a critical problem in radiology that has a significant impact on public health. With the rise of deep learning, especially in generative models, we have seen a diverse range of methods for reconstructing LDCT images. However, existing LDCT reconstruction methods are often evaluated under inconsistent experimental settings, including different dataset splits, preprocessing pipelines, and noise-generation procedures, hindering fair comparisons across approaches. In addition, many studies do not explicitly assess 1 generalization across diverse datasets with different acquisition characteristics, limiting the practical relevance of the reported results. Therefore, we present a comprehensive fair study of modern generative models for LDCT reconstructions. Beyond effectiveness on a single dataset, our main goal is to assess the models’ generalization across datasets. Moreover, we propose a new semantic segmentation-based metric, in addition to traditional image quality metrics, to evaluate the effectiveness of the reconstructed images in a medical task. Our results show that diffusion-based models with a small number of iterations out-perform UNet and GAN, especially on out-of-distribution datasets. However, there are still challenges that require further study regarding effectiveness and efficiency.

items.title: Community-Based Surveillance Information Pathway in Decentralized One Health Systems in Uganda
items.abstract: Abstract Background Community-based surveillance is increasingly used to extend One Health surveillance into rural settings where formal systems have limited reach. However, evidence often emphasizes the number of reports or the performance of community-based actors, while less is known about the information pathway through which community observations are recorded, classified, communicated, and linked to wider surveillance processes. This gap is especially important in decentralized systems, where information generated at community level must move across multiple actors and surveillance functions before it can contribute to wider public health action. Objective The objective is to examine how community-generated human, animal, and wildlife observations move through a decentralized One Health surveillance system in Uganda, and to assess how far these information pathways can be traced from observation and recording to notification and potential downstream surveillance action. Methods We conducted a retrospective empirical analysis of COHRIE-Uganda community surveillance records, complemented by program documentation on reporting and implementation processes. The dataset contained 25,646 records from four conservation landscapes, including 24,868 routine Logbook/Surveillance records and 778 Detection/Outbreak records. We described the domains and characteristics of observations, examined notification following abnormal livestock deaths, identified reported notification recipients, assessed Detection/Outbreak classification, and evaluated data completeness and information traceability using available household, geographic, temporal, and event-level fields. Conclusions The records captured observations across human, livestock, and wildlife domains, including 3,455 reports of ticks in livestock, 1,906 livestock abortions, 2,541 abnormal livestock deaths, 5,641 wild animals in gardens or homes, 2,066 contacts with wild animals elsewhere and 1,115 wildlife attacks. Among 6,170, 5,958 had records with a valid notification response following an abnormal livestock death; 3,220 (54%) indicated that someone had been notified. Reported recipients included local leaders and veterinary and animal-health personnel. The Detection/Outbreak branch contained 778 records; 273 (35.0%) lacked a populated detection-type field. Household, geographic, and event-level fields provided a basis for tracing observations, but incomplete identifiers, classification fields, and notification documentation limited the ability to establish continuity beyond initial reporting. Community surveillance generated a broad upstream layer of decentralized One Health information and documented pathways from community observation to local and sectoral notification. Its contribution to epidemic intelligence cannot be inferred from reporting volume or notification alone. It depends on whether observations can be consistently classified, linked to subsequent verification and response, and fed back into wider surveillance processes. Strengthening persistent event identifiers, cross-sector linkage and downstream documentation could improve the traceability and operational value of community-generated surveillance information.

items.title: Where Dimensions Fuse: A Culturally Grounded Measure of Addiction Attitudes Among Saudi Youth Using Exploratory Graph Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Substance use among youth is a pressing public health concern, yet Saudi Arabia critically lacks culturally grounded assessment instruments. This study developed the Saudi Youth Attitude Toward Addiction Scale (SYAAS) and examined whether addiction-related attitudes in this population are cognitively organised into discrete dimensions or integrated into culturally fused evaluative schemas. A sequential exploratory-confirmatory design employed 909 Saudi university students (Mage = 21.4, 50.1% female) recruited via snowball sampling from King Abdulaziz University, Jeddah, during February 2026. Exploratory Graph Analysis (EGA) revealed a five-factor emergent structure consolidating knowledge, motives, self-efficacy, stigma, and familial concerns into integrated dimensions. Bootstrap EGA confirmed the stability of three of the five dimensions (structural consistency ≥ 0.90), while two dimensions showed lower stability (0.38–0.56), consistent with the hypothesised cognitive integration in this collectivist context. The five-factor model demonstrated acceptable CFA fit (CFI = 0.984, RMSEA = 0.079), comparable to the imported nine-factor model (CFI = 0.986, RMSEA = 0.075) while employing substantially fewer parameters. ESEM cultural probe analysis identified 14 cross-loadings exceeding |λ| = 0.30, clustering systematically at the intersections that the study's theoretical framework predicted—psychological motives with behavioural resistance, behavioural intentions with risk perception, family protection with stigma, vulnerability with peer influence, and awareness with perceived risk. These cross-loadings reflect the cognitive integration of addiction-related attitudes in the Saudi context. Composite reliability was excellent (CR = 0.871–0.959), and convergent validity was strong (AVE = 0.523–0.667). The five-factor structure reveals that addiction-related attitudes among Saudi youth are cognitively fused rather than compartmentalised, and that culturally grounded measurement tools are essential for capturing this integrated evaluative architecture. These findings provide preliminary evidence and require replication in independent samples.

items.title: Prevalence, Perceptions, and Factors Associated with Smokeless Tobacco Use among Adults in a Rural Community in South-Eastern Nigeria: A Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background : Smokeless tobacco use remains an important public health concern, particularly in communities where snuff is traditionally available. Evidence on its prevalence, patterns, and associated perceptions in rural South-Eastern Nigeria remains limited. Objective : This study assessed the prevalence, patterns of use, perceptions, and factors associated with smokeless tobacco use among adults in Ukpo community, Dunukofia Local Government Area, Anambra State, Nigeria. Methods : A cross-sectional study was conducted among 490 respondents using a structured questionnaire adapted from the Adult Tobacco Survey. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, tobacco-use history, frequency and type of use, exposure to tobacco use, reasons for use, and perceptions were collected. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, chi-square/Fisher’s exact tests and multivariable logistic regression, with significance set at P Results : Of 490 respondents, 210 (42.9%) reported ever using smokeless tobacco. Among ever users, 129 (61.4%) were daily users. Dry snuff was the predominant product (155, 73.8%). Ever use of smoked tobacco was reported by 116 (23.7%), while 101 (20.6%) reported dual use. Stress relief was the most frequently reported reason for smokeless tobacco use (115, 61.2%). Social exposure was evident, with 87 (41.4%) reporting use among close friends. More than half (254, 51.8%) perceived smokeless tobacco as safer than cigarettes. Significant associations with smokeless tobacco use were observed for age, sex, marital status, and educational attainment. Conclusion : Smokeless tobacco use was common in this community, with dry snuff predominating. Findings highlight the need for context-specific tobacco education, risk communication, and prevention and cessation interventions targeting users and influential social networks.

items.title: Barriers to nurse-physician communication in patient care among nurse and physician working in public hospitals of west Arsi zones, Oromia Region, South East of Ethiopia, 2021: An Exploratory Qualitative Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Communication failure between nurse and physician is one of the problems occurs daily in healthcare organizations and has been recognized as a cause of preventable harm to patients. Study on nurse-physician communication (NPC) in Africa has been limited, with little information available specifically for sub-Saharan Africa, particularly Ethiopia. Objectives: This study aimed to assess barriers to nurse and physician communication in patient care among nurse and physician working in public hospitals of west Arsi zones, Oromia Region, South East of Ethiopia, 2021 Methods: A exploratory qualitative study design was utilized to explore barriers to nurse and physician communication in patient care. Six focus group discussion and six key informant In-depth interviews were conducted among nurses and physicians, selected through purposive sampling. The interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using Atlas.ti Software Version 23 to facilitate systematic coding and thematic analysis. Inductive thematic analysis was employed to identify themes and subthemes, providing a deeper understanding of the barriers to nurse-physician communication. Results: Three main key themes emerged, illustrating hospital-related, health system-related, and professional and behavioral-related barriers. The sub-theme analysis encompasses: the absence of communication strategies in hospitals, lack of forum preparation and training on communication systems, insufficient equipment supply, lack of recognition and encouragement, discrepancies between theoretical knowledge and practical application, salary dissatisfaction and disparities, excluded communication strategies from educational curricula, unsafe workplace environments, feelings of authority and power, and illegible prescriptions. Conclusion and recommendation: The findings highlighted to overcome barriers to effective nurse-physician communication, hospitals should implement formal communication strategies through regular training sessions and open dialogue forums. Ensuring adequate equipment supply via regular audits and promptly addressing shortages is crucial. Bridging the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application through continuous professional development and hands-on training is essential. Again, addressing salary disparities and improving workplace safety by ensuring cleanliness, and housing can enhance morale and communication among staff. Furthermore, promoting a culture of respect and collaboration by addressing disruptive behaviors and power dynamics through training and policy changes is vital.

items.title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis and molecular dynamics simulations predict andrographolide -TLR3 interaction and potential anti-IAV immune responses
items.abstract: Abstract Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a serious global public health threat. Andrographolide, the predominant bioactive component of Andrographis paniculata, exerts broad-spectrum antiviral effects. Nevertheless, the molecular targets and mechanisms underlying its anti-IAV activity remain unclear. This study intended to identify the key functional target of andrographolide and elucidate its immune regulatory mechanism against IAV infection. Bulk transcriptome sequencing, protein interaction network analysis and multiple machine learning methods were integrated to screen key functional genes regulated by andrographolide during IAV infection. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were used to verify the binding affinity between andrographolide and the hub gene, while single-cell transcriptomic analysis and virtual gene knockout assays were performed to explore cell-specific functional mechanisms. TLR3 was screened and confirmed as the core hub gene, and andrographolide could stably bind to TLR3. Single-cell results showed that TLR3 was specifically enriched in pulmonary NK cells of IAV-infected tissues; virtual TLR3 knockout significantly altered the transcriptional profiles of NK cells related to antiviral defense, cytotoxicity and cytokine signaling, confirming the critical regulatory function of TLR3. This transcriptomic analysis study verifies TLR3 as a direct functional target of andrographolide and identifies a novel NK cell-dependent immune axis, which provides a new mechanistic insight into the immunomodulatory and anti-influenza activity of andrographolide.

items.title: Association of perceived discrimination and ill-treatment with depressive symptoms among older adults in India
items.abstract: Abstract Background Depression is an important public health issue among older adults and is related to poor quality of life, functional decline, and increased healthcare burden. Social stressors: perceived discrimination and ill-treatment may adversely affect the mental well-being of older adults; however, nationally representative evidence from India remains limited. The objective is to examine the association of perceived discrimination and ill-treatment with depressive symptoms among older adults in India. Methods The study utilised data from the Longitudinal Ageing Study in India, Wave 1 (LASI, 2017–18). The analytical sample included 30,765 older adults aged 60 years and older. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the 10-item Centre for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D), with a score of ≥ 4 indicating depressive symptoms. Perceived discrimination was measured with six questions on everyday discriminatory experiences, while ill-treatment was assessed using self-reported mistreatment. Descriptive statistics and weighted bivariate analyses were performed using Pearson’s chi-square test. Binary logistic regression models were employed to estimate adjusted odds ratios (AORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for depressive symptoms. Results Overall, 30.09% of older adults reported depressive symptoms. The prevalence of depressive symptoms was significantly higher among respondents reporting perceived discrimination (47.75%) and ill-treatment (50.07%) compared with their counterparts. In the adjusted analysis, older adults experiencing perceived discrimination had significantly higher odds of depressive symptoms (AOR: 1.96; 95% CI: 1.70–2.26). Similarly, ill-treatment was positively associated with depressive symptoms (AOR: 1.39; 95% CI: 1.15–1.68). Higher odds of depressive symptoms were also observed among widowed older adults, individuals with ADL and IADL limitations, and those with multimorbidity. Conversely, higher educational attainment and greater life satisfaction were associated with lower odds of depressive symptoms. Conclusions Perceived discrimination and ill-treatment are significant predictors of depressive symptoms among older adults in India. The findings highlight the importance of addressing social discrimination, elder mistreatment, and psychosocial vulnerabilities through age-friendly policies, social support systems, and mental health interventions. Strengthening community-based care and promoting social inclusion may help improve mental well-being among India’s ageing population.

items.title: The psychological care gap in rare diseases: evidence of barriers and inequalities in access in Spain
items.abstract: Abstract Background Rare diseases (RDs) are associated with unique emotional and psychosocial challenges for affected individuals and their families. Despite increasing recognition of mental health as an important component of comprehensive care for RDs, evidence regarding access to psychological services remains limited. This study examined access to psychological care in RDs in Spain to identify barriers, facilitators, inequalities and unmet needs. Methods A national cross-sectional online survey was conducted between December 2023 and October 2024 through the Share4Rare digital platform in partnership with the Spanish Federation of Rare Diseases (FEDER). Adult patients and caregivers of individuals with RDs completed a questionnaire assessing access to psychological care, including referral pathways, perceived barriers, funding sources, satisfaction, adherence, and unmet needs. Descriptive and comparative analyses were performed according to age, gender, diagnosis group, and region of residence. Results The 792 responses comprised 56.9% (n = 451) adult patients and 43.1% (n = 341) caregivers. Nearly half of participants (49.7%, n = 394) reported not having received psychological care during the previous year. The most frequent barrier was the absence of a recommendation or referral from a healthcare professional (79,7%, n = 310), followed by financial barriers (13%, n = 54) and logistical constraints (6%, n = 25). Only 33.7% (n = 84) of individual therapy interventions, 24.3% (n = 18) of family interventions, and 31.6% (n = 24) of group interventions were funded through the public healthcare system. Significant inequalities in access to psychological care were observed according to gender, age, diagnostic group, and region of residence. Individual therapy received the highest satisfaction ratings (85.8%, n = 205) and showed greater adherence (70.1%, n = 169 completed all sessions) than family- or group-based interventions. Patient organisations emerged as key facilitators of access by providing psychological services and/or contributing to treatment costs. Conclusions One in two people affected by RDs reported not receiving psychological support during the previous year. Lack of referral or recommendation from healthcare professionals emerged as the principal barrier to access, over financial and logistical constraints. These findings suggest that psychological care remains insufficiently integrated into RD care pathways and highlight the need for systematic psychological assessment, routine referral mechanisms, equitable public funding, and stronger integration of mental health services within RDs care models.

items.title: Association Between Peak Expiratory Flow Trajectory and Risk Of Sarcopenia : A Multi-National Cross-Cohort Comparative Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Sarcopenia can affect 10%-27% of adults ≥ 60 years, which is a major public health challenge. Peak expiratory flow (PEF) reflects the function of respiratory muscle. The associations between repeated PEF measurements and sarcopenia are unclear. Methods This prospective cohort study included three nationally representative aging cohorts: China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS, n = 3,806), English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA, n = 2,231) and Health and Retirement Study (HRS, n = 724). Statistical analyses were conducted using R 4.2.0 and Stata 17.0, encompassing K-means trajectory clustering, Cox proportional hazards regression with Schoenfeld residual verification and random-effects meta-analysis with I² heterogeneity quantification. Results Three PEF trajectories (low-stable, moderate-stable, high-stable) were identified in all cohorts. High-stable PEF was associated with a 62%-73% lower risk of sarcopenia (CHARLS: HR = 0.31; ELSA: HR = 0.38; HRS: HR = 0.27), with consistent direction across cohorts and no heterogeneity (I²=0%). Trajectory clustering showed more stable dose-response relationships than single-point measurements, whereas prediction-equation-derived PEF metrics showed cross-cohort heterogeneity. Conclusions Repeatedly measured PEF levels were stably associated with incident sarcopenia across Chinese, British and American older adults, supporting PEF as a low-cost screening indicator. Differences among single-time, cumulative and prediction-equation-derived PEF metrics highlight the need for population-specific validation. Trial registration Clinical trial number: not applicable. This study is an observational cohort study based on three population-based aging cohorts and is not a clinical trial.

items.title: Effectiveness of Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention in Reducing Burden of Malaria Among Under Five Years Children in Yamaltu Deba Lga, Gombe State Nigeria
items.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the effectiveness of Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention (SMC) using Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine plus Amodiaquine (SPAQ) in reducing the malaria burden among children aged 3 to 59 months in Yamaltu Deba Local Government Area (LGA), Gombe State, Nigeria. Drawing on a comprehensive review of 18,876 clinical records from ten health facilities, the study compares malaria incidence before (2017–2020) and after (2021–2024) the implementation of SMC. The results indicate a substantial reduction in malaria cases averaging a 41.14% overall decline, with some facilities achieving over 30% reduction. Monthly trend analysis confirms that SMC was particularly effective during the peak transmission seasons (July to September). Inferential statistical analysis using paired sample t-tests demonstrated that the reductions were statistically significant (p , validating the intervention's impact. These findings provide strong empirical support for scaling up SMC as a cost-effective, life-saving public health strategy in malaria-endemic regions of Nigeria. They also highlight the importance of integrating SMC with routine healthcare delivery, strengthening community-based implementation, and addressing disparities in program performance across health facilities. The study recommends sustained investment in SMC, enhanced monitoring and evaluation systems, and cross-sectoral collaboration to ensure the continued success and expansion of malaria prevention efforts nationwide.

items.title: Aflatoxin Contamination in Local Foods and Associated Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices of Consumers in East Gojjam Zone, Ethiopia: An Integrated KAP Study
items.abstract: Abstract Aflatoxin contamination in staple foods poses a significant public health challenge, particularly in developing countries where inadequate post-harvest handling and limited regulatory enforcement prevail. This study investigated the occurrence, levels, and distribution of major aflatoxins (AFB₁, AFB₂, AFG₁, and AFG₂) in commonly consumed local foods in East Gojjam Zone, Ethiopia, and assessed consumers’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) related to food safety. A cross-sectional design was employed, combining advanced analytical determination using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography with fluorescence detection (UHPLC-FLD) and immunoaffinity column clean-up, with a structured KAP survey involving 398 respondents. The analytical method demonstrated excellent performance, with strong linearity (R² > 0.998), low detection limits (0.249–1.008 µg/L), and high recovery (90.7–104.3%), confirming its suitability for trace-level aflatoxin analysis. The results revealed widespread contamination across several food categories, with extremely high total aflatoxin levels detected in popped nuts (111.61 µg/kg) and berbere (108.74 µg/kg), far exceeding international safety limits. Moderate contamination was observed in mitimita, yeshay qimem, maize injera, and maize bread, while no detectable aflatoxins were found in teff injera and some cereal products. Observational findings indicated that poor storage conditions, moisture exposure, and unethical market practices significantly contributed to contamination. The KAP survey highlighted critically low public awareness, with only 2.5% of respondents aware of aflatoxins and over 90% mistakenly believing that processing eliminates toxin risks. Overall, the study demonstrates a substantial risk of chronic dietary exposure to aflatoxins in the study area, driven by both environmental and behavioral factors. These findings underscore the urgent need for strengthened food safety regulations, improved post-harvest management, and targeted public health education to mitigate aflatoxin exposure and associated health risks.

items.title: Strengthening National Health Security: Multi-country Implementation Experiences from Tackling Deadly Diseases in Africa Programme
items.abstract: Abstract Introduction Sub-Saharan Africa faces the highest burden of recurrent epidemic-prone diseases, yet health systems of most countries lack the health system capacity to effectively prevent, detect, and respond to public health emergencies. In 2024, the Tackling Deadly Diseases in Africa Programme (TDDAP2) was launched to strengthen health security capacities in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, and Uganda. We describe experiences in strengthening national health security through co-designed implementation models and collaborative government-embedded technical assistance. Methods We employed a mixed-methods design for programme review, based on technical reports generated between October 2024 and March 2026. Data sources included technical reports, field debriefs, case studies, Joint External Evaluations (JEEs), and stakeholder coordination meetings. Project activity completion and milestone data were abstracted from the project results framework. Qualitative data were analysed thematically, whereas quantitative data were summarised descriptively. Results TDDAP2 interventions were aligned with nationally determined health security priorities, grounded in JEEs, and coherent with the broader technical assistance landscape. Key features of the embedded technical assistance model were: in-country consultant deployment, collaboration with Ministries, Departments, Agencies (MDAs) throughout planning, implementation, and evaluation of activities, and oversight coordination by Palladium Country Leads. Cross-country outputs included: validated and costed NAPHS adopted in Kenya, Malawi, Ghana, and DRC; 991 health workers trained in IDSR in Uganda (mean knowledge scores: 66.7% − 87%); 22 MDAs adopting a digital NAPHS M&E tracker in Uganda; and Mpox coordination tools adopted by DRC PHEOC and subsequently adapted for EVD outbreak declared in September 2025. Conclusion Government-anchored and co-designed technical assistance can strengthen IHR core capacities across diverse contexts. Embedding in-country consultants within national systems and deploying digital monitoring tools produced measurable institutional gains, offering practical pathways for operationalising health security frameworks and advancing emergency preparedness and response.

items.title: An Update on the Biochemical Staging of Nutritional Rickets: A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: Nutritional rickets remains a significant global public health concern affecting infants and young children in regions with limited sunlight exposure or inadequate dietary vitamin D and calcium. This review revisits the biochemical staging system applicable to severe combined vitamin D and calcium deficiency. We propose that the classical three-stage model may be supplemented by recognition of a Nutritional Pseudohypoparathyroidism / PTH Resistance Variant—characterized by profound hypocalcemia, paradoxically normal or elevated serum phosphate, and markedly elevated parathyroid hormone (PTH)—reflecting acquired renal PTH resistance. Hypomagnesemia must be excluded before this designation is applied, as it constitutes a reversible and mechanistically distinct cause of functional PTH resistance. This phenotype is reversible with treatment and requires prospective validation. Evidence-based treatment strategies for each stage are summarized.

items.title: Prevalence and Associated Risk Factors of Hypertension and Pre-Hypertension Among the Adult Population: Findings from the Dubai Household Survey, 2024
items.abstract: Objectives: This study aims to determine the prevalence of hypertension (HTN) and pre-hypertension (PHTN) among adults in Dubai, the United Arab Emirates. Furthermore, it seeks to identify the associated sociodemographic characteristics and cardiometabolic risk within this population. Methods: This investigation utilized data from the 2024 Dubai Household Health Survey (DHHS), a population-based cross-sectional study employing a multistage stratified cluster sampling methodology. Data on socio-demographic characteristics, behavioral risk factors, blood pressure measurements, anthropometric parameters, and blood glucose levels were collected from 2530 adult participants representing the population of Dubai. All analyses were conducted using R statistical software, incorporating survey analysis procedures to account for the complex sampling design. Results: The weighted prevalence of HTN was 36.9% (95% CI: 35.1–40.3), and PHTN was 32.2% (95% CI: 27.9–36.4) among adults aged ≥18 years in Dubai, indicating that 69.1% of the adult population had elevated blood pressure. HTN prevalence increased with age, was higher in males than females, and was more prevalent among non-nationals and those with lower educational attainment. Cardiometabolic risk factors such as high cholesterol (56.6% in HTN, 53.9% in PHTN) and obesity (26.9% in HTN, 20.6% in PHTN) were common in both groups, with diabetes being significantly higher in the HTN group (20.7% vs 11.8%). Conclusions: The study reveals a high burden of HTN and PHTN in Dubai's adult population, with significant associations with age, gender, nationality, education, and various cardiometabolic risk factors. These findings underscore the urgent need for targeted public health interventions and early detection strategies to mitigate the rising prevalence of elevated blood pressure and associated cardiovascular risks in Dubai, the UAE.

items.title: Literature Review on the Impact of COVID-19 on the Development of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism
items.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic catalyzed a reconfiguration of tourism, forcing its transition towards more resilient and sustainable paradigms. This literature review synthesizes current knowledge on this transformation, analyzing the conceptual evolution of sustainability, research trends, methodological limitations, and future lines of study. Findings indicate a redefinition of the concept integrating public health and equity, greater effectiveness of strategies such as diversification and proximity tourism, and the persistence of gaps such as scarce longitudinal data. It concludes by underscoring the need for interdisciplinary approaches, such as the circular economy and the “One Health” model, to establish a transformative and lasting recovery.

items.title: Governance, Financing, and Service Delivery Challenges in Pakistan’s Healthcare System: A Critical Narrative Review
items.abstract: In Pakistan, rapid population growth, financial constraints, and chronic underinvestment have weakened the public healthcare system. Following the 2010–2011 constitutional devolution, healthcare governance and financing were transferred to provincial governments through a three-tiered public network comprising primary, secondary, and tertiary facilities. This critical review analyzes structural issues and inter-provincial disparities following the devolution of authority, based on the WHO’s “Health System Building Blocks” framework. A total of 40 peer-reviewed studies and 7 official documents (n = 47) were examined. The findings reveal that despite the devolution of authority and the scaling back of social health protection programs such as Sehat Sahulat, Pakistan continues to lag behind South Asian benchmarks in maternal and child survival and public health investments. Public health expenditure stagnates at 0.8–0.9% of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), leaving out-of-pocket (OOP) payments at 52.93% of total health spending—more than triple the global average of 17.33%. Progress across the WHO’s six core building blocks is hindered by an imbalance between nurses and physicians (5.2 nurses per 10,000 population), a shortage of healthcare workers in rural areas, and fragmented pharmaceutical regulations. The District Health Information System (DHIS2) fails to integrate with other systems. Macro-fiscal constraints, such as low tax revenues, a heavy debt burden, and the channeling of resources toward treatment-focused hospitals, continue to weaken the state's capacity for implementation. To achieve Universal Health Coverage (UHC), priority must be given to primary healthcare services and public health policies. It is essential to restructure insurance packages through local health taxes, regulate informal healthcare providers at the provincial level, and institutionalize coordination between federal and provincial authorities.

items.title: Adoption and use of the 7-1-7 timeliness metrics for detection, notification, and early response actions to public health events: a public health system evaluation in Liberia, January 2024 – June 2025
items.abstract: Background: In July 2021, a new global target of 7-1-7 was proposed to improve early detection, notification and rapid control of public health threats. Liberia adopted 7-1-7 metrics in September 2023, with the framework embedded in the health and data monitoring systems by January 2024. The study aimed to document factors that influenced 7-1-7 adoption and assess how well the health systems performed for 7-1-7 metrics between January 2024 and June 2025. Methods This was a public health system evaluation using a survey of staff with primary data collection and data extraction from routinely available information. Five national and 105 subnational staff were interviewed using a semi-structured questionnaire on 7-1-7 adoption, with data presented as frequencies and proportions. Research assistants extracted 7-1-7 performance data along with recorded bottlenecks and enablers from the 7-1-7 data consolidation spreadsheet. 7-1-7 data were presented as medians (range) and proportions meeting 7-1-7 targets, while bottlenecks and enablers were mapped to themes and categories listed in the established 7-1-7 toolkit. Results Key factors in successful adoption of 7-1-7 involved having a 7-1-7 champion, a dedicated coordination team, strong and committed leadership and effective stakeholder engagement at both national and subnational levels. Of 138 public health events, 134 (97%) were recorded against 7-1-7 targets. Mpox constituted 81 (61%) of these events. The median (range) times to detection, notification and completion of early response actions were 6 days (0-69), 0 days (0-6) and 7 days (1-129) respectively. The 7-day detection target was met in 97 (71%) events, the 1-day notification target in 131 (98%) and the 7-day response target in 79 (59%). Overall, 58 (43%) events met all three targets. Key systematic barriers to implementation (bottlenecks) were: inadequately trained health-care workers and poor community engagement for detection; electronic surveillance issues and poor network coverage for notification; and inadequate resources, logistics and delayed laboratory reporting for early response actions. Strong coordination among public health units was a key facilitator for implementation (enabler). Conclusions This system evaluation showed that the 7-1-7 metrics are measurable and achievable, while at the same time indicating the key systematic barriers that need improvement and increased investment.

items.title: Association Between Renal Failure and Non-Prescription Cosmetic/Skin Care and Herbal Product Use: A Case-Control Study at UNTH, Enugu, Nigeria.
items.abstract: Background: Renal failure associated with exposure to potentially nephrotoxic substances in non-prescription cosmetic products, skincare preparations, and herbal remedies represents an emerging public health concern, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where regulation and safety monitoring remain limited. This study investigated the association between renal failure and exposure to cosmetic/skincare and herbal products among adults attending the University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital (UNTH), Enugu. Methods A hospital-based unmatched case–control study was conducted among 300 participants comprising 150 renal failure cases and 150 controls between September and December 2025. Cases included adults with confirmed chronic kidney disease stages 3–5, while controls had normal renal function. Bivariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Results Renal failure cases were older than controls (54 ± 14 years vs 41 ± 15 years) and demonstrated lower educational attainment and income levels. Secondary cosmetic exposure was independently associated with renal failure (AOR = 3.40; 95% CI: 1.56–7.44; p = 0.002), while primary and secondary herbal exposure were independently associated with higher odds of disease (AOR = 4.00; 95% CI: 1.88–8.53; p < 0.001 and AOR = 7.50; 95% CI: 3.26–17.27; p < 0.001, respectively). Middle-aged and elderly individuals had higher odds of renal failure compared with younger adults (AOR = 4.46; 95% CI: 2.18–9.09; p < 0.001). Diabetes mellitus (AOR = 14.35; p < 0.001) and hypertension (AOR = 9.83; p < 0.001) were the strongest clinical correlates. Conclusion Renal failure among adults attending UNTH was statistically associated with repeated herbal exposure, secondary cosmetic exposure, older age, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus. These findings do not establish causation because CKD etiology, chemical exposure, and renal histology were not assessed; prospective and toxicological studies are needed.

items.title: Trends and inequalities in smoking initiation, quitting, and relapse among Australians with and without disabilities, 2002-2024.
items.abstract: Introduction Despite declining smoking prevalence, tobacco remains the second leading risk factor for disease burden in Australia. Smoking inequalities between people with and without disabilities are well documented, but smoking transitions (initiation, quitting, and relapse) remain poorly understood. We aimed to estimate smoking prevalence and the rates of smoking transitions among Australians with and without disabilities from 2002-2024. Methods We analyzed 183 725 unique interviews from the Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia Survey from 2002-2024. We estimated the prevalence of not smoking, smoking, and former smoking, and rates of initiation, quitting, and relapse by disability status among people aged 15-44 years, standardizing by age and sex. Initiation, quitting, and relapse were based on changing smoking status between two consecutive years. Results Smoking prevalence decreased from 38.0% to 20.8% among people with disabilities, and from 26.8% to 13.7% among those without disabilities. Quitting rates increased for both groups but remained consistently lower among people with disabilities: 9.3% to 21.2% among people with disabilities vs. 16.3% to 23.3% among those without disabilities. Initiation and relapse annual rates remained unchanged during the study period, with initiation at approximately 3% among people who did not smoke and relapse at 15% among people who formerly smoked, regardless of disability status. Conclusions People with disabilities now have relatively similar smoking prevalence to people without disabilities two decades prior, reflecting a persistent, generation-long gap driven by lower quitting rates and limited success of public policies to reduce smoking inequality and prevent initiation and relapse.

items.title: App-based tobacco deliveries to university campuses.
items.abstract: Introduction The tobacco industry has a long history of targeting young adults by increasing product appeal and access. In recent years, Duffl and Snag Delivery introduced a novel way for young adults to access tobacco by offering on-demand delivery to university campuses. This study examined tobacco product availability, and purchase and delivery practices from Duffl and Snag at California universities and assessed compliance with local, state, and federal laws. Methods Young Adult Tobacco Purchase Surveys were conducted at four California universities with a nearby Duffl and/or Snag store: University of California (UC) Berkeley, UC Santa Barbara, University of Southern California, and San Diego State University. Students (> =21 years) from each campus purchased tobacco products from the Duffl and/or Snag app or online store to assess compliance with federal, state, and local laws. Results Of the 25 successful online orders, 11 were delivered on or near campus and 14 were picked up at the store. An ID was requested at the point of purchase for most online orders (21/25). However, none of the deliveries requested ID (0/11) and approximately half of the orders picked up at the store requested ID (8/14), which violates the Federal PACT Act. A total of 40 tobacco products were purchased, and approximately half were flavored (20/40) and offered a price discount (25/40), violating California's flavored tobacco sales restriction and local price discounting policies. Conclusions Many purchases from Duffl and Snag were out of compliance with federal, state, and local tobacco control policies. This investigation of two novel online delivery apps highlights how easy it is for young adults in college to purchase and receive tobacco products.

items.title: Fatal dengue cases in travellers from 1995 to 2025: A targeted review.
items.abstract: Background Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease endemic in 136 countries and territories, with over 14 million cases and more than 10,000 deaths reported globally in 2024 alone. International travellers are at risk of infection when visiting endemic regions. While dengue in travellers is well described, dengue-related mortality in this population has not been comprehensively synthesised. We compiled and critically assessed available data on reports of fatal dengue cases among international travellers over a 30-year period. Methods A targeted review was conducted to identify dengue-related fatalities in travellers from non-endemic countries acquiring infection in endemic regions between 1995 and November 2025. PubMed searches using terms related to dengue, mortality, and travel were complemented by hand-searching conference proceedings, national and international surveillance reports, publicly accessible national infectious disease databases, media reports, and anecdotal notifications. Cases were classified as confirmed or probable based on diagnostic method and/or inclusion in surveillance systems. Data were extracted, cross-referenced to avoid duplication, and analysed descriptively. Results Sixty-seven fatal travel-related dengue cases were identified, of which 55 were classified as confirmed/probable and 12 cases had limited information. Of the 55 confirmed/probable cases, 22 reported both country of residence and acquisition, spanning 14 endemic destinations. Confirmed/probable fatal cases occurred among patients aged Conclusions Dengue-related mortality among travellers is rare but likely under-recognised and underreported. Strengthened diagnostic capacity and heightened clinical awareness may support earlier recognition and management of severe cases in travellers, while harmonised international reporting systems could improve case ascertainment and contribute to future prevention strategies.

items.title: Predictors of COVID-19 Hospitalization Costs in a Tertiary Hospital in Kuwait: Evidence From Real-World Data.
items.abstract: Objectives COVID-19 has imposed significant economic pressures on healthcare systems worldwide, with hospitalization costs constituting a major component. In Kuwait, previous estimates have reported average inpatient costs but lacked granularity on cost predictors across diverse patient subgroups. This study examined predictors of COVID-19 hospitalization costs and variations in costs across admission periods in 2021. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of all patients (N = 7569) admitted to Jaber Al-Ahmed Hospital, the national tertiary referral center for COVID-19 in Kuwait, in 2021. Patient-level hospitalization costs were derived using the microcosting approach reported previously elsewhere from the same cohort. Multivariable generalized linear models were used to estimate marginal cost differences, while accounting for demographic, clinical, and treatment-related characteristics. The month of admission and pandemic wave were included to assess differences in costs across admission periods in 2021. Results Intensive care unit admission and the use of remdesivir, corticosteroids, antibiotics, and immunosuppressants were associated with significantly higher costs. Patients with cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, or cancer also incurred higher costs. COVID-19 vaccination and hypertension were associated with lower costs. South Asian and Arab patients had lower estimated costs than Kuwaiti nationals. Costs declined by 24.7% over the year and by 8.6% across pandemic waves. Conclusions COVID-19 hospitalization costs varied substantially by patient characteristics, treatment regimens, and over time. Cost differences suggest further investigation into potential differences in disease severity, treatment pathways, and healthcare access. These findings support the need for data-informed, and equitable healthcare planning.
