items.title: Real-World Data in Economic Evaluations of Schizophrenia: A Systematic Review of Roles, Applications and Methodological Gaps.
items.abstract: Real-world data (RWD) are increasingly used in health economic evaluation and health technology assessment (HTA). However, there is limited understanding of how RWD are incorporated into economic evaluations of schizophrenia, a condition characterised by complex care pathways and long-term disease trajectories. This review aims to systematically examine how RWD have been incorporated into economic evaluations of schizophrenia, with particular attention to their roles, patterns of use, reporting transparency and methodological limitations. A systematic review was conducted following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO). MEDLINE, Embase and PsycINFO were searched for studies published between 2015 and 2025 reporting full economic evaluations incorporating RWD. Data were extracted on study characteristics, methodological approaches and the use of RWD across analytical domains. Findings were synthesised narratively due to heterogeneity across studies. Reporting completeness was assessed using the Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards (CHEERS) 2022 checklist, and the suitability of electronic health record (EHR) data was evaluated using The Professional Society for Health Economics and Outcomes Research (ISPOR) Suitability of EHR Data (SUITABILITY) Checklist. In total, 30 studies were included: 15 model-based, 12 observational and three trial-based evaluations. RWD use was concentrated in clinical inputs, including event-rate parameters, as well as healthcare utilisation and costs, with limited application to health utilities and broader societal outcomes. In model-based evaluations, RWD primarily informed individual parameters rather than model structure or complete treatment pathways. Observational evaluations used patient-level RWD directly, but several had small samples, and only a minority reported formal confounding adjustment. Trial-based evaluations mainly used RWD to supplement resource-use and cost data. Reporting of data processing, missingness and validation was incomplete, limiting assessment of data suitability and analytical credibility. RWD use in schizophrenia economic evaluations remains concentrated in individual inputs, with limited application to model structure and long-term care pathways, where evidence on routine practice may offer particular added value. Priorities include better aligning RWD use with decision-relevant evidence needs, strengthening analytical methods and improving reporting transparency. RWD should be used selectively, alongside complementary evidence sources, where they are fit for purpose and their likely contribution to decision-making justifies the additional resources required.

items.title: Single‑Cell Transcriptomic Reanalysis Reveals Neuronal Transcriptional States and Neuro‑Immune Remodeling After Peripheral Nerve Injury.
items.abstract: Peripheral nerve injury (PNI) causes severe sensorimotor deficits and neuropathic pain, yet the cellular and molecular mechanisms in the dorsal root ganglia (DRG) remain incompletely understood. In this study, we aimed to identify the transcriptional states of specific neuronal subtypes after PNI and to characterize potentially associated neuro-immune remodeling. We reanalyzed a public scRNA-seq dataset (GSE255014) from mouse L4-L5 DRG at day 3 after chronic constriction injury (CCI). Neuronal subtype-associated transcriptional states, macrophage heterogeneity, and predicted ligand-receptor interactions were systematically analyzed using unbiased clustering, differential expression, AUCell, SCENIC, pseudotime trajectory inference, and CellChat. PNI was associated with cell type proportion imbalance and apoptosis pathway activation. Among nine confirmed neuronal subtypes, the recovered Nefm⁺ neurofilament-containing neuronal subpopulation showed an apparent reduction after CCI, accompanied by expansion of a Sprr1a⁺ regeneration-associated neurons. Moreover, Atf3 and Jun were significantly upregulated in Nefm⁺ neurons and may serve as candidate key regulators cooperatively driving the transition of this subtype toward an injury/regeneration-associated state. In macrophages, six subpopulations with distinct transcriptomic profiles were identified. The dominant resident-like Cd163⁺ subpopulation decreased noticeably after CCI, whereas the Ccr2⁺ pro-inflammatory subpopulation expanded markedly. Pseudotime ordering revealed a transcriptional continuum from resident‑like to pro-inflammatory states. Cell-cell communication analysis showed that incoming signaling to Ccr2⁺ macrophages was considerably enhanced during PNI. Notably, App-Cd74 signaling axes was weakened between Nefm⁺ neurons and Cd163⁺ macrophages but enhanced between Nefm⁺ neurons and Ccr2⁺ macrophages, which may specifically promote local infiltration and pro-inflammatory activation of Ccr2⁺ macrophages. Our study indicates that day 3 post-CCI induced marked transcriptional remodeling of Nefm+ neurons in the DRG and highlighted abnormal crosstalk between these neurons and macrophages. These findings deepen our understanding of the neuroimmune pathogenic mechanisms in the early stage of PNI and may therefore inform future improved therapeutic strategies for neuropathic pain.

items.title: Bistability and intermittency: linking synaptic variability and slow potassium currents to spontaneous seizures generation.
items.abstract: Spontaneous seizures emerge from abrupt transitions between asynchronous neural activity and pathological burst synchronization. In this work, we combine 24-hour recordings from rats with spontaneous absence seizures and a conductance-based neuronal network model to investigate the mechanisms underlying these transitions. By systematically varying excitatory and inhibitory coupling, we show that the model reproduces bistable and intermittent dynamical regimes and captures the duration and variability of seizure-like events observed experimentally. The similarity between simulated and experimental seizure duration distributions is supported by Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistics. To identify dynamical signatures of the transition from physiological to pathological activity, we analyzed postsynaptic potentials and the slow potassium current using recurrence-based measures. We find that the increase in inhibition enhances postsynaptic potential variability, thereby facilitating spontaneous switching between down and up-states. At the same time, the slow potassium currents exhibit a marked reorganization of its temporal structure, indicating that intrinsic ionic dynamics are also reshaped in the intermittent regime. Together, these findings suggest that spontaneous seizure-like activity emerges from the combined action of synaptic variability and intrinsic slow-current dynamics. More broadly, our results provide a computational framework for linking recurrence-based dynamical fingerprints to biophysical mechanisms of spontaneous seizure generation.

items.title: Impact of Foslevodopa/Foscarbidopa on Key Clinical and Patient-Reported Outcomes in Patients With Advanced Parkinson's Disease: Responder Analysis of Two Phase 3 Clinical Trials.
items.abstract: A post hoc responder analysis was conducted to evaluate the impact of foslevodopa/foscarbidopa (LDp/CDp) on achieving meaningful responses in clinical and patient reported outcomes among people with advanced Parkinson's disease (PwaP). Data from two trials evaluating 24-h/day continuous subcutaneous LDp/CDp infusion in PwaP were included: (1) a 12-week, randomized, double-blind, phase 3 trial (ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT04380142) and (2) a 52-week, open-label, multicenter study (NCT03781167). Responders were identified relative to baseline for increased "On" time without troublesome dyskinesia (ONwoTD) and reduced "Off" time using ≥ 1-h and ≥ 3-h thresholds (robust responder). Established minimal clinically important differences evaluated Movement Disorder Society-Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale Part II (MDS-UPDRS-II), Parkinson's Disease Questionnaire-39 (PDQ-39), European Quality of Life 5-Dimensions 5-Level (EQ-5D-5L), and Parkinson's Disease Sleep Scale-2 (PDSS-2) responders. Adjusted generalized linear models compared responder proportions treated with LDp/CDp versus oral levodopa/carbidopa (LD/CD) at weeks 4 and 12, and outcomes through week 52. By week 12, a greater percentage of patients on LDp/CDp versus those on oral LD/CD experienced statistically significant (*P < 0.05) outcome improvements with 82.7%* versus 50.2% achieving 1-h reductions in "Off" time and 61.2%* versus 27.8% achieving ≥ 3-h reductions. Similarly, 83.1%* versus 48.3% of patients achieved ≥ 1-h increases in ONwoTD and 63.4%* versus 26.1% achieved ≥ 3-h increases. A greater proportion of patients on LDp/CDp achieved complete (100%) "Off" time resolution (42.7%* vs 14.4%), as well as reduced MDS-UPDRS-II (46.6%* vs 21.9%) and PDSS-2 scores (68.6%* vs 45.4%). Response rates for PDQ-39 (47.1% vs 31.9%) and EQ-5D-5L (36.8% vs 21.7%) scores were numerically higher, although differences were not statistically significant. Treatment benefits were observed as early as 4 weeks and maintained through 52 weeks. LDp/CDp may offer rapid, consistent, and meaningful reductions in motor fluctuations, nonmotor symptoms, and increased quality of life than oral LD/CD. The sustained LDp/CDp treatment benefits suggest long-term efficacy for PwaP. ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers, NCT04380142, NCT03781167.

items.title: STAR-Net: A Spatio-Temporal Attentive Representation Network with Iterative Refinement for ASD Diagnosis.
items.abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a lifelong neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by social deficits that typically emerge in early childhood. With advances in neuroimaging, resting-state fMRI provides a non-invasive way to study brain connectivity, facilitating early ASD diagnosis and differentiation from normal control. However, conventional methods fail to effectively model functional connectivity patterns due to their reliance on predefined atlases and ignorance of fMRI spatiotemporal information. In this paper, we propose the Spatio-Temporal Attentive Representation Network (STAR-Net), which jointly models spatial patterns and temporal dynamics through an adaptive fusion strategy for ASD diagnosis. Specifically, the network incorporates a Random Temporal Masking module as a training-only data augmentation technique to mitigate overfitting, an Adaptive Time-modulated Transformer to capture temporal dependencies, and an Iterative Attention-Guided Region Refinement module that progressively selects discriminative brain regions based on temporal-aware attention-derived importance scores across layers. Experiments across six sites from the publicly available ABIDE dataset demonstrate that STAR-Net outperforms existing spatio-temporal analysis methods. This work advances ASD diagnosis by providing an end-to-end solution that preserves essential spatio-temporal information in fMRI data.

items.title: Surgical resection versus biopsy in primary central nervous system lymphoma: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL) is usually diagnosed by stereotactic biopsy followed by high-dose methotrexate-based therapy; however, the role of upfront resection in selected patients remains debated. This systematic review and meta-analysis was reported according to PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from January 2001 to June 2026 for comparative studies of upfront resection versus biopsy in newly diagnosed intracranial PCNSL. Hazard ratios (HRs) for overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were pooled using random-effects models. The primary analysis was restricted to biopsy-only comparative studies, while broader non-biopsy comparator studies were assessed in exploratory sensitivity analyses. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I domains and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Nine studies including 1,333 patients contributed to the OS analysis and five studies including 962 patients to the PFS analysis. Resection was associated with improved OS compared with biopsy (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.55-0.95; I2 = 52.7%), but the effect was attenuated after inclusion of recent anatomically restricted and propensity-matched cohorts. The PFS association was not statistically significant (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.55-1.18; I2 = 80.3%). Evidence certainty was low for OS and very low for PFS. Upfront resection may be associated with improved OS in selected PCNSL patients, but the absence of robust PFS benefit and the high risk of selection bias argue against routine cytoreductive surgery. Biopsy remains the standard approach, with resection reserved for carefully selected cases.

items.title: Host Availability and Host Contacts of Mosquitoes Using Environmental DNA.
items.abstract: Host availability is an important parameter when studying vector-borne diseases, especially in the case of opportunistic mosquito vectors. To study host feeding patterns of mosquitoes in the field, we integrated three sources of information: (1) host feeding, by identifying the origin of DNA in bloodmeals; (2) host contact, inferred from eDNA detected on mosquito legs; and (3) host availability, estimated via airborne eDNA using the frequency of host detection via airborne eDNA as a proxy for their relative abundance. At four field locations, we deployed Burkard 7-day spore traps next to BG-sentinel 2 traps to capture airborne eDNA and blood-fed mosquitoes, respectively. We found that mosquitoes caught on dairy farms fed most on the animal species that were most frequently detected by airborne eDNA. However, Culex pipiens pipiens fed significantly more on birds compared to Cx. p. molestus , Anopheles daciae , An. messeae and Culiseta annulata ( p < 0.01), which fed more on mammals. Animal DNA on mosquito legs via direct contact could be detected, but results were inconsistent and prone to contamination, thereby limiting the use of mosquito legs to study host contacts. This study shows that airborne eDNA is a promising method to assess the presence, and to a certain extent also the relative abundance of vertebrate animal species as potential available hosts for mosquitoes. This method could ultimately provide better insights into the context dependency of host preference of opportunistic mosquito vectors.

items.title: Prokaryotic community structure, functional traits, and potential pathogens in a multi-stage waste stabilization pond system.
items.abstract: Waste stabilization ponds (WSPs) are widely used for wastewater treatment in low-resource settings, the structure of prokaryotic communities and the attenuation of potential pathogens in full-scale systems remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the prokaryotic community structure, predicted functional profiles, and environmental drivers across a full-scale WSP system in Egypt. Forty-eight water samples were collected over one year four sampling points along the treatment train: inlet, anaerobic pond, facultative pond, and final outlet. Samples were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing and physicochemical profiling. Prokaryotic communities showed distinct spatial structuring among sampling points, with most pairwise comparisons showing strong separation (PERMANOVA R² > 0.3, p < 0.001), accompanied by sampling point-associated differences in alpha diversity, including significantly lower diversity in the anaerobic pond than in the other sampling points. Linear discrimination analysis (LDA) revealed sampling points-specific biomarkers, highlighting Firmicutes in the inlet, Gammaproteobacteria in the anaerobic pond, and Actinobacteriota in the outlet, reflecting adaptation to local conditions. Redundancy analysis and Mantel test identified dissolved oxygen, ammonium, and nitrogen species as key environmental filters. Functional prediction suggested enrichment of fermentative and methanogenic pathways in anaerobic zones, while nitrification and photoautotrophy dominated downstream. Forty-six taxa assigned as potential bacterial pathogens were detected, including World Health Organization (WHO)-priority species such as Klebsiella pneumoniae and Legionella pneumophila. While K. pneumoniae was substantially reduced (up to 77.9%), its persistence-along with L. pneumophila detection in the final effluent-highlights reuse-associated risks. This study provides system-specific insights into the prokaryotic community dynamics, predicted functional stratification, and potential pathogen attenuation in a full-scale WSP system, emphasizing the need for targeted prokaryotic monitoring and improved management strategies to ensure biosafe and sustainable wastewater reuse.

items.title: Microscopic and molecular detection of blood pathogens in reptiles from South Carolina (USA).
items.abstract: Reptiles host a wide diversity of vector-borne blood pathogens. South Carolina (SC), USA, remains understudied despite its high herpetofaunal diversity. The aim of this study was to detect the diversity, prevalence, and parasitemia of some blood pathogens in reptiles from 11 localities in SC. A total of 305 individuals representing 19 snake species (N = 164), 11 lizard species (N = 136), and 3 turtle species (N = 5) were sampled between February and July 2020. Blood smears prepared from live reptiles were examined microscopically for the presence of apicomplexans. Molecular analyses (PCR and sequencing) were performed on available blood samples from live reptiles and blood-rich organs collected from fresh road-killed individuals to detect haemogregarines, members of the family Anaplasmataceae, Rickettsia spp., and Borrelia miyamotoi. Microscopy revealed haemogregarine infections in 21.5% of examined individuals, with the highest prevalence in snakes (37.8%) and turtles (40%). PCR detected DNA from apicomplexans identified as Hepatozoon sp. and Haemogregarina sp. in 29.3% of the samples. In addition, 2% of the animals tested were positive for the presence of Anaplasmataceae including Candidatus Allocryptoplasma californiense. No sample tested positive for Rickettsia spp. or B. miyamotoi. Parasitemia varied widely among hosts (3.21-3504.85 parasites per 10,000 erythrocytes), and statistical analyses confirmed significant differences among reptile species and sampling locations. Phylogenetic analysis placed the detected haemogregarines within known clades of Hepatozoon and Haemogregarina. These results provide the first comprehensive survey of blood pathogens, including parasites, in reptiles from SC and highlight substantial variation in infection patterns among taxa and localities.

items.title: A candidate IMS framework for local-systemic regulation and multiorgan protection by rhubarb in sepsis.
items.abstract: Ethnopharmacological relevance Rhubarb has traditionally been used to clear heat and remove toxins, dispel blood stasis, and promote blood circulation. Its traditional oral use and bowel-purging properties provide ethnopharmacological clues for exploring links of local-systemic regulation in sepsis. Aim of the study To examine candidate intermediate substances (IMS) in local-systemic regulation and multiorgan protection by rhubarb and representative anthraquinones, and propose a testable framework from an indirect pharmacology perspective. Materials and methods For this narrative review, PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure and Google Scholar were searched through October 12, 2026. Evidence on emodin, rhein, aloe-emodin and chrysophanol was synthesized alongside traditional use, pharmacokinetics, safety and clinical findings. IMS links were appraised by mechanistic support; exploratory protein-protein interaction network analysis and molecular docking were performed. Results Preclinical studies showed modulation of inflammation, immunity, oxidative stress and coagulation alongside reduced injury across multiple organs. Within the IMS framework, soluble mediators and immune cells represent candidate signal-transmitting links, whereas barrier integrity and microbial ecology regulate conditions for generating and propagating injurious stimuli. Exploratory network analysis prioritized candidates including AKT1, while docking suggested potential anthraquinone-protein interactions. Conclusions The candidate IMS framework offers a testable explanation for local-systemic links underlying multiorgan protection by rhubarb and its representative anthraquinones in sepsis. Translation requires standardized formulations, exposure characterization, functional mediator validation and clinical evaluation of benefit and safety alongside standard care.

items.title: Atmospheric Deposition and Soil-profile Accumulation of Heavy Metals in a Non-ferrous Smelting Region of Southern Hunan, China.
items.abstract: Atmospheric deposition is an important pathway of metal inputs to agricultural soils around smelters, but its correspondence with soil-profile distributions remains insufficiently resolved. This study combined 20 months of bulk deposition monitoring at five sites with soil-profile sampling at four sites in November 2023 and November 2024 in southern Hunan, China. Nine heavy metal(loid)s were quantified in 100 deposition samples and 40 soil samples spanning 0-100 cm. Enrichment factors (EFs), principal component analysis (PCA), linear regression, and conditional health risk screening were applied. Zn, Pb, and As accounted for 77.55% of the deposited metal load. Fluxes varied among months and generally decreased with distance, particularly for As, Cd, Cu, and Pb. Soil profiles displayed element- and site-specific vertical patterns, including As and Pb surface enrichment and subsurface maxima for Cu, Ni, Sb, and Zn. Cd showed the highest mean EFs (29.75-123.10), followed by Sb, while PCA identified a recurring As-Pb-Sb association at D1-D3. Pb deposition flux was positively associated with topsoil Pb concentration (r = 0.91). Under the conditional D1 scenario, total hazard indices were 4.46 × 10 -2 and 4.80 × 10 -3 , and total cancer risks were 6.28 × 10 -7 and 2.70 × 10 -7 for children and adults, respectively. Ingestion dominated the modeled risk contributions. These findings support seasonal emission control, depth-resolved soil monitoring, and targeted exposure characterization in smelting-affected areas.

items.title: Effects of Tidal Processes on Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Distribution and Occurrence in a Tidal River.
items.abstract: Tidal rivers are influenced by periodic hydrodynamic processes that affect contaminant transport and distribution. However, studies on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in these environments remain limited. In this study, the Mulan River was selected as a case study to investigate PFAS occurrence and evaluate the influence of tidal processes on their distribution. PFAS were widely detected, with ∑PFAS concentrations ranging from 4.27 to 23.0 ng/L. Perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA), perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), and perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) were the dominant compounds. ∑PFAS concentrations in both surface and bottom waters were significantly higher during ebb tide than during flood tide. The composition of PFAS also varied between tidal phases, with a higher relative contribution of long-chain PFAS during ebb tide and short-chain PFAS during flood tide. Under the same tidal conditions, ∑PFAS concentrations did not differ significantly among sampling sites along the river or between surface and bottom waters. Salinity-related water quality parameters were correlated with PFAS concentrations, particularly for long-chain PFAS. The ecological risk assessment indicated that PFAS posed negligible ecological risks to both freshwater and saltwater organisms. This study provides insights into PFAS distribution in tidal rivers and its potential relationship with tidal processes.

items.title: Exploring the occurrence of microplastic translocation in marine vertebrates with guidelines for harmonisation.
items.abstract: Plastic pollution is a major global issue due to its pervasiveness in marine ecosystems. Microplastics (MPs; plastic < 5mm in size) are ubiquitous and persistent within these environments and can enter marine organisms via three primary exposure routes - ingestion (direct and indirect), inhalation, and dermal contact. While the presence of MPs in the gastrointestinal tract, lungs, gills, and skin as a result of these routes is well documented, movement of MPs to other organs and tissues following uptake - known as translocation - remains poorly understood, particularly in marine vertebrates (fish, pinnipeds, cetaceans, elasmobranchs, seabirds, and sea turtles). Here we conducted a systematic review of scientific literature to understand which taxa and organ systems MP translocation occurs in and to identify knowledge gaps and future directions. We use the term "putative translocation" to recognise that detection of MPs in distal tissues or organs does not necessarily demonstrate movement of particles between compartments, but may provide evidence consistent with translocation. Across 89 peer-reviewed studies identified, putative MP translocation was suggested in all six marine vertebrate taxa, with the majority (93%; n = 83) focussing on fish. MPs were detected across a range of organ systems, occurring most frequently in the hearts and spleens of fish, blubber of pinnipeds, acoustic fats of cetaceans, reproductive organs of elasmobranchs, and muscles of seabirds. In sea turtles, MPs were detected in all analysed organs (subcutaneous fat, heart, kidney, liver, muscle, reproductive organs, and spleen). Several knowledge gaps were identified, such as understanding the mechanisms and health impacts of MP translocation. Additionally, a lack of methodological standardisation in sample processing, contamination control, and reporting across the studies was detected. A guideline of best practices is provided to facilitate harmonisation across future studies to better understand the extent of MP translocation and the potential health risks posed.

items.title: Decoding the microbiome behind medium-chain fatty acids co-fermentation of food waste and sludge.
items.abstract: The co-fermentation of food waste (FW) and waste activated sludge (WAS) is a promising biorefinery pathway for medium-chain fatty acids (MCFAs) production via microbial chain elongation (CE). However, optimizing this process is hindered by a limited understanding of the active syntrophic networks within mixed cultures. This study elucidates the microbial drivers of lactate-based CE under varied substrate pretreatments and feeding regimes without chemical additives. A multi-level molecular approach, integrating FISH, qPCR/RT-qPCR of the functional BCoAT gene, and high-throughput sequencing (Illumina and Oxford Nanopore Technologies) of both DNA and cDNA, was deployed to map the active transcriptionally engaged microbiome. The results revealed a marked divergence between genomic potential and metabolic activity: while Actinobacteria (Olsenella) dominated the DNA profile, Firmicutes drove the active metabolic profile (cDNA). Increasing the feeding frequency to five events per weekimposed a strong selective pressure that enriched and transcriptionally activated specialized chain-elongating specialists, particularly Caproiciproducens, yielding the highest caproate yield (45.0 ± 3.1 g kg -1 VS). Conversely, raw feed configurations maintained high alpha-diversity via microbial immigration; however, the system exhibited robust functional redundancy that buffered overall reactor performance. Tracing the BCoAT gene revealed an average sevenfold increase in cDNA expression compared to DNA, confirming the up-regulation of the reverse β-oxidation pathway under high-frequency feeding regimes. In conclusion, this study demonstrates that tailored feeding regimes serve as effective operational levers to manipulate microbiome ecology, offering crucial guidelines for the scalable and predictable production of bio-based chemicals.

items.title: Patient-derived gastric adenocarcinoma cultures reveal heterogeneous metabolic response to lysosomal inhibition by Bafilomycin A1.
items.abstract: Background and purpose Gastric adenocarcinoma exhibits substantial inter-patient heterogeneity that limits therapeutic efficacy. Pharmacological inhibition of lysosomal function is a promising anticancer strategy but patient-derived gastric cancer responsiveness to lysosome-targeting agents is unknown. This study investigated the pharmacological response of patient-derived gastric tumor cultures to lysosomal inhibition induced by the V-ATPase inhibitor Bafilomycin A1 (BafA1). Experimental approach Primary cultures were established from surgically resected gastric adenocarcinomas and exposed to increasing concentrations of the lysosomal V-ATPase inhibitor BafA1 for 24, 48, and 72 h. Metabolic activity was assessed using the MTT assay, and morphological characteristics were evaluated by Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) staining. Key results BafA1 exposure was associated with heterogeneous and, in some cultures, non-monotonic changes in relative MTT activity, with the largest mean reduction observed after 72 h. At 10 μM, mean metabolic activity decreased from 85.9 ± 11.9% of control after 24 h to 34.9 ± 1.4% after 72 h. Marked inter-patient variability was detected, with individual cultures displaying distinct temporal patterns of MTT response to BafA1 exposure for lysosomal inhibition. PAS staining revealed considerable morphological diversity, including spindle-shaped cultures with predominantly intracellular PAS positivity and cultures characterized by abundant extracellular PAS-positive material. The observed variation in MTT responses occurred alongside morphological differences among the cultures; however, the limited sample size and incomplete characterization of cellular composition preclude conclusions regarding associations between morphology and pharmacological response. Conclusions and implications Patient-derived gastric tumor cultures exhibited heterogeneous changes in relative MTT metabolic activity following BafA1 exposure, alongside distinct morphological characteristics. These preliminary findings suggest that patient-derived cultures may provide a useful exploratory model for investigating responses to lysosome-targeting compounds. However, differences in cellular composition may have contributed to the observed variability. Further studies involving independent experimental replication, detailed cellular characterization, and complementary functional assays are required to establish the reproducibility and biological significance of these responses.

items.title: Single-cell genomics reveals genome streamlining and functional traits in dominant uncultured marine protists.
items.abstract: Marine protists are key players in marine ecosystems, yet a large fraction, particularly among the smallest taxa, belongs to uncultured lineages lacking genomic data, limiting our understanding of their ecology and evolution. Beyond determining their gene repertoires, genomic information is essential to reveal how genomes are organized. Features such as genome size, GC content, and structural gene architecture represent physical constraints that shape evolutionary fitness and adaptability in marine environments. Here, we present a genomic catalog of 147 marine picoplanktonic protist species, greatly expanding the genomic representation of uncultured and ecologically relevant lineages through a single-cell approach. This dataset enables refined phylogenomic placement of previously uncharacterized marine eukaryotes, including abundant marine protistan players as well as a few species belonging to novel or poorly known groups that are crucial for resolving deep questions in eukaryotic evolution. We uncover pronounced genome streamlining in ecologically successful lineages, coupled with extensive, mostly lineage-specific functional adaptations. At a broader scale, we identify functional traits enriched independently across several marine eukaryotic lineages, including genes involved in complex carbohydrate degradation in heterotrophic organisms and the presence of polyketide synthases. Together, these results provide a framework for investigating the genomic drivers and molecular mechanisms behind the ecological success of marine eukaryotic microbes.

items.title: Structural basis of plastid Mg2+ transport by the magnesium channel MGT10 in Arabidopsis.
items.abstract: Magnesium ions (Mg 2+ ) are vital for photosynthesis, serving as central metal ions in chlorophyll molecules and activating RuBisCO. MGT10 is the only member of the CorA/MRS2 superfamily bound to the chloroplast envelope membrane, where it mediates Mg 2+ uptake and homeostasis in chloroplasts. Despite its importance, the mechanism of MGT10-mediated Mg 2+ transport remains unclear. Here, we report cryoelectron microscopy structures of Arabidopsis MGT10 in two conformations, along with functional characterizations. MGT10 assembles into a homopentameric structure with a central tunnel connecting the transmembrane and soluble domains. A constriction ring consisting of five conserved arginine residues arranged asymmetrically in the tunnel is crucial for Mg 2+ conduction. Our structures reveal an unexpected gating mechanism involving a conformational transition from a symmetric closed state to an asymmetric, putatively open state. In addition, we identified an intramolecular disulfide bond within each soluble domain as a unique structural feature of MGT10. Structural and functional analyses show that this disulfide bond is required for MGT10's structural integrity and for regulating its function in photosynthesis. Taken together, our findings provide insights into Mg 2+ transport and regulatory mechanisms of MGT10 in chloroplasts.

items.title: Vegetation decay enhances terrestrial nitrous acid emissions through nitrate reduction.
items.abstract: Photolysis of nitrous acid (HONO) drives ozone and secondary aerosol formation, yet its sources remain poorly constrained. We identify HONO emissions from decaying aboveground plant residues as a previously overlooked plant-derived component of terrestrial HONO emissions. Field observations and dual-isotope ( 15 N- 18 O) tracing reveal that HONO arises mainly from nitrate reduction within decomposing plants. We integrated global datasets on vegetation nitrate, litter decomposition, soil, and climate to estimate HONO emissions from vegetation decay at 1.1 ± 0.1 Tg N y -1 . This substantially narrows the long-standing uncertainty in HONO budget. This plant-mediated pathway extends the soil-atmosphere paradigm to soil-plant-atmosphere framework. Moreover, we identify emission hotspots and drivers, assess their climate-driven shifts, and propose region-specific mitigation strategies. These findings uncover a missing link between terrestrial nitrogen cycling and atmospheric reactivity, highlighting biogeochemical controls on air quality.

items.title: A herbivore-induced plant volatile facilitates group foraging in locusts.
items.abstract: Plants have evolved sophisticated defense strategies against herbivory, often releasing volatile compounds upon attack to deter further feeding. Here, we demonstrate the induced volatile S-linalool promotes phase- and stage-specific group foraging in the migratory locust ( Locusta migratoria ). We show that S-linalool, a volatile whose emission increases more than 10-fold following damage by gregarious nymphs, acts as a potent attractant that drives other nymphs to aggregate and feed on previously attacked rice plants. Mechanistically, we identified the olfactory receptor LmOR49 that detects S-linalool and used genome editing to make this receptor nonfunctional, thereby abolishing both electrophysiological responses and behavioral attraction. We also inactivated rice genes required for S-linalool biosynthesis, abolishing its emission, rendering plants unattractive, and disrupting locust feeding preference. Although feeding on previously attacked plants provides no detectable direct fitness benefit under our experimental conditions, prior locust feeding suppresses the accumulation of deterrent metabolites, potentially increasing plant palatability for subsequent feeding. S-linalool thus serves as an olfactory cue that guides gregarious nymphs toward previously attacked, more palatable plants. Collectively, these findings uncover a comprehensive mechanism whereby a plant defense volatile is exploited by an insect herbivore to promote group foraging, broadening our understanding of plant-insect interactions and suggesting molecular targets for locust control.

items.title: Reinforcement learning-guided Dandelion Optimizer for techno-economic optimisation of PV-PEM hydrogen production systems.
items.abstract: Photovoltaic-proton exchange membrane (PV-PEM) hydrogen production involves strong interactions among PV generation, electrical matching, electrolyser operation, thermal regulation, hydrogen storage, and lifecycle cost. This study develops a reinforcement learning-guided Dandelion Optimizer (RL_DO) for the constrained techno-economic optimisation of a PV-PEM hydrogen production system. Reinforcement learning is used as a behavioural decision layer to regulate the rising, descending, and landing stages of the original Dandelion Optimizer according to the current population state, while retaining the original search operators and the prescribed function evaluation budget. RL_DO is evaluated using the CEC2017 benchmark suite, nine constrained engineering design problems, and an 11-variable PV-PEM design case. In the PV-PEM application, the mean unpenalised levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) decreases from 6.0455 USD kg-1 H2 for DO to 5.9982 USD kg-1 H2 for RL_DO. The standard deviation decreases from 0.0696 to 0.0310, and the feasibility rate increases from 63.33% to 86.67% over 30 runs. The best feasible RL_DO design gives an LCOH of 5.9813 USD kg-1 H2 and annual hydrogen production of 604.43 kg yr-1. The sensitivity analysis shows that PEM electrolyser CAPEX, PV CAPEX, and the discount rate have the largest effects on LCOH within the ranges examined. The results indicate that the economic performance of the studied PV-PEM system depends on the combined effects of system sizing, operating conditions, electrical matching, and lifecycle expenditure. For the case considered, state-dependent behavioural regulation improves the consistency of obtaining low-cost feasible solutions.

items.title: Influence of CO2/CH4 production ratios on the isotope signature of methane.
items.abstract: Stable carbon isotopes are often used to infer dominant methanogenic pathways in wetland ecosystems. We performed closed system incubations with Sphagnum bog peat, monitoring CO2 and CH4 production and isotopic composition across incubation temperatures and over time. We observed higher CO2 production relative to CH4 production (CO2/CH4 > 1). Whereas for closed methanogenic systems one would typically expect the CO2 pool and resultant CH4 to become increasingly enriched as 13C-depleted carbon is transformed to CH4, we saw the stable carbon isotopic composition of both gases became increasingly 13C-depleted in parallel over the course of the incubations. We hypothesized that these unusual trends were due to CO2 with organic matter isotopic composition (‑25 ‰) being added by non-fractionating catabolic processes at a higher rate than CO2 reduction to CH4, resulting in increasing 13C depletion in the CO2 pool over time. Methane was formed from that increasingly depleted CO2 pool at a relatively constant apparent fractionation factor and thus its δ13C became more depleted over time as well. We developed an explanatory mass balance model which reproduced our observations and was consistent with our hypothesis. The isotope mass balance model accurately reproduced changes in δ13C-CO2 and δ13C-CH4 under conditions consistent with hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis drawing from a progressively 13C-depleted CO2 pool. These results show the CO2/CH4 production ratio strongly influences δ13C-CH4 by controlling the δ13C-CO2. Small shifts in CO2-dominated versus CH4-dominated metabolism can substantially alter δ13C-CH4 even in the absence of major changes in methanogenic pathway, potentially leading to misinterpretation of isotope signals from incubations, porewaters, or emissions if not considered.

items.title: Species diversity increases information flow about predation in bird communities.
items.abstract: The Biodiversity-Ecosystem Functioning (BEF) literature has shown species diversity to be essential for ecosystem functioning and services. Yet this concept has not been extended often to behavioral ecology, so that although it is understood that acquiring social information from heterospecific individuals is an important component of ecosystem functioning, it is unclear how animal signaling at the community level, and subsequent information flow, is related to increased species diversity. Eliciting vocal responses using predator models across 10 nature reserves on a latitudinal gradient, we first show that the species diversity of birds is correlated with signaling about predation, both in the low-risk system of mobbing and in the higher-risk system of alarm calls. After finding a similar result across a fragment area gradient in one reserve, we used this system to test how interspecific information flow is affected by species diversity. Potential mechanisms behind this effect include that species are complementary in the characteristics of their mobbing calls, so more species translates into more cumulative information, or there are higher signaling rates as more individuals are involved, or a specific keystone species is more likely to occur. This experiment varied the number of species producing mobbing calls (one, two, four, eight species), with two playback construction methods (standardizing call rate, as typical for BEF experiments, or letting it increase with species richness, as in natural assemblages). Heterospecific mobbing participation (number of vocal species, number of participating individuals), and responses (call rate, probability to call in the first minute and frequency range) increased with species richness. Construction method significantly interacted with species richness, as non-standardized exemplars showed accentuated response as species richness increased. These results match expectations that complementary differences among species in the acoustic characteristics of mobbing calls, and increased call rate, both contribute to the result. There was little evidence that the signals of one particular species changed the experimental result. The overall evidence thus supports the hypothesis that the species diversity of a community is a key component influencing the quantity and the characteristics of signaling and information flow inside it.

items.title: A novel family of polysaccharide lyase proteins are deployed in rice to negatively control arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis.
items.abstract: As the core structure of arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) symbiosis, arbuscules exhibit an unusually short lifespan, yet the underlying mechanisms remain largely obscure. In this study, a novel family of bacteria-originated polysaccharide lyases (designated chitin-binding and lyase proteins, CBLPs) was investigated in rice. After inoculation with the AM fungus Rhizophagus irregularis, OsCBLP1 was specifically induced in arbusculated cells while OsCBLP2 was expressed in both arbusculated and adjacent cells. Loss-of-function of either OsCBLP1 or OsCBLP2 resulted in enhanced root colonization, and the double mutant oscblp1 oscblp2 exhibited an even more exaggerated phenotype, indicating that the two OsCBLPs act additively to negatively regulate AM symbiosis. Overexpression of OsCBLPs significantly decreased arbuscule abundance in rice and Medicago truncatula roots. Both OsCBLPs were localized to the apoplastic space after plasmolysis, and purified OsCBLP1 not only efficiently bound and lysed chitin but also significantly inhibited hyphal elongation of germinated R. irregularis spores. Moreover, OsCBLP2 was induced in rice leaves during symbiosis and conferred effective resistance to the blast fungus. Together, this work reveals a common set of polysaccharide lyase genes that are used by plants to control both symbiotic and pathogenic fungi. It also indicates that arbuscule degradation is likely a consequence of active host defense.

items.title: Structuring laboratory directorates to strengthen national laboratory systems: A case study of the West African network of biomedical analysis laboratories (RESAOLAB).
items.abstract: The governance of national laboratory systems is a key factor in strengthening biological diagnostic capacity across the board. WHO AFRO's 2014 Guidance for Establishing a National Health Laboratory System emphasised the importance of structuring this sector around a national laboratory directorate (LD) within the health ministry. This study analyses the structure and role of these entities in seven West African countries, based on the experience of the West African Network of Biomedical Analysis Laboratories (RESAOLAB). The study adopted a qualitative approach, combining structured background research, document analysis, and semi-structured interviews. LDs play a key role in increasing the visibility of the clinical laboratories sector, centralising stakeholders and coordinating efforts to strengthen laboratory systems. RESAOLAB has also facilitated the creation of peer-to-peer exchange forums that promote the sharing of strategic documents and good practices. LDs contribute to the politicisation of the medical biology sector by helping to transform its issues into national priorities. This model of governance promotes a joined-up approach to building diagnostic capacity. Consolidating regional cooperation and developing harmonised standards appear to be potential levers for strengthening the legitimacy and effectiveness of these structures.

items.title: Species-specific patterns of use of anthropogenic nesting materials by oasis-dwelling open-cup nesting passerines, in relation to their environmental availability.
items.abstract: The interactions of anthropogenic debris (AD) with wildlife are increasingly recognized as a global environmental concern, but detailed data are still lacking in areas where this issue is more likely to arise due to ineffective waste management systems. Here, we investigated the use of AD as nesting materials by four open-cup nesting passerines in a Tunisian oasis habitat, an original agro-ecosystem with a poor waste management system. Among 326 nests sampled, nearly 60% contained AD (plastic, fabric, paper, and metal) which accounted for 1% of the weight of nest materials. Different AD categories were incorporated into nests proportionally to their relative availability in the environment, with plastics being the most common AD in the nests and their surroundings. Our results also revealed species-specific patterns of AD use, partly linked to nest size differences; larger nests contained more AD. Controlling for this nest size effect, there was a tendency for greater use of AD by resident species compared to migrants which begin nesting later. Furthermore, three species, namely the Common Blackbird (Turdus merula), Western Orphean Warbler (Curruca hortensis), and Rufous-tailed Scrub Robin (Cercotrichas galactotes), exhibited positive relationships of the amount of plastics in the nests with the availability of these materials in the environment, suggesting the usefulness of these species as biomonitors of plastic contamination in the oasis environment. In sum, we believe that our findings contribute to the assessment of the extent of human waste incorporation into terrestrial ecosystems, with a view to raising awareness of this major environmental concern.

items.title: A double-edged sword: toxic synergies of zinc oxide nanoparticles and thermal stress on the eco-physiological responses of Mystus gulio.
items.abstract: Global climate change acts as a major catalyst behind unforeseen temperature fluctuations. Concurrently, the widespread application of nanotechnology has expanded, significantly increasing the discharge of nanomaterials into aquatic ecosystems and posing a potential risk to aquatic systems. The paucity of information regarding the combined impact of multiple stressors relative to a single stressor often impedes us from getting a comprehensive understanding of their impact on aquatic organisms and ecosystems. The present study investigates the toxicological effects of zinc oxide nanoparticles (1 and 5 mg/L) under elevated temperature (34°C) over 15 days on the eco-physiological responses of Mystus gulio from the Sundarbans. Key physiological energetics, including ingestion, absorption, respiration, and excretion rates, were assessed on days 5 and 15 to gauge organismal energy allocation through the scope for growth (SfG). Additionally, biomarkers across various biological hierarchies, including antioxidant activity, detoxification pathways, lipid peroxidation, and apoptotic responses, were thoroughly evaluated in muscle tissue at 24 hr, day 7 and 15. These findings clearly indicate a significant reduction in ingestion, absorption efficiency, and SfG, along with elevated oxidative stress biomarkers and apoptotic activity on day 15. Antioxidant defence responses also showed significant alterations under combined conditions, indicating physiological disruption. The current study unequivocally demonstrates that the combination of elevated temperature and nanoparticle exposure intensifies physiological stress, jeopardising homeostasis. In conclusion, this investigation emphasises the necessity of evaluating concurrent stressors' impacts for a profound understanding of the resilience of an organism under changing climatic and contaminant scenarios.

items.title: Cumulative Effects Assessment of Offshore Wind Farms: Insights from Environmental Assessment Practice.
items.abstract: To effectively understand and address multiple development pressures on marine ecosystems is imperative to support the sustainable growth of the offshore wind energy sector. Cumulative effects assessment (CEA), a mandatory requirement under European Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) and Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) legislation, ensures that the combined effects of construction, operation and decommissioning of a windfarm, and its interactions with other overlapping or adjacent projects and plans are identified, assessed, and mitigated. This paper systematically reviews 16 SEA and 30 EIA reports, with a focus on understanding to which extent and how CEA is implemented in practice across seven jurisdictions. This is driven by a dearth of CEA research across projects and countries, and a need to establish the state-of-the-art of CEA in the European offshore wind energy sector. The findings reveal a disparity of approaches and largely qualitative assessment methods, with limited consideration of cumulative effects in some countries, particularly at project level. In some jurisdictions, methodological guidance promotes consistent and enhanced approaches, supported by mapping, modelling and expert judgements. Despite some critical and necessary advancements in assessment practice, this review suggests that significant limitations remain, particularly with regards to lack of knowledge (e.g. on pressure-receptor interactions) and data gaps (e.g. on existing and planned development details or spatio-temporal distribution of receptors). Cumulative effects also gain little attention in the measures for monitoring plans and developments. Ultimately, this paper concludes with some reflections on challenges and opportunities for improving the assessment of cumulative effects in the sector.

items.title: Executive function, pragmatic communication, and sensory processing as independent correlates of psychosocial difficulties in 6- to 10-year-old children with ADHD.
items.abstract: Psychosocial difficulties in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) are often attributed primarily to executive dysfunction, while the independent roles of pragmatic communication and sensory processing remain unclear. This study compared these domains between children aged 6-10 years with ADHD and healthy controls. Within the ADHD group, it tested whether each domain was independently associated with psychosocial difficulties. Participants were 102 children with ADHD, diagnosed by semi-structured interview, and 59 healthy controls. Parents completed the Behavior Rating Inventory of Executive Function, Children's Communication Checklist-2, Dunn Sensory Profile, and Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ); children with ADHD completed an intelligence test (WISC-R). Groups were compared using covariate-adjusted MANCOVA and regression. Within the ADHD group, independent associations with SDQ Total Difficulties were tested by hierarchical regression adjusting for demographic and clinical covariates and Full-Scale IQ. Children with ADHD showed greater difficulties across all four primary outcomes (Pillai's V = .287, p < .001; adjusted standardized mean differences = 0.91-1.43), persisting in sociodemographic sensitivity analyses. Within the ADHD group, executive function (β = .37), pragmatic communication (β = .30), and sensory processing (β = -.29) were each independently associated with SDQ Total Difficulties (all Holm-adjusted p < .001; R2 = .79), contributing similarly. In exploratory analyses, pragmatic communication was associated with internalizing difficulties, whereas executive function and sensory processing were associated with externalizing difficulties. Full-Scale IQ was not associated with any psychosocial outcome. Psychosocial difficulties in ADHD reflect partially distinct executive, communicative, and sensory correlates, supporting a multidimensional account of functioning.

items.title: Children's Perceptions of Gamification Elements in an Interdisciplinary Family-Based Pediatric Obesity Intervention: A Pilot Acceptability Study.
items.abstract: The aim was to assess participants' experiences with the gamification elements of "ENTREN-Galaxy," a gamified e-Health intervention for pediatric obesity, through a pilot single-arm study. To enhance motivation and adherence, a psycho-family, group-based, interdisciplinary program was adapted to a digital delivery method incorporating gamification elements. ENTREN-Galaxy consists of 16 sessions in which children aged 8 to 12 with overweight/obesity and their families explore the "Galaxy of Health," with each planet addressing a theme related to pediatric obesity. The gamification structure followed Koivisto and Hamari's50 framework, integrating achievement/progression, social, immersion, and non-digital elements. Children completed a questionnaire assessing their perceptions, attendance and mission completion were also recorded. Findings indicated generally positive perceptions of the gamification elements, with many children reporting that they found them motivating, enjoyable, and helpful for completing the missions and participating in the program. Participants also reported that they perceived the missions as supporting the adoption of healthier habits.

items.title: Distracted Eating in the Digital Age: An Ecological Momentary Assessment of Screen Use While Eating, Mindfulness, and Eating Behaviors.
items.abstract: Screen use while eating has become increasingly common, yet little is known about how this digitally-oriented behavior relates to everyday eating experiences. Given that screen use occurs within specific eating contexts and fluctuates across situations, examining its momentary associations with eating behaviors in naturalistic settings can provide important insights into how screen use relates to everyday eating experiences. This study used an ecological momentary assessment (EMA) design to examine how screen use while eating is associated with disordered eating urges, thoughts, and behaviors, mindful eating, intuitive eating, and state mindfulness. A total of 274 college students (36% male; Mage = 20.74 years, SD = 1.7) completed EMA surveys after each meal (breakfast, lunch, dinner) over a seven-day period. Linear mixed-effects regression models tested associations, including within and between-person effects, between screen use while eating and each outcome. At the within-person level, screen use while eating was associated with increased urges for restrictive eating and exercise, more exercise-related thoughts, greater restriction attempts, less self-induced vomiting, and more binge eating at the subsequent assessment, as well as lower mindful and intuitive eating during the same meal. At the between-person level, individuals who reported more screen use while eating showed reduced mindful eating and mindfulness. This study expands on prior cross-sectional findings to suggest that screen use during meals may be associated with reduced mindfulness and more disruptions in adaptive eating behaviors. These findings suggest that reducing screen use during meals may represent a promising target for future intervention to promote healthier eating behaviors.

items.title: Identifying subgroups of unmet needs in hospitalized stroke patients: A latent profile analysis.
items.abstract: This study aimed to explore the latent profiles of unmet needs among stroke patients and examine characteristic differences across profiles. A total of 494 stroke patients were recruited through convenience sampling between May and October, 2023. The patients' unmet needs were assessed using the Chinese version of the Longer-term Unmet Needs after Stroke monitoring tool, which covers informational, physical, psychological, and social needs. Three distinct profiles emerged: low needs group, high information-focused needs group, and high functional and psychosocial needs group. Patients with lower incomes were more likely to belong to the low needs group than the high functional and psychosocial needs group. Those with greater functional disability, more severe depressive symptoms, and lower quality of life were more likely to be classified into the high functional and psychosocial needs group than the low needs group. These findings highlight the importance of stratified, evidence-based interventions tailored to different patient profiles.

items.title: Why Reconstruct Historical Experiments? History and Prospects of a Contested Practice*.
items.abstract: The practice of re-building and re-enacting experiments or recipes from the past is generally motivated by the argument that it allows access to the tacit dimension of knowledge, i.e., inarticulable knowledge. We argue that this method is especially underutilized in the history of psychology and psychophysics, wherein the human body is an important (often, missing) piece of the material history of experimentation. Our argument is built on our experience reconstructing Charles S. Peirce and Joseph Jastrow's 1885 experiment, "On Small Differences of Sensation." This experiment was praised by Ian Hacking (1988) for introducing blinding, a crucial methodological innovation in psychology. Through reconstructing the experimental apparatus (the "pressure balance") and replicating the protocol, we were able to clarify what "blinding" actually meant in terms of what experimental subjects (and experimenters) experience and feel-a meaning which contrasts the presentist understanding of this term.

items.title: Factors influencing readmissions and bed-days for people on community treatment orders: A Victoria-wide study using linked administrative health data.
items.abstract: Use of community treatment orders remains commonplace in many jurisdictions despite mixed evidence of efficacy. We therefore investigated variables associated with community treatment order placement following hospital discharge and whether these had any effect on psychiatric admissions and bed-days in the subsequent 12 months, including differences by diagnosis. Cases and controls from Victoria-wide administrative health data were matched by age, sex and time of hospital discharge (the index date) with up to two controls per person on a community treatment order. We used multivariate analyses to examine factors associated with community treatment order use, as well as subsequent admissions and bed-days. There were 7944 people on community treatment orders and 15,872 controls from January 2018 to December 2022 (total n = 23,816). Community treatment order use was greater among single people, metropolitan residents or those born outside Australia, New Zealand and Northwest Europe. In the full sample, community treatment order placement was associated with significantly more psychiatric admissions (ORadj = 2.72, 95% confidence interval = 2.54-2.92) and bed-days (log βadj = 0.78, 95% confidence interval = 0.73-0.83) in the following 12 months. However, within the community treatment order group, cases with a principal diagnosis of non-affective psychosis had significantly fewer readmissions (ORadj = 0.79, 95% confidence interval = 0.71-0.88) and bed-days (log βadj = -0.22, 95% confidence interval = -0.31 to -0.12) compared to people with other diagnoses. While community treatment order placement was associated with more psychiatric readmissions and bed-days in the overall sample, there were significant reductions in both outcomes for people on community treatment orders with non-affective psychosis compared to those with other diagnoses. Restricting community treatment orders to situations where they have the most effect on inpatient service use could reduce overuse.

items.title: Creating a culture of research with undergraduate students: a primer for faculty.
items.abstract: As newly hired faculty members start their research programs, one important consideration is the recruitment of trainees to help advance their research activities. While institutional offices will undoubtedly have advice and protocols related to hiring trainees, such as graduate students at research-intensive institutions, offices that focus on undergraduate research can assist faculty members in creating a culture of research with undergraduate students, trainees who are often doing research for the very first time. Such guidance becomes key at primarily undergraduate institutions (PUIs), where a faculty's trainee pool is most likely composed of only undergraduate students. However, not all institutions have an office for undergraduate research. To help fill this gap, this article discusses ways in which a faculty member can set the foundation for undergraduate researchers, including recruiting and onboarding, training and differentiating such experiences to be tailored to students' interests and needs, and off-boarding as students transition out of research.

items.title: What predicts evidence-based reasoning and argumentation in higher education: study domain, study progress or individual learning prerequisites?
items.abstract: Skills for evidence-based reasoning and argumentation (ERA) are crucial to distinguish valuable from less reliable information whether students search the World Wide Web or encounter AI-generated content, such as answers from large language models when interacting with AI-tools. Discriminating "information from the internet", such as user- or AI-generated content, from "scientifically backed knowledge" requires an epistemological understanding how knowledge is generated and how reliable it is. Previous research suggests that ERA skills do not seem to develop sufficiently during higher education without targeted training. We investigated the extent to which the acquisition of ERA skills in students is predicted by study domain, study progress, and individual differences in learning prerequisites. Using a scenario-based approach, we designed a test to assess students' ERA skills evidence evaluation and drawing conclusions in a medical context. In a 2 × 2 design beginning and advanced students from medicine and physics were compared to analyze the effects of study domain and study progress. Individual learning prerequisites were assessed as verbal intelligence, medical statistical literacy, and epistemological beliefs (i.e., subjective beliefs about knowledge and the process of acquiring knowledge). ERA skills vary more by individual learning prerequisites than by study domain and study phase. Verbal skills were a significant positive predictor for both ERA skills, whereas medical statistical literacy correlated only weakly with drawing conclusions. In contrast, epistemological beliefs were strong predictors: Particularly, the epistemological belief that "facts in science depend on ones' personal point of view" (personal justification) negatively predicted evidence evaluation. Medical students reported stronger beliefs in personal justification.

items.title: EXPRESS: The Psychological Asymmetry of Big and Small Ratios.
items.abstract: Relative magnitudes can be quantified as a 'big ratio' of the larger to the smaller magnitude, or a 'small ratio' of the smaller to the larger. Although mathematically equivalent, we predicted that relative magnitudes expressed as big ratios would be perceived as more extreme because these lack an upper bound. We asked 348 adult U.S. participants to evaluate equivalent big and small ratio pairs by rating the relative likelihood of hypothetical events on a 7-point scale. Likelihoods expressed as big ratios were judged as significantly more extreme than their small ratio equivalents, and the discrepancy increased with the ordinal extremity of the ratio pair. Participants subsequently mapped seven big and seven small ratios (corresponding to geographic areas) to an analogue scale. Average scaling of small ratios was linear, while scaling of big ratios was best modelled logarithmically. These results show that big and small ratios have asymmetric subjective representations, carrying implications for mathematical cognition and science communication.

items.title: Psychological distress in rectal cancer: A narrative review across the treatment pathway.
items.abstract: Rectal cancer accounts for approximately 35% of colorectal cancers in Europe. Management of locally advanced rectal cancer frequently involves multimodal treatment. Although these strategies have improved oncological outcomes, they are associated with functional sequelae and may affect psychological well-being. This narrative review aims to examine psychological distress in patients with rectal cancer throughout the treatment pathway. Nineteen studies were included. The moment of diagnosis appears to represent a major source of psychological vulnerability. Low pre-treatment quality of life is associated with intrusive thoughts and increased emotional distress. Patients undergoing preoperative chemoradiotherapy frequently report elevated anxiety and disruption of social and professional activities. The perioperative period is also characterized by high levels of anxiety and depressive symptoms, particularly in patients experiencing altered body image or permanent stoma formation. During follow-up, uncertainty regarding disease progression and fear of recurrence remain important sources of long-term psychological burden. Several studies suggest that supportive care, patient education, and multidisciplinary management may improve psychological adaptation and treatment adherence. Although the included studies were heterogeneous in methodology and assessment tools, this review highlights the dynamic nature of psychological distress throughout the rectal cancer care pathway and supports the integration of psychological assessment into routine oncological care.

items.title: Oscillatory power and functional network coordination during graded semantic Go/NoGo processing in amnestic mild cognitive impairment.
items.abstract: Amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI) may involve altered associative-executive coordination during semantic Go/NoGo processing, but the underlying oscillatory and network-level EEG differences remain incompletely characterized. To characterize oscillatory activity and functional network coordination in aMCI across Go/NoGo tasks differing in semantic demand. EEG was recorded from 31 patients with aMCI and 30 healthy controls during three Go/NoGo paradigms. Delta/theta power and weighted phase-lag index (wPLI)-based networks were examined in predefined N2 (130-210 ms) and P3 (300-400 ms) windows, with complementary alpha/beta analyses. Exploratory frontal-theta (4-8 Hz)/central-beta (13-30 Hz) phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) and amplitude-amplitude coupling (AAC) were assessed over 0-1000 ms. aMCI participants showed lower accuracy in Go/NoGo1 and Go/NoGo2 and longer reaction time in Go/NoGo2. The clearest power difference was lower frontal NoGo theta during the Go/NoGo3 P3 window (2.00 ± 0.28 vs. 3.23 ± 0.39 dB; p = 0.014). During Go/NoGo1 P3-window NoGo trials, aMCI showed nominally lower theta-network global efficiency and clustering and longer characteristic path length (p = 0.008-0.010); Group × Task interactions were not significant. Exploratory Go/NoGo2 NoGo PAC and AAC were higher in aMCI in the total signal (p = 0.039 and 0.029), as was the AAC NoGo-Go contrast (p = 0.036). These effects were not significant after subtraction of the condition-averaged ERP. The findings indicate heterogeneous task-dependent electrophysiological differences consistent with altered associative-executive coordination in aMCI. Cross-frequency effects were preliminary and sensitive to ERP subtraction.

items.title: Integrated Surveillance of Bloodborne Pathogen Exposure and Suboptimal Health Status for Occupational Infection Prevention Among Healthcare Workers: A Pre-Post Intervention Study.
items.abstract: Bloodborne pathogen exposure (BBPE) remains a major occupational hazard among healthcare workers (HCWs). Universal precautions overlook individual susceptibility. Suboptimal health status (SHS) is linked to impaired occupational performance, yet is rarely integrated into prevention strategies. We conducted a pre-post intervention study among HCWs at a tertiary hospital. Baseline data were collected in July 2024 (n=2,637), followed by an 11-month integrated intervention combining training, surveillance, post-exposure management, and wellness support. Post-intervention evaluation was conducted in July 2025 (n=2,590). BBPE and SHS outcomes were compared across periods. Independent risk factors were identified for risk-stratified modelling. BBPE incidence decreased from 7.02% to 3.47%. Reporting increased from 58.4% to 82.2%, while mastery of prevention knowledge improved from 23.9% to 56.7%. Male sex, physician occupation, surgical/emergency staff, lower post-exposure management compliance, and higher SHS burden were independently associated with BBPE. A risk prediction model showed moderate discrimination (AUC=0.714). A nonlinear association between SHS scores and BBPE was verified. The prediction model combined with SHS threshold facilitates targeted stratified prevention. Integration of occupational exposure surveillance with wellness assessment reduced BBPE and improved infection prevention practices. Routine SHS assessment supports stratified prevention and optimized infection control resource allocation.

items.title: Gaps and Variability in Transition and Adult Care for Esophageal Atresia and Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia: A European Survey.
items.abstract: Patients with esophageal atresia (EA) and congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) have long-term morbidity. However, European data about access to transition of care (TOC) for these conditions are limited. The aim of this international study was to assess the current status of TOC and adult care (AC) programs for patients with EA and/or CDH. A survey was developed by members of EUPSA, ERNICA, eUROGEN, and ePAGs, comprising four domains: center characteristics, general questions about transition to adulthood, and disease-specific questions regarding TOC and AC programs. Recruitment of centers was done by the ERNs and EUPSA, using mailing lists and social media accounts. Only one survey could be filled out by each participating center. To test differences in categorical data, the chi-square test was used. Eighty-two centers participated. Seventy-two centers (87.8%) had a self-reported area of expertise for EA and CDH. TOC programs were installed in 45.8% of the centers (EA n = 32, CDH n = 13), and AC programs in 27.8% (EA n = 19, CDH n = 11). Adult gastroenterologists and pulmonologists were most often responsible for the care of EA and CDH patients, respectively. When comparing centers, wide variation was observed in the content of the programs. This study reveals that fewer than half of European centers have TOC or AC programs for EA and CDH patients, with significant variation in their implementation. Standardized, multidisciplinary TOC and AC programs are needed to improve long-term care for these patients. III.

items.title: Strengthening public health research on urban green and blue space interventions: the GIFT framework for theory development.
items.abstract: Urban green and blue space (UGBS) interventions are increasingly promoted as strategies to improve population health and reduce health inequities. Yet the evidence needed to guide policy and practice remains difficult to interpret because evaluations often report mixed findings, with limited understanding of how and why health effects vary. This partly reflects a lack of explicit programme theory specifying how interventions are expected to generate health outcomes, and why effects might differ across population groups and contexts. Without a robust, evidence-informed understanding of how interventions produce effects, policy and practice might rely on insufficiently tested assumptions about expected health benefits from UGBS interventions. In this Viewpoint, we introduce the green and blue space intervention framework for theory development (GIFT), which supports the development of programme theory for UGBS intervention studies. GIFT was developed through a survey, workshop, and iterative feedback involving 25 international researchers. It provides guiding questions covering intervention components, pathways and mechanisms, population variation, contextual conditions, outcomes, and timescales. By providing a shared approach to articulating how UGBS interventions are expected to work, GIFT can support more theory-informed evaluations, improve interpretation of findings, strengthen judgements about transferability, and generate more actionable evidence for effective and equitable urban green and blue space interventions.

items.title: Brain insulin resistance in the development of obesity and type 2 diabetes: temporal trajectories in humans.
items.abstract: Brain insulin resistance might promote dysregulated eating and impaired systemic metabolism. This Review addresses the central question of temporality-whether brain insulin resistance precedes peripheral insulin resistance. We summarise human approaches to quantify brain insulin resistance and scalable biomarkers anchored to imaging-defined phenotypes. Across the metabolic continuum, alterations appear to emerge early in hypothalamic and mesolimbic systems and are modified by sex and metabolic health. Functional neuroimaging readouts often shift after modest lifestyle or pharmacological interventions, whereas insulin-stimulated brain glucose uptake might require more sustained systemic change. Evidence of hypothalamic gliosis suggests that inflammatory responses could link metabolic stress to impaired brain insulin action. Collectively, the data are consistent with a trajectory from diet-sensitive central alterations to later bidirectional reinforcement of central and peripheral insulin resistance, accelerating progression towards metabolic disease. GLP-1 receptor agonists, GLP-1/GIP dual agonists, and emerging multi-agonists may engage overlapping circuits, raising the possibility that part of their benefit arises from restoring, bypassing, or compensating for impaired brain insulin action.

items.title: Drought tolerance-enhancing fungal pathogens reprogram plant cell identity through mRNA turnover.
items.abstract: The co-occurrence of drought stress and pathogen infections, intensified by climate change, poses a major challenge in plant science. Wilt pathogens that colonize water-conducting plant tissues can aggravate the problem. Whereas Verticillium dahliae infections typically trigger wilt symptoms resulting from xylem occlusion, its relative V. longisporum induces formation of new tracheary elements. This developmental reprogramming associates with altered drought responses. Here, we identify a Verticillium protein, TRANSDIFFERENTIATION EFFECTOR (TRADE), which stimulates conversion of plant cells into tracheary elements. TRADE associates with the plant protein VARICOSE (VCS), a conserved component of the mRNA turnover machinery in plants and metazoans. This is accompanied by SUCROSE NON-FERMENTING 1 (SNF1)-related protein kinase (SRK)-dependent phosphorylation and dysfunction of VCS, altering the abundance of mRNAs regulating xylem differentiation, including WOUND INDUCED DEDIFFERENTIATION 1, a key transcription factor in tissue regeneration. Our findings reveal how a single pathogen effector hijacks cell fate and promotes ectopic xylem formation.

items.title: The effect of a multimodal non-pharmacological intervention among community-dwelling people with dementia: The Dementzia Bizitzen program.
items.abstract: Multimodal non-pharmacological interventions (MNPIs) have been shown to be effective in mitigating cognitive decline. In this study, we designed an innovative, person-centered MNPI program called Dementzia Bizitzen, and implemented it among community-dwelling people with dementia (PwD). A total of 35 PwD were initially enrolled in the study, and 26 were included in the final analyses due to attrition. All participants attended MNPI sessions three times per week over a 12-week period. Sessions were divided into three parts: Mugitzen (physical exercise training), Sentitzen (sensory, emotional, and activities of daily living [ADL] training), and Gogoratzen (cognitive training). Cognitive (MEC, WAIS-IV Digit Span), psychological (QoL-AD, MBCL), and physical variables (6MWT, TUG, FallSkip, SPPB, LBI) were assessed at baseline and post-intervention. The program was well received, with an attendance rate of over 74%. Findings indicated that Dementzia Bizitzen effectively stabilized cognitive function, behavioral status, quality of life, and performance in the instrumental activities of daily living, while also enhancing gait speed and reducing the risk of falls and frailty (p < 0.05). These findings may help inform future clinical practice and support the use of MNPIs as an intervention method for improving the treatment of community-dwelling PwD.
