items.title: Covid-19 orphans and their torrent of prolonged grief: Needed actions for now and learned lessons for future pandemics.
items.abstract: COVID-19 orphans are vulnerable to prolonged, unresolved grief. This study aimed to identify prolonged grief symptoms and their determinants in this population. Orphans under 18-year-old were identified in Fars province, Iran. The Inventory of Prolonged Grief for Children (IPGC, ages 8-12) and Adolescents (IPG-A, ages 13-18) were administered (maximum score = 90). Data were expressed as mean ± standard deviation (SD) to provide an approximate estimate of the severity of probable prolonged grief disorder (PGD) cases. Risk factors were examined using univariable and linear regression analyses in SPSS version 25. 183 orphans (103 females, 56.3%; 80 males, 43.7%); with mean age 12.6 ± 3.1 years and father-to-mother loss ratio 1.7 participated in this study. Mean IPG-C score was 60.6 ± 15.4, and IPG-A was 58.9 ± 15.5. Approximately 16% and 2.5% of the participants in each group were estimated to have moderate and severe symptoms of PGD, respectively. Yearning ("I would like to be with him/her" for children; "I long for him/her" for adolescents) was the most prominent symptom across age groups. In children, shorter time since parental death (B = -0.4, CI [-1.3, -0.2], p-value = 0.004) and in adolescents, educational failure (B = 0.2, CI [0.8, 10.9], p-value = 0.02) and worse economic status of the family (B = 0.3, [4.0, 17.7], p-value = 0.002) were the significant determinants of the probable prolonged grief. Despite the declared ending of COVID-19 pandemic, prolonged grief persists among most orphans. Nationwide advocacy and guideline-based interventions are urgently needed for this vulnerable group and for future pandemics or crises.

items.title: Associations of affective temperament and bedtime mobile phone use with purpose in life.
items.abstract: Purpose in life (PIL) is a psychological construct that contributes toward positive well-being. This study aimed to examine the association of affective temperaments and bedtime mobile phone use with purpose in life in healthy middle-aged participants. As an opt-out study, we used the dataset of 130 participants. In the present study, we excluded 22 male subjects and focused our analysis on 108 female subjects to mitigate gender-related heterogeneity, given the significantly smaller male sample size. Multiple regression analyses using the forced entry method were conducted for PIL scores as dependent factor, with age and affective temperament scores as independent factors in model 1, adding bedtime mobile phone use as independent factor in model 2, the association was adjusted by the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD) scores in model 3, finally the association was further adjusted by total sleep time and physical activity in model 4. In the final model 4, depressive temperament, irritable temperament and bedtime mobile phone use were significantly and negatively associated with PIL, whereas hyperthymic temperament was positively associated with PIL. In conclusion, these findings suggest that depressive temperament, irritable temperament and bedtime mobile phone use may be negatively associated with PIL, whereas hyperthymic temperament may be positively associated with PIL in middle-aged women.

items.title: Trust repair in E-commerce: How attributions of ability, benevolence and integrity mediate the effectiveness of trust repair strategies.
items.abstract: Trust repair after trust violations is shaped by how customers attribute the violation to its cause. However, the attribution process itself has rarely been examined as the affective mediating mechanism through which trust repair strategies exert their effects. In an online experiment (N = 646), we examined six common trust repair strategies, i.e., (1) apology, (2) explanation focused on benevolence, (3) explanation focused on integrity, (4) explanation focused on ability, (5) partial compensation, and (6) overcompensation. These strategies were tested in a hypothetical consumer durable goods e-commerce scenario to determine how they shape customers' affective attributions of the violation to deficits in ability, benevolence, or integrity following the repair strategy. ANOVA indicates that overcompensation was the only condition associated with effective trust repair, whereas partial compensation further eroded customer trust. Mediation analysis indicates that the effectiveness of compensation/overcompensation as a trust repair strategy is associated with the extent to which customers attribute the trust violation/repair sequence to a lack of benevolence. Benevolence attribution emerges as a consequential pathway in trust repair, operating bidirectionally: more favorable benevolence attributions are associated with higher trust repair effectiveness after overcompensation; less favorable benevolence attributions are associated with lower trust repair effectiveness after partial compensation. Theoretically, the findings highlight benevolence attribution as a key mechanism in trust repair. Practically, e-commerce firms should avoid partial compensation and consider overcompensation to repair customer trust.

items.title: Alignment between computational language models and human neural responses during language comprehension: A systematic review.
items.abstract: Computational language models have become a standard tool for studying language comprehension, but how well they align with human neural responses and where this alignment breaks down remains unclear. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, this review included 45 empirical studies, classified by primary analytical purpose into two types: Core Alignment studies, which directly match model representations against neural signals of language comprehension; and Mechanistic Support studies, which use model-derived predictors (e.g., surprisal) to test whether specific predictive information can explain neural responses. Three crucial issues were addressed in this study: the scope of alignment, predictor contributions, and boundary conditions. The included studies were appraised using a new exploratory quality checklist, the Brain-Model Alignment Quality Checklist (BMA-Q), and the evidence was synthesized narratively. A consistently supported pattern in the current evidence is that Transformer contextual representations predict fMRI neural responses during naturalistic language comprehension, while ECoG studies also provide emerging evidence for related alignment. Furthermore, layer analyses showed that the layers best predicting neural responses differed across brain regions, and that ECoG encoding models based on deeper layers reached peak performance later within some language regions. Alignment weakened or failed when the model's training distribution mismatched the test materials and for signals dominated by low-level acoustic processing. Current evidence does not establish that large language models (LLMs) and the brain implement the same computational mechanisms. Causal methods beyond correlation are needed to bridge this significant gap.

items.title: Childhood maltreatment and epigenetic age acceleration in adulthood: Moderation by obesity risk.
items.abstract: Childhood maltreatment is associated with elevated morbidity and mortality, potentially through accelerated epigenetic aging. Whether this association varies by adult body mass index (BMI) remains unclear. This 20-year prospective longitudinal study examined the main and interactive effects of childhood maltreatment and adult BMI on epigenetic aging. Participants were drawn from a cohort with documented childhood maltreatment and socioeconomically matched non-maltreated children. The adult sample included 368 participants (mean age = 30.92 years; 51% female; 57.3% Black, 25.3% White, and 5.1% multiracial); blood-derived DNA methylation data were available for 173. Participants with BMI data were predominantly overweight or had obesity. Childhood maltreatment (experiences occurring through age 12) was assessed using coded Child Protective Services records supplemented by adult retrospective reports. Epigenetic aging was indexed using Horvath, PhenoAge, DunedinPACE, GrimAge 1, and GrimAge 2. Regression models tested maltreatment, BMI, and their interaction, adjusting for covariates. Higher adult BMI was associated with accelerated epigenetic aging across multiple clocks. Significant maltreatment-by-BMI interactions emerged using the composite maltreatment measure for GrimAge 1 (β = -0.27) and GrimAge 2 (β = -0.36). Childhood maltreatment was associated with greater age acceleration among individuals with lower BMI, whereas those with higher BMI showed accelerated aging regardless of maltreatment history. Childhood maltreatment may have long-term implications for epigenetic aging, with associations varying by adult BMI. Findings highlight the value of examining how early adversity and adult metabolic risk jointly shape biological aging.

items.title: Integrating Behavioral Science into Public Health Systems: From Commitments to Actions.
items.abstract: Behavioral sciences are critical for understanding and addressing the human factors that shape public health outcomes. Human behavior plays a central role in disease prevention and response, uptake of health services, and the overall effectiveness and sustainability of public health systems. Recognizing this, the 76th World Health Assembly adopted Resolution WHA76.7 on Behavioral Sciences for Better Health, calling for the systematic integration of behavioral sciences as a core function of public health systems. At the 79th World Health Assembly in May 2026, the WHO launched a conceptual framework and indicators to guide and monitor implementation of the resolution across public health systems. These tools provide a timely opportunity for countries to institutionalize behavioral science as a core system capability, strengthen measurement and accountability, and move from global commitments to measurable action.

items.title: Illness Identity Portraits of Adolescents With Epilepsy: A Qualitative Study.
items.abstract: PurposeThis study aimed to explore the heterogeneity of illness identity among adolescents with epilepsy and to construct illness identity portraits to address the unique challenges and needs of different patient subgroups.DesignA phenomenological design was adopted.MethodsAdolescents with epilepsy were purposively sampled and underwent semi-structured in-depth interviews. Data were analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step method. The results were integrated with the dual-function model of social adjustment and portrait analysis techniques, and the portraits were visualized using word clouds and tables.FindingsA total of 26 eligible adolescents with epilepsy participated. Four dimensions for portrait construction were identified: demographic characteristics, disease-cognitive characteristics, psychological characteristics, and social adjustment characteristics. Based on these, four distinct illness identity portraits were developed: adaptive, ambivalent, vulnerable, and denial.ConclusionsPrecision interventions based on illness identity portraits are essential for improving illness identity among adolescents with epilepsy. items.title: Occupational Role Influences Physical Activity, Structured Training, and Sedentary Behavior Among Active-Duty Spanish Police Officers.
items.abstract: To analyze physical activity (PA), structured training, and sedentary behavior in Spanish National Police officers. A cross-sectional study surveyed 948 officers using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire and training items. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors controlling for occupational and sociodemographic variables. While 84.4% met World Health Organization (WHO) recommendations and 62.2% showed high PA, 31.9% presented high sedentary behavior (≥6 h/day) and only 34.9% met all three structured training components. Seniority was associated with reduced WHO adherence. Officers present an active-but-sedentary pattern. Job type was the factor most consistently associated with physical activity levels, structured training, and sedentary behavior.

items.title: Beyond symptom reduction: The effectiveness of cognitive behavioural therapy for interpersonal problems.
items.abstract: Interpersonal problems are important transdiagnostic features in the development and treatment of mental disorders. However, evidence on causal effects of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) and differential treatment effects on interpersonal problems is scarce. We emulated two treatment arms comparing modern routine CBT (nCBT = 256) with a naturalistic waitlist control condition (nwaiting condition = 431) using observational data of outpatients with various mental disorders assessed at three measurement points: waitlist intake, pre- and post-therapy. Causal forest analysis was applied to estimate treatment effects on self-reported interpersonal problems, given observed baseline variables. Analyses indicate moderate effectiveness of CBT for perceived interpersonal distress, alongside an estimated increase in self-reported dominance. No patient characteristics predicted a substantial treatment advantage of CBT over waiting. Although the findings are subject to methodological limitations and should be interpreted cautiously, they provide preliminary evidence that CBT may be an effective and broadly applicable treatment for interpersonal problems. Future randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these results and establish causal inference.Clinical or methodological significance of this articleAlthough a few studies have established causal effects of cognitive behavioural therapy on interpersonal outcomes, comparable evidence from routine clinical practice has been lacking. This study demonstrates how novel machine learning approaches can be used to approximate treatment effects using routine outcome data, thereby providing valuable insights into effectiveness across both global and dimensional measures of interpersonal problems.

items.title: Family involvement and shared decision-making in mental health treatment among Latinxs with schizophrenia.
items.abstract: For many patients with schizophrenia, family plays an important role in illness management and often involves engagement in treatment decisions. Using qualitative methods, this study explored family involvement and the management of shared decision-making among Latinxs with schizophrenia and their families, including challenges and facilitators involved in this process. Semistructured interviews were conducted with 34 participants (20 family caregivers, 14 patients) in their preferred language. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis. Challenges included feeling powerless due to the inability to compel patient treatment, limits to supporting the patient's medication adherence, and lack of family understanding of the patient's lived experience. Shared decision-making was facilitated by effective communication strategies, support from family members, the patient's trust that family members had their best interest in mind, and provider-family communication that enhanced patient outcomes. Communication was a prominent theme in the shared decision-making process. Provider support of family involvement, as demonstrated in their willingness to engage families and patients in treatment, was key to families and patients' communication and openness regarding treatment decisions. Findings highlight the need for interventions targeting shared decision-making processes that include all involved parties.

items.title: From Intelligence to Attention Control: Are We Discovering New Cognitive Abilities or Renaming Old Ones?
items.abstract: Psychological science repeatedly generates new constructs that appear to offer more mechanistic explanations of behavior than their predecessors. Intelligence was supplemented by working memory, executive functioning, and attention control; cognitive reserve was proposed to explain resilience to neuropathology; cognitive training sought to strengthen underlying capacities; and bilingualism was hypothesized to enhance domain-general cognition. Such developments are often interpreted as evidence of scientific progress, but their broader implications remain unclear. Three competing interpretations of this pattern are considered. Progressive refinement holds that newer constructs increasingly approximate underlying mechanisms and should eventually replace earlier explanations. Conceptual relabeling posits that successive constructs often redescribe overlapping sources of variance. Hierarchical integration proposes that older and newer constructs occupy different levels of explanation within a layered cognitive architecture. To evaluate these alternatives, we examine four influential research traditions: the succession of constructs from intelligence to attention control, the mixed record of cognitive-training interventions, the heterogeneous associations among cognitive reserve proxies, and the evolution of bilingualism research. Across these cases, evidence for broad transfer, convergent validity, and explanatory specificity is reviewed. The analysis suggests that hierarchical integration provides the most comprehensive account of how psychological constructs accumulate, interact, and persist across successive generations of theory.

items.title: Differences in Substance Use Motives by Religiosity and Parental Support Among Arab American Young Adult College Students During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
items.abstract: Arab Americans tend to show different patterns of substance use relative to other ethnic groups, although few studies have characterized their motives for use. Because motives can confer risk for health outcomes including substance use disorders, identifying cultural values that relate to motives for use can facilitate the development of targeted interventions. Religiosity and parental support are two cultural values that can discourage using substances for varied reasons including to regulate emotion and conform with peers. The present study examined associations between religiosity, parental support, and motives for alcohol, cannabis, and tobacco product use in Arab American young adult college students. Participants (N = 125; Mage = 20.2, range 18-23; 61.9% female; 52.4% Christian upbringing, 37.3% Muslim upbringing) completed a psychosocial survey regarding religiosity, parental support, perceived changes in use during the pandemic, and motives for using alcohol, cannabis, and tobacco products. Greater religiosity was related to lower odds of using cannabis for relaxation and sleep and to higher odds of experimentation motives. In contrast, greater parental support was associated with lower odds of using alcohol for conformity and enhancement motives. Findings suggested that cultural values relate to substance use motives among Arab Americans. Given the implications of motives for problems with substance use, substance use interventions for Arab American young adult college students should be culturally-centered and address religiosity and parental support. Institutions of higher education may impact Arab American students' substance use risk by supporting resources such as cultural clubs and festivities that can cultivate these values.

items.title: Taking Stock of Social Identity and Self-Categorization Theories: Exploring Points of Tension Between Contemporary Research and Foundational Principles.
items.abstract: The social identity approach (SIA), encompassing social identity theory and self-categorization theory, has profoundly shaped research on the self, group processes, and intergroup relations. Yet contemporary developments increasingly diverge from original SIA premises. This article identifies five departures: first, a tendency to downplay the SIA's claim that group behavior inherently involves intergroup comparisons; second, an emphasis on intergroup dynamics at the expense of (inter)individual processes along the interpersonal-intergroup continuum; third, unresolved tensions between the principle of functional antagonism and the reality of multiple group memberships; fourth, neglect of contextual factors that undermines the SIA's emphasis on flexible, situational categorization; and fifth, a drift toward methodological individualism that risks reinstating the reductionism the SIA challenged. I evaluate each trend and development and conclude by exploring ways in which we should protect, update, revise, and develop classic SIA principles to ensure their continued currency.

items.title: Sleep Characteristics and Sleep Problems in Vietnamese Toddlers with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
items.abstract: To describe sleep characteristics and sleep problems in Vietnamese toddlers with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) using the Brief Infant Sleep Questionnaire (BISQ) and to examine their association with autism severity. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 78 toddlers aged 18 to 36 months with ASD receiving care at a tertiary pediatric hospital in Vietnam, between August 2024 and April 2025. Caregivers completed the Vietnamese version of the BISQ. Autism severity was assessed using the Childhood Autism Rating Scale, Second Edition, Standard Version (CARS2-ST). The mean age of participants was 26.9 ± 5.1 months, and 80.8% were boys. Bedtime and sleep practices included high rates of screen exposure (85.9%), feeding at bedtime (82.1%), and co-sleeping (93.6%). Mean total sleep duration was 9.9 ± 1.2 hours per 24 hours, with a median sleep-onset latency of 45 minutes and frequent nocturnal awakenings. Overall, 79.5% of toddlers had at least 1 sleep problem. There was no statistically significant difference in the observed frequency of sleep problems between children with severe ASD and those with mild-moderate ASD (87.9% vs. 73.3%, p = 0.116). Sleep problems are frequently observed in Vietnamese toddlers with ASD in routine clinical care. Brief caregiver-report sleep screening may help clinicians identify sleep-related concerns early and support parent-focused guidance in developmental-behavioral pediatric practice.

items.title: Sea-fishing cultures show rare blend of tight social ties and openness to strangers.
items.abstract: Research has linked cultural differences to historical subsistence styles, but most studies have focused on farming or herding. Sea fishing is a major subsistence style, yet we know much less about whether fishing shapes culture. We propose an explanation for why fishing has received less attention-its cultural patterns do not fit neatly into the individualism-collectivism dichotomy that has been so useful in studies of farming and herding. First, we tested 1,010 people from nearby regions in Japan as a more controlled comparison. Then we tested the generalizability of the findings across 150 contemporary nations and historical records from 1,265 ethnic groups worldwide. People from fishing regions think holistically and emphasize responsibilities in close relationships more than people in nonfishing cultures (culture level d = 0.91). These characteristics are more common in collectivistic cultures and may have been adaptive for cooperation in dangerous seas. However, they show less ingroup loyalty and less outgroup discrimination (d = 1.37), which is more similar to individualistic cultures. Openness to outsiders may have been adaptive for fishing's mobility and flexible labor networks. We address reverse causality by running instrumental variable analyses using data on environmental suitability for fishing. To pinpoint fishing, we compare regions that have coastlines, some by seas that support large fish populations and others that support few fish. Results show access to the ocean, trade, or transportation are not linked to these cultural differences. Finally, the cultural patterns do not extend to freshwater fishing, which has different demands from sea fishing.

items.title: Determining the Challenges and Opportunities for Increasing HPV Vaccine Awareness in Bangladesh: A Qualitative Study.
items.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major public health issue in low- and middle-income countries, including Bangladesh, where awareness of cervical cancer and the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine is limited. To reduce the disease burden, Bangladesh launched a free HPV vaccination program for girls ages 10-14 in 2023. However, coverage remains low due to limited reach, low awareness, and cultural resistance. This study examined the challenges and opportunities that influence HPV vaccine awareness and uptake in Bangladesh. A total of 25 Key Informant Interviews (KIIs) and In-Depth Interviews (IDIs) were completed, comprising 9 KIIs and 16 IDIs, including an Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) program manager (n = 2); a Civil Surgeon (n = 1); community health workers (n = 3); religious leaders (n = 3); parents (n = 4); teachers (n = 6); and students (n = 6) from Dhaka, Chittagong, and Cox's Bazar districts. All interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis (Braun & Clarke) to identify key themes related to barriers and facilitators of vaccine awareness and acceptance. We identified four major themes and 12 sub-themes. Findings revealed a significant lack of understanding among adolescent girls about cervical cancer symptoms, prevention, and the importance of HPV vaccination. Negative perceptions among community health workers, parents, and teachers, particularly in rural areas, further hindered vaccine uptake. Religious and cultural concerns were major barriers to acceptance. Participants suggested that organizing teacher-parent meetings, school-based health education sessions, and awareness campaigns could help increase vaccine acceptance and understanding. Knowledge and perceptions about HPV vaccination varied across stakeholder groups, influencing overall vaccine acceptance. Tailored, community-based educational interventions are crucial to address misconceptions and enhance awareness among adolescents and key community influencers. Strengthening multi-sectoral collaboration could increase HPV vaccination coverage and support cervical cancer prevention efforts in Bangladesh.

items.title: Dual Adenosine-Modulating Nanoparticles for Metabolic-Epigenetic Reinvigoration of Antitumor Immunity.
items.abstract: Tumors co-opt extracellular adenosine (eADO) signaling and intracellular N6-methyladenosine (m6A) demethylation to evade CD8+ T cell immunity, creating dual immunotherapy barriers. Single-pathway targeting remains inadequate due to compensatory crosstalk. Here, we engineer core-shell structured dual adenosine-modulating nanoparticles (DAMNs) for sequential response to microenvironmental cues and site-specific agent delivery. DAMN shells disintegrate in the tumor microenvironment to release a CD73 inhibitor, blocking eADO generation and adenosine receptor signaling. Meanwhile, the cores deliver an FTO (fat mass and obesity-associated protein) inhibitor intracellularly, abrogating m6A demethylation-dependent upregulation of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) and antioxidant defense. In colorectal and triple-negative breast cancer models, concerted CD73 and FTO inhibition synergistically lowers interstitial eADO, dually disrupts the PD-1/PD-L1 axis, disables tumor redox adaptation, and enhances CD8+ T cell recruitment and activation, driving potent tumor suppression and preventing post-surgical relapse and metastasis. This spatiotemporally orchestrated platform introduces a therapeutic paradigm to simultaneously overcome immune evasion and impose intrinsic metabolic-epigenetic vulnerability for enhanced cancer therapy.

items.title: Relationship Between Thyroid Function and Glucose Levels in Chinese Adult Population: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Thyroid hormones play a critical role in regulating metabolism, and their potential influence on glucose homeostasis remains of increasing clinical interest, particularly within the euthyroid range. This study aimed to examine the associations between thyroid hormone concentrations and fasting glucose levels in a large sample of nonpregnant adults, with analyses stratified by sex. Concentrations of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), total triiodothyronine (TT3), total thyroxine (TT4), free triiodothyronine (FT3), and free thyroxine (FT4) were measured alongside fasting glucose levels. Participants were categorized into quartiles based on thyroid hormone levels, and mean fasting glucose levels were compared across quartiles. Multivariable linear regression models were used to assess the associations between blood glucose and thyroid function parameters. A total of 1411 adults were included in the study. No statistically significant associations were observed between quartiles of TSH, TT3, TT4, FT3, or FT4 and fasting glucose levels in the overall sample (all p for trend > 0.05). In multivariable linear regression analyses adjusted for age, sex, BMI, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, thyroid antibody status, and diabetes status, fasting glucose level was not associated with TSH (B = -0.005, 95% CI: -0.048 to 0.038; p = 0.818), TT3 (B = -0.003, 95% CI: -0.027 to 0.022; p = 0.841), FT3 (B = 0.010, 95% CI: 0.000 to 0.021; p = 0.05), TT4 (B = -0.148, 95% CI: -0.481 to 0.186; p = 0.385), and FT4 (B = -0.004, 95% CI: -0.038 to 0.031; p = 0.836). In this Chinese population, thyroid hormone concentrations were not significantly associated with fasting glucose levels. Our findings suggested that, within the normal range, thyroid function may have a limited role in modulating glucose metabolism. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify potential mechanisms, especially in high-risk subgroups.

items.title: International Variation in Aesthetic Breast Surgery Practices: A Comparative Survey of Plastic Surgeons.
items.abstract: Aesthetic breast surgery practices vary considerably between countries because of differences in surgical training, regulatory environments, cultural norms, and patient preferences. The United States and Brazil represent the 2 highest-volume nations for aesthetic breast procedures globally. This study evaluates differences in aesthetic breast surgery training and practices between plastic surgeons in the United States and Brazil, hypothesizing that both nations demonstrate significant differences in training, operative techniques, and surgical considerations. A cross-sectional electronic survey was distributed to members of The Aesthetic Society, Brazilian Society of Plastic Surgeons, and faculty at US-based plastic surgery residencies accredited by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME). Questions assessed implant selection, pocket choice, irrigation strategy, funnel technique, fat grafting, drain use, and mesh or acellular dermal matrix (ADM) use. Chi-square tests, the Mann-Whitney U test, and k-means cluster analysis characterized practice profiles. A total of 397 surgeons' responses were analyzed (298 Brazil, 99 United States). Brazilian surgeons favored microtextured or textured implants (74.5%), whereas American surgeons preferred smooth or nanotextured implants (97.0%; P < .001). Funnel-assisted insertion (79.8% vs 46.6%), mesh or ADM use in augmentation mastopexy (61.6% vs 5.4%), and drain avoidance (97.0% vs 79.2%) were more common in the United States. Autologous fat grafting was more common in Brazil (79.5% vs 42.4%). The US surgeons favored larger implant volumes. Practice patterns clustered strongly by country. Aesthetic breast surgery practices differ substantially between Brazil and the United States, reflecting distinct but internally coherent surgical philosophies shaped by regulatory history, cost, and training. These findings support the need for continued international collaboration and evidence-based standardization. For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.

items.title: Interpretable Blood Transcriptomic Classification of Ebola Survivors: A Machine Learning Framework for Post-Recovery Immune Profiling.
items.abstract: Ebola virus disease (EVD) survivors may experience persistent immune dysfunction and inflammatory complications after recovery, highlighting the need for blood-based approaches to characterize post-Ebola biological changes. We investigated whether whole-blood transcriptomics could distinguish EVD survivors (EVD-Ss) from healthy controls and identify candidate transcriptional features associated with survivor status. Public whole-blood RNA-sequencing data from 26 EVD-Ss and 33 healthy donors from the same geographical region in Guinea [Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO): GSE143549] were analyzed using DESeq2 for differential expression. An elastic-net logistic regression classifier underwent nested cross-validation (5 outer, 3 inner folds), with gene ranking, feature selection, and hyperparameter tuning restricted exclusively to training splits. Performance was assessed using 100 repeated partitions and a full-pipeline permutation test (1,000 permutations). Gene-selection stability was evaluated across 500 cross-validation fits and 200 subsamples, with comparisons against principal-component-only, cell-composition-only, and sex-only models. The classifier achieved a pooled out-of-fold area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.962 [95% DeLong confidence interval (CI): 0.917 to 1.000] and mean repeated-cross-validation AUC of 0.960 (95% subject-bootstrap CI: 0.926 to 0.987). Gene selection varied from 1 to 50 genes across resampled fits; a principal-component-only model showed comparable discrimination. Candidate genes require further validation of reproducibility and biological relevance and represent an exploratory, unstable set rather than a validated signature. These findings identify a whole-blood transcriptional signal associated with EVD-S status, supporting further investigation of transcriptomic profiling to characterize post-Ebola biological changes. Independent validation and linkage with immune functions and clinical outcomes are required before its effectiveness for routine clinical survivor monitoring can be reliably assessed.

items.title: Mothers Requesting Infant Formula in the Early Postpartum Period: A Qualitative Study of Midwives' and Nurses' Experiences in a Baby-Friendly Hospital in Türkiye.
items.abstract: Mothers who request infant formula in the first days after birth can make breastfeeding counseling more complicated. Understanding how midwives and nurses handle these requests can help improve breastfeeding support and women-centered care. This study looked at the experiences of midwives and nurses who provide breastfeeding counseling to mothers requesting formula in the early postpartum period. The study, conducted using an interpretive descriptive approach, involved 15 midwives and nurses working in the postpartum unit of a public hospital in Turkey. The data were collected through face-to-face semi-structured interviews conducted between November 2025 and January 2026. The interviews were recorded and transcribed word for word. The data were analyzed through an inductive and iterative process, and MAXQDA 24 was used for data management. Four themes were identified: (1) Understanding the Reasons Behind Requests for Formula, (2) Providing Individualized Breastfeeding Counseling, (3) Balancing Maternal Preferences and Clinical Needs, and (4) Strengthening Breastfeeding Counseling. Participants linked requests for formula to perceived insufficient milk supply, interpreting infant behaviors as signs of hunger, breastfeeding difficulties, fatigue, and family influence. They evaluated the mother and infant together, provided active support, and respected the mother's informed decision. Lack of time and staff, along with different practices within the team, made counseling difficult. Effective breastfeeding counseling should start with understanding the reason for the formula request. Support should be individualized according to the needs of the mother and infant, and the mother's decision should be respected. Adequate staffing, a team-based approach, regular training, and clear clinical guidelines can strengthen counseling.

items.title: Community engagement is the research: a framework for early community engagement informed by the Sámi ethical guidelines in Finland.
items.abstract: Research involving Sámi communities has been shaped by colonial practices and unequal control over research processes. The Ethical Guidelines for Research Involving Sámi People in Finland provide a foundation for ethical research, yet limited attention has been given to how ethical research principles can be implemented to uphold Sámi self-determination and prevent extractive practices. This article proposes a framework for early community engagement in Sámi health research in Finland that centres Sámi governance and relational accountability. The framework operationalises the Ethical Guidelines for Research Involving Sámi People in Finland by translating core principles into concrete relational processes. Developed during the preparatory phase (2023-2025) of a doctoral study conducted by a non-Sámi Finnish researcher, the framework draws on consultations with Sámi community members, the Sámi Parliament, and an institutional partner. The resulting framework identifies key relational processes that precede formal research activities, including early relationship-building, co-creation of research topic and methods, sustained dialogue with Sámi governance structures, and formalised shared oversight. This framework addresses an implementation gap by demonstrating how Sámi ethical principles can be enacted at the outset of research. Centreing Sámi governance is essential for respecting Indigenous self-determination and strengthening accountability in Sámi and other Circumpolar public health contexts.

items.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices of Breastfeeding Among North African Populations: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Breastfeeding is recommended by the World Health Organization from the first hour after birth, exclusively for the first 6 months, and continued up to 2 years or beyond. Adherence depends on knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding breastfeeding. The aim of this systematic review is to examine breastfeeding-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices among North African populations. A systematic search following PRISMA guidelines in PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science up to October 2025. Methodological quality was assessed using AXIS and NHLBI tools. Studies from North Africa (Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt, and Sudan) addressing breastfeeding knowledge, attitudes, and practices were included. Twenty-six studies were included: 12 from Egypt, five from Morocco, five from Sudan, three from Tunisia, and one from Algeria (none from Libya). Across studies, knowledge of breastfeeding benefits for child health ranged from 42.6% to 73.3%; awareness of disease prevention reached 90.8%, while understanding immunity and cognitive benefits was lower (12.2%-43.3%). Maternal health benefits, particularly cancer prevention, were less recognized (4.8%-67.8%). Knowledge of timely initiation and colostrum benefits was relatively high (up to 89.3%), though one study reported no participants with good overall knowledge. Attitudes showed a general intention to breastfeed, with variation in exclusivity and duration. Practices varied widely across studies: early initiation (6.2%-89.6%), exclusive breastfeeding (< 1 month -35 months), colostrum feeding (55.1%-93.8%), and prelactal feeding (42%-68.2%). Breastfeeding-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices varied considerably across North African populations, with important gaps and inconsistencies observed across the three domains. items.title: Trust Her: A Collaborative Autoethnography of Black Women Navigating Maternal Care and Severe Maternal Morbidity.
items.abstract: IntroductionBlack maternal health disparities are well documented, yet these statistics do not fully capture the social and health-system complexities of Black women's experiences navigating maternal care. This study examined the perinatal experiences of two Black maternal health researchers to identify facilitators, barriers, and lessons learned from birthing while Black and experiencing severe maternal morbidity (SMM).MethodsWe used a collaborative autoethnographic design integrating rapid qualitative analysis (RQA) and narrative inquiry. Participant-researchers independently documented their perinatal experiences using structured StoryMaps, which were summarized and analyzed using RQA theme logs and cross-case comparison. Analytic procedures emphasized independent interpretation, collaborative synthesis, and attention to shared and divergent experiences. Study methods and reporting were aligned with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) guidelines.ResultsNine themes characterized how participants experienced and navigated maternal care, including dismissal of concerns, fragmented care, delayed clinical responsiveness, self-advocacy, embodied knowledge, postpartum care gaps, emotional consequences, family and community support, and experiences with midwifery care. Across cases, participants described substantial responsibility for recognizing concerns, seeking care, and coordinating across fragmented systems, while differences emerged in timing, care pathways, and sources of support.ConclusionThese findings highlight opportunities to strengthen maternal care through greater responsiveness to patient concerns, improved continuity across care settings, and reduced reliance on patients to coordinate and advocate for their own care. Patient knowledge, supportive relationships, and relational care models should be considered alongside system-level improvements in postpartum care.

items.title: Primary Care Physiotherapy and Principles of Care in Persons With Rare Bleeding Disorders Across Europe-An EAHAD Survey.
items.abstract: In 2022 the European principles of care (PoC) recommendations for physiotherapy provision for persons with bleeding disorders (PWBD) were developed. Information on implementation of the PoC as well as data on use of primary care physiotherapy is lacking. This study aimed to gain insight into implementation of the PoC for physiotherapy for PWBD across Europe, and provide insight into experiences and needs regarding primary care physiotherapy for PWBD. This was a multinational, cross sectional survey. European persons with inherited bleeding disorders (or caregivers) and physiotherapists working at a Haemophilia Treatment Centre (HTC) were eligible to participate. Separate surveys were designed for PWBD and HTC physiotherapists. In total 214 PWBD or their caregivers from 14 countries and 55 HTC physiotherapists from 16 countries responded to the survey. Access to physiotherapy varied largely between countries. HTC physiotherapists were more positive about the implementation of the PoC than PWBD. PWBD were positive about the implementation of shared decision making and support of self-management, and less positive about physiotherapists partnership with other health professionals to inform care. A third of the PWBD visiting primary care physiotherapy experienced barriers including the need for a referral and financial barriers. A lack of trust in primary care physiotherapy was identified by both PWBD and HTC physiotherapists. This study demonstrates the need for further work to provide equitable access to physiotherapy for PWBD across Europe. HTCs need to lead in care coordination and communication and provide educational and clinical support to primary care physiotherapists.

items.title: Effectiveness and Safety of Nutritional Interventions on Taste Function and Nutritional Biomarkers in Patients With Chronic Diseases Experiencing Dysgeusia: A Meta-Analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials.
items.abstract: Dysgeusia impairs taste function and nutritional biomarkers in chronic disease. Existing meta-analytic evidence on nutritional interventions is limited to zinc supplementation and serum zinc outcomes and has not been synthesised across chronic disease populations. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of nutritional interventions on taste function and nutritional biomarkers in patients with chronic diseases experiencing dysgeusia. Seven electronic databases and one trial registry (CINAHL-EBSCO, Cochrane Library, Embase, PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, MEDLINE-OVID and ClinicalTrials.gov) were searched from inception to September 2026, supplemented by Google Scholar and citation searching, to identify randomised controlled trials (RCTs). Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data, with disagreements resolved by discussion and adjudication by a third reviewer. Eligible trials evaluated the effect of nutritional interventions in patients with chronic diseases who experienced dysgeusia. The primary outcome was taste function, and the secondary outcomes were serum zinc, albumin, and cholesterol concentrations; body mass index; and safety. Effects were pooled as Hedges' g (g) or odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Nine RCTs contributing 13 intervention-versus-control comparisons (661 participants) were included. Taste function showed a significant small-to-moderate improvement at posttest (g = 0.39, 95% CI 0.19 to 0.59; p < 0.001). Serum zinc (g = 0.60, 95% CI 0.30 to 0.90; p < 0.001) and albumin (g = 0.52, 95% CI 0.05 to 0.98; p = 0.03) showed significant moderate improvements at posttest. Adverse events did not differ between groups (OR 0.63, 95% CI 0.35 to 1.14; p = 0.13). Nutritional interventions appear safe and improve taste function and serum zinc and albumin levels, with benefits that appear more specific to gustatory function and selected biomarkers than to overall nutritional status. These findings support integrating nutritional intervention into the multidisciplinary management of dysgeusia in patients with chronic diseases. Nutritional interventions may improve taste function and selected nutritional biomarkers in chronic disease-related dysgeusia without increasing adverse events, but the evidence is limited in quantity and certainty and the benefit was not sustained at follow-up: confirmation in larger trials is needed before routine adoption within multidisciplinary care. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (registration number CRD420261361336).

items.title: A Cost-Benefit Analysis of Community Water Fluoridation in England.
items.abstract: Community water fluoridation (CWF) is a safe and effective public health intervention for reducing dental caries, but schemes only serve < 10% of England's population. Recent government actions have shown a commitment by policymakers to expand CWF to other parts of England, subject to the outcome of public consultation. Economic analyses can play an important part in informing the decision-making process and determining if CWF offers good value for money. The aim of this study was to conduct the first true cost-benefit analysis (i.e., with monetary valuation of benefits) of CWF. A probabilistic Markov model was used to calculate expected costs and benefits of CWF compared to no fluoridation, over a lifetime horizon from a societal perspective. Five health states described the progression of dental decay according to different levels of severity and treatment need. The model was populated with data from literature searches, freedom of information requests, and clinical expert opinion. A contingent valuation exercise was undertaken to value states of dental decay. Assuming a whole of England population size and fluoride effectiveness sourced from the totality of evidence, the Incremental Net Benefit over the average lifespan is £258, with CWF having a 100% probability of being an optimal public health intervention. However, results were much more uncertain, with a probability of positive cost-benefit of 60% when using more recently published UK evidence on the effectiveness of fluoridation. CWF remained cost-beneficial where assumptions on time to treatment re-intervention rates were increased. CWF has a low per person average implementation cost and is likely to generate positive net benefit compared to no fluoridation, even at modest fluoride effect sizes. Further work is required to determine cost-benefit compared to other public health programmes.

items.title: Slow Nursing in Dementia and Long-Term Care: A Concept Analysis.
items.abstract: To analyse slow nursing by identifying its defining attributes, antecedents, consequences and empirical referents, and to position the concept within nursing theory and in dementia and long-term care. The eight-step Walker and Avant's concept analysis framework was employed to define slow nursing attributes, antecedents, consequences and empirical referents. A focused literature review was conducted in January 2026 across seven databases (Medline, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Web of Science, Scopus, Oria and Google Scholar) to identify and analyse the defining characteristics of Slow Nursing. A total of 18 articles were included in the current analysis. The analyses demonstrate that slow nursing is characterized by four defining attributes: intentional presence, relational depth, attuned care delivery and reflective practice. Antecedents include organizational flexibility, nursing competence, ethical sensitivity and patients' willingness or capacity to engage in meaningful interactions. Consequences include preserved personhood, enhanced well-being, improved clinical insight, strengthened moral resilience and less rushed or missed care. Empirical referents include the Slow Nursing Tool, observational indicators, patient and family experiences and reflective clinical documentation. Slow nursing in dementia and long-term care is a holistic, relational and temporally attuned approach that supports person-centred care and may help re-humanize nursing practice within increasingly accelerated healthcare systems. Demands for efficiency and productivity challenge nurses' ability to provide relational, person-centred care. This concept analysis establishes slow nursing as a holistic, relational and temporally attuned approach in dementia and long-term care and identifies its attributes and theoretical foundations. The findings may guide clinical practice, education and research in developing dementia and long-term care practices and environments that promote personhood, dignity and high-quality nursing care. No EQUATOR reporting guidelines are available for concept analysis studies. This study did not include patient or public involvement in its design, conduct or reporting.

items.title: Utilization of Dental Care Among Young American Indian Children From the Northern Plains.
items.abstract: American Indian (AI) children have high rates of caries. This study described dental service utilization among AI children and examined relationships of social determinants of health (SDOH) with utilization and oral health. This secondary data analysis used data extracted from a randomized controlled trial of a motivational interviewing (MI) intervention implemented to reduce dental decay in AI children aged 0-3 years (N = 535 parent-child dyads). Parents self-reported demographic, SDOH and child dental service utilization information. Utilization measures between 0 and 36 months of age included: (1) initiation of dental care by age 1 year, (2) fluoride varnish (FV) in the past year and (3) routine dental visit in the past year. Oral health was measured as decayed, missing and filled tooth surfaces (dmfs) from the 36-month dental evaluation. Regressions were estimated to examine the relationships of SDOH with utilization and dmfs. Dental care was initiated by age 1 for 34% of children. At 24 and 36 months, 47% and 58% of children, respectively, received FV in the past year. At these ages, 29% and 46% of children, respectively, had ≥ 1 routine visits in the past year. Access to a working vehicle (OR = 1.79; CI: 1.04, 3.07), shorter travel times to closest dental clinic (OR = 0.49; CI: 0.31, 0.78) and stronger health literacy (OR = 1.46; CI: 1.11, 1.93) were associated with routine visits. Higher income was negatively associated with dmfs (RR = 0.32; CI: 0.17, 0.58). Participation in the MI intervention was associated with receiving FV (OR = 1.45; CI: 1.03, 2.04). Many children did not receive recommended dental care. Specific SDOH were associated with service utilization.

items.title: Same symptom, different decision: paired consultation review for teaching primary care judgement to medical students.
items.abstract: Medical students often see similar problems in general practice, yet discussing each case on its own can hide how assessment and management change between consultations. Paired Consultation Review places two patients with comparable presenting problems side by side and traces each person's care over time.Students compare the patients with each other and each patient with their earlier presentation. Three questions guide supervision: what makes the presentations similar, what has been learned as care continued, and why care should remain similar or differ now. Initial assessment, conservative management, investigations and planned review are considered alongside subsequent clinical findings, treatment experience, patient priorities, clinician judgement and the circumstances of care.A clinical knee-pain pair illustrates how ongoing symptoms can acquire different meanings as information accumulates. The educational task is to explain why an approach remains appropriate, needs adaptation or warrants specialist input, without treating referral as the endpoint or later change as proof of an earlier error. Students participate in routine follow-up where possible; records can support reconstruction when personal continuity is unavailable.The method structures routine undergraduate GP supervision without extra patient appointments or a compulsory worksheet. Its educational focus is the combination of case similarity and longitudinal care. Feasibility, acceptability and independent application of learning require evaluation.

items.title: Percutaneous Brachial Artery Access in Swine for Cardiac and Vascular Interventions.
items.abstract: Swine are increasingly utilized as a large-animal model organism for cardiac and vascular research due to anatomic and physiological similarities to humans. Although methods for surgical and percutaneous femoral artery access in swine are well established, percutaneous approaches are often preferred for serial survival studies because they avoid surgical vessel exposure and may reduce procedural invasiveness. In clinical practice, percutaneous radial artery access has largely superseded femoral access for many diagnostic and interventional cardiac and vascular procedures, driven by lower bleeding risk and improved patient comfort and recovery times. Here, we describe a percutaneous brachial artery access technique in swine that closely parallels human radial artery access. This approach may enhance the translational relevance of swine models and broaden their utility for investigational device testing and drug development.

items.title: Phenotyping of cardiac pathologies in Afro-caribbeans: a scoping review.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) claims 18.6 million lives annually worldwide. Caribbean nations are particularly vulnerable to CVDs, as by Western standards they are largely comprised of racial/ethnic minorities and classified as Low-and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs); with race/ethnicity and socioeconomics affecting health outcomes. Cardiac pathology phenotypes (morphologic descriptions) can guide targeted diagnostics and therapeutics, yet despite this, there exists paucity of literature on Afro-Caribbean cardiac pathologies. This scoping review mapped existing cardiac pathology phenotyping literature across thirteen predominantly Black Caribbean nations and the diaspora; summarizing existing data, identifying gaps and setting the stage to prioritize future CVD cohort studies to reduce Afro-Caribbean under representation in the medical literature. This review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. Four academic databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Bireme - Latin America and the Caribbean Literature on Health Sciences), and Google Scholar were queried with predefined search terms to obtain articles in English between 1990 - 2025, with Afro-Caribbeans from 13 nations or diaspora (United States of America (USA), Europe or Canada), with cardiac pathology phenotyping data derived from ECG, imaging or autopsy. Forty studies featuring 17 cardiac foci across 9 countries were identified with the United Kingdom (UK) having the most (13). Seventeen were cross-sectional, 9 prospective cohorts, 6 retrospective cohorts, 5 retrospective case series, 1 prospective case series, and 2 case-control studies. Foci included left ventricular structure/function (9), heart failure (6), peripartum cardiomyopathy (4), ischemic heart disease (4), transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (3), valvulopathies (2), cardiorenal disorders (2), and miscellaneous (10). Sample sizes ranged from N = 15 to 5329, with N ≥ 100 in 22 of the 40 studies. Phenotyping utilized echocardiography (31), ECG (13), stress echocardiography (1), CT angiography (1), coronary angiography (2), cardiac MRI (1), and transesophageal echocardiography (2). A review of literature on cardiac pathology phenotypes in Afro-Caribbean populations was performed, demonstrating paucity of large, prospective studies and use of advanced imaging, resulting in scarcity of data. Future work should prioritize multicenter cohorts, standardized multimodal imaging, and longitudinal follow-up to describe phenotypes and regional epidemiology and potentially guide resource allocation.

items.title: A comprehensive analysis of YouTube videos as an educational resource for plain radiographic anatomy across major body regions.
items.abstract: This study comprehensively evaluates YouTube videos on plain radiographic anatomy across major body regions using multiple assessment instruments. A comprehensive search using 110 predefined keywords identified 3300 videos, of which 253 (7.7%) met inclusion criteria covering the seven major anatomical regions. Two anatomists independently evaluated videos using Anatomy Content Score for Radiology (ACS-R), Global Quality Score (GQS), modified DISCERN (mDISCERN), and JAMA benchmark criteria. Engagement metrics and creator characteristics were analyzed for associations with educational quality. Mean quality scores were moderately high (ACS-R: 13.4 ± 2.5; GQS: 3.8 ± 0.8), with 64% of videos classified as useful. However, reliability scores were substantially lower (mDISCERN: 2.7 ± 0.9; JAMA: 2.4 ± 1.0). Useful videos were significantly longer (median: 729.5 vs. 369.0 s, p < 0.001). A strong correlation existed between ACS-R and GQS (rs = 0.849), with moderate positive correlations between quality scores and video duration (ACS-R: rs = 0.479; GQS: rs = 0.483). The public engagement metrics (views, likes, like-to-view ratio) were positively correlated with both ACS-R and GQS (all p < 0.01). However, creator credentials, channel verification, institutional affiliation, and upload timing were not associated with content quality. Additionally, there was no difference in content usefulness between videos uploaded before and after the COVID-19 pandemic. While YouTube provides moderately high-quality radiographic anatomy content, significant deficiencies exist in transparency and source attribution. Longer videos received higher educational-quality scores, but optimal duration and learning effectiveness across levels of viewer expertise remain undetermined. Public engagement metrics may reflect the specialized nature of the audience for these videos, who are better able to recognize high-quality educational content.

items.title: From Surveillance to Structural Accountability: A Critical Suicidology Framework for Black Youth Suicide Prevention Policy.
items.abstract: Suicide among Black youth in the United States is an urgent public health and social work concern. Surveillance, screening, assessment, and referral remain necessary, but they are insufficient when treated as the whole response. This conceptual article integrates critical suicidology, structural racism scholarship, public health social work, and implementation science to propose an equity-centered framework for Black youth suicide prevention policy. It distinguishes policy adoption from prevention capacity across seven domains: school mental health and belonging; crisis response; behavioral health access and continuity; anti-racist institutional practice; family and economic support; community-based prevention; and postvention. Eight criteria assess financing, authority, implementation infrastructure, equity specificity, community governance, reach, unintended harms, and meaningful outcomes. The framework directs attention to whether prevention is accessible, culturally meaningful, non-punitive, and accountable to Black youth and families. It complements care while giving social workers and public health practitioners a structure for design, implementation review, advocacy, and evaluation.

items.title: Event Analysis after Caries Arrest with Silver Diamine Fluoride in Adults.
items.abstract: The objectives of this retrospective analysis of longitudinal clinical treatment records from the US Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) were to determine whether teeth treated with silver diamine fluoride (SDF) to arrest a cavitated or noncavitated carious lesion required subsequent caries-related extraction/root canal therapy or direct/indirect restoration and whether 2 or more applications of SDF were more effective than 1 application. Inclusion criteria were Veterans eligible for continuing/comprehensive dental care, with at least 1 tooth treated with SDF (CDT code = D1354), a minimum 1-y follow-up time following index SDF, and were VA dental service patients for at least 1 y prior to index SDF. Multiple applications of SDF on a tooth and multiple teeth per veteran were included. Demographic covariates were age, sex, race, and ethnicity. Medical covariates included medical complexity/illness burden, prescription medication burden, and use of medications with strong anticholinergic properties. Dental covariates were the dentist's clinical assessment of xerostomia, receipt of in-office applied fluoride, and count of caries-related restorations in the year prior to index SDF treatment. Cox proportional hazards-based regression models for repeated data on teeth clustered within patients were used to allow for inclusion of time-dependent cumulative SDF treatments and to identify factors predictive of time to failure and estimate their associations with the outcomes. The analyses included 66,199 SDF-treated teeth in 20,833 Veterans. Most teeth (69%) received 1 SDF application, 19% received 2 SDF applications, and 12% received 3+ SDF applications. For teeth with multiple applications, the median time between applications was 180 d. Seventy-five percent of teeth survived (mean follow-up = 3 y); 7% failed due to caries-related extraction/root canal therapy (mean follow-up = 1.5 y) and 18% due to direct/indirect restoration (mean follow-up = 1 y). Multiple SDF applications versus 1 application decreased the hazard by 90% for extraction/root canal therapy and 98% for direct/indirect restoration, demonstrating clinically meaningful caries arrest in adults.

items.title: Pre-operative Endocrine Therapy Preserves Health-related Quality of Life in the POWER-trial.
items.abstract: Adjuvant therapies for breast cancer have an impact on health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Prior studies reported worse HRQoL with endocrine therapy than with radiation therapy (RT). In the POWER trial, patients received preoperative endocrine therapy (pre-ET) to assess tolerability and guide RT decisions. The study assessed whether HRQoL was preserved across adjuvant treatment combinations and whether HRQoL during pre-ET was associated with endocrine therapy adherence. The POWER trial participants received 90 days of pre-ET. Their HRQoL was measured using the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) Quality of Life Questionnaire (QLQ)-C30 and BR23 questionnaire before and after pre-ET, at adjuvant therapy initiation, and 6 and 12 months postoperatively. The patients were grouped by RT receipt and adherence to adjuvant ET (AET) at 12-months: +RT/+AET, +RT/-AET, -RT/+AET, and -RT/-AET. The primary endpoint was change in global HRQoL from pre-ET completion to 12-months. A ≥5-point change was considered clinically meaningful. The 73 patients who completed HRQoL surveys had a mean age of 73.6 ± 6 years, and 90.4 % were Non-Hispanic white. At 12 months, the treatment groups included 39 patients (53.4 %) with -RT/+AET, 20 patients (27.4 %) with +RT/+AET, 10 patients (13.7 %) with +RT/-AET, and 4 patients (5.5 %) with -RT/-AET. The median HRQoL scores remained stable at 83.3 (IQR, 66.7-91.7) from pre-ET completion to 12 months, with similar C30 and BR23 subscale changes across the groups. At the individual level, 22 patients (30.1 %) had a clinically meaningful decline, 23 patients (31.5 %) improved, and 38.4 % had no meaningful change in global HRQoL. During pre-ET, HRQoL was not associated with AET adherence. Although adjuvant therapies are known to affect HRQoL, receipt of pre-ET may mitigate their detrimental effects on HRQoL by informing treatment decisions.

items.title: Comparative biometric analysis in high axial anisomyopia.
items.abstract: High myopia is a public health burden and is commonly associated with a longer eyeball. Mechanisms governing ocular growth are not clearly known yet. By leveraging anisomyopia as a unique natural model, this study provides insights into the biometric determinants of ocular growth. This study compares the contributions of ocular biometric components to axial length (AL) in highly myopic eyes versus low- or non-myopic eyes in individuals with high anisomyopia. A hospital-based case-control study. Biometric data from 181 individuals with high myopia in a single eye (axial length [AL] > 26.00 mm in the case eye and < 24.5 mm in the fellow control eye), without pathological or visual complications was acquired. Detailed biometric measurements included AL, central corneal thickness (CCT), anterior chamber depth (ACD), lens thickness (LT), anterior segment length (ASL), posterior segment length (PSL), and derived ratios (PSL:AL, ASL:AL, and PSL:ASL). Correlations among these biometric components were compared between case and control eyes, and the relative contribution of each feature to AL was assessed using random forest analysis. PSL showed the strongest correlation with AL in both myopic (r = 0.89) and control eyes (r = 0.87). However, random forest analysis revealed a greater relative difference in the feature importance of anterior segment length (ASL) between the two groups, with a 53% lower contribution in case eyes. LT demonstrated a larger difference in its contribution to AL between case and control eyes compared with ACD. While PSL appears to be the primary determinant of axial length, anterior segment parameters-particularly LT-exhibit distinctive contributions between the two eyes of individuals with high anisomyopia. Further longitudinal studies in paediatric cohorts during periods of active ocular elongation are recommended to provide deeper insights into ocular biometric interactions.

items.title: Policy literacy and educational gaps in national cancer control among physicians certified by the Japanese Board of Cancer Therapy: a nationwide survey.
items.abstract: The Cancer Control Act and the Fourth Basic Plan to Promote Cancer Control Programs provide the structural foundation for cancer policy in Japan. However, the level of policy literacy among clinicians certified by the Japanese Board of Cancer Therapy (JBCT) is unclear. A nationwide web-based survey was sent to 19,059 JBCT-certified physicians and dentists, of whom 2425 responded (response rate, 12.7%). Participants rated their recognition of national cancer policy, as well as the importance of each of the 17 domains of the Fourth Basic Plan and their own understanding of each domain. Responses were summarized descriptively, including by age group. Overall, 4.9% reported full understanding of the national and prefectural planning framework under the Cancer Control Act, and 25.4% were completely unaware of the Fourth Basic Plan's overall goal. For 16 of 17 domains, more than two-thirds of respondents rated the domain as important or very important. The highest understanding category (sufficient understanding with consistent awareness) was selected more often for secondary prevention (51.2%) and palliative care (46.3%) than for patient and public involvement (20.2%), digital transformation (20.4%), cancer education (25.2%), or research promotion (26.5%). Prior educational exposure to the Fourth Basic Plan was reported by 20.1% and was more common in older age groups. Among responding JBCT-certified clinicians, self-reported understanding of national cancer policy varied across domains, with lower proportions selecting the highest category in several infrastructure-related domains. The findings may inform the content and delivery of policy education within the JBCT.

items.title: Choroidal volume and thickness associations with myopia and myopic maculopathy in the Aier-SERI High Myopia Adult Study.
items.abstract: To assess choroidal thickness and volume and their sectoral associations with axial length (AL), refractive error and myopic maculopathy in highly myopic adults. Participants with high myopia (spherical equivalent [SE] ≤ - 5 dioptres [D]) underwent swept-source optical coherence tomography imaging. Volumetric choroidal segmentation was performed using deep learning and corrected for ocular magnification. Myopic maculopathy was assessed with META-PM grading. Choroidal thinning in dependence on AL or SE, and associations with myopic maculopathy, were evaluated across the Early Treatment of Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) grid. 248 highly myopic participants with an age of 42.0 ± 6.7 (SD) years, SE of -7.7 ± 2.5 D, and AL of 26.6 ± 1.2 mm were included, with 111 (45%) having META-PM grading≥1 and 30 (12%) with myopic macular degeneration (MMD). Thinner choroids were associated with longer AL or more myopic SE, and with more severe myopic maculopathy. Odds ratios (OR) of any myopic maculopathy, including tessellation and MMD per 25 µm of global choroidal thinning were 2.29 (95% CI 1.81-2.88), 3.15 (95% CI 2.23-4.46) and 3.11 (95% CI 2.28-4.26) for the central, nasal and mean ETDRS subfields compared to eyes without maculopathy. For MMD, the OR was 2.92 (95% CI 1.78-4.81), 6.07 (95% CI 3.,13, 11.77) and 4.44 (95% CI 2.47-7.97), respectively. Choroidal thicknesses and volumes were associated with AL or SE. Thinner choroidal measurements for the nasal and overall ETDRS show increased odds of myopic maculopathy compared to the central subfield. Comprehensive choroidal assessment may benefit evaluations of ocular health and risks of myopic degeneration.

items.title: The EHRNavigator multi-agent system for patient-level clinical question answering over heterogeneous electronic health records.
items.abstract: Clinical workflows increasingly depend on timely, context-aware access to electronic health record (EHR) data, but heterogeneous institutional schemas limit the portability of information-retrieval tools. Large language model (LLM)-based question-answering systems show promise yet typically address a single modality and are evaluated on point-in-time benchmarks. We introduce EHRNavigator, a multi-agent system that adapts to new EHR schemas without supervised training and answers patient-level questions by reasoning across structured tables, unstructured clinical narratives, and temporal relationships. Specialized agents iteratively explore EHR structure and use tools to formulate cross-modal queries without manual schema mappings. We evaluated EHRNavigator on three public benchmarks spanning structured, unstructured, and multimodal questions, and on an institutional OMOP database at Yale New Haven Hospital. EHRNavigator outperformed chain-of-thought prompting, retrieval-augmented generation, and dedicated text-to-SQL baselines. Without schema-specific retraining or manual table mapping, it achieved 85% accuracy on a physician-curated patient-trajectory benchmark with interactive latency. By returning answers with supporting structured and unstructured evidence and operating across MIMIC and OMOP schemas, EHRNavigator provides a reproducible cross-institution foundation for LLM-based clinical question answering.

items.title: AI-supported digital infrastructures in human health chemical risk assessment: recommendations from a joint VHP4Safety/ONTOX workshop.
items.abstract: Chemical risk assessment is undergoing a fundamental transition driven by the need for human-relevant, mechanistically informed, and animal-free approaches. Digital infrastructures that integrate New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), including computational models and emerging artificial intelligence (AI) tools, are increasingly considered drivers of this transition. However, their regulatory uptake depends on several factors, including trust, transparency, scientific validity, and the sustainability of the infrastructures.This paper summarises the outcomes from a multi-stakeholder expert workshop, jointly organised by the European Centre for Ecotoxicology and Toxicology of Chemicals (ECETOC), the VHP4Safety project, and the ONTOX project, focusing on the application of AI-supported digital infrastructures in human health risk assessment of chemicals. The workshop explored technical, regulatory, and governance challenges associated with the integration of AI-supported NAMs into regulatory workflows. This was achieved through demonstrations of two recently developed platforms, the Virtual Human Platform (VHP) and Ontology-driven Probabilistic Risk Assessment (OPRA).Key insights highlight that transparency, traceability and explainability tailored to user needs are necessary for adoption and regulatory acceptance, as well as sustained engagement with regulators. Participants emphasised the importance of platform interoperability, and the need for targeted training for end users. Furthermore, long-term sustainability of digital infrastructures emerged as a critical concern, requiring distinct governance beyond project-based funding.Based on these insights, actionable recommendations for the design, implementation, and governance of AI-supported digital infrastructures to enable regulatory uptake of NAMs are reported. These recommendations are intended to inform developers, regulators and stakeholders advancing next-generation chemical risk assessment across regulatory domains.

items.title: The Marauder's Map: Bézier Manifolds Reveal Hidden Surfaces for Model Merging and Ensembling
items.abstract: Neural circuits are famously more robust than deep networks. This is often explained through degeneracy, where structurally distinct configurations support the same function. However, real biological systems exhibit a more flexible form of degeneracy in which specialized circuits continually adapt towards new competencies through localized changes while preserving existing function. Deep learning studies degeneracy through mode connectivity, which connects same-task networks by low-loss curves, sheets, or volumes. However, the field lacks a counterpart to flexible degeneracy, which demands more than ordinary mode connectivity. Defining such an analogue requires asking whether many independently initialized models trained on distinct tasks can be connected by a high-dimensional region of multi-task solutions. We introduce $\textit{Nimbus}$, which learns a high-dimensional Bézier manifold connecting $N$ specialists, going beyond the one-dimensional paths and two-dimensional sheets of mode connectivity work. A naive parameterization would scale combinatorially with $N$, but $\textit{Nimbus}$ requires learning corrections of only 3 interaction orders, showing that the connecting manifold has surprisingly low complexity yet supports multi-task competencies. The resulting manifold forms a navigable "Marauder's Map" that connects specialist models through a shared geometry of competent solutions. Trained across vision and language domains, $\textit{Nimbus}$ produces manifolds that are functionally and locally weight-flat: ensembles sampled from them degrade more gracefully than baselines under input and weight perturbations, with the largest gains in NLL loss and calibration error. $\textit{Nimbus}$ supplies a deep learning interpretation of flexible degeneracy, recasting model connectivity from a low-dimensional path between distant solutions into a high-dimensional volume of nearby ones.

items.title: Escape Time with Quenched Extrinsic Fluctuations in Positive Feedback Systems
items.abstract: Gene regulatory networks with positive feedback often exhibit multiple stable steady states representing distinct cellular phenotypes, allowing stochastic fluctuations to drive phenotypic switching between basins of attraction. Such transitions are commonly characterized by escape-time statistics. While previous studies have typically analyzed intrinsic fluctuation or dynamical environmental fluctuation separately, the combined effect of intrinsic biochemical fluctuation and quenched (slowly varying) extrinsic cell-to-cell parameter heterogeneity on population-level switching dynamics remains less understood. In this study, we formulate a theoretical framework to compute escape-time moments by combining the backward chemical Fokker--Planck equation with population averaging over a stationary distribution of kinetic parameters. We apply this approach to two paradigmatic bistable motifs---positive autoregulation and the genetic Toggle Switch---and quantify how quenched extrinsic heterogeneity modifies switching times across a population of autonomous cells. Our results show that extrinsic parameter variability can substantially alter the mean switching time and, more prominently, increase its dispersion, producing highly heterogeneous switching kinetics across genetically identical cells. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for cell-to-cell parameter heterogeneity when characterizing stochastic phenotypic switching in biological populations.
