items.title: Born on Rhythms: Mother–Foetus and -Infant Neurophysiology as a Dynamic System of Metastable Coupled Oscillators
items.abstract: The human embryo grows within a pulsatile maternal milieu structured by cardiac, respiratory, locomotor, vocal and circadian rhythms. Here we integrate evidence from embryology, foetal physiology, developmental cognitive neuroscience and chronobiology: we review how the foetal heart and placenta co-develop under maternal haemodynamic forcing, how maternal rhythms reach the foetus and how they may modulate foetal physiology. We propose that multimodal, semi-periodic input streams may provide a temporal reference frame scaffolding early timing abilities and autonomic self-regulation. In this view, we discuss that co-regulation may ground interoception and allostasis. Next, we formalize the mother–foetus and mother-infant dyads as multiscale systems of coupled oscillators spanning about seven orders of magnitude in frequency - from circadian cycles to neural oscillations. Within this coordination-dynamics framework we propose that healthy co-regulation is marked by metastability: flexible and transient coordination, preserving the endogenous tendencies for systems to display endogenous behaviours and to couple with other systems in an adaptive manner. The framework yields testable predictions on the link between dyadic coordination dynamics and developmental outcome. We are, quite literally, born on rhythms.

items.title: Global reporting of Brugada syndrome in VigiBase®: A disproportionality analysis.
items.abstract: Brugada syndrome (BrS) represents a rare but potentially malignant cardiac channelopathy, which may be precipitated by drugs, although data mainly derive from case reports/series. To describe the global reporting of BrS with drugs, including co-occurrence patterns, and identify novel potential associations. We used VigiBase® to perform descriptive and disproportionality analyses. The reporting odds ratio (ROR) and Bayesian information component (IC) with relevant 95% confidence/credibility intervals (95% CI) were used as disproportionality measures to identify signals of disproportionate reporting (SDR). We performed a network analysis to assess the co-occurrence patterns of related medications based on Jaccard similarity. We included 544 deduplicated cases of BrS (94.7% serious events, 30.9% females, median time to onset of 30 days, 40.8% physician-reported, 63% from North America), with bupropion (n = 50), nortriptyline (n = 40) and flecainide (n = 34) as most frequently reported suspected drugs. Among 39 drugs with at least four reports, 32 emerged with an SDR, of which 17 were not listed in the BrS website (http://www.brugadadrugs.org), such as clozapine and loperamide (often overdosed). The co-occurrence network included 17 medications, regardless of the labelled role (suspected, interacting or concomitant), with a total of 12 potential co-occurrences; fentanyl exhibited the highest closeness centrality (1.0), whereas the strongest co-occurrence was reported between bupropion and nortriptyline (Jaccard similarity of 0.31). Notwithstanding limitations related to pharmacovigilance and the complex BrS pathophysiology, we identified 32 medications with over-reporting of BrS, including 17 drugs not listed in the BrS website as well as clusters in affective disorders and anaesthesia.

items.title: Influence of regional white matter lesion volume differences related to cardiorespiratory fitness on cognition in healthy older adults.
items.abstract: Greater cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) has been associated with reduced global burden of white matter hyperintensity (WMH) lesions, a neuroimaging marker of small vessel cerebrovascular disease, and lower risk of age-related cognitive impairment and dementia. However, little is known about how CRF relates to regional patterns of WMH volume and the associated impact on cognitive aging. In a cohort of 166 community-dwelling, healthy older adults (mean age = 70.49 ± 9.96 years, 48.8% women), we investigated the association of CRF with regionally distributed WMH burden using multivariate regional network analysis of hemispheric lobar WMH volumes. We additionally evaluated the moderating role of CRF-related regional WMH volumetric differences for cognition. Higher CRF, distinct from self-reported habitual physical activity, was associated with a distributed covariance pattern of WMH volume reductions in bilateral frontal and right parietal lobes, with relative increases in bilateral occipital lobes. Greater CRF-WMH pattern expression was associated with younger age and male sex. Additionally, there was a significant age-by-CRF-WMH network pattern interaction for memory, but not for information processing speed and executive functioning, such that the higher the pattern expression, the weaker the inverse association between age and memory performance. Our findings suggest that having greater CRF may help to maintain cerebrovascular health in older adults as reflected in its association with reduced WMH burden in regions particularly vulnerable to brain aging and associated memory dysfunction. Multivariate CRF-WMH pattern expression may provide a marker of cerebrovascular health that may help to identify those at increased risk for age-related cognitive impairment.

items.title: Development of the CRS-7: psychometric properties and percentile reference values for a brief life-course measure of cognitive reserve.
items.abstract: Cognitive reserve (CR) is the capacity of cognitive processes and brain networks to maintain cognitive functioning despite aging, brain pathology or damage through efficiency, flexibility, and compensatory mechanisms. Existing life-course CR questionnaires are often lengthy and burdensome. This study developed a short form of the Cognitive Reserve Scale (CRS-7), examined its preliminary psychometric properties, and generated empirical percentile reference values. A total of 587 adults aged 18-89 years completed the Italian CRS. Scores were averaged across the life stages available to each participant. Exploratory factor analysis identified the CRS-7 item set. Internal consistency was assessed with Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's omega. Associations with the original CRS and the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) were examined. A two one-sided tests (TOST) procedure tested mean-score equivalence, and sample percentiles were derived. The data were suitable for factor analysis (KMO=0.75; Bartlett's test, p<.001). A seven-item, one-factor solution accounted for 31.60% of variance and showed acceptable internal consistency (alpha=0.75; omega=0.76). CRS-7 scores correlated strongly with the original CRS (r=.73, p<.001) and moderately with MoCA scores (rho=0.42, p<.001). TOST supported equivalence of mean scores within prespecified bounds. Empirical percentile reference values were generated for CRS-7 total scores. The CRS-7 is a promising brief life-course measure of CR that may reduce respondent burden while retaining convergence with the original instrument. Results support its feasibility and provide evidence of internal consistency and convergence with the original CRS, alongside preliminary evidence of a one-factor structure.

items.title: Neuroprotective effects of metformin on cognition, mTOR, and inflammatory cytokines in a scopolamine-induced cognitive impairment model in ovariectomized rats.
items.abstract: Metformin, with its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuroprotective properties, exhibits protective activity on the central nervous system (CNS). This study examined metformin's impact on anxiety-related cognitive deficits and hippocampal level of cytokines in Alzheimer's (AD)-like and ovariectomized rats. Eighty female Wistar rats were divided into eight groups: control, sham, ovariectomy (ovx), scopolamine (sco), ovariectomy +scopolamine (ovx + sco), metformin + scopolamine (met + sco), metformin + ovariectomy (met + ovx), and metformin + ovariectomy + scopolamine (met + ovx+sco). Morris Water Maze (MWM), Elevated Plus Maze (EPM) tests, Nissl and Thioflavin staining, ELISA, and Western Blot were used. In all groups, Metformin was administered before intraperitoneal injection of scopolamine and before ovariectomy surgery.MWM behavioral test results showed that metformin improved spatial memory in impaired groups (SCO, OVX + SCO and OVX). The EPM behavioral test indicated that metformin could improve the increased anxiety levels found in the impaired groups. Nissl staining revealed the neuronal damage in the rats of the impaired group. Thioflavin staining showed that metformin reduced the number of beta-amyloid plaques in the treatment groups. ELISA results demonstrated increased the levels of cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6) in the impaired groups, and metformin reduced these levels. Western blot results showed increased mTOR expression in the affected groups, which metformin was able to reduce. The results indicated that metformin administration prior to intraperitoneal scopolamine injection and ovariectomy surgery was associated with improved learning and spatial memory, reduced anxiety and inflammatory cytokine levels and decreased mTOR expression.

items.title: Alcohol cue-induced functional connectivity in rats: effects of age of onset and drinking severity.
items.abstract: Adolescents' heightened reward sensitivity has been suggested to contribute to increased risky drinking during this developmental period compared to adulthood. However, little is known about how age of onset and drinking severity relate to alcohol cue-reactivity, a potential biomarker of addiction. The present study investigated alcohol cue-induced functional connectivity in rats defined by age of onset (adolescent or adult) and drinking level (low vs. high; LD vs. HD), following two months of intermittent alcohol exposure. Three to six days after alcohol exposure, rats underwent an fMRI olfactory cue-reactivity paradigm, including ethanol, appetitive sugar water and neutral water odour cues. Cue-induced functional connectivity was estimated using trial-wise beta-series correlations. An age effect was observed, with higher medial prefrontal cortex-retrosplenial cortex connectivity for both ethanol > water and ethanol > sugar + water contrasts in adolescent- versus adult-onset rats. However, neither effect met the corrected threshold after adjusting for abstinence duration. No main effects of drinking severity survived correction. However, interactions between age of onset and severity were found. Adolescent-onset HD was associated with reduced prelimbic-anterior cingulate cortex connectivity for ethanol > water compared to LD, while adult-onset LD rats exhibited reduced connectivity compared to adolescent-onset LD rats. Similarly, adolescent-onset HD was associated with reduced amygdala-insula connectivity for ethanol > sugar + water compared to LD and adult-onset HD rats. These interaction effects remained significant after adjusting for abstinence duration. High adolescent-onset alcohol use was associated with reduced prefrontal and limbic connectivity during alcohol cue exposure. These findings suggest that cue-induced functional connectivity may be sensitive to heavy alcohol exposure during adolescence. While effects may reflect developmental differences, alcohol exposure, or both, they highlight adolescence as a potentially sensitive period for differences in neural cue processing.

items.title: Is psychomotor retardation associated with treatment response in adults with depression? A secondary analysis of nine randomized controlled trials.
items.abstract: Psychomotor retardation is characterized by slowed motor and cognitive processes. Although associated with greater illness severity in depression, its relationship with treatment response is unclear. We examined whether psychomotor retardation is associated with treatment outcomes in depression. We conducted a secondary analysis of individual participant data from nine randomized controlled trials of pharmacological, psychological, and exercise-based treatments for unipolar depression in primary care (Dep-GP). Self-reported psychomotor retardation was assessed at baseline using the Revised Clinical Interview Schedule. The primary outcome was the standardized z-score of each trial's validated self-report depression measure at 3-4 months post-randomization; the secondary outcome was remission. Within-study regression models were adjusted for established prognostic factors, with secondary analyses additionally adjusting for baseline core depressive symptoms and depression severity. Effect estimates were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. Among 4,290 participants, 2,754 (64.2%) reported psychomotor retardation. Psychomotor retardation was associated with greater depression severity at follow-up (pooled z-score = 0.184, 95% CI [0.059, 0.309], p = 0.004, I2 = 68.7%) and lower odds of remission (pooled OR = 0.737, 95% CI [0.577, 0.941], p = 0.015, I2 = 57.7%), adjusting for age, sex, ethnicity, marital status, employment status and allocated treatment. Findings were robust to adjustment for baseline core depressive symptoms but not after adjustment for full baseline severity. Psychomotor retardation is associated with poorer treatment outcomes in depression, though this may reflect underlying severity. Recognition of psychomotor retardation may help identify patients at risk of poorer response and inform clinical management.

items.title: The Tragedy of Sand Commons and Environmental Justice in India’s Riverine Ecosystems
items.abstract: Abstract Riverbed sand, a vital ecological component and an indispensable resource for India’s infrastructure boom, has become the site of a profound constitutional and environmental crisis. The unregulated and extensive extraction of sand epitomizes the ‘Tragedy of Sand Commons’, where developmental imperatives override ecological and community interests creating a crisis of law and sustainability. The foundational legal flaw is the classification of sand as a "minor mineral" under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957. This framework prioritises revenue over ecology, creating a systemic failure of governance and a profound implementation gap in the State's constitutional mandate to protect the environment under the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), particularly Article 48A. The Supreme Court's landmark judgment in Deepak Kumar v. State of Haryana (2012) and subsequent interventions by the National Green Tribunal (NGT) recognised the massive ecological damage caused by unregulated extraction and closed the exemption under which minor mineral leases below five hectares had escaped environmental appraisal altogether. This judicial activism is rooted in the Public Trust Doctrine, which reframes the State’s role from a mere licensor to a trustee, constitutionally bound to protect rivers as a public resource. This paper situates riverbed sand mining within the broader discourse of constitutional environmentalism, exploring how India’s environmental jurisprudence has evolved to recognise nature’s intrinsic rights and the state’s duty as trustee of natural resources. It also critically examines the "SDG Paradox": the aggressive pursuit of SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure) is proceeding at the cost of progressive degradation of riverine ecosystems, directly undermining SDG 14 (Life Below Water) and SDG 15 (Life on Land). Through doctrinal and policy analysis, the paper argues that achieving true environmental justice requires a doctrinal shift: legally re-classifying riverbed sand from “minor mineral” to a “vital ecosystem component” under a unified national legislation, and embedding ecological restoration and community participation within the legal framework.

items.title: Harnessing field investigations and high-resolution genomic analyses to gain insights into the emergence and spatiotemporal spread of a bacterial pathogen associated with widespread muskox mortalities in the Canadian Arctic
items.abstract: Abstract Populations of muskoxen ( Ovibos moschatus ), an important food and cultural resource for Inuit communities, have substantially declined in the Canadian Arctic Archipelago (CAA) over the last two decades. This has coincided with the detection of the ‘Arctic clone’ (AC) of the bacterium Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae in association with mass mortality events since 2010. We conducted multi-year field investigations during mortality events on Ellesmere and Axel Heiberg Islands (2021–2025), sampling carcass sites, potential wildlife hosts, and environmental sources. We analysed 181 newly sequenced Er genomes to reassess the clone’s geographic distribution and reconstruct its spatiotemporal spread. The AC became established on southwestern Victoria and Banks Islands as early as 2006, subsequently seeding at least two independent introductions to nearby Prince Patrick Island and spreading over 1000 km to Ellesmere and Axel Heiberg Islands within a decade. We found strong support that wolves and Arctic foxes contribute to pathogen dispersal, with possible roles for birds and marine mammals in its epidemiology. We also established that the AC can persist for up to seven years in insect larvae/pupae at carcass sites. Our findings provide new insights into the ecology, persistence and spread of this emerging Arctic pathogen.

items.title: AB-2004, an autism candidate therapeutic, drives distinct taxonomic and functional potential changes in the gut microbiome of wild-type and Shank3B-/- mice
items.abstract: Abstract The gut microbiome is increasingly implicated in the pathophysiology of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), with reports of compositional and functional dysbiosis. Microbially derived metabolites, including 4-ethylphenol and p -cresol are associated with heightened levels of anxiety and irritability seen in ASD. AB-2004 is an investigational therapeutic designed to sequester these metabolites, but its effects on gut microbial ecology in mice remain uncharacterised. We examined the impact of AB-2004 on the gut microbiome in the Shank3B ⁻/⁻ mouse model of autism as well as wild-type (WT) littermate controls. Mouse faecal DNA across nine timepoints underwent 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, diversity analyses, differential abundance testing, functional-potential inference, and random forest classification. AB-2004 induced distinct taxonomic and functional shifts in both genotypes. Alpha diversity changes were significant only in WT animals, while beta diversity differed between treated and control groups in both genotypes. Differential abundance analysis identified treatment-associated changes in Lachnospiraceae and Muribaculaceae and shifts in KEGG orthologs mapping to microbial communication, cell-wall remodelling, and aminobenzoate degradation, suggesting competitive pathway diversion as a candidate mechanism. Random forest models reliably discriminated treated from control animals and identified candidate microbiome biomarkers of treatment response. Overall, AB-2004 selectively modulates taxonomic and functional profiles without broadly disrupting microbial community structure. These data suggest AB-2004 may influence microbial pathways linked to aromatic compound processing, but mechanisms require direct validation. This study provides a foundation for multiomic investigations to determine whether microbiome shifts translate to altered metabolite profiles and host-relevant outcomes.

items.title: Matching provides rapid effective decisions
items.abstract: Abstract How humans and animals distribute their behavior across choice options has been of keyinterest to economics, psychology, ecology, and related fields. Neoclassical andbehavioral economics have provided prescriptions for how decision-makers can maximizetheir reward or utility, but these formalisms are used by decision-makers rarely. Instead,individuals allocate their behavior in proportion to the worth of their options, aphenomenon captured by the generalized matching law. Why biological decision-makersadopt this strategy has been unclear. To provide insight into this issue, this articleevaluates the performance of matching across a broad spectrum of decision situations,using simulations. Matching is found to deliver favorable decisions rapidly, following asingle evaluation of the decision options. The finding holds across a wide range of choiceenvironments. This finding offers a quantitative explanation for the broad adoption ofmatching by biological decision-makers.

items.title: Habitat-Trait dependent evolution in Poales: Unveiling Dependencies via Hidden State Models.
items.abstract: Understanding how species traits evolve across different habitats is key to explaining plant evolution. Open and closed habitats impose distinct ecological filters and pressures. Poales, comprising 14 families and over 24,000 species, have global dominance via parallel evolution in many open and closed habitats. We test the hypothesis that key plant traits (photosynthetic system, annual/perennial, wind/animal pollination, epiphyte/non-epiphyte, presence/absence of silica, adaptation to inundated habitats) evolve at different rates among lineages within discrete habitats (open vs. closed), leading to spatiotemporal heterogeneity in the evolution of families. We used a comprehensive published phylogeny and compiled trait data from the literature checked by taxonomic experts. We sampled 8,740-8,833 Poales species, depending on the pair of traits analyzed, representing the geographic and habitat diversity of all families. We applied Hidden Markov Models (corHMM) to estimate transition rates among the studied traits. Overall, the models incorporating three rate categories are better supported than those with two rate categories, which in turn outperform the ones with a single rate category. Dependent evolution was found in pollination mode and epiphytism with open or closed habitats, while the evolution of life history (annual/perennial), photosynthetic pathways, silica presence and adaptation to habitat inundation appeared independent of open/closed habitat. There is robust evidence for dependent evolution between habitat structure and key plant traits (pollination, epiphytism) underscoring the fundamental role of environmental filtering and adaptation in shaping the immense diversity of the Poales. Speciose lineages have frequent transitions in multiple traits, observed in similar and/or different habitat types, indicating that trait innovations occur in tandem, thereby allowing transitions between open and closed habitats.

items.title: Powering Up Cognitive Psychology: Comparing Statistical Methods for Reaction Time Data Using Virtual Experiments
items.abstract: Generalized linear mixed-effects models (GLMMs) are increasingly used to analyze reaction time (RT) data in cognitive psychology. Yet, whether they outperform linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) or t-tests on aggregated data in realistic experimental settings remains unclear. In this preregistered simulation study, we systematically compared three types of GLMMs – a Gamma GLMM, an Inverse Gaussian GLMM, and a novel Probit GLMM – to LMMs and the t-test on aggregated data. As the main performance metric, we introduced adjusted power, a measure that adjusts statistical power to equalize methods in terms of confidence interval coverage. To this end, we used virtual experiments derived from five large datasets: three from numerical cognition experiments investigating the SNARC effect (Spatial-Numerical Association of Response Codes), and two from inhibitory control tasks. Across 1,480,000 simulations covering 36 configurations and including RTs from over 2,000 participants, we found that Gamma and Probit GLMMs outperform LMMs and the t-test on average, with the Probit GLMM showing a particular advantage for detecting the SNARC effect. However, no single method dominates across all configurations: performance depends substantially on the dataset and effect considered, and some mixed-effects models require robust error estimation to provide adequate coverage at small sample sizes. Furthermore, a meta-simulation supported the virtual experiments approach, yielding performance estimates consistent with ground-truth benchmarks from fully parametric data-generating processes. To make these findings actionable, we provide the interactive Shiny app Powering Up Cognitive Psychology, which allows researchers to explore the results and select statistical methods suited to their experimental context.

items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Virtual Patients for Eating Disorders
items.abstract: Background: Language models can generate fluent virtual patient dialogue, but its clinical plausibility requires evaluation. Objective: We describe a locally deployed simulator for anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, and binge-eating disorder and examine the perceived realism of its responses. Method: A Unity application links a three-dimensional avatar to Llama 3 8B. A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) configuration uses Nomic Embed Text and ChromaDB to retrieve clinical material. Six raters from psychology or nutrition assessed 45 Brazilian Portuguese responses to 15 questions under three conditions: Llama 3 8B without RAG, Llama 3 8B with RAG, and GPT-4o. Each response received six ratings on a five-point realism scale, yielding 270 ratings. Comparisons were descriptive, and agreement was assessed using quadratically weighted Gwet’s AC2. Results: Mean realism was 3.81 without RAG, 3.76 with RAG, and 4.65 for GPT-4o. Observed agreement was 83.5%, with AC2 = .60. Qualitative comments emphasized clinical plausibility concerns without RAG and language quality concerns with RAG; error frequencies were not quantified. Conclusions: RAG was not associated with a higher overall realism mean in this response set. Clinical plausibility and linguistic naturalness warrant separate assessment in a comparison that controls generation settings. The study did not evaluate avatar effects, multi-turn coherence, safety, or learning outcomes.

items.title: Sequential Priming Builder: A Free, No-Code Tool for Implementing Sequential Priming Paradigms
items.abstract: Sequential priming tasks are a family of methods widely used in psychology. However, implementing sequential priming tasks typically requires custom programming and deployment through third-party platforms. To address these challenges, we developed a free tool that requires no coding skills — the Sequential Priming Builder (SP-Builder: spbuilder.org). This tool uses a graphical user interface that enables researchers to easily build different types of sequential priming tasks, which can be integrated into the widely used online survey platform Qualtrics. We assessed the tool’s reliability and timing accuracy in online environments across two studies. In Study 1, we showed that it correctly presented the predefined stimulus sequence and accurately recorded elapsed time. We also evaluated the timing error of stimulus presentation under conditions where typical online participant interactions were simulated. We conducted Study 2 using a preregistered Affect Misattribution Procedure (AMP; N = 92), a widely used sequential priming task. We built the study with SP-Builder, and the results replicated the published findings.

items.title: Feeling Good Sustains Acting Green: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Warm Glow and Pro-Environmental Behavior
items.abstract: When we engage in pro-environmental behaviors that align with our personal values, we can experience positive feelings, known as warm glow. Theories suggest a potential positive feedback loop such that people who anticipate feeling more warm glow are more likely to act pro-environmentally, and acting in line with their personal values may in turn elicit warm glow, thereby encouraging further pro-environmental behavior. There is considerable empirical work from psychology, marketing and economics investigating these relationships, but to date this work has not been systematically synthesized. A test of the strength and robustness of the theorized links is needed to answer the question of whether warm glow is in fact consistently related to pro-environmental behavior. We report a systematic review and meta-analysis probing the robustness of the associations between warm glow and pro-environmental intentions and behaviors. Following the PRISMA guidance, we identified 94 papers with 251 effects based on 58,313 participants. A pre-registered three-level random-effects meta-analytic model was used to estimate overall effects and to examine moderation by behavioral domain and measurement approach. The associations between both anticipated and experienced warm glow and pro-environmental intentions and behaviors were robust and medium-to-large (rs: .43 – .53). Substantial heterogeneity persisted after accounting for moderators, suggesting meaningful variation in effect sizes across studies. Overall, these findings provide strong evidence of robust links between warm glow and pro-environmental intentions and behaviors. Future research using experimental and longitudinal designs is needed to help test the causal pathways in the positive feedback loop.

items.title: Researching Traditionally Rooted Psychological Concepts: Methodological Implications from Traditional Chinese Psychology
items.abstract: Research on psychological concepts rooted in historical intellectual traditions has attracted growing attention, yet studies in this field may investigate fundamentally different psychological objects. The present article conceptualizes the modern and traditional approaches to such research and systematically examines their methodological implications. Whereas the modern approach constitutes its objects primarily through contemporary manifestations within a population, the traditional approach specifies psychological targets through theoretical formulations grounded in classical accounts. Such targets may have theoretically specified internal relations and need not already be realized in the populations available for research. Drawing on existing studies of traditional Chinese psychology, the analysis identifies potential methodological mismatches and demonstrates their implications for empirical investigation. Ordinary participants may not possess the understanding or degree of realization required to investigate a target mentality; cultivation may be a methodological precondition rather than merely an intervention to modify existing tendencies; and satisfactory psychometric results do not necessarily establish that a measure represents the target’s intended meanings and internal relations. Moreover, findings from partial realizations cannot simply be generalized to fully cultivated forms. These analyses provide principles for selecting participants, determining the role of intervention, evaluating measurement, and delimiting the scope of inference according to the intended research object and question. The article also considers how empirical evidence can inform the evaluation and possible revision of classical psychological claims, while distinguishing empirical investigation from the normative justification of cultivation. Beyond traditional psychology, these methodological insights may inform empirical research on psychological possibilities specified through other theoretical sources.

items.title: Do Scales Semantically Resemble the Sources They Cite? Embedding Analysis of Construct Proliferation in Five Anomy Instruments
items.abstract: Construct proliferation in psychology is associated with jingle and jangle fallacies that psychometric methods are not designed to detect. Semantic embeddings offer a complementary approach, but existing applications have compared scales within a single level without bringing in the theoretical texts a construct's tradition rests on. This study extends the embedding framework of Wulff and Mata (2025a) to across-level comparison paired with a documentary audit of citation acts. We embedded 43 items from five anomy scales alongside 3,762 propositions extracted from nine source texts at three analytical levels (foundational texts, scale articles, and items), using six embedding models from three architectural families, and we coded every passage in which a scale article cites a theoretical source. Items formed thematic clusters that crossed scale boundaries, beyond the expression of a single homogeneous theme per instrument, while retaining within-scale cohesion, and were rarely nearest to the article that introduced them (14%). All five scale articles were semantically nearest to Merton's (1938) text, a pattern identical across models, stable under bootstrap resampling, and not reproduced by two genre-matched control texts. The documentary audit showed that no article adopts Merton's formulation; the two articles that adopt a foundational text both adopt Durkheim's Suicide, which was the nearest foundation for neither of them. This proximity coexists with the absence of any direct adoption of Merton. This extension, combining semantic proximity with documented citation acts, offers an approach for examining whether the sources an instrument cites are also the ones its content most resembles.

items.title: Calculadora CVC: una aplicación web abierta para calcular el coeficiente de validez de contenido corregido por azar de Hernández-Nieto.
items.abstract: Background Hernández-Nieto’s Content Validity Coefficient (CVC) includes a correction for chance agreement (Pei) suited to small expert panels, the usual scenario in education, psychology and health. No general-purpose statistical platform implements it, so each team computes it in its own spreadsheet, without traceability or verification. Methods We present CVC-Calculator, an open-source web application that runs in the browser (Angular 18, TypeScript) and computes the item-level CVC, Pei, the dimension-level CVC and the interpretive category, with input validation and export of the complete calculation record to Excel. The core was verified by differential testing against a reference implementation in exact rational arithmetic over a reproducible corpus of 1,793 matrices (3- to 20-point scales, 3 to 15 judges, 2 to 200 items, matrices on the thresholds and invalid inputs), metamorphic relations, unit tests, a second JavaScript engine and end-to-end verification of the deployed interface in Chromium, following ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119. The effect of the most common manual errors in computing Pei was quantified. Results The maximum deviation of the total CVC from the exact value was 2.6 × 10 −15 , with 100% category agreement, bitwise-identical outputs across runs and engines, and 155 of 155 checks passed in the interface. Three behaviours of the original version were detected and corrected. The tool reproduces two published studies (28 of 28 and 81 of 93 exact values; the rest is explained by truncation or omission of Pei in the originals). Omitting Pei changes the category of 31% of matrices with three judges; computing it with the number of categories changes 42% with a three-point scale. Conclusions CVC-Calculator provides a verified, auditable and reproducible CVC computation, and delimits empirically when the chance correction matters.

items.title: Different Facial EMG and Emotional Expressivity Responses to Insomnia-Related and Sadness-Related Video Clips in People With Insomnia Disorder Compared to Healthy Sleepers With and Without Sleep Restriction.
items.abstract: Research into emotional processes in insomnia disorder is growing, yet more studies are needed on patients' emotional functioning. This study investigates emotional responses of individuals with insomnia disorder and healthy controls to dynamic emotional stimuli related and unrelated to insomnia. The assessment incorporates physiological, subjective, and behavioural measures of emotional reactivity. The study involved 97 patients with insomnia disorder, 49 healthy controls under moderate sleep restriction, and 47 healthy controls without sleep restriction. In a controlled laboratory setting, participants watched an insomnia-related and a sadness-related video clip. Emotional reactivity was assessed through facial electromyography (EMG), self-report, and coding of video-recorded facial expressions. The spontaneous use of emotion regulation strategies was also assessed. The emotional responses to the two video clips in the three groups were compared in multiple MANCOVAs with emotion-related assessments as dependent variables. EMG revealed a distinct pattern in insomnia patients, showing higher zygomatic and lower corrugator muscle activity during the insomnia-related compared to the sadness-related video clip. Only patients with insomnia disorder reported a pre-to-post video clip increase in arousal in response to the insomnia-related clip. The findings indicate a unique engagement of patients with insomnia when processing emotional stimuli related to their condition. More research using multi-method approaches is needed to differentiate the effect of sleep restriction from that of chronic insomnia disorder. Strategies aimed at addressing emotional processes may prove beneficial in modulating emotional responses to symptoms-related stimuli.

items.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of a School-Based Suicide Prevention Program in Reducing Suicidal Ideation and Improving the Mental Well-Being of School-Going Adolescents in the Northern Region of Pakistan: A Pre/Post-Intervention Study.
items.abstract: This study evaluated the effectiveness of two culturally adapted, school-based suicide prevention interventions (RAAHI and SafeTALK) in reducing suicidal ideation and improving mental well-being among adolescents in the Northern Region of Pakistan. A single-group pre-post quasi-experimental design was employed, including 266 students (mean age 15.56 years) from grades 9 and 10 across four public secondary schools. The interventions comprised a 3-h suicide literacy module (RAAHI) and a 4-h skills-based workshop (SafeTALK), delivered by trained psychologists. Suicidal ideation, measured using the Modified Scale for Suicidal Ideation (MSSI), significantly decreased from a mean score of 24.44 at baseline to 17.14 at follow-up (p < 0.001). Significant improvements were also observed in suicide literacy, perceived awareness, self-efficacy, and psychological well-being, with reductions in depression, anxiety, and stress levels. These findings suggest that culturally adapted, school-based interventions can effectively reduce suicidal ideation and improve mental health outcomes among adolescents in low-resource settings. Integrating such programs within school systems may offer a scalable approach to adolescent suicide prevention in similar contexts.

items.title: The role of illness perception in shaping quality of life among patients with colorectal cancer and ascites.
items.abstract: This cross-sectional study examined the association between illness perception and health-related quality of life (QoL) in 218 patients with colorectal cancer and ascites. Participants completed the Brief Illness Perception Questionnaire (BIPQ) and European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30. More threatening illness perceptions were associated with poorer QoL across functional domains. In multivariable linear regression, the reverse-coded BIPQ total threat score was independently associated with lower global QoL (B = -0.54, p < 0.001), whereas higher Karnofsky Performance Status was associated with better QoL (B = 0.06, p = 0.020). Age, disease duration, histological grade, and tumor diameter were not independently significant. The model explained 54.5% of the variance in global QoL (R2 = 0.55; adjusted R2 = 0.53). These findings highlight illness perception as an important psychosocial correlate of QoL and support prospective evaluation of interventions targeting maladaptive illness perceptions.

items.title: A Preliminary Examination of Learning in Daily Life and Self-Harm Urges Among People With and Without Suicide Attempt Histories.
items.abstract: Background: Studies have begun to demonstrate links between self-harm/suicide and deficits in processing feedback. Yet, this work has not examined whether learning predicts near-term risk of self-harm behaviors. Aims: The goal was to examine how learning assessed in daily life predicted near-term self-harm among people with and without suicide attempt (SA) histories. Method: Participants (N = 50) were recruited via an online recruitment platform based on the presence of past-year SA (n = 24) or no SA-history (n = 26). Participants completed 7 daily surveys of affect, self-harm urges, and web-based learning task. Results: Results revealed poorer learning accuracy among those with suicide attempt histories. Interactions between SA-history and learning on self-harm urges revealed that individuals with a past-year attempt history had lower self-harm urges when this learning rate was higher. Negative affect did not influence associations. Limitations: Small effects may not be detected with this sample size. Conclusions: These findings underscore links between self-harm and learning, and are among the first to examine learning dynamically in daily life. This study sets the stage to pinpoint processes that may mark time periods of increased risk for self-injury among people with SA histories.

items.title: Beyond Depression - The Moderating Roles of Somatic Symptoms and Interpersonal Difficulties in Adolescent Suicidal Ideation.
items.abstract: Background: Depression is a central risk factor for adolescent suicidal ideation (SI), yet depressive symptoms alone do not fully explain why some adolescents develop suicidal thoughts. Somatic symptoms and interpersonal difficulties may mark forms of distress that heighten vulnerability to SI. Aims: This study examined whether somatization and interpersonal difficulties are associated with adolescent SI beyond depression, and whether they moderate the association between depression and SI. Method: Data were drawn from 8,052 adolescents attending vocational high schools in Israel. Participants completed adapted Brief Symptom Inventory subscales assessing depression, somatization, and interpersonal difficulties, along with selected Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale items assessing SI. Alcohol use, drug use, and truancy were also assessed. Analyses included descriptive statistics, hierarchical logistic regression, and moderation models using Hayes' PROCESS macro. Results: Overall, 9.7% of adolescents endorsed SI. Depression was the strongest predictor of SI, while somatization and interpersonal difficulties also made independent contributions after accounting for demographic and behavioral risk factors. Separate moderation models showed that both somatization and interpersonal difficulties strengthened the association between depression and SI, with the depression-SI link becoming stronger at higher levels of each moderator. In the full simultaneous regression model, these effects showed a more complex pattern, suggesting that moderation should be interpreted in relation to the analytic model. Limitations: The cross-sectional design, self-report measures, gender imbalance, adapted BSI subscales, selected C-SSRS items, and lack of direct trauma-related measures should be considered. Conclusion: Findings suggest that adolescent SI is shaped not only by depressive symptoms but also by somatic and interpersonal expressions of distress. School-based assessment may benefit from attending to somatic complaints and relational difficulties alongside depression.

items.title: Evaluation of Rehabilitation Outcomes Following Therapy With the Luna EMG Diagnostic and Rehabilitation Robot for the Upper Limb and Hand in Individuals in the Chronic Post-Stroke Phase.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND This study compared a rehabilitation program using Luna EMG biofeedback with conventional physiotherapy in patients in the chronic phase after stroke, focusing on hand motor function, upper limb proprioception, and functional ability. MATERIAL AND METHODS A total of 124 post-stroke patients aged 45-75 years were randomly assigned to a test group (n=63) or control group (n=61). Both groups completed a 3-week rehabilitation program. The control group received conventional physiotherapy, while the test group received Luna EMG biofeedback training for the same total therapy time. Outcomes included upper limb proprioception, Fugl-Meyer Assessment of the Upper Extremity (FMA-UE), Barthel Index, Box and Blocks Test, and Frenchay scale. RESULTS Both groups showed significant post-intervention improvements (P<0.001). Compared with controls, the test group demonstrated significantly greater improvements in upper limb proprioception, FMA-UE scores, manual dexterity, and grip function (all padj<0.001; rrb=0.40-0.89). The between-group difference in Barthel Index scores was not significant after Bonferroni correction (padj=0.138), although the test group showed slightly greater improvement. CONCLUSIONS Adding Luna EMG-based biofeedback to conventional rehabilitation may provide short-term benefits in upper limb proprioception, motor function, manual dexterity, and grip function after stroke. Further studies are needed to determine long-term effects and clinically meaningful changes.

items.title: Prospective Relations of Sex Hormones with Internalizing Psychopathology Across Adolescence.
items.abstract: Marked sex differences in rates of internalizing psychopathology emerge in adolescence, but underlying mechanisms are unclear. Sex hormone release is one biological process that changes markedly during this period. Few studies have examined the prospective relation between sex hormones and internalizing psychopathology, and findings are mixed. None has tested whether sex hormones help explain the sex difference in psychopathology. We examined the prospective relations between estradiol and testosterone (measured at age 12) and anxiety and depression at ages 15 and 18, adjusting for concurrent psychopathology. Hormones were assayed from saliva. Psychopathology was assessed with a semi-structured diagnostic interview and well-validated symptom rating scales. Sex did not moderate relations between sex hormones and psychopathology, so sex X hormone interaction terms were not included in the models. With sex included as a covariate, estradiol positively predicted most anxiety outcomes, and testosterone negatively predicted anxiety diagnoses. Neither hormone predicted depression outcomes. Results held after controlling for physical pubertal development. Parallel mediation models showed a significant total indirect effect of sex on all anxiety outcomes through sex hormones. Findings suggest that sex hormones contribute to the sex difference in anxiety but not depression, and that these associations do not differ between sexes, suggesting that sex hormones are not simply proxies for sex, but exert effects through different mechanisms. Results also indicate that sex hormones' influence persists across adolescence rather than being limited to proximal pubertal activation effects, highlighting their importance for understanding the emergence of internalizing psychopathology during this period.

items.title: When difficulty helps and when it hurts: Target-matching cues yield transient capture while mismatching cues lead to dwelling.
items.abstract: How top-down goals and bottom-up saliency interact over time remains a central debate in visual search. Recent models, such as the Attentional Dwelling Account and the Priority Accumulation Framework, propose that attentional capture by salient, non-matching cues (e.g., abrupt onsets) increases under difficult search conditions (longer reaction times (RTs)), challenging the classical view of transient capture. To test whether this difficulty-dependent modulation generalizes across cue types, we conducted two visual search experiments using target-matching color cues across both feature and singleton search, manipulating task difficulty via color similarity. Across both search types, we observed the inverse of the onset-cue pattern: spatial cueing effects (valid vs. invalid) were pronounced during easy search (short RTs) but virtually eliminated during difficult search (long RTs). These findings indicate that target-matching peripheral cues exert a transient influence, modulating early attentional selection but dissipating before prolonged visual search decisions conclude. Consequently, while attentional dwelling and priority accumulation accounts capture the dynamics of non-matching onset cues, they do not generalize to feature-matching color cues. We conclude that cue type, specifically whether a cue shares defining features with the target, fundamentally determines how task difficulty modulates the time course and magnitude of attentional capture. The data and analysis scripts are available at https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/2CXHE . OPEN PRACTICES STATEMENT: The following software was used: MATLAB 2022 a (The Mathworks, Natick, MA, USA) with the Psychtoolbox (Brainard, 1997; Kleiner et al., 2007) was used to run the experiment. Statistical analyses were performed using R 4.4.2 (R Core Team, 2024) and RStudio 2025.09.1 (Posit team, 2025). The pre-processed data and the analysis code in R are available on the Open Science Framework at https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/2CXHE . The study's design and its analysis were not preregistered. The program code used to run the experiments is available on request. Please send an email to dirk.kerzel@unige.ch. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This paper re-evaluates current priority accumulation and attentional dwelling frameworks. While these models propose that search difficulty increases attentional capture, our findings suggest a more nuanced dynamic: for target-matching color cues, capture appears transient and dissipates as difficulty grows. By showing that the relationship between difficulty and capture depends on cue type, this work highlights important boundary conditions and helps reconcile diverging accounts of attentional control.

items.title: Feeling Good Sustains Acting Green: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Warm Glow and Pro-Environmental Behavior
items.abstract: When we engage in pro-environmental behaviors that align with our personal values, we can experience positive feelings, known as warm glow. Theories suggest a potential positive feedback loop such that people who anticipate feeling more warm glow are more likely to act pro-environmentally, and acting in line with their personal values may in turn elicit warm glow, thereby encouraging further pro-environmental behavior. There is considerable empirical work from psychology, marketing and economics investigating these relationships, but to date this work has not been systematically synthesized. A test of the strength and robustness of the theorized links is needed to answer the question of whether warm glow is in fact consistently related to pro-environmental behavior. We report a systematic review and meta-analysis probing the robustness of the associations between warm glow and pro-environmental intentions and behaviors. Following the PRISMA guidance, we identified 94 papers with 251 effects based on 58,313 participants. A pre-registered three-level random-effects meta-analytic model was used to estimate overall effects and to examine moderation by behavioral domain and measurement approach. The associations between both anticipated and experienced warm glow and pro-environmental intentions and behaviors were robust and medium-to-large (rs: .43 – .53). Substantial heterogeneity persisted after accounting for moderators, suggesting meaningful variation in effect sizes across studies. Overall, these findings provide strong evidence of robust links between warm glow and pro-environmental intentions and behaviors. Future research using experimental and longitudinal designs is needed to help test the causal pathways in the positive feedback loop.

items.title: Machine Learning-based Transcriptomic Data Analysis of Long COVID Patients: Generating Hypotheses for Molecular Signatures
items.abstract: Introduction: Long COVID (LC) remains a global public-health challenge, affecting an estimated 10-30% of COVID-19-survivors. Machine learning (ML) can help identify molecular features associated with LC. Human ion channels (HICs), that regulate immune-cell signaling and cellular homeostasis, may contribute to LC-associated processes and offer insights into relevant pathways and potential drug-repurposing candidates. Methodology: RNA-seq data from COVID-19-recovered and LC patients across six datasets were integrated, preprocessed, and corrected for batch effects. Supervised ML models were evaluated using leave-one-batch-out validation, with SHAP identifying features across validation folds. Functional enrichment, host-host and host-viral protein-protein interaction analyses were performed, followed by drug interaction analysis of potential HICs within the resulting interactome. Results: A support vector classifier with an RBF kernel achieved a mean-AUC of 0.664 across six validation folds. SHAP analysis of the three selected folds (AUC = 0.722, 0.836, and 0.817) identified 225, 153, and 241 genes, respectively. Functional enrichment highlighted pathways including histidine metabolism and TNF signaling. Among the 613 genes identified across these folds, 9 were HICs and 39 were immune signaling-related genes (ISGs), whose protein-protein interaction analysis revealed a pharmacologically relevant interactome. Furthermore, four HICs including CLCN3, KCNQ3, RYR1, and ZACN interacted with 30 approved drugs. Conclusion: ML-based analysis of integrated RNA-seq data identified HICs and ISGs associated with LC, while functional enrichment and PPI analyses provided insights into their potential biological relevance. Drug interaction analysis further highlighted candidate HIC-targeting drugs for future investigation in LC management. This computational framework provides preliminary, hypothesis-generating insights to guide future research.

items.title: ADTSIM2.0: An updated simulation of American dog tick (Dermacentor variabilis Acari: Ixodidae) population dynamics
items.abstract: The American dog tick, Dermacentor variabilis (Say), is found across most of the central and eastern portions of North America, and is a known vector of human and veterinary pathogens. While this tick has been found throughout this region for decades, there is still little understanding of the drivers for the highly variable annual densities. To explore the relative effects of hosts, environmental conditions, and tick biology, we introduce ADTSIM 2.0, an upgraded version of the ADTSIM model that simulates the lifecycle of D. variabilis. The model uses a weekly time step and follows the life stages (egg, larvae, nymph, and adult), questing behavior, host-seeking dynamics, and survival rates under varying environmental conditions. The model includes calculations for tick interactions with small- and medium-sized mammal hosts and factors in critical environmental influences such as temperature on tick development and questing activity. It addresses the effect of questing behavior on tick longevity, emphasizing the trade off between survival and host-seeking. The results show that accurate estimates of both host densities and weather information are critical to predict local D. variabilis densities. This model provides the first step to building a tool for public health information, offering a framework for assessing tick control measures and is adaptable to add tick-borne pathogen dynamics for both human and animal diseases.

items.title: Heterogeneity in excess respiratory acute care utilization during wildfire smoke waves in California
items.abstract: Rationale: Wildfire smoke is an increasing public health threat, yet most epidemiologic studies estimate average smoke-health associations across broad spatial or temporal scales. Such approaches may obscure substantial heterogeneity across individual smoke waves, leaving an important evidence gap for dynamic public health preparedness, risk communication, and clinical practice. Objectives: To estimate event-specific excess respiratory acute care utilization during smoke waves and identify smoke wave features associated with higher excess utilization. Methods: We conducted a statewide study of 18,271,754 respiratory acute care encounters in California from 2006 to 2019. A smoke wave was defined as at least 2 consecutive days during which county-level wildfire smoke fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exceeded the 95th percentile over the study period. We applied a machine learning-integrated two-stage interrupted time-series design to estimate excess respiratory acute care utilization during each event. We then used meta-regressions to examine multiple spatiotemporally varying effect modifiers such as smoke wave duration, intensity, timing, and co-occurring climate and meteorological conditions. Measurements and Main Results: A total of 1,249 smoke waves were identified and examined in this study. Excess respiratory acute care utilization varied substantially across smoke waves. Higher excess utilization was associated with longer smoke wave duration, greater intensity, winter occurrence, short recovery period, overlap with holidays, drought conditions, or co-occurrence with precipitation or extreme heat events. Conclusions: This study proposes a novel analytical framework to systematically evaluate spatiotemporal drivers of heterogeneity in wildfire smoke respiratory health effects. The findings can inform dynamic preparedness and public health response to smoke events.

items.title: Enhancing Access to and Utilization of Maternal and Child Health Service through Implementation of a District-led Integrated Mobile Health Service Delivery Model in Pastoral Ethiopia: A Multi-Method Implementation Research
items.abstract: Introduction: Lack of access to essential health services has remained a significant public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa. The conventional health service delivery models often fail to account for the mobility patterns and socio-cultural values of these communities. These communities are frequently affected by recurrent droughts, conflicts, floods, and disease outbreaks. This study assessed the contribution of a mobile health services (MHS) delivery model designed to improve access to and utilisation of maternal, neonatal, and child health services in pastoralist contexts of Ethiopia. Methods: A multi-method embedded implementation research with a non-randomized controlled quasi-experimental study design was employed in four selected Woredas of Ethiopia. Baseline data from July 2022 to June 2023 and endline data from July 2023 to June 2024 were extracted from DHIS2. The MHS delivery model was co-designed with stakeholders, redefined communitycentred outreach sites, and established a multidisciplinary team, that was implemented monthly. The average distance between the health facility and the centre of the targeted community village was 29.6 kilometres. Data were captured from routine health service records, MHS databases, and program reports, and 143 in-depth interviews among service providers and beneficiaries. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistical methods and difference-indifferences using Stata 18, while qualitative data were coded and analysed using ATLAS.ti. Results: During the twelve months, the MHS reached 79,404 people through 190 sessions held and offered an integrated essential health service in 20 hard-to-reach villages. In the study area, ANC use was 64.0% in Chifra and 75.6% in Dasenech. In addition, penta-3 antigen vaccination improved from 66.0% to 69.7% in Chifra and from 91.2% to 102.1% in Dasenech, respectively. In the difference-indifferences analysis, the MHS significantly enhanced access to ANC follow-up and completion of pentavalent and full vaccination coverage. A Woreda-led approach, community engagement, context-tailored and timely communication, and comprehensive service delivery by a multidisciplinary team enhanced the use and acceptability of the MHS in the pastoral setting. The contribution of MHS to ensuring access and use of MNCH services ranged from 13.0% to 19.1% for continuing family planning and antenatal care, respectively. Conclusions: The study highlights that the MHS delivery model is a suitable platform that has substantially contributed to improving access to and use of maternal, newborn, and child health services in pastoral, agropastoral, and scattered settlements. Being a woreda-led, participatory codesign, community-centred approach, and context-tailored health service delivery approach enhanced the acceptability and effectiveness of the MHS in reaching the underserved community. Integration of MHS with the existing PHC system, with an innovative, sustainable financing mechanism, is recommended to ensure access and use of MNCH in hard-to-reach settings.

items.title: Additional Vascular Imaging in Women With Acute Cerebral Ischemia: Thresholds for Cost-Effectiveness
items.abstract: Background: Women with acute cerebral ischemia receive intracranial vascular imaging less often than men, but the value of expanding imaging is uncertain. We estimated the treatment rates and functional benefits required for additional imaging to be cost-effective. Methods: We developed a decision tree and state-transition model comparing additional imaging followed by timely endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for M1 occlusion with current care from Ontario public-payer and US Medicare perspectives. Women-specific 90-day modified Rankin Scale distributions from HERMES were projected over a lifetime. We jointly varied the proportion of additional scans leading to additional timely EVT and the treatment effect relative to HERMES. Cost-effectiveness thresholds were CAD 50,000 and USD 100,000 per quality-adjusted life-year. Program costs represented health-care resources in Ontario and additional payments under Medicare. Results: At variable program costs of CAD 1,000 or USD 1,000 per additional scan, assuming the full HERMES effect and no additional fixed costs or pathway-related harm, expected cost-effectiveness required one additional timely EVT per 48 scans in Ontario and 57 under Medicare (2.07% and 1.74%, respectively). Treatment rates of 3.07% and 2.65% were required for a 90% probability of cost-effectiveness under these assumptions. At three additional thrombectomies per 100 scans and the same costs, treatment effects had to reach 76.9% and 67.3% of the HERMES effect. With the full effect, 1,000 additional scans at this treatment rate yielded approximately 5 additional functionally independent survivors at 90 days. Deterministic analyses restricted to 5 years increased the required treatment rates to 4.44% and 4.22%. Conclusions: Additional vascular imaging in women could be cost-effective when a small proportion of scans leads to timely thrombectomy, provided sufficient functional benefit is retained. Prospective evaluations should assess additional treatment opportunities, functional outcomes and program costs against these conditional thresholds, which depend on projected long-term outcomes.

items.title: The Lincolnshire Unit for Mental Health Research: a programme pre-protocol for place-based, co-produced, applied mental health research
items.abstract: Background: Mental health research opportunities are unevenly distributed. Lincolnshire, a county in England, combines dispersed rural populations, coastal deprivation, and small urban areas, with substantial variation in mental health need and access to support. The Lincolnshire Unit for Mental Health Research (LUMHR) programme has received five years of foundational National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) funding to establish lasting research capability and generate evidence relevant locally and beyond. Methods This programme pre-protocol describes three connected themes: Connect (access), Prevent (wellbeing), and Respond (crisis and suicide prevention), informed by previous priority-setting with 520 regional stakeholders. Their common approach combines evidence synthesis and local insight, co-design or contextual adaptation, feasibility testing, and assessment of the evidence needed for subsequent decisions. Further synthesis, primary research and externally funded definitive or multicentre evaluation will be pursued where required. A county-wide observatory will connect learning from linked health records, geospatial analysis, crisis intelligence, and the Living in Lincolnshire citizen-science panel. Public involvement, inclusion, responsible research and innovation, health economics, knowledge mobilisation, and research capacity development run throughout. Anticipated outputs and outcomes Anticipated contributions include studies and reusable and transferable methods, governed analytical infrastructure, citizen-science participation, opportunities for research progression and leadership development, follow-on funding proposals, and evidence informing service and community decisions about effectiveness, equity, and resource use. A programme logic model sets out intended achievements across research, capability, service change, population equity, and sustainability. Internal learning will be aligned with NIHR evaluation requirements. Conclusions LUMHR aims to establish enduring capability for communities and partners to shape, conduct, and use mental health research. The programme will develop nationally and internationally relevant questions and methods while retaining flexibility for co-production and study-specific protocols.

items.title: Examining HiTOP Through Naturalistic Symptom Descriptions in Anonymous Online Mental Health Forums: A Mixed-Methods Study Protocol
items.abstract: AbstractBackground: The Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology (HiTOP) organises covarying symptoms and maladaptive traits into transdiagnostic dimensions to address limitations of categorical diagnosis. Naturalistic symptom descriptions may complement structured assessments. Objective: This protocol describes a reproducible mixed-methods workflow to derive symptom indicators from forum posts and examine their organisation relative to HiTOP. Methods and analysis: The target sample is 80,000 public Reddit posts. After local de-identification, a large language model (LLM) will extract symptom labels and supporting paraphrases. Two human experts will independently review outputs for up to 250 posts. Three embedding models will flag potentially equivalent symptom labels for local LLM assessment. Two experts will qualitatively review the most frequent canonical symptom labels (at least 1,000) and develop a codebook of symptom categories, continuing until a prespecified saturation criterion is met. An LLM will assign canonical symptom labels to these categories, producing binary post-level indicators. Multiverse-inspired structural analyses will compare network, component, factor, and clustering representations across discovery, internal tuning, and holdout partitions. Evaluation will assess interpretability, stability, and agreement with expert mapping to HiTOP. Supplementary analyses will include agent-assisted exploration, codebook application to DepressionEmo and the Reddit Mental Health Dataset, and pooled integrative analysis that may include additional comparable corpora. Discussion: The study will examine whether symptom co-expression within posts forms interpretable patterns corresponding to HiTOP.Ethics: The Ethics Committee of Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin approved the study (EA2/274/25). The study was preregistered on 8 May 2026 (German Clinical Trials Register, DRKS00040244). Keywords: Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology, natural language processing, large language models, Reddit, mixed methods, study protocol

items.title: Quality of Life and Perceived Cognitive Dysfunction in Patients with Major Depressive Disorder: A Longitudinal Observational Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is recognized as one of the most prevalent public health disorders globally associated with increased rates of mortality, morbidity and disability. Numerous research has yielded inconclusive findings about the impact of depression treatment on quality of life (QOL). Aim To evaluate the severity of depression symptoms and their relationship to QOL and perceived cognitive dysfunction in Jordanian patients diagnosed with MDD. Method The study included patients from both genders, between 18-65 years old, and diagnosed with MDD. They attended two visits with 6-week interval period and completed three self- administered questionnaires in both visits: a 9-item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) assesses depression severity, patient-rated Perceived Deficit Questionnaire (PDQ-5) assesses cognitive function, and World Health Organization Quality of Life Brief (WHOQOL-BREF) format for assessing the quality of life and health satisfaction. Results A total of 112 patients were included in the study. Twenty patients withdrew their consent to participate therefore only 92 patients (34 males and 58 females) completed both sets of questionnaires. Significant reductions were found in the scores (mean ±SD) for PHQ-9 before and after treatment (19±5.4 and 7.1±5.1, respectively, P P Conclusion Patients with MDD showed significant improvement in their depression symptoms, cognition and QOL after treatment. Depression severity showed significant positive correlation with QOL and inverse correlation with cognition in these patients.

items.title: Minorities' Diminished Returns of Educational Attainment on Disability Among California Adults: CHIS 2025
items.abstract: Abstract Background. Minorities' diminished returns (MDR) is the finding that socioeconomic resources, such as educational attainment, produce smaller health gains for racial and ethnic minority groups than for White Americans. Most MDR research uses national samples, and it is not known whether the pattern replicates in states such as California, which has more equity-oriented public and social policies. Disability is a useful test of MDR because it reflects accumulated physical, mental and emotional health and is tied to work and income. California has many equity-oriented public, social and health policies that may protect the health of minority populations. California's diverse population makes it possible to compare educational attainment gradients across several groups in one survey. Methods. We used survey-weighted prevalence estimates and 95% confidence intervals from the 2025 California Health Interview Survey (CHIS), a population-based probability sample of California households, accessed through the AskCHIS dashboard. The outcome was self-reported disability due to a physical, mental or emotional condition. We compared prevalence at high school, bachelor's and master's level for California White, Black, Latino, Asian and Two or More Races adults (all non-Latino except Latino) and for all California adults combined. We estimated each group's absolute and relative change with educational attainment and its difference-in-differences from White adults. Results. Among White adults in California, disability prevalence fell from 27.8% at high school to 13.6% at a bachelor's degree (− 14.2 points) and 9.5% at a master's degree, and among all California adults it fell from 21.8% to 13.5% and 10.3%. Among Black adults it was 20.8%, 22.3% and 13.5%, so disability prevalence did not fall between high school and a bachelor's degree. The high-school-to-bachelor's change in disability prevalence differed from White adults by + 15.7 points for Black (95% CI 6.4 to 25.0), + 10.9 for Latino (5.8 to 16.0) and + 7.1 for Asian adults (0.8 to 13.4), and the change to a master's degree differed for all four minority groups. At a bachelor's degree, disability prevalence was 8.7 points higher in Black adults than White adults (1.6 to 15.8), while Latino adults did not differ and Asian adults were 3.7 points lower. In relative terms Asian adults (− 42%) were close to White adults (− 51%), whereas Latino (− 18%) and Black adults (+ 7%) were not. Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander and American Indian/Alaska Native estimates were too unstable to report. Conclusions. In California, we found some evidence in line with minorities' diminished returns for many racial and ethnic groups, particularly Black adults. Educational attainment was linked to smaller absolute reductions in disability for Black, Latino and Asian adults than for White adults, and only Black adults ended up worse off than White adults at the bachelor's level. These patterns appeared in a state with more equity-oriented public and social policies, which calls for additional research on how to reduce MDR and equalize the returns to educational attainment across racial and ethnic groups.

items.title: Socioeconomic status among patients with uveitis: Association with Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease
items.abstract: Abstract Purpose Uveitis is an important cause of visual impairment and blindness worldwide. Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease (VKH) is a common cause of uveitis in East Asia and Southern Cone countries. Although studies regarding uveitis epidemiology have been published, the relationship between socioeconomic status and VKH has not been described. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional, observational, multicenter study at two tertiary referral centers in Santiago, Chile, over a three-year period. The study included 270 patients diagnosed with uveitis. Data were obtained from electronic medical records and included demographic characteristics, etiological diagnosis, health insurance type (public or private), and the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) and Human Development Index (HDI) corresponding to each patient's area of residence. Results Of 270 patients with uveitis, 128 (47.4%) had idiopathic uveitis, with idiopathic anterior uveitis being the most common anatomical subtype (93 [34.4%]). A specific etiology was identified in 142 (52.6%) patients, with VKH being the most common identified etiology (28 [10.4%]). Patients with VKH resided in areas with a higher median MPI than those with non-VKH uveitis (23.5 [IQR 13.2–24.9] vs 17.2 [4.2–24.5]; p = 0.0287) and a lower median HDI (0.609 [IQR 0.580–0.733] vs 0.630 [0.600-0.972]; p = 0.0041). Conclusion Patients with VKH resided in areas characterized by greater MPI and lower HDI than patients with non-VKH uveitis. These findings suggest a potential association between socioeconomic status and VKH in Chile. Future studies with larger and more representative populations incorporating individual-level socioeconomic measures are needed to confirm this association and explore its underlying determinants.

items.title: Nowhere to Report: Vulnerability Disclosure Channels at US Hospitals, Medical Device Makers, and Health IT Developers. A Cross-sectional Web Measurement
items.abstract: Abstract Objective To measure whether US hospitals, medical device manufacturers and certified electronic health record (EHR) developers publish any channel for reporting a security vulnerability. Materials and Methods A cross-sectional crawl in November 2026 visited domains on five public lists: hospitals listing a website (2,652), companies on FDA's list of AI-enabled medical devices (device makers, 525), vendors named in CISA medical advisories (advisory vendors, 75), developers of ONC-certified API technology (EHR developers, 200) and federal health agencies (the federal control, 124). Channels were security.txt, a disclosure policy page (judged by language models), a platform listing or CVE Numbering Authority status. Results Of these, 1,721 hospital domains could be measured (615 unreachable), as could 436 device-maker, 67 advisory-vendor, 181 EHR-developer and 101 federal-control domains. A channel was found at 87.6% (95% CI, 79.0%-93.7%) of federal-control, 8.2% (6.9%-9.6%) of hospital, 20.5% (16.7%-24.8%) of device-maker, 41.0% (28.6%-54.3%) of advisory-vendor and 7.9% (4.3%-13.2%) of EHR-developer domains. One health system's file served 95 of 132 hospital domains with security.txt; per distinct final site (post hoc), 3.1% (2.2%-4.1%) had one. On the same domains, 91.0% served a valid cms-hpt.txt, required by a price-transparency rule, and 7.9% security.txt. Discussion Channels were common where a directive requires them and rarer elsewhere, an association, not an effect of regulation. Per-domain counts overstate how many hospital organizations publish one. Conclusion Most organizations on these lists published no vulnerability reporting channel; most federal-control domains did. Among hospitals, channels came mostly from a few health systems. Whether such reports are answered remains untested.

items.title: An Exploration of Heavy Metals Research in Commonly Consumed Fish Species Across the Globe
items.abstract: Abstract Heavy metal contamination in fish species has become a major environmental and public health concern due to its potential effects on aquatic ecosystems and human consumers. This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of global research on heavy metals in selected fish species from 1947 to 2026. Data retrieved from the Scopus database yielded 9,317 documents published across 1,047 sources, with an annual growth rate of 7.47%. Original research articles dominated the literature (95.62%), highlighting the field’s strong emphasis on primary data generation. Publication trends revealed two distinct phases: a period of limited growth (1947–1982) followed by rapid expansion from 1983 onwards, reflecting increased awareness of environmental pollution, food safety concerns, and advancements in analytical technologies. China emerged as the leading contributor, followed by Egypt, Brazil, the United States, and Thailand, while Chinese institutions and authors dominated productivity rankings. Keyword and thematic analyses demonstrated an evolution from early studies focused on fish physiology and histology to contemporary investigations emphasizing molecular biology, oxidative stress, gene expression, bioaccumulation, and environmental monitoring. Collaboration networks revealed extensive international partnerships spanning Asia, Europe, Africa, and the Americas. The synthesis of systematic reviews highlighted major concerns related to heavy metal accumulation, food safety risks, fish health, environmental contamination, and sustainable aquaculture practices. Overall, the field has evolved into a highly interdisciplinary research domain integrating toxicology, environmental science, molecular biology, and aquaculture, with increasing relevance for public health and ecosystem sustainability.
