items.title: Non-Adherence to Antenatal Care Appointments and Associated Factors Among Pregnant Women at a Tertiary Hospital in Northern Uganda
items.abstract: Abstract Background Non-adherence to antenatal care (ANC) appointments among pregnant women remains a significant public health challenge in Uganda, contributing to adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, including stillbirths. Despite high initial ANC attendance, sustained follow-up remains low and inconsistent. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of non-adherence to ANC appointments and associated factors among pregnant women attending Lira Regional Referral Hospital (LRRH). Methods A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted at LRRH between January and March 2024. A total of 591 pregnant women were selected using systematic random sampling. Data were collected through structured questionnaires and abstraction forms and analysed using SPSS version 25. Descriptive statistics were used to summarise participant characteristics. Binary logistic regression and multivariate logistic regression were performed to identify factors associated with non-adherence. Results The prevalence of non-adherence to ANC appointments was 15.4% (95% CI: 12.5–18.6). Multivariate analysis revealed that living more than 5 kilometres from the health facility significantly increased the odds of non-adherence [aOR = 2.687, 95% CI: 1.124–6.427, p = 0.026]. Other individual, obstetric, and facility-related factors were not independently associated with non-adherence. Conclusion Approximately one in six pregnant women at LRRH missed scheduled ANC appointments, with distance to the health facility identified as the most significant barrier. To improve adherence to ANC appointments, targeted interventions such as community outreach programs, telephone reminders, and strengthening community midwifery services are recommended, particularly for women residing in remote areas.

items.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Perceived Facilitators and Barriers to Patient and Public Involvement and Engagement in Health-relate Research: A Cross-Regional Survey of Healthcare Professionals and Researchers in the Greater Bay Area of China
items.abstract: Abstract Background Patient and public involvement and engagement (PPIE) is increasingly recognised as essential for improving the relevance, quality, and impact of health-related research. However, evidence on the adoption and implementation of PPIE in China, particularly in the Greater Bay Area (GBA), remains limited. This study aimed to examine the knowledge, experience, attitudes, and perceived facilitators and barriers regarding PPIE among healthcare professionals (HCPs) and researchers in the GBA of China. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between December 2024 and April 2025 across six health and academic institutions in Guangdong Province, Hong Kong, and Macao. A structured questionnaire was developed based on a literature review, expert consultation, and the Context and Implementation of Complex Interventions (CICI) framework. Descriptive statistics and the Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel (CMH) chi-square test were used to examine regional differences, with adjustment for age group, educational level, and period of clinical experience. Results A total of 396 HCPs and researchers completed the survey. Most participants (68.7%) had no prior PPIE experience. Understanding of PPIE was limited, particularly in 55.2% Guangdong Province reported "little understanding" to the adoption and implementation of PPIE. Despite this, 97.5% recognized the importance of PPIE and expressed interest in training. Key perceived facilitators included improved participant recruitment (66.9%), enhanced trust (62.6%), and improved healthcare quality (61.6%). Major barriers were uncertainty about implementation (79.5%), patients' limited health literacy (63.9%), and insufficient resources (63.6%). Significant regional differences were observed in knowledge, confidence, willingness to engage, and perceptions of facilitators and barriers. Conclusions This first cross-regional survey in the GBA of China shows that HCPs and researchers generally hold positive attitudes towards PPIE but face substantial knowledge gaps, limited practical experience, and institutional and resource constraints. Regionally tailored training, enhanced institutional support, and clear operational and ethical guidelines are needed to translate positive attitudes into sustainable PPIE practice.

items.title: Strengthening routine malaria surveillance through amplicon sequencing in Western Equatoria State, South Sudan: drug resistance and transmission dynamics
items.abstract: Abstract Background Malaria is a major public health burden in South Sudan. However, the absence of routine molecular surveillance of malaria parasites limits evidence-based malaria control strategies able to counteract biological threats such as resistance to antimalarial drugs. To address this knowledge gap, a large molecular epidemiology study was conducted using targeted Amplicon Next-Generation Sequencing (AmpSeq). Methods Between November 2021 and June 2022 children under five years and pregnant women attending outpatient or antenatal care (ANC) at three Primary Health Care Centres (Mundri, Mvolo, and Lakamadi) in Western Equatoria State were enrolled. Participants underwent rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) and Dried Blood Spots were collected. Data generated with AmpSeq were used to evaluate Plasmodium species, barcode call rate (proxy for parasite density), complexity of infection (COI), genetic differentiation (Fst) and drug resistance markers. Results Among 1,873 samples, Plasmodium was detected in 64.2% of samples by AmpSeq versus 26.5% by RDT (p P. falciparum accounted for 97.3% of positive infections, while non- falciparum species were detected in 11.6%. Positivity and barcode call rate were higher in children than pregnant women (p pfkelch13 mutations were detected in 1.6% of samples, including the WHO-validated A675V marker. Mutant mdr1 haplotypes associated with resistance to the artemisinin partner drugs occurred in 59.4% of samples, and the quintuple dhfr-dhps mutant haplotype associated with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance reached a 67.5% frequency. Conclusions This is the first comprehensive AmpSeq-based molecular investigation of malaria parasites in South Sudan, providing the foundation for routine genomic surveillance. The findings highlight perennial transmission with monthly and regional variations, a substantial proportion of submicroscopic infections, and relevant circulation of non- falciparum species. items.title: Whose shift? Demographic variation in willingness to adopt plant-rich diets and its mitigation consequences
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Dietary transitions towards plant-rich diets are critical to reducing the environmental burden of the food system and improving public health, yet consumer adoption remains slow and uneven globally. Global dietary transition models typically assume uniform and universal uptake of alternative diets, overlooking how willingness to change varies across countries and population groups. Modelling dietary transitions that reflect stated consumer willingness can reveal how much of the expected mitigation is achievable, for whom, and what residual gap needs to be bridged by policy action Methods: We coupled consumer adoption willingness data from a representative survey of 30,218 respondents across 31 countries with the MATILDA dietary impact model to compare dietary greenhouse gas emissions (GHGE) under willingness-adjusted and population-wide adoption of the EAT-Lancet 2.0 reference diet. Random forest regression identified demographic and attitudinal predictors of adoption willingness.

items.title: Mathematical Modeling of Co-Infection Dynamics of Malaria and Typhoid Fever with Control Measures
items.abstract: Abstract Co-infection with malaria and typhoid fever poses a major public health challenge, especially in tropical regions. This study develops a mathematical model to analyze the co-infection dynamics, incorporating environmental sanitation and treatment interventions. The model uses differential equations to represent human populations in various disease states and derives the basic reproduction number to assess disease persistence or eradication. Stability analysis shows that when, the disease-free equilibrium is stable, indicating eradication, while leads to a stable endemic equilibrium, signifying persistent co-infection. Sensitivity analysis identifies key parameters influencing and numerical simulations reveal that combining environmental sanitation and treatment significantly reduces co-infection prevalence. The study provides insights for public health strategies by highlighting the effectiveness of integrated interventions in controlling both malaria and typhoid fever.

items.title: MammoTrace Academic for teaching critical appraisal of mammography AI Software development and technical verification with worked educational activities
items.abstract: Abstract Background Medical students and health-profession trainees need to judge whether claims about artificial intelligence (AI) are supported by the data and procedures behind them. We aimed to develop and technically verify MammoTrace Academic v4.1.0 and translate its documented outputs into supervised critical-appraisal activities using mammography as the learning context. This developer-led software study combined a retained audit of public mammography records, execution of versioned automated tests, direct characterization of selected report texts, and documentary comparison with Orange and 3D Slicer. New tests used the archived public release and were interpreted separately from historical data-dependent findings. Constructive alignment linked five appraisal objectives to activities and expected explanations; the teaching materials were developed after the technical audit. Results The educational package comprises six activities, 27 questions, worked answers, a facilitator guide and a proposed formative rubric. Learners are asked to attribute sources, identify the unit of independence, distinguish annotations from model outputs, interpret report context and justify uncertainty. An evidence-only route requires neither software installation nor image downloads; optional application exercises demonstrate documented checks. A final synthetic case asks learners to apply the reasoning to a new problem. In the retained audit, 31 subjects overlapped between development and test sets; excluding 83 development annotations preserved all 704 test annotations. Model fitting was blocked when only one of 3020 metadata-eligible full-image series was unambiguously indexed locally. Direct report characterization exposed punctuation-sensitive confirmation of a historical category. New public-release execution produced 281 passing and 59 skipped core tests and 11 passing and two skipped application checks, without failures. Documentary comparison showed that established tools share core capabilities; MammoTrace combines mammography-specific checks, report examples and appraisal tasks. Comparative performance was not tested. No learners were recruited, and educational outcomes and scoring reliability were not evaluated. Conclusions MammoTrace provides a technically documented resource for supervised teaching of AI critical appraisal in medicine. Its contribution is the explicit connection between inspectable evidence and worked reasoning tasks. Comparative learner evaluation is needed to establish effects on appraisal competence, retention and transfer.

items.abstract: Abstract Background Road traffic injuries remain a major public health challenge, particularly among vulnerable road users. However, national evidence from Rwanda describing variations in police-reported injury outcomes by road-user category, injury severity, sex, crash location, and time remains limited. Methods We conducted a retrospective ecological study using aggregated Rwanda National Police data on road traffic injury outcomes recorded from January 2015 to August 2024. We described minor injuries, serious injuries, and crash-scene fatalities by road-user category, sex, crash location (Kigali versus outside Kigali), and time. Separate quasi-Poisson regression models examined associations between road-user category and reported injury counts, including interactions with crash location and adjusting for sex, season, and observation duration. Adjusted count ratios (aCRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported. Results Among 57,066 police-reported injury outcomes, 74.5% were minor injuries, 13.5% serious injuries, and 11.9% crash-scene fatalities. Motorcycles (37.7%), pedestrians (22.7%), and bicycles (15.7%) collectively accounted for 76.1% of reported outcomes. Although motorcycles contributed the largest number of reported outcomes, crash-scene fatalities represented a greater proportion of pedestrian-related outcomes (16.9%) than motorcycle-related outcomes (7.9%). items.title: Depressive symptom networks across physical activity levels among junior high school students following the winter break: a cross-sectional network comparison analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Background Adolescent depression has become an increasingly serious public health challenge, and physical activity is one of the validated intervention approaches. During the winter break, their physical activity shifts from school-organized physical education to self-directed exercise, which may widen variations in overall activity levels. We therefore focused on this period to compare the depressive symptom networks across junior high school students with different physical activity levels and to examine how network features differed across these groups. Methods A cross-sectional dataset was obtained from 1,459 Chinese junior high school students following the winter break. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the 10-item Center for Epidemiological Studies-Depression Scale (CES-D-10). Based on self-reported physical activity and the World Health Organization (WHO) guideline for moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), students were divided into Non-MVPA, Insufficient MVPA, and Sufficient MVPA groups. Depressive symptom networks were estimated using polychoric correlations and EBICglasso (gamma = 0.5), with strength and expected influence centrality computed. Network Comparison Tests (1000 permutations) compared network structure, global strength, edges, and centrality across the three MVPA groups, with Benjamini–Hochberg correction. Results No significant differences in network structure were observed between the Non-MVPA and Insufficient MVPA groups, but the Sufficient MVPA group showed a significantly distinct network. “Depressed” was the most central symptom across all three groups. The Sufficient MVPA group exhibited a specific rewiring: the edges linking “Lonely” to “Fearful”, “Effort”, and “Restless Sleep” weakened; the “Depressed” and “Lonely” edge strengthened; and the “Depressed” and “Get Going” edge shifted from positive to negative. Conclusion This study reveals a threshold pattern in the relationship between physical activity and depressive symptoms among junior high school students following the winter break. Interventions targeting central symptoms and strong edges may play a crucial role in the early prevention of depression. Furthermore, strategies aimed at providing guidance on physical activity during the break may be beneficial for safeguarding their mental health.

items.title: Machine Learning-Based Assessment of Geochemical Controls on Groundwater Arsenic Hazard in Bangladesh
items.abstract: Abstract Arsenic contamination in groundwater is a major global public health concern, affecting millions of people, particularly in Bangladesh. Understanding the mechanisms controlling arsenic mobilization is therefore essential for hazard assessment and mitigation. This study presents assessment of groundwater arsenic hazard by examining its association with selected geochemical factors through statistical analysis, machine learning, and spatial interpolation techniques. Although previous studies have applied machine learning to groundwater arsenic prediction in Bangladesh, the combined evaluation of geochemical associations, model performance, and spatial validation remains limited. To address this gap, principal component analysis (PCA), ANOVA F-test feature selection, Chi-square scoring function, and L-index were used to identify geochemical variables associated with arsenic occurrence. Three supervised machine learning algorithms were then applied to classify arsenic hazard levels. Among the individual predictors, Fe provided the highest maximum accuracy for As-level classification at approximately 92%, while P and Mn achieved accuracies of approximately 89%; sulfate also demonstrated predictive capability, although its spatial relationship with As was less consistent. The model outputs were further compared with spatial arsenic hotspots derived from Kriging interpolation. The findings improve understanding of the geochemical factors associated with arsenic mobilization and demonstrate the usefulness of data-driven models for groundwater arsenic hazard assessment.

items.title: Identification of Knee Osteoarthritis–Related Markers and Development of an Interpretable Random Forest Model Using SHAP
items.abstract: Abstract Background Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common chronic degenerative joint disorder associated with substantial impairment of quality of life and increasing public health burden. Early identification of individuals at elevated risk may facilitate timely risk stratification and intervention. This study aimed to identify key KOA-related markers using machine-learning approaches, interpret model predictions using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), and determine clinically relevant cut-off values for early screening. Methods This cross-sectional study included 1,243 participants. Candidate features were selected using three complementary approaches: least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and Boruta. Nine machine-learning algorithms were developed and compared, including logistic regression, XGBoost, random forest, LightGBM, and support vector machine. The optimal model was interpreted using SHAP to quantify feature contributions. Model performance was evaluated using multiple metrics, including area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, and Cohen’s kappa. Univariable ROC analyses were performed to estimate optimal cut-off values for candidate markers. Results Random forest achieved the best overall classification performance among the nine models. SHAP analysis identified 11 informative features for KOA prediction: age, EO%, uric acid (UA), MONO%, hemoglobin (HGB), CO₂, MCHC, LDL, TG, Urea/Crea, and CHOL/TG, with age showing the greatest contribution. The model achieved an AUC of 0.988 (95% CI, 0.979–0.998), accuracy of 0.941, sensitivity of 0.934, and specificity of 0.963 in the internal validation set. In the temporal validation cohort, performance remained strong, with an AUC of 0.972, accuracy of 0.910, sensitivity of 0.900, and specificity of 0.920. Age demonstrated the highest individual discrimination, with an optimal cut-off value of 51 years. Conclusions n interpretable random forest model based on routinely available demographic and laboratory variables showed strong discrimination for KOA classification. The SHAP-identified features, particularly age, may provide a multidimensional basis for KOA risk stratification. Further prospective multicenter studies are required to validate its clinical applicability.

items.title: Integrated Care Policy and Downward Intergenerational Support
items.abstract: Abstract Understanding how formal social protection alters intra-household resource allocation is vital for assessing public policy spillovers. Exploiting China’s Integrated Medical and Elderly Care Pilot Program as a quasi-experiment and using 2011–2018 CHARLS panel data, this study employs a difference-in-differences design to examine the policy’s impact on downward intergenerational financial transfers. We find that the program significantly increases both the probability (extensive margin) and amount (intensive margin) of financial support provided by older parents to adult children. These positive effects are stronger among low-income, younger-old, and less-educated households. Mechanism analyses indicate that care integration mitigates future health risk uncertainty and reduces precautionary savings, thereby relaxing intertemporal budget constraints. The released household resources primarily fuel non-periodic financial transfers rather than rigid commitments. Overall, this paper demonstrates that formal care integration crowds in family-based intergenerational support, providing important insights for optimizing public eldercare provision in rapidly aging societies.

items.title: Predicting and Analyzing Factors Influencing Breastfeeding Practices in Ethiopia Using Ensemble Machine Learning Algorithms
items.abstract: Abstract Background This explores the prediction of breastfeeding practices in Ethiopia using Ensemble machine learning algorithms. Exclusive breastfeeding is crucial for infant health and well-being, and understanding the factors influencing breastfeeding behaviors is vital for public health interventions. In Ethiopia, approximately one-third of infants are introduced to solid or liquid foods before the recommended six months of exclusive breastfeeding. Research shows that sub-optimal breastfeeding practices contribute to a significant percentage (24.0% − 27.0%) of infant deaths in Ethiopia and extend globally, with two-thirds of child deaths worldwide attributed to inadequate exclusive breastfeeding practices [9]. Therefore, this study aims to predict and identify factors associated with breastfeeding practices among Ethiopian children. A child who does not get proper breastfeeding has higher risks of health issues and several diseases such as Respiratory Infections, Allergies, Cognitive Development, Chronic Diseases, and sudden infant death syndrome (SIDS). generally, sub-optimal breastfeeding practices contribute to infant morbidity and mortality rates in Ethiopia [2]. Therefore, we need research and interventions to promote and support breastfeeding in our country people. Methods We collected data for the research from the Ethiopian Demographic and Health Survey (EDHS). The survey interviewed 23007 women of reproductive age between 15–49. Detailed information was collected on respondents’ background characteristics, marriage, maternal demographics, socioeconomic status, health indicators, cultural influences, preceding birth interval (months), succeeding birth interval (months), Education level, etc. The study discusses different types of ensemble learning techniques, such as bagging, boosting, and stacking, including algorithms like the Bagging Meta-Estimator, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Ada-boost, K Neighbors Classifier, Logistic Regression, and Cat-boost and using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recalls, and F1-score for performance evaluated. Results The Bagging Meta-Estimator Algorithm appears to be the best-performing model, with the highest Cross-Validation Accuracy of (97.30%) and strong overall performance metrics and Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Ada-boost, K Neighbors Classifier, Logistic Regression, and Cat-boost appears 96.23%, 95.93%, 95%, 95%, 91.89% and 96.25% respectively. Conclusion This study highlights the effectiveness of ensemble machine learning algorithms in predicting and analyzing factors affecting breastfeeding practices in Ethiopia. Utilizing a comprehensive dataset from the Ethiopian Demographic and Health Survey (EDHS), various ensemble learning techniques such as bagging, boosting, and stacking were applied to identify the most accurate predictive models. The findings reveal that ensemble methods significantly outperform traditional statistical models and simpler machine learning approaches in terms of prediction accuracy and robustness.

items.title: Cardiometabolic abnormality burden and the emergence and recovery of health deficits in middle-aged and older adults: a harmonized longitudinal study across three national cohorts
items.abstract: Abstract Background Cardiometabolic abnormalities are common, potentially modifiable public health concerns, but studies of frailty usually examine net deficit burden or incident frailty and cannot show whether associations reflect more new deficits, less recovery, or both. We examined these two transition processes across three national aging cohorts. Methods This harmonized longitudinal secondary analysis included 25,590 adults aged 50 years or older from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, the Health and Retirement Study, and the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing. Baseline burden counted central obesity, high blood pressure, and diagnosed or treated diabetes (0–3). Weighted discrete-time complementary log-log models estimated item-level emergence and recovery across 18 potentially reversible deficits. Cohort-specific estimates were combined by random-effects meta-analysis, and marginal standardization yielded model-based annualized one-year transition probabilities and expected net change. Results Emergence analyses included 23,689 participants and 130,915 person-item-interval transition events; recovery analyses included 22,216 participants and 99,789 events. Per additional abnormality, pooled Model A hazard ratios were 1.125 (95% confidence interval 1.073–1.179; I²=90.9%) for emergence and 0.933 (0.921–0.946; I²=0%) for recovery. Estimates remained directionally consistent after additional adjustment for interval-start deficit proportion. Across cohorts, three versus zero abnormalities corresponded to a 1.54–1.89-percentage-point higher annualized emergence probability, a 3.38–4.58-point lower recovery probability, and a 2.00–2.27-point more adverse expected one-year change in health-deficit proportion. Conclusions Greater cardiometabolic abnormality burden was associated with both more observed deficit emergence and less observed recovery across cohorts in China, the United States, and England. Separating these processes adds dynamic information to aggregate deficit measures and may inform chronic-disease and healthy-aging research. The observational, model-based estimates do not establish causal effects, intervention benefits, or predictive utility.

items.title: Health and occupational implications of heatwave exposure in Southern India
items.abstract: Abstract Background and Objective The global average surface temperature has surpassed 1.55°C, driving climate and environmental changes that pose an explicit and escalating threat to public health. People with low socio-economic status and the elderly are susceptible to heat-induced illnesses. This study aimed to examine outcomes of heatwave exposure and its association with physical and mental health, work productivity, and coping mechanisms. Methods The study used an analytical cross-sectional design to examine health outcomes, work productivity, and coping mechanisms associated with heatwave exposure in Chennai and Chengalpattu districts, Tamil Nadu, India. A convenience sampling technique was employed to recruit 944 participants. The semi-structured interview schedule was used to collect information. Results 92.8% of study participants were exposed to heatwaves. There was an association between heatwave exposure and outcomes of physical health, mental health issues, work productivity, and coping strategies . Monthly mean income loss differences across occupational groups due to exposure were found across occupational groups (F (2746) =3.49, p=.031, η²=.009). items.title: Kindergarten measles vaccination coverage and the 2025–2026 measles resurgence in the United States: a state-level analysis of public surveillance data
items.abstract: Abstract Background In November 2026, the United States lost the measles elimination status it had held since 2000. This study examined whether states with lower kindergarten measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccination coverage had more measles during the 2025–2026 resurgence, and how coverage changed before, during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods In this ecological study, kindergarten MMR coverage and non-medical exemptions (CDC SchoolVaxView, 2009–10 to 2025–26) were combined with state and county measles case counts, census population estimates and national data for Canada and Mexico. Associations were assessed with Spearman correlation and negative binomial regression. Results National coverage fell from 95.2% in 2019–20 to 92.4% in 2025–26, and non-medical exemptions rose from 2.2% to 4.0%. Coverage dropped in most states during the pandemic and did not recover afterward. Measles cases averaged 410 per year before the pandemic, 61 during it and 2,011 after it. Each 1-percentage-point decrease in coverage was associated with 15% more cases (incidence rate ratio 1.15, 95% CI 1.01–1.31), although the association was sensitive to the exclusion of single states and coverage did not predict large outbreaks. Of 8,025 cases with county data, 96.8% were locally acquired, and half occurred in 18 counties or health regions. Conclusions Kindergarten MMR coverage fell during the pandemic and has not recovered. States with lower coverage had more measles, and cases were concentrated in a few counties. Restoring coverage above 95% is needed to re-establish elimination.

items.title: Disenfranchised Grief: Emergency Department Nurses’ Experiences of Suicide Deaths Among Children and Adolescents : A Qualitative Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Suicide among children and adolescents has emerged as a major global public health concern. As frontline professionals involved in resuscitation, death management, and family support, emergency department nurses may experience substantial occupational emotional burden following these events. However, nurses’ experiences following suicide deaths among children and adolescents remain insufficiently understood, particularly within cultural contexts where suicide-related loss may be difficult to openly acknowledge. Methods: A qualitative descriptive study design was adopted. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 16 emergency department nurses from three tertiary hospitals in Zhejiang Province, China. Participants were recruited using purposive sampling combined with snowball sampling. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis. Results: Three overarching themes were identified: (1) emotional impact—nurses experienced profound initial emotional and sensory responses, followed by grief, helplessness, guilt, persistent recollection, and emotional distress; participants who were parents described particularly strong emotional involvement; (2) cognitive reconstruction—through reflection on these events, nurses developed greater empathy toward bereaved families, gained more nuanced understandings of suicidal behavior, reconsidered their own family and parenting beliefs, and expanded their professional roles; and (3) practical dilemmas—nurses encountered challenges related to their competence in pediatric emergency care, communication with bereaved families, and ethical decision-making during resuscitation. These challenges reflected the need for enhanced professional training and organizational support within emergency care settings. Conclusion: Suicide deaths among children and adolescents represent highly challenging clinical events that may evoke significant emotional distress, trauma-related responses, and changes in emergency department nurses’ professional perspectives. These findings highlight the need for structured occupational psychological support, targeted competency-based education, and humanistic care strategies to support nurses involved in suicide-related emergency care and improve care for bereaved families. Patient or Public Contribution Patients and members of the public were not involved in the design, conduct, analysis, or reporting of this study.

items.title: Coordination and joint authority in the global health architecture: a document-based mapping of current mechanisms and implications for reform
items.abstract: Abstract Background Reform of the global health architecture seeks stronger coordination and joint decision-making among organisations, but proposals rarely specify what existing mechanisms can decide or whom their decisions bind. We mapped the formal authority of the mechanisms in which organisations and governments meet. Methods We compiled 167 current coordination and decision-making mechanisms from public documents and analysed 156 after excluding 11 technical networks. The main analysis covered 44 co-led mechanisms, in which two or more organisations participate as full members alongside governments; 112 other mechanisms provided comparisons. Two coders independently assessed the initial 151 entries on a five-step authority scale. Later additions were checked by the lead author. We examined decision rules, decision objects, co-location and shared membership, with alternative coding and classification scenarios. Results Of the 44 co-led mechanisms, 16 (36.4%) held decision rights under the main coding and 24 (54.5%) under an alternative coding of eight disputed cases. Under both scenarios, decisions concerned defined funds, partnerships, programmes or frameworks. Nine of 13 mechanisms coded as taking binding decisions had rules permitting non-unanimous decisions. No document reviewed gave a co-led mechanism authority over participating organisations' separate budgets or policies. Between 55% and 79% of mechanisms of each type shared a health area and level with another. Shared-member comparisons were limited by incomplete name extraction and did not establish duplication. Illustrative precedents existed for four designs of coordination across governing bodies, with different sources and limits of authority. Conclusions Joint decision-making among organisations exists, but within defined instruments. Reform proposals should state what is to be decided, whether existing mandates cover it and which changes need new agreements; options that confer new binding authority require approval by the competent bodies under the applicable instruments.

items.title: Impact of Antimicrobial Stewardship on Guideline-concordant initial antibiotic therapy for Community-Acquired Pneumonia: An Emergency Department Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Deviations from antibiotic guidelines remain public health issue for antimicrobial resistance in community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). In emergency department (ED) setting, antimicrobial stewardship interventions (ASI) have shown variable efficacy in addressing this issue. Objective To assess the impact of a combined educational and computerized ASI on prescribing concordance. Methods We conducted a prospective observational study in two French EDs (Center 1 and Center 2) between June and November 2022. Patients with CAP who required hospitalization were included. Phase 1 included data from both centers. In Phase 2, conducted only in Center 1, the intervention consisted of a 30-minute training session and deployment of a computerized pop-up alert. The primary outcome was the rate of guideline-concordant initial prescription with CAP guidelines. Results Among the 241 patients included, antibiotic guideline-concordant initial antibiotic prescription in Phase 1 was 72% at Center 1. The most frequent cause of non-concordance involved the use of monotherapy when dual therapy was recommended (55% of non-concordant prescriptions). In Phase 2, global concordance remained stable at 73%. We noted an increase in non-concordant monotherapy (71% of non-compliant prescriptions). Conclusion Initial antibiotic prescribing for CAP in the ED shows persistent gaps in concordance with current guidelines, particularly in adjusting therapy to severity. A single-session educational and computerized ASI did not significantly improve prescription concordance. Further studies using controlled designs and sustained interventions are needed to assess effective strategies for improving antibiotic prescribing in the ED.

items.title: Case Report: From Weight Loss Supplement to Heavy Metal Toxicity: A Case Report of Chronic Lead Poisoning
items.abstract: Introduction Lead poisoning is a significant environmental health hazard that can affect multiple organ systems, particularly the nervous, gastrointestinal, and hematological systems. Both acute and chronic low-level exposures can cause serious health consequences. Case presentation We report the case of a 38-years-old female presenting with non-specific gastrointestinal and neurological symptoms, later diagnosed with chronic lead poisoning attributed to the use of Garcinia cambogia contaminated with lead. The patient exhibited severe anemia, chronic fatigue, and seizures. The diagnosis was supported by findings of basophilic stippling on a peripheral blood smear and elevated blood lead levels (>65 mcg/dL). She was managed successfully with a combination of chelation therapy using Dimercaprol and Penicillamine, which resulted in symptomatic improvement and reduced lead levels. Conclusion This case highlights the diagnostic challenges due to vague clinical presentations of heavy metal poisoning and reinforces the need for stringent regulation of complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) and cosmetic products as well as public awareness to prevent such environmental health hazards.

items.title: Gambling and gambling harms in the offspring generation of the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children.
items.abstract: Gambling in Great Britain is a multi-billion-pound industry that has expanded exponentially over the past 30 years. At the same time, gambling is increasingly recognised as a significant public health issue due to its harmful impact on health and wellbeing of people experiencing gambling problems, those around them, communities and wider society. The increased availability of gambling and the expansion of opportunities to gamble online have led to increases in the number of young people who gamble on a regular basis. There is, however, a lack of longitudinal data that tracks young people’s experiences of gambling and gambling harms over time. Data from the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC), a prospective population-based cohort study, continues to help address this gap. Pregnant women (Generation 0 - G0s) with expected delivery dates in 1991 and 1992 were recruited, and the study has followed them, their partners and their offspring (Generation 1 - G1s) for over 30 years. Data on gambling activity and gambling harms were collected from the study offspring at ages 17, 20, 24, 28 (during the COVID-19 pandemic) and 30. This data note documents the questionnaire data relating to the G1’s gambling activity and gambling behaviours at these five timepoints. The ALSPAC gambling study has previously utilised these data to identify antecedents for regular gambling in young adults and investigate harms associated with gambling. This data note offers a valuable opportunity for researchers to better understand the ALSPAC gambling variables and how they are typically handled, and investigate the growing issue of gambling in young adults, longitudinally.

items.title: Biotechnological Innovations and Health Communication: An Interprofessional Education Challenge
items.abstract: Introduction: The rapid pace of biotechnological advances, exemplified by the development of mRNA vaccines, represents a milestone in the response to public health emergencies. These advances, however, coexist with high levels of vaccine hesitancy and erosion of public trust. Traditional health professions education, predominantly uniprofessional and fragmented, deepens technocratic asymmetry and generates communication noise that amplifies epistemological misalignment and facilitates the spread of misinformation. In this context, Interprofessional Education (IPE) emerges as a structural response capable of integrating teams, dismantling disciplinary silos, and unifying scientific discourse at the frontline of care. Methods This is a narrative review of the literature with an analytical and conceptual character. Institutional frameworks (WHO and IPEC), epidemiological literature on hesitancy and vaccination coverage, and empirical studies evaluating the impact of educational interventions (uniprofessional and interprofessional) on knowledge, self-efficacy, and communication skills of health students and professionals were analyzed. Results The literature shows that prior knowledge of medical, nursing, and pharmacy students regarding immunization is critically low (often <50%). While uniprofessional approaches focus on theoretical memorization, IPE interventions based on clinical simulations with standardized patients produced marked gains in practical skills, with 98% of participants reporting the ability to address misinformation in clinical encounters. These interventions also promoted standardization of guidance and shared responsibility across professions. Conclusion Susceptibility to false narratives functions as a symptom of educational gaps and communication failures within the health system itself. IPE consolidates risk communication as a transversal, human, and empathic competence that is essential for restoring community trust and ensuring the social effectiveness of biotechnological innovations.

items.title: Omnichannel retailing, service quality, brand trust, and customer brand engagement as drivers of brand advocacy in Indonesian health care services: A cross-sectional PLS-SEM study
items.abstract: Background: Indonesian health care providers increasingly integrate physical and digital channels, yet how patients come to advocate for a provider remains poorly understood. This study extends the stimulus–organism–response (S-O-R) framework to Indonesian health care, examining omnichannel retailing, service quality, brand trust, customer brand engagement, and brand advocacy in a single model, and asks whether channel integration or service quality is more strongly associated with patient trust. Methods A purposive sample of 324 patients at a primary clinic, a private hospital, and a regional public hospital in Greater Jakarta completed a digitally administered 49-item, five-point Likert-type questionnaire after the service encounter. The instrument was adapted from validated English-language scales through back-translation, expert content validation, face validation, and a pretest (n = 50). Partial least squares structural equation modelling used a disjoint two-stage approach for higher-order constructs and 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. Results All six hypotheses were supported. Service quality was associated with trust (β = 0.430) almost twice as strongly as omnichannel retailing (β = 0.259). Trust was associated with customer brand engagement (β = 0.442), the strongest path. The three paths into advocacy, from engagement (β = 0.239), trust (β = 0.209), and omnichannel retailing (β = 0.206), were of comparable size. All seven indirect paths were significant; 71.8% of omnichannel retailing

items.title: Association between immune–inflammatory biomarkers and circulating levels of carbohydrate Antigen 125 in heart failure: protocol for a systematic review.
items.abstract: Background Cardiovascular diseases remain one of the leading causes of death worldwide, and heart failure (HF) represents a major global public health challenge, affecting an estimated 64 million people globally. The pathophysiology of HF is multifactorially complex and poorly understood. Understanding the role of inflammation in relation to CA125 levels will consolidate and enhance their clinical and prognostic value in the risk assessment, stratification and clinical management of HF. Hence, this review aims to provide a comprehensive synthesis of the available evidence on the relationship between immune-inflammatory activation and circulating CA125 concentrations in heart failure. Methods An extensive search will be conducted on the following databases: MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science. The Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL) and Cochrane Central Register of Clinical Trials (CENTRAL) will also be searched. Two reviewers will independently screen studies for eligibility using predefined criteria. The quality assessment and risk of bias of included studies will be assessed using the modified Downs and Black’s checklist. The Review Manager will be used for statistical analysis. The overall quality of included studies will be assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation assessment tool. Discussions In HF management, biomarkers are essential for accurate diagnosis and risk stratification. CA125 has emerged as a key link between clinical congestion, immune-inflammatory activation, and adverse patient outcomes; however, current evidence regarding its inflammatory trigger remains fragmented. This review explores whether inflammatory pathways drive CA125 elevation independently of mechanical congestion, establishing its clinical utility and biological significance alongside conventional HF biomarkers. Ethics, patient and public involvement This is a review of existing studies and will not require ethical approval. Hence, patients and the public will not be involved in the study. Systematic review registration : PROSPERO registration number: CRD42022310386.

items.title: Using Stimulants to Treat Pain Among a Cohort of People With Non-Cancer Chronic Pain.
items.abstract: Chronic pain is prevalent in the United States, especially among people who use substances. There is evidence that stimulants may help people achieve pain relief. We examined using unregulated stimulants (cocaine or methamphetamine) to self-manage pain and subsequent pain, depression, and psychological distress. We used data from the Cohort Study of Opioids, Pain, and Safety in an era of Changing Policy study, which enrolled participants with chronic non-cancer pain who were prescribed opioid analgesics for ≥3 of the last 12 months and used unregulated opioids or stimulants in their lifetime. At baseline and up to 4 annual visits, we asked about unregulated stimulant use, whether unregulated stimulants were used for pain management, average pain level (0-10), depression, and psychological distress. Among participants who used unregulated stimulants, we compared characteristics by whether or not participants used unregulated stimulants to self-manage pain. We used Pearson chi-squared tests to compare categorical variables, with Fisher's exact tests for expected cell counts <5, and Wilcoxon rank sum tests to compare medians. We conducted 3 generalized estimating equations to assess the association of using stimulants for pain management with subsequent pain, depression, and psychological distress. Among 123 (41%) participants who used stimulants during the study, 72 (59%) used them to treat pain. A significantly higher proportion who used stimulants to treat pain had experienced homelessness (92% vs 73%, P < .01). Using stimulants to treat pain was associated with 1.67 (95% CI: 1.09-2.55, P = .02) and 2.16 (95% CI: 1.33-3.51, P < .01) times the adjusted odds of an increase in average pain of 1 point and depression, respectively. There was no association with psychological distress. This manuscript provides credible longitudinal observational evidence that pain-directed stimulant use is common and marks those with a worse clinical trajectory, but it does not establish that stimulant use causes worsening pain or depression. Providers should consider pain management when addressing stimulant use and future research should investigate these relationships in more depth.

items.title: Embedding sexual and reproductive health in climate and disaster preparedness: a MISP-based comparative policy analysis of Indonesia and Kenya.
items.abstract: Climate-related hazards disrupt essential health services, while sexual and reproductive health remains weakly integrated into preparedness planning. The Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) defines priority reproductive-health functions during humanitarian emergencies and major service disruptions. This study compared how Indonesian and Kenyan national policies operationalise MISP-aligned functions within climate and disaster preparedness. Six national policy instruments were analysed across disaster governance, health preparedness, and reproductive-health policy domains. A pre-specified codebook assessed six MISP service domains and four implementation-enabling domains across the included documents. Document-domain cells were classified as absent, recognised without operationalisation, or operationalised through at least one verifiable feature. Indonesia contained operational features in 12 of 30 document-domain cells, compared with three in Kenya. Implementation density was 36/60 (60.0%) for Indonesia and 26/60 (43.3%) for Kenya. Indonesia's assessed regulations linked the emergency service mandate to health-crisis coordination. Kenya's assessed instruments provided detailed climate-health planning but did not specify an explicit MISP activation pathway. The assessed instruments contained complementary yet incomplete provisions for reproductive-health continuity during climate-related emergencies. Connecting crisis triggers, leadership, minimum services, commodities, financing, and monitoring could strengthen continuity. Other settings could adapt these policy design features to their governance arrangements and resources.

items.title: Perspectives of adolescents and youth on a task-shifting mental health intervention in urban slum communities of Freetown, Sierra Leone.
items.abstract: Mental health disorders and substance use among young people represent critical public health challenges in Sierra Leone, yet access to care remains severely limited. Task-shifting interventions that train young people to deliver peer-based mental health support offer a promising approach for addressing service gaps in resource-constrained settings. This study explored young people's perceptions and lived experiences of the Brave Heart task-shifting training program. We used a qualitative descriptive design, incorporating in-depth interviews and focus group discussions with 18 youths (ages 10-24 y) who completed the Brave Heart training program in two urban slum communities in Freetown, Sierra Leone. We purposively selected participants based on post-training competency scores (≥70%) and willingness to participate. We collected data in July 2025 and analysed them using inductive thematic analysis. Four themes emerged: understanding of mental health and substance use, lived experiences of the task-shifting intervention training program, confidence in applying learned skills and readiness to support peers. Participants demonstrated enhanced mental health literacy, identified diverse substance types and associated risks and reported increased confidence in refusing substances. Participants perceived the program as highly relevant and a critical addition to community-based prevention. Several participants had already initiated peer education conversations before training concluded. Participants perceived the Brave Heart program as effectively preparing young people to serve as peer mental health supporters in resource-constrained settings, suggesting the potential for scalable youth-led prevention in similar contexts.

items.title: Impact of a sepsis clinical decision support system and workflow on sepsis-associated mortality or hospice discharge: A multihospital quasi-experimental study from 2018 to 2024.
items.abstract: Clinical decision support (CDS) tools may enhance sepsis care delivery by streamlining recognition, reducing workflow-related delays, and facilitating timely treatment initiation. This study evaluated the impact of the sepsis navigation tool (SNT), a CDS-driven quality improvement initiative, on all-cause in-hospital mortality or hospice discharge and adherence to key sepsis care processes. This retrospective, quasi-experimental study utilized electronic health record data from 631,620 adult acute care hospitalizations discharged from 10 hospitals within a large health system between 2018 and 2024. The SNT provided an optimized interface displaying sepsis metrics, a real-time sepsis timer, and shortcuts to sepsis documentation and order sets. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, piecewise linear regression models, and multivariable logistic regression models. Sepsis was present in 50,911 (8.1%) hospitalizations. Following SNT implementation, mortality/hospice rates declined among sepsis (18.8%-16.3%; p < .001) and septic shock (40.0%-36.4%; p < .001) hospitalizations. Monthly mortality/hospice trends improved among sepsis hospitalizations (adjusted slope difference: 0.217%; p < .001) but not non-sepsis hospitalizations (adjusted slope difference: 0.014%; p = .207). Compared with pre-intervention, the post-intervention period had lower odds of mortality/hospice for sepsis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=0.73; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.69-0.77) and septic shock (aOR=0.73; 95% CI = 0.68-0.79) hospitalizations, respectively. Intensive care unit admission rates, order set utilization, hospital length of stay, blood culture collection timing, and antibiotic administration timing also improved in sepsis hospitalizations. This multihospital study demonstrated improvements in sepsis outcomes and care process measures following SNT implementation. Continued evaluation and optimization of sepsis CDS and artificial intelligence tools will be critical to further improving sepsis care.

items.title: Effectiveness of a safe inhalation pipe provision intervention on health risk practices and engagement in services for people who use crack in England: Findings from a quasi-experimental study.
items.abstract: To evaluate the effectiveness of a safe inhalation pipe provision (SIPP) intervention on use of someone else's pipe, homemade pipes and ash-based filters, injecting, respiratory symptoms and engagement with drug services among people who use crack-cocaine in England. Non-randomised pre-post intervention evaluation with non-equivalent control groups using cross-sectional surveys 6 months apart (February 2023-July 2024). Survey data were linked to drug service records to measure attendance. Intervention uptake was monitored at point of contact. Two independent drug services and one national provider (Change Grow Live, CGL), a sex worker organisation and peer networks delivered SIPP in Bristol, Nottingham and Mansfield. CGL provided treatment as usual in Birmingham, Coventry and Warwickshire. Adults aged ≥18 years who had smoked or injected crack in the past 28 days recruited at baseline (n = 733) and endline (n = 738). Drug services and peer networks distributed SIPP kits (glass pipe, gauzes, mouthpieces and push-stick) over six months. Drug service providers received e-learning on harm reduction to promote safer crack use, including use of other people's pipes. Comparison sites delivered treatment as usual. Primary outcome was use of someone else's pipe in the past 28 days. Secondary outcomes included: use of homemade pipes and improvised ash-based filters, injecting, acute injuries, respiratory symptoms (28 days) and drug service engagement (six months). Frequency (days) of using someone else's pipe, homemade pipes and injecting was also assessed. Participants had a median age of 42 years and 30% were female at baseline; the proportion female at SIPP sites fell to 21% at endline. At endline, participants in intervention sites were less likely than those in comparison sites to smoke with someone else's pipe [203/502 (40.5%) vs. 112/236 (47.5%); adjusted odds ratio (AOR) = 0.65, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.46-0.92]. They were less likely to use homemade pipes (AOR = 0.25, 95% CI = 0.15-0.42), ash-based filters (AOR = 0.57, 95% CI = 0.35-0.93) or inject (AOR = 0.50, 95% CI = 0.33-0.73). They reported 2.98 fewer days using someone else's pipe (95% CI = -4.17 to -1.79), 3.36 fewer days injecting (95% CI = -4.69 to -2.04) and 5.57 fewer days using homemade pipes (95% CI = -7.21 to -3.94). There was no evidence for differences in respiratory symptoms (AOR = 1.13, 95% CI = 0.81-1.59) or attendance at drug services measured via data linkage (AOR = 1.04 95% CI = 0.72-1.50). Self-reported attendance was lower in intervention sites, but intervention monitoring suggest SIPP provision facilitated first-time contact with services. Safer inhalation pipe provision appears to be associated with reductions in high-risk crack-cocaine use practices and may create opportunities for engagement with drug services.

items.title: The role of visual and vestibular disturbances in predicting four-week recovery following acute concussion: a cohort study by sex (from the Toronto concussion study).
items.abstract: Visual and vestibular disturbances (VVD) are common following concussion, but their relationship with recovery and potential sex differences remains unclear. To examine the relationship between early VVD and four-week recovery overall and by sex in community-dwelling adults. This prospective longitudinal study included 122 adults (mean age 36.6 years; 64.6% female) assessed within one week and again four weeks post-concussion. VVD were assessed using the Sport Concussion Assessment Tool-5th Edition (SCAT-5) and a modified Vestibular/Ocular Motor Screen (mVOMS). Recovery was determined by physician evaluation. Logistic regression examined associations between early VVD and recovery while adjusting for injury and sociodemographic covariates. Male and female participants demonstrated different baseline VVD patterns on the SCAT-5 and mVOMS. At four weeks, 27.9% had recovered. Baseline SCAT-5 visual and vestibular symptoms were not associated with recovery, whereas mVOMS positivity (symptom increase ≥ 4) was associated with non-recovery. No significant sex differences were observed in the association between early VVD and recovery. Early mVOMS positivity may have prognostic value for identifying community-dwelling adults at risk of delayed concussion recovery, whereas self-reported visual and vestibular symptoms alone may not. Although early symptom profiles differed by sex, recovery trajectories did not.

items.title: Effectiveness of Equipment, Nutrition, Pharmacology, and Behavioural Interventions for Reducing Injury and Attrition in Tactical Recruits: A Systematic Review With Meta-Analyses.
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To estimate the effectiveness of equipment, nutrition, pharmacology, and behavioural interventions in reducing injury and attrition in tactical recruits. DESIGN: Systematic review with meta-analysis of intervention studies LITERATURE Search: Six databases searched from 2000 to 2025 STUDY SELECTION CRITERIA: Quasi-experimental and randomised controlled trials (RCTs) examining the effectiveness of non-exercise interventions on injury and attrition (regardless of cause) in tactical recruits. DATA SYNTHESIS: Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool. Intervention effects were estimated using inverse-variance random-effects meta-analyses, yielding log odds ratios (log ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Certainty of evidence was judged using Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. RESULTS: This review included thirty-two studies (18 quasi-experimental, 14 RCTs; n = 319,791 recruits). From all interventions identified, footwear and orthoses did not reduce injuries (Log OR=-0.081, 95%CI=-0.235 to 0.072) or attrition (Log OR=-0.141, 95%CI=-0.340 to 0.058). Nutrition interventions reduced injuries (education) (Log OR=1.147, 95%CI=0.254 to 2.041) and attrition (supplementation) (Log OR=0.187, 95%CI=0.015 to 0.360). Attrition was reduced by additional healthcare provider oversight (Log OR=0.144, 95%CI=0.003 to 0.286), but not by mental health-focused interventions (Log OR=0.221, 95%CI=-0.159 to 0.601). The certainty of the evidence was very low for all estimates. CONCLUSIONS: Footwear, orthoses, and mental health-focused interventions did not reduce injury or attrition in military recruits. Nutrition appears to be effective in reducing injury and attrition, whereas healthcare provider oversight may reduce attrition in tactical personnel. These findings are based on very low certainty evidence and require cautious interpretation. REGISTRATION: CRD420251010400 (PROSPERO).

items.title: The COVID-19 pandemic and changes in biopharma financing and mergers and acquisitions (M&A): a comparative analysis of pandemic and Post-pandemic periods (2020-2025).
items.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent monetary tightening may have changed biopharma financing and mergers and acquisitions (M&A), but transaction-level comparative evidence is limited. Using Crunchbase, we extracted 11,571 financing deals and 1,615 M&A transactions in Health Care-Biopharma and Pharmaceutical industries from 1 January 2020 to 31 December 2025, comparing 2020-2022 (pandemic) with 2023-2025 (post-pandemic). We described deal counts, disclosed amounts, deal-size distributions, instrument mix, industry, geography and M&A characteristics, with period-specific outlier sensitivity and disclosure-bias assessments. Financing deal counts fell 8.6% (6,045 to 5,526), while disclosed funding rose 43.0% (USD 233.74B to 334.20B). This increase was more than accounted for by Post-initial public offering (IPO) Debt (+USD 116.46B); excluding Post-IPO Debt, disclosed financing fell approximately 9.3%. Median deal size fell from USD 9.65M to 6.50M, while mean rose from USD 50.70M to 77.00M. Seed/Series A/Series B combined fell from 34.7% to 28.1% of deals. M&A counts fell 32.8% (966 to 649); among disclosed deals, mean value rose 46.8% to USD 1.56B, but aggregate disclosed value fell slightly. Post-pandemic patterns are consistent with greater capital concentration and later-stage/public-market financing, but high non-disclosure and confounding limit causal and structural-break claims.

items.title: Association Between prenatal cannabis use and pregnancy loss: a population-based retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Biological evidence suggests prenatal cannabis exposure may increase risks of miscarriage and stillbirth, but epidemiologic studies are limited by methodological weaknesses. Addressing these gaps, we evaluated associations between prenatal cannabis use and pregnancy loss in a population-based retrospective cohort. The study included 233,860 pregnancies (184,296 individuals) universally screened for substance use upon entry into prenatal care (~8-10 gestational weeks) between January 1, 2011 and September 30, 2019. Prenatal cannabis use was defined as any use (self-report or urine toxicology) and frequency (self-report). Miscarriage and stillbirth outcomes were obtained from electronic health records and California vital records. Cox proportional hazards models were conducted separately for miscarriage and stillbirth adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics, maternal comorbidities, and maternal prenatal use of other non-cannabis substances. The cohort was 38.6% non-Hispanic White, with mean (SD) maternal age 30.6 (5.5) years; 6.6% screened positive for cannabis. Overall, 5.5% of pregnancies ended in miscarriage and 0.4% in stillbirth. Prenatal cannabis use (vs. none) was associated with a 13% increased risk of miscarriage occurring after entry into prenatal care (~8-10 weeks gestation; aHR: 1.13,95%CI: 1.03-1.22), rising to ~30% after excluding other substance use. Weekly (aHR: 1.32,95%CI: 1.07-1.63) and daily (aHR: 1.29,95% CI: 1.02-1.63) use (vs. no use) showed similar increases. No association was observed for stillbirth. These findings add to the growing body of evidence linking prenatal cannabis use with adverse pregnancy outcomes and may help inform clinical counseling, harm reduction strategies, and public health policies.

items.title: Comparing randomized trials.
items.abstract: Disagreements between well-conducted randomized trials addressing the same causal question generate intense discussion of possible explanations and sometimes stir controversy. In this issue of the Journal, Virkud et al. (Am J Epidemiol. 2025; doi:10.1093/aje/kwaf202) compared two double-blind randomized trials of 17-α-hydroxyprogesterone caproate (17-OHPC) for the prevention of recurrent preterm birth, considering differences in population characteristics as the leading explanation for the disagreement between the trials' marginal (population-averaged) results. In this commentary, we outline considerations for comparing randomized trials addressing the same causal question, including explanations beyond differences in population characteristics. We highlight parallels between comparing trials and benchmarking observational analyses against trials, and note that selection of between-study comparisons for interrogation may introduce statistical complications that should be considered alongside causal issues. We emphasize that formal between-study comparisons rest on long chains of causal and statistical assumptions, and that the interpretation of disagreements requires substantive knowledge to assess the plausibility of competing explanations. Technical details are presented in a companion report.

items.title: The prevalence and economic burden of disease-related malnutrition in Ireland: an update.
items.abstract: To update estimated prevalence of disease-related malnutrition (DRM) in Ireland and its impact on public health and social-care expenditure in 2023. Prevalence by care setting was derived from the 2023 IrSPEN/INDI National Malnutrition Survey (NMS23) and age-standardised comparisons with UK and European studies where Irish data were incomplete. Public costs were estimated by applying unit-cost data from official sources to activity attributable to DRM, based on point prevalence, with sensitivity analyses used to reflect uncertainty regarding variation in prevalence and higher healthcare utilisation of patients with DRM not captured in point prevalence estimates. Acute hospitals (excluding maternity), long-term and primary care. Adults aged ≥18 years receiving hospital or specified community health/social-care services in 2023. Point prevalence of DRM in 2023 was 5·1 % of the adult population, affecting approximately 220 000 people, 59 % aged ≥65 years. The annual public cost attributable to DRM was estimated at €2·7 billion, 11·5 % of the 2023 public healthcare budget. Hospital care accounted for 61 % of DRM-related costs. Since 2008, the national burden has increased by 90 %, driven by ageing, higher hospital activity and rising unit costs. Public expenditure on oral and enteral nutrition support represented less than 2 % of DRM-attributable costs. DRM imposes a substantial and growing burden on Ireland's healthcare system, concentrated in older adults. While screening is now routine in hospitals and nursing homes, extending systematic screening and dietetic intervention to high-risk day-ward and community settings is warranted to prevent continued increases in prevalence and cost.

items.title: Time to public reimbursement of new medical technologies in Australia and England: a systematic review.
items.abstract: This study aimed to synthesize reported timelines to health technology assessment (HTA) recommendation and publicly funded reimbursement for new medical technologies in Australia and England and to identify reported determinants of delay. A qualitative systematic review was conducted according to a prespecified protocol. Embase, PubMed, and Scopus were searched for English-language studies published from 2015 onward, supplemented by targeted grey literature searches. Eligible studies reported extractable quantitative HTA or reimbursement timelines for new technologies (pharmaceuticals, devices, or diagnostics) funded in Australia or England. Reported time metrics were mapped to a time-event framework including registration, HTA, and publicly funded access milestones. Given substantial heterogeneity in end point definitions and reporting, synthesis was descriptive. Nine studies met the inclusion criteria. All reported on pharmaceuticals and no eligible studies were identified for medical devices or diagnostics. Most studies reported timelines for England and focused on time from registration to final HTA outcome, whereas Australian evidence more clearly captured the interval between positive HTA recommendation and reimbursement. Reported time from registration to final HTA outcome ranged from 265 to 840 days depending on study scope. Reported time from registration to publicly funded access ranged from 310 to 679 days. Evidence on determinants of delay was sparse and inconsistently reported. Reported timelines to HTA recommendation and public reimbursement are substantial and highly variable in Australia and England, but are measured inconsistently across the literature. Greater standardization in reporting, clearer distinction between HTA and reimbursement milestones, and dedicated research on device and diagnostic pathways are needed.

items.title: Effect of Cysteamine on 90-Day Mortality in Patients With Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia: The REMAP-CAP (Randomized Embedded Multifactorial Adaptive Platform for Community-Acquired Pneumonia) Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract: Cysteamine has antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory and antibiotic-potentiating effects. We evaluated IV cysteamine in critically ill patients with community-acquired pneumonia within REMAP-CAP (Randomized Embedded Multifactorial Adaptive Platform for Community-Acquired Pneumonia) trial, an international adaptive platform trial evaluating multiple interventions across several therapeutic domains. Adults requiring respiratory or cardiovascular organ support were randomized within the cysteamine domain to IV cysteamine (5 mg/kg every 8 hr for up to 10 d) or control. The dichotomous primary outcome was 90-day all-cause mortality, analyzed using Bayesian logistic regression. Recruitment to this domain stopped for operational futility before predefined statistical thresholds were met. Thirty-six patients received cysteamine (n = 19) or control (n = 17). Ninety-day mortality was 26% vs. 35%, respectively (odds ratio 0.64, 95% credible interval 0.18-2.19), with a 76% posterior probability of benefit. One serious adverse event occurred, unrelated to cysteamine. These preliminary findings suggest possible benefit, but the small sample size precludes definitive efficacy conclusions. Further studies of cysteamine in severe pneumonia are warranted.

items.title: The burden of disease for children diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome - a European cohort study.
items.abstract: To investigate the burden of disease for European children diagnosed prenatally or in infancy with Klinefelter syndrome for better counselling of parents after the diagnosis. Thirteen registries in ten countries from the EUROCAT network participated. Data for children born between 1995 and 2014 and diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome were linked to mortality and hospital records. Data for children born with any major congenital anomaly and children without a congenital anomaly (reference children) were included for comparisons. Out of 5.8 million liveborn children, 278 were diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome in the 13 registry areas and with an infant mortality of 3.2% (95% CI 1.5;6.1). Two out of three were admitted to hospital during the first year with a median length of stay of 3.9 (95% CI 3.0;4.7) days compared to 3.0 days for reference children and 7.9 days for children with any congenital anomaly. In the age group 1-4 years, the median length of stay for children with Klinefelter syndrome decreased to 0.7 (95% CI 0.3;1.1) days per year compared to 0.4 days per year for reference children. Within the first year, 12.3% (95% CI 7.1;18.9) of the children with Klinefelter syndrome underwent surgery increasing to 19.7% (95% CI 10.2;31.4) at age 1-4 years. There is a high burden of disease for children diagnosed prenatally or in infancy with Klinefelter syndrome in the first year after birth but this falls during age 1-4 years. Parents can be reassured that the prognosis in childhood is good. • Mortality and morbidity are increased among adults with Klinefelter syndrome and studies indicate that this start from the early childhood. • This multicenter population-based study including boys diagnosed prenatally and in infancy with Klinefelter syndrome showed a higher morbidity within the first five years of life compared to children without congenital anomalies. One out of eight underwent surgery within the first year after birth and one in five underwent surgery at age 1-4 years.

items.title: Antibiotic prescriptions in children with community-acquired empyema: an Italian multicentric study.
items.abstract: The limited evidence guiding antibiotic therapy for pediatric empyema contributes to the frequent prescription of broad-spectrum agents, often including antibiotics categorized as "Watch" or "Reserve" according to the WHO AWaRe classification. We aimed primarily to describe antibiotic prescribing patterns in a large national cohort of children hospitalized with empyema and, secondarily, to explore associations between antibiotic exposure categories and clinical outcomes. We conducted a multicenter retrospective study including children (< 18 years) admitted with pleural empyema to 19 Italian hospitals (2018-2023). Data on antibiotic regimens, duration, route of administration, and clinical outcomes were collected. Prescriptions were categorized according to the AWaRe classification. Associations between antibiotic classes and clinical outcomes were assessed using multilevel models and inverse probability weighting with regression adjustment. All 263 patients with empyema included in the study received antibiotic therapy for a median of 27 days (IQR 20-40), including 20 days (IQR 14-28) of intravenous treatment. The most frequently prescribed agents were ceftriaxone/cefotaxime (71.9%) and glycopeptides (46.8%). Only 8.7% of patients received an antibiotic with a narrow anti-pneumococcal spectrum. Meanwhile, 97.3% received at least one "Watch" antibiotic, and 33.1% received at least one "Reserve" antibiotic. Considerable heterogeneity in antibiotic regimens was observed across centers. No demographic, clinical, laboratory, or radiological variables were consistently associated with antibiotic category selection. Exploratory adjusted analyses showed no consistent association between the evaluated antibiotic exposure categories and lower probabilities of CPAP use, mechanical ventilation, or PICU admission. Several isolated associations were observed for secondary outcomes, including lower VATS use among children exposed to anti-MRSA therapy, to be interpreted cautiously. In this large national cohort, prolonged and broad-spectrum antibiotic exposure was common and highly variable across patients and centers. Watch and Reserve antibiotics were frequently prescribed. Exploratory adjusted analyses did not identify consistent associations between broader-spectrum exposure and major respiratory or intensive-care outcomes, but causal effects cannot be inferred from these retrospective data. These findings primarily highlight substantial stewardship opportunities and support prospective studies designed to evaluate treatment strategies with explicit consideration of treatment timing and disease severity. • Pediatric Empyema is a severe complication of pneumonia. • The optimal antibiotic management of empyema remains unclear, leading historically to antibiotic overuse. • In a 19-center Italian cohort, prolonged antibiotic courses and exposure to WHO Watch and Reserve antibiotics were common, with marked heterogeneity in prescribing patterns. • Exploratory adjusted analyses did not show consistent associations between broader-spectrum antibiotic exposure and major respiratory or intensive-care outcomes.

items.title: A critical exploration of microbial extracellular polymeric substances in the bioremediation of heavy metal-contaminated sites.
items.abstract: Heavy metal contamination from industrialization, mining, agricultural activities, and improper waste disposal represents a critical environmental and public health challenge due to the persistence, toxicity, and bioaccumulative potential of metals such as Cd, Pb, Hg, Cr, As, Ni, and Cu. Conventional physicochemical remediation approaches, although effective, are constrained by high operational costs, secondary waste generation, limited selectivity, and sustainability concerns. Microbial extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) have therefore emerged as promising bio-based materials for sustainable heavy metal remediation. This review critically evaluates the structural composition, physicochemical properties, and functional characteristics of microbial EPS involved in metal interactions through biosorption, ion exchange, complexation, precipitation, and biofilm-associated immobilization mechanisms. Particular attention is given to EPS functional groups, including carboxyl, hydroxyl, phosphate, amine, and thiol moieties, which contribute to metal-binding capacity and environmental stability. EPS-mediated applications in wastewater treatment, contaminated soils, sediments, and biofilm-based remediation systems are discussed, along with emerging strategies involving engineered microorganisms, EPS-based hybrid nanocomposites, biochar-integrated systems, magnetic biosorbents, and bioelectrochemical platforms. The review also highlights key challenges associated with EPS heterogeneity, process optimization, regeneration, environmental stability, and large-scale translation. Future research directions involving synthetic biology, molecular characterization, pilot-scale validation, circular bioeconomy integration, and multi-contaminant remediation are proposed to advance EPS-based environmental restoration technologies.
