items.title: Source population identity predicts success better than environmental matching in stickleback introductions.
items.abstract: Species introductions and transplants offer powerful contexts to understand evolutionary patterns and processes, and they are increasingly critical for conservation. However, introduction success varies widely, and predicting outcomes remains challenging. Using multiple source populations should increase the chance of introduction success, while also providing an opportunity to explore the factors that predict success of individual source populations in the same environment. We used replicated, mixed-population introductions of >12,000 threespine stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus) to test whether source population success could be predicted by environmental matching between source and recipient environments and/or by source population characteristics. We introduced four to eight source populations of stickleback into each of nine natural lakes with no other stickleback and tracked their relative success over the following 2 years (up to two generations). Source population success was largely consistent across lakes, despite divergent environmental conditions. These results point to the importance of consistent source population differences rather than environmental matching in determining introduction success in natural settings. Source populations that were consistently successful tended to have greater stress tolerance and higher genetic diversity, though these relationships were not conclusive. Our study highlights the value of considering factors that generate fitness differences independent of environmental context when predicting ecological and evolutionary dynamics and planning conservation programs.

items.title: PBPK-based prediction of human health risks from cadmium-contaminated shellfish under ocean warming and acidification.
items.abstract: Climate-driven changes in seawater temperature and acidification may alter Cd bioaccumulation in shellfish and associated human health risks. We integrated a generalized additive model, dietary data, a physiologically based pharmacokinetic model, and Monte Carlo simulations to assess Cd exposure in Taiwanese adults aged 19-65 years under current conditions (20.1 °C, pH 8.1) and a hypothetical 2100 scenario under SSP5-8.5 (23.7 °C, pH 7.7). Urinary Cd concentrations were simulated after 46 years of exposure, and hazard quotients (HQs) were evaluated using a conservative screening value of 0.2. Under the 2100 scenario, the geometric mean shellfish Cd concentration increased from 0.11 to 0.59 μg/g. In the whole group (WG), median urinary Cd concentrations increased from 0.021 to 0.069 μg/g creatinine in males and from 0.023 to 0.097 μg/g creatinine in females; corresponding 90th-percentile (P90) HQs reached 0.235 and 0.351. The consumer-only (CO) group had higher predicted exposure, with P90 HQs reaching 0.780 in males and 1.163 in females. These scenario-specific findings indicate potential renal health concerns requiring further assessment, particularly in the CO group. Future food safety regulations should incorporate climate change projections and an acceptable-risk framework when establishing or reviewing Cd limits in shellfish.

items.title: Coupling relationship and threshold calculation between forest degradation/improvement and carbon-water use efficiencies in Northeast Asia.
items.abstract: Carbon use efficiency (CUE) and water use efficiency (WUE) are key parameters of terrestrial carbon-water cycling that strongly influence forest degradation and improvement. Previous studies have mainly focused on the independent spatial-temporal dynamics of CUE and WUE, while the coupling relationships, ecological thresholds, and coordinated responses between CUE-WUE and forest degradation/improvement remain insufficiently explored. Focusing on the temperate-boreal transition zone of Northeast Asia, this study constructed an analytical framework integrating MK-Sen trend analysis, coupling coordination degree, and ROC analysis-based threshold identification to examine relationships between forest degradation/improvement and the long-term evolution of carbon-water use efficiencies between 2001 and 2021. The results showed that CUE in Northeast Asia exhibited a declining trend, while WUE showed an increasing trend, with 31.08% and 50.78% of the forest area experiencing increase trend, respectively. The coupling coordination degrees between forest degradation/improvement and carbon-water use efficiencies were 0.711 and 0.663, indicating moderate coordination. Moreover, the CUE and WUE spearman's correlation coefficient are -0.0231 (-0.0234--0.0228, 95% CI, P < 0.001***) and -0.0270 (-0.0273--0.0267, 95%CI, P < 0.001***), indicating the weak negative correlation. When the CUE trend exceeded 0.0005 and the WUE trend surpassed -0.005, forests shifted toward improvement. Approximately 51.54% of improved forests were driven by WUE increases, while 21.11% of the region showed degradation risks. This study advances the understanding by linking CUE-WUE trajectories with forest degradation/improvement processes and identifying critical ecological thresholds associated with forest transition risks., offering carbon-water efficiencies-based evidence for identifying areas at risk of forest degradation as well as supporting the assessment work for SDG 15.3.1 (Land Degradation Neutrality, LDN).

items.title: Ecosystem multifunctionality responses to post-restoration grazing in seeded versus fenced alpine grasslands on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau.
items.abstract: Current grassland restoration assessments largely focus on vegetation and soil improvements during grazing exclusion, yet the long-term trajectories and plant-soil regulatory mechanisms of ecosystem multifunctionality (EMF) following grazing resumes remain unclear. We constructed a 13-year post-restoration grazing experiment on the Qinghai-Xizang Plateau (QXP), integrating field vegetation surveys, multi-index soil measurements, Bayesian regression, structural equation modeling and driver-EMF correlation analysis to compare EMF sustainability between seeded grasslands (SG) and fenced grasslands (FG). Our results demonstrated FG maintained significantly higher EMF than degraded grasslands over the full 13-year period, declining at a slow annual rate. This stability was sustained by a streamlined cascade centered on vegetation height that connects native species richness and soil nitrate nitrogen. Weak linear coupling between individual drivers and EMF endows naturally restored FG with sufficient functional redundancy to buffer sustained grazing pressure. By contrast, SG achieved striking EMF elevation during the first three years of re-grazing, however, it experienced rapid functional degradation, falling below the degraded grassland (DG) reference level by year nine. SG's multifunctionality relies on a strongly coupled, ammonium-dominated network; grazing-induced reductions in vegetation height, soil moisture, species abundance, and mineral nitrogen availability, driving rapid functional decline that, within the 13-year observation window, reduced EMF below the reference degraded level, despite minor compensatory effects from nitrate pools. A unified critical intervention window spanning 3-5 years after grazing resumption was identified, during which Bayes factors provided anecdotal evidence (<3) for EMF divergence between restoration modes and soil nitrogen cycling remained intact. Synthesising our mechanistic findings, we reveal that fenced grasslands sustain long-term EMF via a streamlined height-nitrate-species richness cascade with consistently weak driver-EMF coupling, whereas seeded grasslands exhibit a strongly coupled, ammonium-dominated multi-pathway network that delivers short-term productivity gains but undergoes rapid functional decline after five years of grazing. These contrasting plant-soil functional frameworks provide a mechanistic basis for designing differentiated post-restoration management strategies on the QXP.

items.title: Integrating citizen observations and microbial sequencing to characterize seasonal cyanobacterial dynamics in a shallow temperate lake.
items.abstract: Cyanobacterial harmful algal blooms (cHABs) threaten freshwater ecosystems by degrading water quality, ecosystem functioning, and public health. Although nutrient loading and climate change are recognized bloom drivers, microbial community dynamics are increasingly recognized as important components of cyanobacterial bloom ecology. This study examined microbial community shifts associated with cyanobacteria presence and bloom development in a shallow Quebec lake, Lac Drolet, based on citizen science monitoring. Weekly citizen observations revealed consistent temporal patterns of cyanobacterial presence in Lac Drolet, with more blooms occurring in 2022 than 2023. Microbial community analyses using 16S rRNA and 18S rRNA amplicon sequencing revealed temporal and spatial variation in bacterial and eukaryotic communities across the 2023 sampling season. Water temperature was significantly associated with both bacterial and eukaryotic community composition, while nitrate was significantly associated with eukaryotic community composition but showed only a marginal association with bacterial community composition. Phosphate was not significantly associated with either community. Aphanizomenon_NIES81 increased in relative abundance during the late-summer bloom period and was associated with taxon-specific changes in bacterial and eukaryotic ASVs. These findings highlight associations among cyanobacterial dynamics, microbial community composition, and environmental conditions and demonstrate the value of combining citizen science observations with sequencing-based ecological monitoring in lakes.

items.title: Rethinking broad diet breadth as a sign of scarcity: A 50,000-y record of subsistence from northwestern Australia.
items.abstract: The prey choice model, widely applied in archaeological reconstructions of Pleistocene diet, predicts that people will initially focus on a narrow suite of high-ranked prey before broadening their diet to include lower-ranked species as necessitated by subsistence needs. However, evidence from arid and semiarid northern Australia challenges this assumption. Archaeological faunal records demonstrate that a broad diet was established early and persisted through the Holocene. We argue that these diverse diets do not indicate resource scarcity, but rather represent an ideal strategy for exploiting abundant, low-risk hidden, or cryptic prey, as well as high-risk, conspicuous prey within an environment characterized by unpredictable rainfall. This pattern also necessitates reconceptualizing traditional notions of prey rank and dietary breadth. Rather than adhering to static prey rankings, northern Australian peoples skillfully adapted their hunting strategies in response to fluctuating nutritional content and pursuit costs of different species. The most successful subsistence strategy in this region was therefore one of high responsiveness and flexibility, manifesting as a consistently broad diet. This case study suggests that the relationship between human dietary breadth and resource abundance is more nuanced in situations of abundant, cryptic prey.

items.title: Failure of a tropical upwelling rapidly collapsed Panama's anchoveta fishery and its exports.
items.abstract: In 2025 the seasonal upwelling of the Gulf of Panama failed. Net primary production fell by 64% across the Gulf and industrial anchoveta landings dropped to 11% of the average, the lowest since the fishery became fully exploited in 1966. Anchoveta caught per purse-seine set fell to under a third of the normal rate while total catch per set stayed within its normal range. Landed fish carried about half their usual lipid content, and fish oil exports fell by 88% in both volume and value. The effects of one failed season reached international trade within months. Seasonal upwellings like this are common across the tropics yet far less studied than the large eastern boundary systems. The very strong El Niño now under way makes the 2027 season more uncertain.

items.title: Phase coding supports neuronal replication and enables combinatorial problem solving.
items.abstract: Darwinian neurodynamics posits that the brain searches large solution spaces through iterated cycles of variation and selection on competing neural representations. Testing this hypothesis requires a biologically plausible neural replicator: a mechanism that copies spatiotemporal signals faithfully enough to cumulatively improve good solutions, yet loosely enough to allow exploration. We show that phase-coded spike patterns constitute such a replicator. Spike timing referenced to a local field oscillation is compressed into a transferable spike train and reconstructed by coincidence with the receiver's own field, without synaptic plasticity or a shared code key. As replication noise rises, the system crosses two thresholds. Below the first, faithful copying sustains patterns as dynamic memory. Between the two thresholds, pattern populations evolve. On two hard combinatorial benchmarks, the traveling salesman problem and NK fitness landscapes, neural replication remains competitive with standard search methods at a matched evaluation budget. Beyond the second, an Eigen-like error threshold, inherited information collapses. The network architecture tunes the exploration-exploitation balance: high-degree lattices, where local competition is stronger, exploit smooth landscapes, while low-degree lattices, where weaker competition preserves diversity, search more broadly on rugged landscapes. The framework predicts phase-locked information transfer and phylogenetic structure in replay, as well as a selective loss of combinatorial problem solving beyond the error threshold. These results indicate that a single neurobiological substrate can support memory, variation, and selection, and point to evolutionary dynamics as a candidate computational principle for cognition.

items.title: Facilitators and Barriers Influencing Patient Safety Activities in Long-Term Care Facilities: An Integrative Review Guided by the SEIPS 101 Model.
items.abstract: Nurses' patient safety activities in long-term care facilities (LTCFs) are influenced by systemic factors within complex work systems. Despite increasing attention to patient safety in LTCFs, comprehensive syntheses that specifically examine facilitators and barriers influencing nurses' patient safety activities within an established theoretical framework remain limited. This integrative review synthesized evidence on facilitators and barriers influencing nurses' patient safety activities in LTCFs using the Systems Engineering Initiative for Patient Safety (SEIPS) 101 model. The literature search covered publications from January 1, 2010, to June 12, 2025, across CINAHL, PubMed, ProQuest, and MEDLINE, along with two domestic databases (Korean Studies Information Service System and Research Information Sharing Service). The review followed the five-step integrative review framework and was reported according to the PRISMA guidelines. Two independent reviewers conducted data extraction and methodological quality appraisal using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, and the review protocol was registered on OSF (10.17605/OSF.IO/RH6KX). Twenty studies met the inclusion criteria. The findings identified the "socio-organizational environment" domain as both the predominant facilitator and barrier, followed by the "people" and "tasks" domains, which were more frequently reported as barriers than facilitators. The synthesis demonstrates that patient safety activities in LTCFs are shaped by dynamic feedback loops among the work systems, work processes, and work outcomes, rather than by isolated nursing activities. The proposed framework based on the SEIPS 101 model provides a foundation for developing targeted guidelines and intervention strategies to strengthen patient safety activities among nurses in LTCFs.

items.title: Genetic architectures of floral pigment and patterning in hybrid monkeyflowers.
items.abstract: Coloration in living organisms varies in hue, saturation, and pattern. Here we use genetic mapping to investigate all three elements in monkeyflowers Mimulus luteus var. variegatus and M. cupreus, whose flower petals differ in both yellow carotenoid and magenta cyanidin (anthocyanin) pigmentation and whose hybrids exhibit anthocyanin pattern variation not seen in either parent. We report two QTLs associated with carotenoid intensity, and show that lighter yellow petals accumulate relatively high proportions of beta-carotene at the expense of downstream carotenoids. We propose that the derived loss of carotenoid saturation in M. l. variegatus is due to a function-reducing mutation in a Beta-Carotene Hydroxylase candidate gene, possibly coupled with a reduction in the availability of carotenoid-storing chromoplasts influenced by the ORANGE candidate gene. We next identify five QTLs associated with the spatial patterning of anthocyanin pigment. Two QTLs, 9b and 23, each contain genes in the anthocyanin-activating subgroup of the MYB family. We hypothesize that MYB5a/NEGAN, at QTL-9b, activates spot formation in hybrids as part of a Turing-type reaction-diffusion system, while a MYB at QTL-23 activates solid, non-Turing-type anthocyanin pigmentation and may also be able to activate the variegatus allele of MYB5a/NEGAN. In addition to the apparently stochastic placement of most spots (consistent with a Turing mechanism), some pattern aspects - such as spots at the petal tips - appear to conform to a positional specification model in which spot location is predetermined. Collectively, this work begins to identify how combinations of yellow and red hues, shifts in carotenoid intensity, and two cryptic patterning systems all contribute to the complexity of color divergence between two close relatives.

items.title: When should adaptation arise from a polygenic response versus few large-effect changes?
items.abstract: When will adaptation involve a few genetic changes of large effect versus a polygenic response? There are compelling reasons to expect polygenic adaptation to be common, yet direct evidence is lacking. Conversely, there are hundreds of examples of large-effect adaptations across species, but it is unclear whether they occur frequently within any given species. These different lines of evidence are hard to synthesize, in part due to the lack of theory that relates them. To address this gap, we frame the question in terms of the properties of an adaptive trait. We ask how the genetic basis of adaptation depends on key aspects of genetic variation in the trait and on the degree to which its selection pressures have changed. To this end, we consider a quantitative trait subject to stabilizing selection and model its response when a population at mutation-selection-drift balance experiences a sudden shift in the trait optimum. Using this model, we delimit how the contributions of large-effect and polygenic changes to adaptation depend on the genetics and ecology of adaptive traits, as well as on other salient factors. Thus, we formulate testable predictions for when different modes of adaptation are expected.

items.title: Safety collaborative prevention and control technology for coal mining beneath oil pipelines.
items.abstract: Coal mining beneath oil pipelines requires a balance between resource recovery and the control of mining-induced pipeline deformation. Using coal seam at Haichatan Coal Mine and the Jingbian-Yulin refined-oil pipeline as a case study, a coupled analysis framework was developed to link ground movement, relative pipe-soil displacement, and pipeline equivalent stress. The probability integral method was used to predict ground subsidence, tilt, horizontal strain, and curvature. The three-dimensional ground-displacement field was then applied to a nonlinear Winkler foundation model implemented in ANSYS. Sixteen scenarios were defined by combining two pipeline branches, two mining scales, and four mining-thickness levels. For full-thickness extraction of three panels, the maximum predicted ground subsidence along the western and eastern branches was 1 480 and 1 634 mm, respectively. The corresponding maximum pipeline equivalent stresses were 728 and 946 MPa, with strength-utilization ratios of 2.79 and 3.62. Reducing the effective mining thickness to 0.2M decreased these stresses to 255 and 227 MPa; however, the western branch remained close to the adopted limit, with a strength-utilization ratio of 0.977. Effective mining thickness strongly influenced the predicted response within the scenarios examined. A candidate control strategy combining a 2.3 m mining-thickness limit with trench excavation, pressure reduction, and pipeline lifting where necessary was proposed. Its safety requires further verification because the thickness limit alone does not establish compliance. A monitoring framework integrating InSAR, ground surveys, pipeline strain measurements, and trench-displacement measurements was also proposed to support model calibration and staged intervention. The framework provides a basis for assessing coal extraction beneath long-distance pipelines in areas with overlapping coal and petroleum resources.

items.title: Sporothrix brasiliensis in Coastal and Marine Fishes: Implications for Marine-Terrestrial Spillover.
items.abstract: Sporothrix brasiliensis is an emerging zoonotic fungal pathogen that has transformed sporotrichosis in Brazil from a sapronotic 'gardener's disease' into a major zoonotic epidemic in South America. Here, ITS metabarcoding of 989 fish from coastal southern Brazil detected S. brasiliensis-compatible reads in 67.3% of pooled samples, and culture recovered viable isolates from selected samples. Genome typing placed fish-and bird-derived isolates within S. brasiliensis clinical Brazilian lineages, implicating aquatic-coastal interfaces in the ecology of this expanding pathogen.

items.title: Association between Candidozyma auris candiduria and subsequent candidemia in colonized critically ill patients: a nine-year cohort study.
items.abstract: Urinary isolation of Candidozyma auris in colonized critically ill patients is common, but its clinical significance remains poorly defined. We conducted a retrospective cohort study between May 2016 and December 2025 at a 900-bed tertiary hospital in Valencia, Spain, with endemic clade III C. auris. Patients aged 14 years or older with C. auris colonization and at least one urine culture were included. Candiduria was modeled as a time-varying exposure in cause-specific Cox models. The primary outcome was subsequent C. auris candidemia; secondary outcomes were the determinants of candiduria, urinary clearance and management. Of 513 patients, 126 (25%) developed candiduria and 94 (18.3%) candidemia. Candiduria was independently associated with subsequent candidemia (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.63; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.03-2.58; P = .036), as was the Candida score (adjusted HR, 2.10; 95% CI, 1.72-2.56; P < .001); the candiduria estimate was attenuated when candidemia within 72 hours was excluded (HR, 1.50; 95% CI, 0.95-2.36). Female sex and the Candida score were independently associated with candiduria. Among patients with candiduria, 32 (25%) progressed to candidemia after a median of 9 days; neither antifungal therapy nor urinary catheter removal or exchange, modeled as time-dependent exposures, was associated with a lower risk. Urinary clearance was documented in 29 of 115 patients with follow-up cultures (25.2%), falling to 17.4% when two consecutive negative cultures were required. C. auris candiduria identified colonized intensive care unit patients at higher risk of candidemia, but the observational design precludes causal inference and prospective confirmation is required.

items.title: A review: efficient microbial remediation technologies for petroleum-contaminated soils under the concept of ecological civilization.
items.abstract: Petroleum-contaminated soils have become a global environmental concern, posing significant risks to ecosystem integrity and human health. This review systematically analyzed 1105 publications from 2011 to 2026 (with 2026 partially indexed) to summarize the research progress and engineering applications of microbial remediation technologies for petroleum-contaminated soils. Keyword clustering and evolutionary analysis suggested that microbial remediation has evolved from early biostimulation and single-strain bioaugmentation toward the construction of microbial consortia, remediation with functional materials, plant-microbe synergistic strategies, and the integration of multiple technologies. Patent evolution analysis further indicated shifts in technological development and identified potential technology gaps and challenges in engineering applications. The application scenarios and enhancement strategies have continuously expanded. Laboratory, pilot-scale, and field studies indicate that microbial remediation promotes petroleum hydrocarbon degradation through microbial metabolism and cometabolism; however, its application remains constrained by high contaminant concentrations, aging effects, limited bioavailability, insufficient colonization stability of functional microorganisms, and challenges in large-scale field implementation. Combining microbial remediation with biochar, biosurfactants, electrokinetic remediation, and chemical oxidation can further improve remediation performance by optimizing microbial environments, enhancing contaminant bioavailability, and promoting electron transfer. Nevertheless, adaptation to extreme environments, precise regulation of remediation processes, and the establishment of green and low-carbon evaluation frameworks remain key challenges. This review provides theoretical insights and technical references for effective, green, and sustainable remediation of petroleum-contaminated soils.

items.title: Ultra-high hydrostatic pressure combined with tea saponin micelles enhances naringin extraction from pomelo peel.
items.abstract: Pomelo peel is a citrus-processing by-product rich in naringin, a high-value bioactive flavonoid, but its dense tissue matrix and naringin's limited aqueous solubility constrain efficient extraction. We therefore developed an aqueous process combining ultra-high hydrostatic pressure (UHHP) with tea saponin micelles to address both tissue disruption and solubilization. Conductor-like screening model for real solvents (COSMO-RS) calculations, followed by experimental screening, identified tea saponin as the most suitable candidate among the tested surfactants. Response surface methodology gave optimal conditions of 293 MPa, 80.8 mg/mL tea saponin, a liquid-to-solid ratio of 25 mL/g, three pressure cycles, and a holding time of 4.45 min per cycle. Under these conditions, mean naringin recovery and extraction yield reached 80.3% and 9.58 mg/g, respectively. In a laboratory-scale comparison with ethanol maceration and ultrasound- and microwave-assisted extraction, the UHHP-micellar process gave the highest yield and shorter treatment time, together with lower calculated energy use and CO 2 emissions within the laboratory-scale comparison. Scanning electron microscopy indicated marked disruption and increased porosity of the peel matrix, while Fourier transform infrared spectra showed no new major bands attributable to naringin degradation. Density functional theory calculations supported hydrogen-bonding and van der Waals interactions between naringin and the modeled tea saponin structure, and molecular dynamics simulations suggested pressure-induced micellar compaction and retention of naringin after decompression. The enhanced extraction performance is attributed to complementary contributions from tissue disruption, micellar solubilization, and noncovalent association. These findings provide a basis for further scale-up, downstream purification, and life-cycle evaluation of an aqueous route for recovering poorly soluble flavonoids from citrus-processing by-products.

items.title: Lead bioaccumulation in urban wall lizards (Podarcis muralis).
items.abstract: Lead (Pb) has toxic effects on wildlife and humans including anemia, delayed development, and reproductive failure. Anthropogenic land use introduces risks of soil Pb contamination from industrial activity and automobile traffic. Few studies have examined heavy metal toxicokinetics in reptiles, and whether soil Pb concentrations can be used to predict the Pb concentration of reptile tissues. In this study, we examined the Pb content of soils and tissues from common wall lizards (Podarcis muralis) from three sites with differing urban infrastructure in Cincinnati, Ohio (USA). The highest Pb concentrations were observed in soil and lizard blood from a site with elevated vehicle and railroad traffic. Juvenile lizards had lower blood Pb concentrations than adult females, though blood Pb concentrations were not correlated with body size or body condition. Pb concentrations were not correlated among oviductal eggs, blood, and livers within individuals, but blood and livers exhibited higher Pb concentrations than eggs. These results suggest that female lizards may be accumulating Pb, or excreting Pb using pathways besides vitellogenesis. We advocate the need for further study of Pb toxicokinetics in reptiles, including additional tissues that are infrequently examined, such as kidneys, brains, and bones. Reptiles can serve as bioindicators and reveal environmental Pb contamination that could be harmful to wildlife, pets and humans.

items.title: The Self-Powered Nanofiltration Membrane Driven by Pulsed Pressure for Efficient Selective Separation of Na<sup>+</sup>/Ca<sup>2</sup>.
items.abstract: Enhancing electrostatic repulsion against divalent cations in the selective layer is effective in improving monovalent/divalent cation separation in nanofiltration. However, conventional grafting and coating strategies are limited by insufficient reaction sites or poor coating stability, both of which restrict further improvements in monovalent/divalent cation selectivity. Herein, a positively charged nanofiltration membrane with a piezoelectric response (PQNF) was designed via reverse thermally induced phase separation (RTIPS) coupled with interfacial polymerization (IP). RTIPS endowed the poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) substrate with a sponge-like pore structure, a narrow pore-size distribution, and a high β-phase content. Subsequently, the PQNF membrane was prepared via IP, quaternization, and corona poling. Under pulsed pressure operation, a periodic in situ voltage of 0.4 V was generated, which contributed to the 98.7% Ca 2+ rejection and a Na + /Ca 2+ separation factor of 89.6. The membrane also maintained stable separation performance over 144 h and showed enhanced antifouling performance under pulsed pressure operation in a 14 h fouling test. Finally, an "electrostatic-piezoelectric synergistic enhancement" separation mechanism was proposed and supported by molecular dynamics simulations.

items.title: Evolutionary relatedness is a partially reliable predictor of host-associated microbiome composition.
items.abstract: Multicellular animals emerged into a microbial world, and they continue to be influenced by sympatric bacterial species. Host-associated microbiomes are recognized as critical contributors to their living domicile's success. Detailing how microbiomes are assembled and maintained by their hosts has important implications for animal health, agricultural productivity, and biodiversity interventions across the tree of life. Tens to 100s of bacterial genera are frequently detected in animal microbiomes, with some being uniquely and consistently detected in specific host species. Such discoveries have informed theories like phylosymbiosis that assert that host-associated microbiomes often reflect host species relatedness. We explored the predictive limits of this theory by performing a multi-scale dissimilarity-based comparative analyses using publicly available microbiomes drawn from 113 insect species spanning 14 insect orders. We detected a moderate inter-order phylosymbiotic signal (Mantel test: r = 0.392, P r = 0.173, P < 0.001) when the Blattodea were excluded from the analysis. Intra-order level phylosymbiotic signals varied widely for lepidopteran, hymenopteran, hemipteran, and blattodean host species microbiomes. Strong signals were often explained by obligate endosymbionts and/or nestmate-acquired gut bacteria, rather than by the total microbiomes. In short, host species-defining bacterial genera often represented a small fraction of the total observed microbial diversity in their respective insect host species, and these genera were well-integrated into host behaviors and/or physiologies that facilitated reliable intra- and inter-generational transmission. In contrast, microbiome compositional variability was so high in some insect orders that attempts to reflect host speciation events using their microbiomes were impossible.IMPORTANCEWhile all animals have microbiomes, the principles determining their composition remain an incomplete story. We leveraged the diversity of Insecta, arisen from 400 My of evolution, to evaluate if microbiome evolution is synchronized with the evolutionary history of their associated hosts. We found that host evolution plays a limited role in predicting microbiome composition, particularly due to the non-uniformity of host-microbial symbioses across insects. This result is in stark contrast to studies of similar scope in vertebrate organisms that spanned much less evolutionary time (i.e., up to 50 My). While insects of the order Blattodea, in particular, harbor exceptionally diverse microbiomes, many insect microbiomes are characterized by few bacterial genera. Our results suggest that host evolutionary history is but one of many factors, including differences in microbiome transmission modality, influencing insect microbiome evolution.

items.title: A CPK28-GS2 phosphorylation switch uncouples nitrogen-promoted growth from disease susceptibility.
items.abstract: Nitrogen fertilization underpins global crop yields, but it paradoxically increases plant vulnerability to pathogens, a phenomenon known as nitrogen-induced susceptibility (NIS). This phenomenon has been repeatedly observed in both field and laboratory studies; however, the underlying molecular mechanism remains elusive. Here, we show that the nitrogen assimilation gene glutamine synthetase 2 (GS2) plays a central role in NIS in tomato. Genetic analyses revealed that GS2 promotes both biomass accumulation and susceptibility to Ralstonia solanacearum. Using immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry (IP-MS), we identified the calcium-dependent protein kinase CPK28 as an interactor of GS2. CPK28 phosphorylates GS2 at serine 334 in a nitrate-dependent manner, and this modification alters GS2 subcellular localization and is associated with perturbation of the phenylpropanoid pathway. Consequently, lignin deposition is reduced, leading to enhanced bacterial wilt susceptibility. Notably, a phospho-dead GS2 S334A variant abolished NIS without impairing growth. These findings uncover a post-translational switch that uncouples nitrogen-promoted growth from disease susceptibility, thereby offering a framework to achieve agronomic productivity with ecological sustainability.

items.title: Hepatic EPHX1 potentiates liver fibrosis by decreasing eicosatrienoic acids.
items.abstract: Changes in polyunsaturated fatty acid metabolites are thought to contribute to pathogeneses of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and liver fibrosis. This study demonstrated that hepatic microsomal epoxide hydrolase (EPHX1) promotes liver fibrosis by decreasing hepatic eicosatrienoic acid (EET) levels, suggesting that elevation of serum dihydroxyeicosatrienoic acid (DHET) levels is an indicator of advanced fibrosis. Serum lipidomic analysis of 102 patients with MASLD and 121 with chronic hepatitis C, combined with multivariate logistic regression, confirmed elevation of serum 11,12-DHET levels as a predictor of advanced fibrosis. The expression of hepatic EPHX1, which hydrolyzes EET to DHET, increased in patients with advanced fibrosis. MASLD mouse model showed increased hepatic EPHX1 levels and decreased hepatic EET levels. Ephx1-null mice showed suppressed hepatic fibrogenesis and oxidative stress with increasing EET levels. In hepatic stellate cells (HSCs), treatment with 11,12-EET reduced COL1A1 expression, but not 11,12-DHET, attenuated intracellular oxidative stress, and suppressed TGF-β-induced HSC activation. Furthermore, it alleviated liver fibrosis by attenuating hepatic oxidative stress and suppressing HSC activation in mice with thioacetamide-induced liver fibrosis. This study provides evidence that EPHX1 contributes to EET hydrolysis in the liver and participates in liver fibrogenesis, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic target.

items.title: Cats in the dark: A review of our current knowledge of the deep-sea catshark genus Apristurus.
items.abstract: The deep-sea catsharks in the genus Apristurus (Pentanchidae) constitute one of the most species-rich yet least resolved elasmobranch lineages. Herein, we utilised a systematic literature search to synthesise current knowledge on their diversity, morphology, phylogeny, distribution, ecology, reproduction and threats, and outline priorities for research aligned with the UN Decade of Ocean Science. The genus currently comprises 43 described extant species and three extinct taxa. Morphologically, Apristurus species share cephalic dorso-ventral compression, broad spatulate snouts and diagnostic labial-furrow states; meristics (including vertebral counts) and egg-capsule morphology provide additional taxonomic signal. Morphological ratios and fin shapes are also valuable for identification. Phylogenetic evidence generally supports monophyly of the genus and recovery of three species groups (brunneus, spongiceps, longicephalus), although some recent morphology-led hypotheses warrant further genomic testing. Apristurus is circumglobal (excluding polar seas and the Mediterranean), occupies depths ca. 24-2652 m and functions primarily as a generalist mesopredator, with region- and species-specific trophic specialisation. Reproductive ecology is oviparous; egg capsules commonly aggregate on structurally complex substrates (e.g., sponges and corals) where local hydrodynamics likely enhance embryonic ventilation. Fossil egg cases at cold seeps indicate long-standing associations with complex deep-sea habitats. Major threats to the genus arise from deep-sea trawl bycatch and emerging seabed industries. Threats are exacerbated by genus life-history traits (prolonged development, low fecundity) which imply high sensitivity, though many species remain listed as Least Concern owing to a paucity of data due to the depths at which the genus lives. Key research gaps identified include the need for a robust, integrative taxonomy; publicly accessible genetic reference libraries; in situ behavioural and life-history observations; quantification of bycatch and post-release mortality; and assessment of climate and mining impacts on nursery habitats. We provide a consolidated baseline of information to assist with accelerated discovery, identification and conservation of Apristurus across its global range.

items.title: Assessing Guidance and Counseling Needs of Iranian Dental Students: A Cross-Sectional Study in Kerman University of Medical Sciences.
items.abstract: Background Upon admission to the university, students encounter a range of personal, emotional, academic, and occupational challenges that impact their mental health and overall efficiency. This study aimed to evaluate the guidance and counseling needs of dental students at Kerman University of Medical Sciences. Methods This cross-sectional descriptive-analytical study was conducted among dental students at Kerman University of Medical Sciences in 2021. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling, and data were collected from 173 students through the Counseling Needs Assessment Questionnaire, which assesses demographic characteristics as well as guidance and counseling needs. The questionnaire items are scored employing a four-point Likert scale, which spans "no need = 0" to "urgent need = 3." Data were analyzed using SPSS version 27. Descriptive statistics, independent-samples t -tests, one-way analysis of variance, and multiple linear regression were used for data analysis. Results The average score for students' guidance and counseling needs was 40.06 ± 15.75. Occupational counseling had the highest mean score (9.34), whereas family and marriage counseling had the lowest (6.99). The students' scores for guidance and counseling needs did not reveal any significant differences regarding age, marital status, place of residence, or academic level ( p > 0.05). Meanwhile, female participants achieved significantly higher scores on guidance and counseling needs than male participants ( p B = - 7.262, β = -0.231, 95% CI = -11.985 to -2.540, p = 0.003). Conclusion Dental students needed counseling services most frequently for their occupational needs but least frequently for their marital issues. Moreover, their guidance and counseling needs were associated with their gender.

items.title: The Epidemiological Profile of Major Depressive Disorder Among a Nationally Representative Sample in Saudi Arabia.
items.abstract: Aims Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a leading contributor to global disease burden, and national data on its epidemiology in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region remains scarce. This research therefore aimed to estimate the prevalence, sociodemographic correlates, comorbidities, and impairment associated with MDD in Saudi Arabia. Methods A cross-sectional, nationally representative survey was conducted using a validated diagnostic instrument based on DSM-IV criteria. Lifetime, 12-month, and 30-day prevalence estimates of MDD were reported. Associations with sociodemographic factors, age-of-onset, psychiatric comorbidities, functional impairment, and treatment utilization were examined. Results Lifetime prevalence of MDD was 6.0%, with a 12-month prevalence of 3.8% and a 30-day prevalence of 1.3%. Women exhibited higher prevalence (8.9%) compared to men (3.1%). The mean age-of-onset was 20.4 years. There were higher odds for MDD among youth, women, respondents who are employed and with lower education, urban residents, and those who were previously married. MDD showed strong comorbidity with anxiety and substance-use disorders and was associated with significant role impairment, with 71% reporting role impairment. Despite the substantial burden, treatment utilization was low, particularly among the severely impaired. Conclusions MDD is a prevalent and impairing condition in Saudi Arabia, with early onset, marked gender disparity, and strong comorbidity. The findings underscore the urgent need for early detection, targeted prevention, and expansion of accessible mental health services.

items.title: Study demands, self-critical perfectionism and dropout intentions among undergraduates: A six-wave study of weekly within-person associations.
items.abstract: Background Study Demands-Resources theory suggests that study demands and personal demands such as self-critical perfectionism can weaken persistence. However, evidence on their links with dropout intentions comes mostly from between-person comparisons, and little is known about week-to-week processes within students. Aims This study examined reciprocal within-person associations among study load, cognitive demands, self-critical perfectionism and dropout intentions. Sample Participants were 266 first- and second-year undergraduates (73.7% women) in teacher education programmes at a Turkish state university. Methods Six weekly assessments at the end of a semester were analysed using a random-intercept cross-lagged panel model, alternative specifications and design-sensitivity analyses. Hypotheses were tested with cross-lagged paths pooled across intervals. Results Within students, none of the hypothesized cross-lagged associations was statistically significant. The 95% confidence intervals excluded effects larger than about .13 for the paths between self-critical perfectionism and study demands and from study load to dropout intentions, but not for most paths involving dropout intentions. Between students, dropout intentions were significantly correlated only with study load (r = .25), and self-critical perfectionism was correlated with study load and cognitive demands (r = .28 and .35). Conclusions The hypothesized weekly lagged associations were not detected, although the design could reliably detect only unusually large effects. Larger samples are needed to assess typical effects, and measurement intervals should match the timescale of the hypothesized processes. The reported variance decomposition and sensitivity estimates provide design parameters for future studies.

items.title: Barriers to Help-Seeking for Psychological Distress and Wellbeing Among Nurses, Midwives, and Nursing Students: A Convergent Parallel Mixed-Methods Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Aim To identify barriers influencing help-seeking behaviours among nursing/midwifery professionals/students experiencing psychological distress. Design Convergent parallel mixed-methods systematic review. Data sources Six databases (CINAHL, PsycINFO, MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus) were searched between December 2023 and January 2024, with regular updates. The final search was completed in April 2025. Methods Two researchers independently screened and synthesised data following EPPI-Centre methods. Included populations were nurses, midwives, health visitors, and nursing/midwifery students. Eligibility encompassed 12 prespecified mental health and occupational wellbeing domains. All research study designs were eligible; reviews were excluded. Results Twenty studies met inclusion criteria: five quantitative, nine qualitative and six mixed-methods. An empirically-informed logic model highlighted six barriers to help-seeking: (1) perceived career threats, (2) stigma, judgement, and expectations, (3) perceptions of manager and informal support, (4) perceived need for support, (5) availability, accessibility, and adequacy of formal support, and (6) time and workload constraints. Various demographic and occupational factors emerged as potential influencers. Conclusions This review shows how personal, interpersonal, and organisational factors interact to shape help-seeking. The resulting logic model offers a strengthened and integrated explanation linking workplace culture, concerns about professional consequences, and difficulties accessing support to help-seeking barriers among nurses and midwives, bringing together formal and informal pathways that are rarely examined in a single framework. Implications for profession and/or patient care Findings can inform targeted workplace wellbeing interventions and support positive mental health cultures. Future research should test the models' practical applications. Impact The review generated a comprehensive, empirically informed logic model, representing an important step toward consolidating the evidence base, although further testing is required before the model can inform policy or strategy. Reporting method Conducted in accordance with the SWiM and PRISMA guidelines. Patient and public contribution A seven-member nursing/midwifery advisory group informed barrier identification and model development. Trial registration PROSPERO CRD42024518783 (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?RecordID=518783).

items.title: A comparison of Japanese, Taiwanese, and U.S. Normative score patterns on the WISC-V: proposed cultural and educational influences.
items.abstract: Cultural context shapes neuropsychological test performance through interrelated influences of education, language, and test-taking conventions. Building on adult cross-national profile findings, this descriptive and hypothesis-generating study examined whether similar normative score patterns are evident in children using the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children-Fifth Edition (WISC-V). Normative data were obtained from the US English, Japanese, and Taiwanese WISC-V manuals. For Japan and Taiwan, raw score ranges corresponding to a local scaled score of 10 were identified within each age band and converted to US-norm-referenced scaled scores; index scores and FSIQ were derived from the converted subtests. One-sample t-tests compared converted scores with US expectations, and associations with schooling were evaluated across age bands. Both East Asian cohorts showed strengths in processing speed, visual spatial reasoning, and working memory, with Japanese also demonstrating strengths in fluid reasoning. Relatively weaker performances were demonstrated on verbally mediated measures and Picture Concepts, with country-specific weaknesses on Comprehension (Japan) and Similarities (Taiwan). Education-related increases were strongest for verbal and processing speed measures, and East-West differences attenuated from early childhood to adolescence. Overall, the results generate hypotheses regarding possible cultural, linguistic, and educational contexts that may contribute to WISC-V normative score patterns across development.

items.title: Annual Research Review: Ecological momentary assessment in child and adolescent psychopathology - insights, challenges, and future directions.
items.abstract: Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) is a powerful method for understanding daily-life processes associated with the etiology and phenomenology of child and adolescent psychopathology. The present review synthesizes recent work using EMA to reveal novel insights - as well as unique challenges - associated with this methodology across child and adolescent diagnostic categories and domains of psychopathology. We highlight the strengths of EMA for illuminating dynamic, within-person, contextualized processes contributing to the onset, maintenance, and ultimately amelioration of youth psychiatric distress. We identify pressing areas for ongoing research, as well as opportunities to advance the science of EMA through multimodal ambulatory assessment, experimental designs, and the development of ecological momentary interventions.

items.title: The role of ageism, aging anxiety, and death anxiety in understanding psychology trainees' therapeutic expectations for and interest in providing end-of-life care.
items.abstract: Objectives Few psychologists specialize in geropsychology, and even fewer work in the subspecialty of end-of-life care for older adults, despite a growing need for these services. No known research has investigated factors that might predict psychology trainees' therapeutic expectations for and interest in providing end-of-life care. This study examined ageist attitudes, aging anxiety, and death anxiety as potential predictors. Method A sample of 197 doctoral psychology trainees completed survey measures online. Structural equation modeling was used to test the hypothesized relations of ageist attitudes, aging anxiety, and death anxiety with therapeutic expectations and interest in end-of-life care with older adults. Results More aging anxiety related significantly to poorer therapeutic expectations for clients at end-of-life and less interest in providing end-of-life care. More ambivalent ageist attitudes unexpectedly related to greater interest in end-of-life care. Death anxiety did not relate to either therapeutic expectations or interest in end-of-life care. Conclusion These findings suggested that doctoral psychology training programs and early clinical opportunities should consider the role of aging anxiety, as well as ageist attitudes, on trainees' interests and perceptions towards working with older adults living with life-limiting illness.

items.title: Cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric validation of the arabic tokophobia assessment questionnaire (TAQ-Ar) among egyptian pregnant women.
items.abstract: Background Tokophobia, a severe and multidimensional fear of childbirth, is associated with adverse maternal psychological outcomes and increased preference for elective cesarean delivery. Although the Arabic version of the Tokophobia Assessment Questionnaire (TAQ) has recently been psychometrically validated among Jordanian women, independent evidence supporting its application in other Arabic-speaking populations remains limited. Therefore, further validation is needed to strengthen confidence in its broader applicability. This study aimed to independently translate, culturally adapt, and evaluate the psychometric properties of the Tokophobia Assessment Questionnaire (TAQ) among Egyptian pregnant women. Methods A cross-sectional psychometric study was conducted with 426 pregnant women recruited from antenatal clinics and online platforms in Egypt (September 2025-January 2026). The TAQ underwent forward-backward translation and pilot testing. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) using principal axis factoring with oblimin rotation was conducted, with factor retention guided by parallel analysis and Velicer's MAP. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) using WLSMV estimation based on polychoric correlations compared competing models. Reliability was assessed using McDonald's omega. Known-groups validity and multivariable linear regression were conducted to examine discriminative capacity and independent predictors. Results EFA supported a refined 21-item, three-factor structure representing (1) inability to address physical and social needs, (2) fear of childbirth, and (3) avoidance of pregnancy, explaining 75.49% of total variance. CFA demonstrated excellent model fit for the three-factor model, whereas one-factor and six-factor models were rejected. Internal consistency was excellent (ω_total = 0.98; ω_subscales = 0.90-0.96). Bifactor analysis indicated a strong general factor (ωh = 0.94), supporting interpretation of the total score as the primary indicator of severity. Lack of previous pregnancy (primiparity) and the presence of chronic medical conditions were independently associated with higher tokophobia scores (R² = 0.106). Conclusions The TAQ-Ar demonstrates strong structural validity, reliability, and discriminative capacity, supporting its use as a culturally appropriate tool for research applications and structured clinical assessment in Egyptian maternal health settings.

items.title: Differential Efficacy of a Psychoeducational Intervention for Older Adults Across Face-to-Face and Synchronous Online Modalities: A Doubly Robust Quasi-Experimental Analysis.
items.abstract: Objectives This study evaluates the efficacy of a multicomponent psychoeducational program, Improving Your Strengths and Quality of Life , based on Positive Psychology and the FRAG model (Perceived family Functioning, Resilience, Experiential avoidance and acceptance-related responding, and Gratitude), delivered through face-to-face and synchronous online formats. Methods A quasi-experimental study was conducted with 143 participants (M age = 68.4). Conditions included face-to-face ( n = 42), synchronous online ( n = 29), and a waiting-list control group ( n = 61). To address nonrandom attrition (13.4%) and baseline imbalances, a Double Robustness framework was applied, integrating Inverse Probability of Treatment Weighting (IPTW) with ANCOVA using Huber-White heteroscedasticity-consistent estimator type 3 (HC3) robust estimators. Results Both intervention modalities significantly reduced anxiety and depression versus controls. The online format was associated with greater gains in resilience and gratitude than the face-to-face format. Conversely, the face-to-face modality showed greater adjusted posttest scores in QoL and experiential avoidance and acceptance-related responding. A significant decrease in control/ autonomy was observed in the online group, tentatively suggesting a potential reevaluation of perceived personal agency, an interpretation requiring further replication. Conclusions Multicomponent interventions are effective in both formats. Online format optimizes personal strength-building, whereas face-to-face interaction remains critical for holistic well-being. These findings support dual-access services to optimize older adults' mental health care. Clinical implications Dual formats optimize care: online for internal resources; face-to-face for quality of life.

items.title: Epigenetic clocks and adverse childhood experiences: a meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Epigenetic clocks predict biological age from DNA methylation patterns, providing insight into cellular aging. Different clocks capture distinct aspects of aging, and their relevance to research areas may vary - including early-life stress (ELS) and adverse childhood experiences (ACEs). This meta-analysis evaluates which clocks are most associated to biological consequences of ELS and ACEs. A systematic search was conducted following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO registration: CRD420251047805) to identify studies assessing associations between ACEs or ELS and epigenetic age acceleration (EAA). Eligible human studies used validated ACE or ELS measures and reported DNA methylation-based age from peripheral tissues. Data were extracted and pooled using inverse-variance random-effects models to generate beta coefficients and 95% confidence intervals (RevMan 5.4). Seventeen studies (n = 10,940) met inclusion criteria and used 8 epigenetic clocks: Horvath's, Hannum's, PhenoAge, GrimAge, DunedinPACE, DunedinPoAm, Skin & Blood and PedBE. Amongst these, GrimAge and DunedinPACE demonstrated the strongest, most consistent associations with total ACE counts and subdomains including abuse (total, physical, sexual), neglect (total), and household dysfunction (total, socioeconomic impact). Only DunedinPACE demonstrated robust associations across strata, with significant age differences and no sex effects. This meta-analysis highlights variability in how clocks capture the biological imprint of early adversity. Later-generation clocks like GrimAge and DunedinPACE, integrating physiological and mortality-related methylation signatures, show the most consistent with cumulative effects of ELS and ACEs. These findings emphasise the need for careful clock selection and rigorous study design in stress-biology research, with implications for identifying individuals at risk for EAA and stress-related disorders.

items.title: Aligning episodic memory scores from different time points.
items.abstract: To measure episodic memory, recall of sentences or words with or without cues or enactment is commonly used. In longitudinal studies, participants may join at different points or drop out, yet comparison of episodic memory is still desired. The aim of this study is to explore different methods of linking scores obtained at different time points, to allow for comparability between scores from various test administrations. When the same instrument is used across timepoints, a possibility is to use a test equating method to link the scores by aligning scores from different versions or instruments on the same scale. While equating and linking is well researched for knowledge tests, few studies have applied it to health or psychology instruments, and in those cases mainly used an assumption of equivalent groups and equipercentile equating. This paper differs by focus on different methods to compare scales either within the same test group, or by using collateral information about the participants. The results showed that both proposed approaches are useful and which one to use depends on the assumptions on the data at hand.

items.title: Sleep Health Interventions Among Indigenous Peoples: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Objectives Given the disproportionate burden of sleep problems such as insomnia among Indigenous Peoples, we sought to examine the literature on sleep interventions in these populations. In this scoping review, we aimed to describe traditional Indigenous sleep improvement practices as well as non-Indigenous behavioral sleep interventions (e.g. cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia, CBT-I) that have been adapted for and/or tested with Indigenous communities. Method We searched eight health sciences and Indigenous Peoples databases for articles that described or tested sleep health practices or interventions among Indigenous adolescents or adults located in North America, New Zealand, Australia or the Pacific Islands. Articles were screened and reviewed independently by two reviewers. Results Twenty articles met inclusion criteria. None described Indigenous-specific sleep practices. No articles focused on insomnia, and none mentioned CBT-I. Two articles described sleep health interventions with Indigenous Peoples. The remaining articles described recommendations for sleep health interventions based on their original research findings. Conclusions This review underscores the limited published research on sleep health programs among Indigenous populations and the absence of insomnia-specific interventions, including CBT-I. The scarce literature possibly reflects a misalignment of the research questions and strategies with Indigenous views of sleep, rather than an absence of relevant knowledge. Overall, our findings highlight the need for approaches that address sleep health and insomnia among Indigenous populations. These approaches should be based on holistic frameworks nested in Indigenous worldviews that consider socio-economic inequities, community capacity, and culture.

items.title: Exploring the Experience of Receiving Comprehensive Risk Estimates and Genetic Counseling for Substance Use Disorders.
items.abstract: The study team has built a platform that integrates genomic, behavioral, and environmental data to generate comprehensive risk estimates for substance use disorders (SUDs). We conducted a qualitative study to explore how people respond to this information and the role that genetic counselors may play in its communication. We explored the experiences and perceptions of adults who had received comprehensive risk estimates and genetic counseling related to SUDs as part of a larger randomized controlled trial. We conducted semi-structured interviews with 12 participants and used interpretive description to develop a conceptual model of participants' experiences. Overall, participants demonstrated a good understanding of their results and generally described positive experiences, with individual responses shaped by lived experience. While most participants viewed receiving the comprehensive risk results as the primary benefit of the experience, all participants acknowledged the added value of genetic counseling and identified populations they believed would benefit from it. Although no long-term behavioral changes were described, some participants reported reduced anxiety after receiving their results. It was also suggested that receiving comprehensive risk information alongside genetic counseling could help reduce stigma in the population surrounding SUDs.

items.title: Enterochromaffin cells as sensory hubs of the gut-brain axis.
items.abstract: The mucosal epithelium of the gastrointestinal (GI) tract forms one of the largest exposed surfaces of the body, providing a unique interface through which environmental stimuli are integrated and modulate physiological processes. This review focuses on enterochromaffin cells (ECCs), a rare subtype of enteroendocrine cells comprising <1% of all intestinal epithelial cells. ECCs are excitable cells that express a variety of ion channels and receptors, allowing them to react to varied chemical and mechanical stimuli. Recent studies have shown that ECCs are major players in GI epithelial sensing and affect a variety of physiological and pathophysiological states, such as secretion, GI motility, GI sensory afferent nerve hypersensitivity, satiety, nausea, and visceral pain. This review highlights the diverse functions of ECCs, the peripheral 5-hydroxytryptamine they release, and the nerves they interact with.

items.title: Nonlinear association between daily rest period and psychological distress among Japanese public school teachers: a mixed-effects spline analysis.
items.abstract: This cross-sectional study examined the association between daily rest period (DRP) and psychological distress among Japanese public school teachers. Data were obtained from a nationwide survey conducted in 2022. After applying the eligibility criteria and complete-case analysis, 13,754 teachers were included. DRP was calculated as the average interval between the end of one workday and the start of the next across four weekday intervals. Psychological distress was assessed using the Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K6). Linear mixed-effects models with school-level random intercepts were used. A natural cubic spline model examined the nonlinear association between DRP and K6 score, and sequentially adjusted models examined changes after adjustment for post-clock-out work, job stress, and total sleep time. Shorter DRP was associated with higher K6 scores. The spline model showed a better fit than the linear model and indicated that predicted K6 scores decreased as DRP increased, with the slope becoming more gradual around 13 h. Approximately 13 h was interpreted as a descriptive feature of the spline curve rather than as a statistically identified threshold. These findings suggest that avoiding shorter DRPs and securing sufficient post-work recovery time may be important for teachers' mental health.

items.title: Behavioural Presentation of Children With Down Syndrome and Rigorous Diagnosis of Co-Occurring Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder.
items.abstract: Background High rates of co-occurring attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) among youth with Down syndrome (DS) underscore the importance of understanding outcomes for affected youth. There is a need to clearly differentiate children with DS with and without co-occurring ADHD, as diagnostic specificity has implications for treatment options. The current study aimed to better understand the presentation of ADHD in children with DS in terms of developmental, medical and mental health characteristics, as well as behavioural, adaptive, neuropsychological, academic and functional outcome profiles. Methods Rigorous clinical diagnosis of ADHD was made through clinical interviews and parent and teacher symptom reports in 121 children with DS aged 6-17 years. Children with DS with and without co-occurring ADHD were compared on demographics, developmental characteristics, medical and mental health comorbidities, behavioural challenges and adaptive functioning profiles to determine if prior findings could be replicated and extended. Results We found minimal group differences in demographics and co-occurring conditions, and after controlling for ADHD medication use, we replicated and extended previous findings of challenges in behaviour and executive functioning (EF) and demonstrated novel findings of greater negative functional impacts in children with DS and ADHD compared to peers with DS without ADHD. Conclusions The phenotypic profile of children with DS and ADHD provided by the current study may aid in identifying appropriate supports, treatment targets and care for this dual diagnosis.

items.title: Gut microbiota profiles and neurodevelopmental symptoms in children from a prenatal-risk enriched birth cohort: findings from the PREDO study.
items.abstract: Background Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) and Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) are common neurodevelopmental conditions whose early-life biological correlates remain incompletely understood. Children's gut microbiota may represent a biological pathway through which immune-metabolic and gut-brain signalling links early-life adversity with neurodevelopment. We examined gut microbiota profiles associated with ADHD and ASD symptoms in children from the Prediction and Prevention of Preeclampsia and Intrauterine Growth Restriction (PREDO) birth cohort. Methods We analysed data from 323 Finnish children assessed at a mean age of 8.6 years. Stool microbiota composition was profiled using 16S rRNA sequencing and differential taxonomic abundance was assessed using MaAsLin2. ADHD and ASD symptoms were mother-rated using the Conners' Parent Rating Scale-Revised and Autism Spectrum Screening Questionnaire. Results Clinically relevant ADHD and ASD symptoms were associated with metric-specific reductions in alpha diversity, whereas beta diversity did not differ between groups. Male children with clinically relevant ADHD symptoms showed lower abundance of Lachnospiraceae_FCS020_group, Subdoligranulum, Fusicatenibacter, and Anaerostipes (ps ≤ 0.049). Female children with clinically relevant ADHD symptoms showed a distinct profile, including higher Negativibacillus and Faecalibacterium (p ≤ 0.018). Children with clinically relevant ASD symptoms showed lower abundance of six genera, including Anaerostipes and Lachnospiraceae_ND3007_group (p ≤ 0.001). Conclusions In this prenatal-risk enriched cohort, ADHD and ASD symptoms were associated with distinct gut microbiota profiles, including alterations in taxa implicated in short-chain fatty acid metabolism, immune regulation, and gut-brain signalling. These findings support microbiota-immune-brain pathways as a hypothesis-generating framework for future longitudinal and multi-omics research.

items.title: Beyond clinical symptoms: A psychosocial and machine learning approach to understanding suicidal ideation.
items.abstract: Background Suicide is a major public mental health challenge, and many individuals experiencing suicidal ideation do not meet diagnostic criteria for psychiatric disorders or disclose symptoms during clinical encounters. This limits the effectiveness of symptom-based screening commonly used in mental health services. From an epidemiological and social psychiatry perspective, identifying psychosocial risk and protective factors beyond psychopathology is essential for population-level prevention and early intervention. This study examined whether suicidal ideation can be predicted using psychosocial measures and identified socially and developmentally meaningful risk and resilience markers through explainable machine learning models with external validation. Methods Data were obtained from a mixed clinical and community-based sample of 190 adults. Suicidal ideation was defined using self-reported endorsement of suicide-related thoughts. Predictors consisted exclusively of validated psychosocial measures relevant to social psychiatry and life-course epidemiology, including chronic and perceived stress, childhood adversity, personality traits, attachment styles, coping strategies, and emotion regulation capacities. Five supervised machine learning algorithms were implemented using stratified 5-fold cross-validation. To reduce demographic confounding and address class imbalance, analyses were conducted on both the full dataset and a demographically matched subsample (n = 110) matched on age, gender, education level, and income status, although some residual imbalance remained, notably in income. Hyperparameter optimization targeted both area under the curve (AUC) and F1-score (the harmonic mean of precision and recall) to ensure relevance for low-prevalence outcomes. Predictive performance was estimated using fully nested cross-validation, in which predictor selection, standardization, and hyperparameter optimization were repeated within each training fold. Model generalizability was assessed using an independent external validation sample of university students (n = 84). Model interpretability was examined using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results Random Forest models showed the most robust and generalizable performance. In the matched sample, nested cross-validation yielded an AUC of 0.820 ± 0.131 (mean ± SD) with an F1-score of 0.778 ± 0.137 (F1-optimized) and an AUC of 0.825 ± 0.114 with an F1-score of 0.736 ± 0.078 (AUC-optimized). External validation of the F1-optimized model yielded an AUC of 0.792 (95% confidence interval (95%CI): 0.677-0.896). Explainable analyses consistently identified perceived loneliness as the strongest predictor of suicidal ideation, followed by childhood emotional abuse, limited access to emotion regulation strategies, and low perceived self-efficacy. Higher conscientiousness and extraversion were consistently associated with lower predicted probability of suicidal ideation. Conclusion Self-reported recent suicidal ideation can be predicted using psychosocial and developmental indicators, which may provide information complementary to traditional psychiatric symptom-based approaches, although their incremental predictive value beyond psychiatric symptom measures remains to be established. These findings identify loneliness and emotion regulation as candidate modifiable targets and personality-related factors as potential resilience markers, whose relevance for prevention and risk stratification requires prospective evaluation. Integrating such markers into mental health services and surveillance frameworks may help enhance early identification beyond diagnostic approaches, though this remains to be tested.

items.title: Attitudes to HTLV-1 antenatal screening among women and non-binary individuals in the UK: HTLV Antenatal Screening Survey 2025.
items.abstract: Objectives With targeted HTLV-1 antenatal screening under review in the UK, and no existing evidence on public opinion, we conducted a survey to assess perspectives on HTLV antenatal screening in the UK. Methods Non-pregnant women and non-binary individuals, aged 17-54 years living in the UK were sampled via Prolific into three equal groups, born in: (1) HTLV endemic countries (GRP1), (2) the UK and of Black ethnicity (GRP2), and (3) non-endemic countries of other ethnicities (GRP3). A co-designed questionnaire collected views on screening. Universal versus targeted screening and anticipated anxiety were compared using paired t-tests and one-way ANOVA. Results There were 800 participants (mean age: 35 years). Overall, 84.6% (95%CI: 82.0-87.0) reported that they would accept HTLV antenatal screening. Across all groups, mean scores for the importance of universal HTLV screening were significantly higher than acceptance scores for targeted screening, particularly in GRP1 (p Conclusions Participants showed strong support for introducing universal HTLV antenatal screening, with minimal additional anticipatory anxiety. Incorporating the views of those most affected by policy change is essential to the screening review.

items.title: Examining the Role of Adverse Childhood Experiences in Post-Surgical Pain Among Youth Undergoing Major Surgeries.
items.abstract: "Original" (e.g., abuse, neglect) and "expanded" (e.g., peer victimization, neighbourhood violence) adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are associated with worse chronic pain in youth. However, most research has examined this association only after pain has already become chronic. Consequently, the impact of broader social and structural adversities is rarely considered pre-operatively. To address this gap, we examined the association between pre-surgical ACEs and post-surgical pain intensity and interference in pediatric patients. In this prospective cohort study, 97 youth (aged 10-18 years) were recruited from clinics (e.g., spine, orthopedic) at Alberta Children's Hospital and Hospital for Sick Children. ACEs were assessed prior to surgery using a modified Center for Youth Wellness ACE Questionnaire, capturing 10 core and 9 expanded ACEs. Pain intensity (at rest/during movement) was measured pre-surgery and during recovery (i.e., daily from 0-14 days and 4 months post-surgery) using an 11-point numerical rating scale. Pain interference was assessed using the 4-item Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System. Hierarchical regression analyses, adjusting for age, sex, pre-surgical pain intensity, interference, and chronicity and acute post-surgical pain showed that expanded ACEs, but not original ACEs, predicted higher 4-month pain intensity (rest: b = 0.534; p =.005; movement: b = 0.675; p =.004) and pain interference (b = 2.779; p =.012). These findings suggest that expanded ACEs, particularly harassment/bullying and neighbourhood violence, experienced before surgery are associated with higher pain intensity and interference, highlighting the critical role of broader social and structural adversities during childhood in heightening risk for subsequent post-operative pain. PERSPECTIVE STATEMENT: This study demonstrates that expanded (e.g., bullying, neighbourhood violence) but not original (e.g., abuse, neglect) adverse childhood experiences are associated with worsening post-surgical pain intensity and interference. Findings suggest broader social and environmental stressors contribute to pain persistence, underscoring the importance of integrating pre-operative screening of adversity into clinical care.
