items.title: Axial Skeletal Divergence and Body Depth Evolution in an Adaptive Radiation of Midas Cichlid Fishes in Nicaraguan Crater Lakes.
items.abstract: Fish body depth is a common axis of phenotypic diversification. We investigated the evolutionary relationships between postcranial skeletal divergence and body depth evolution in the Nicaraguan Midas cichlid fish species complex (Amphilophus spp.). This lineage of at least 13 species has rapidly differentiated and repeatedly ecologically diverged across several crater lake habitats over the past < 20,000 years. We used X-ray images to examine the osteological axial skeleton of all named Midas species, as well as several genetically distinct Midas populations endemic to isolated crater lakes. Vertebrae numbers and 14 linear size-adjusted axial skeletal measurements were used for phylogenetically controlled correlations to evaluate whether these traits were highly associated with body depth evolution. Vertebral morphometric and meristic traits showed little correlation with body depth in these Central American cichlids. Conversely, we found strong positive phylogenetic correlations among the pectoral girdle depth, several fin-proximal pterygiophores, and the hemal and neural spines, suggesting a cohesive morphological scaffold. Unlike many teleosts, which have evolved more dorso-ventrally compressed and elongate body forms via increases in the number of vertebrae, the Midas cichlid radiation has diverged primarily in the pectoral girdle and spine architecture to produce their body depth divergence.

items.title: Localized Dipoles Enable Synergistic Kinetic and Thermodynamic Piezoreforming of Waste Plastics.
items.abstract: The piezocatalytic plastic wastes into clean fuels at ambient conditions offers considerable promise, but hindering by both rapid carrier recombination in kinetics and slow surface reactions in thermodynamics. Here, we present a conceptually distinct strategy to simultaneously tackle both core challenges by tailoring localized dipole via anchoring FeSe2 nanoclusters onto MoSe2 piezocatalysts. These clusters induce localized lattice distortions via strong metal-support interaction, generating localized dipole that serve a dual function. Kinetically, localized dipole can effectively capture the electrons excited by piezoelectricity, suppressing recombination and establishing a dominant, long-lived interfacial charge transfer channel directly to the reactants. Thermodynamically, localized dipole can lower the d-band center of the active sites, enhance the adsorption of reaction intermediates, and significantly reduce the activation energy barrier of key intermediates. Therefore, the optimized catalyst exhibits carbon monoxide (CO) evolution of 87.65 µmol·g-1 with high selectivity in the piezocatalytic peroxydisulfate (PDS) system, 30.5 times that of MoSe2. Importantly, after simple pretreatment of polylactic acid (PLA), the CO production reaches 1886.55 µmol·g-1 with stable long-term performance. This work elucidates the fundamental role of localized dipole in harmonizing charge dynamics with surface catalysis, providing an effective approach for designing highly efficient and durable piezocatalysts for challenging chemical transformations.

items.title: Concentration-dependent modulation of cadmium toxicity by molybdenum in Chlorella pyrenoidosa: Multi-endpoint evidence for an antioxidant compensation-to-overload transition.
items.abstract: Molybdenum (Mo) is an essential trace element with potential risks under elevated exposure, whereas cadmium (Cd) is a non-essential toxic metal. Although they may co-occur in mining- and industry-affected aquatic environments, multi-endpoint evidence for how Mo modulates Cd toxicity in aquatic primary producers remains limited. Using Chlorella pyrenoidosa as a freshwater microalgal model, we assessed growth, photosynthetic pigments, protein content, lipid peroxidation and antioxidant responses under single-metal exposures and Mo-Cd co-exposure with Cd fixed at 1 mg L-1. Single Mo exposure showed relatively high algal tolerance, with growth stimulation accompanied by mild stress-related regulation, whereas single Cd exposure caused clear concentration-dependent toxicity, with a 96 h IC50 of 3.298 mg L-1. Under fixed Cd stress, Mo modulated Cd toxicity in a concentration-dependent manner. Compared with Cd-only treatment, 5 mg L-1 Mo reduced 96 h growth inhibition from 10.1% to 3.0% and increased total chlorophyll and protein by 26.2% and 21.4%, respectively, indicating a mitigation-like response at 1-5 mg L-1 Mo. In contrast, 200 mg L-1 Mo increased growth inhibition to 16.5%, reduced total chlorophyll and protein by 25.3% and 45.3%, and increased malondialdehyde (MDA) by 179%. Expected-effect deviation analysis supported this biphasic pattern, with integrated toxicity-oriented deviation scores (Dtox) of -0.263 at 5 mg L-1 and 0.270-0.489 at 50-200 mg L-1. Oxidative-response patterns indicated a shift from antioxidant compensation to oxidative overload under high-Mo co-exposure. These findings identify Mo as a concentration-dependent modulator of Cd toxicity and support multi-endpoint algal biomarkers for interpreting combined-metal stress.

items.title: Responses of fungal communities in roots and soil to sulfur-induced acidification in a meadow steppe: A pH threshold for soil fungal richness.
items.abstract: Although atmospheric sulfur (S) deposition has declined substantially in China in recent decades, it remains an important contributor to soil acidification, with its contribution comparable to or greater than that of nitrogen (N) deposition in Asia; whilst substantial S inputs persist in northeastern China and Inner Mongolia. Yet how reduced soil pH would affect fungal diversity loss and the driving factors underlying diversity changes remains poorly understood. Based on a 6-year field experiment with eight S addition rates ranging from 0 to 50 g S m-2 yr-1 in a meadow steppe in Inner Mongolia, we elucidated how S addition modulates root and soil fungal communities. Our results show that the effects of S addition on fungal α-diversity were niche-specific. S15 and S20 increased root symbiotic fungal richness, possibly in association with changes in plant-fungal mutualisms, whereas soil fungal α-diversity was lowest at S50, possibly reflecting soil acidification induced by S addition. Soil fungal richness at S50 did not differ significantly from the control. Segmented regression estimated pH breakpoints of 5.88 (95% CI 4.51-6.29) for soil fungal richness and 5.62 (95% CI 4.89-6.42) for root fungal richness. The Davies test supported a change in slope in soil (P = 0.042), with limited evidence for a slope change in roots (P = 0.14). Variance partitioning analyses showed that below the soil pH threshold, the largest fraction of variation in soil fungal richness was jointly explained by soil properties, plant factors, and fungal network attributes. Overall, root and soil fungal communities responded differently to S addition, and the factors associated with fungal richness differed above and below the fitted pH breakpoints.

items.title: Age- and sex-related differences in Staphylococcus epidermidis and Corynebacterium spp. on the adult ocular surface.
items.abstract: Ocular surface bacterial flora is a potential source of bacterial keratitis and post-operative endophthalmitis, but age- and sex-related differences in ocular surface bacterial flora and antimicrobial resistance remain unclear. We investigated these differences in bacterial isolates and levofloxacin (LVFX) susceptibility in adults. Retrospective study. We reviewed microbiological data on conjunctival isolates from 18,053 eyes of 11,677 adults without ocular infection undergoing ophthalmic surgery at the Miyata Eye Hospital between June 2018 and December 2023. Data were analyzed using generalized additive and log-linear model. LVFX susceptibility was determined using the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute broth microdilution protocol. 22,561 bacterial isolates (11,081 from women; 11480 from men) were obtained from adults aged >19 years. The number of species isolated from women was lower than men, and increased at a rate of 1.19 and 1.09 per 10 years of age in women and men, respectively (p < 0.0001). Staphylococcus epidermidis and Corynebacterium spp. were predominant across all age groups. Under 80 years of age, methicillin-sensitive S. epidermidis (MSSE) was isolated more frequently from men than from women. Corynebacterium spp. increased with age in both sexes. Between age 40-90 years, LVFX resistance in MSSE was higher in women than in men, whereas LVFX resistance in Corynebacterium spp. increased with age regardless of sex. S. epidermidis and Corynebacterium spp. showed age- and sex-related differences in isolation frequency and fluoroquinolone susceptibility. Age and sex may influence ocular surface microbial ecology, antimicrobial resistance, and perioperative infection control.

items.title: Biodegradation of corn stover cuticle by Streptomyces griseorubens CUT-1: Performance, key enzymes, and metabolic pathway.
items.abstract: Efficient biodegradation of crop stover is important for agricultural waste management and sustainable biomass utilization. In this study, an esterase-producing strain, Streptomyces griseorubens CUT-1, was screened using polycaprolactone selective medium and evaluated for its ability to transform the corn stover epidermal surface. The strain was able to grow with pretreated corn stover epidermis as the sole carbon source. SEM and AFM analyses showed disruption of the epidermal surface and a marked increase in surface roughness after strain treatment. XPS analysis revealed increased oxygen-containing functional groups and surface polarity, while the average water contact angle decreased from 90.55° to 60.59°, indicating reduced surface hydrophobicity and modification of the associated cuticular barrier. Transcriptomic analysis showed significant changes in genes related to carbon metabolism, substrate transport, and lignocellulose-associated functions. Genes encoding putative cuticle-related enzymes, including cutinase, esterases, lipases, oxidases, and dehydrogenases, were also up-regulated. LC-MS analysis detected several C16- and C18-derived metabolites, including 16-hydroxyhexadecanoic acid, consistent with the transformation of cutin-derived components. Based on the combined surface characterization, transcriptomic responses, and metabolite profiles, a potential biodegradation process involving hydrolysis of ester-linked cuticular components, subsequent oxidation and chain shortening of aliphatic compounds, and further incorporation into central carbon metabolism was proposed. These results provide new insights into actinomycete-mediated transformation of corn stover epidermal and cuticular components.

items.title: Ultrasonic piezoelectric and heterojunction nanocatalytic probe of MXene@ZrMOF for the RRS determination of carbaryl.
items.abstract: Ultrasound is the most commonly used means for generating the piezoelectric effect, by which a safe and convenient new approach was provided for the development and application of piezoelectric-nanocatalytic molecular recognition probes. Carbaryl (CB) is a carbamate pesticide that was widely used in agricultural production. Therefore, the development of a new ultrasonic piezoelectric nanocatalytic analytical method for detecting trace levels of pesticide residues is of great significance. In this study, an ultrastrong piezoelectric surface-imprinted nanocatalytic probe of MXene@ZrMOF was prepared. The two piezoelectric fields of MXene and Zr metal-organic framework ZrMOF were coupled with the heterojunction fields to enhance the indicator reaction of HAuCl4-malic acid (MA). The produced gold nanoparticles (AuNP) exhibit strong resonance Rayleigh scattering effect (RRS) at 370 nm. CB could be specifically recognized by the probe, and its catalysis was enhanced linearly. CB can be determined by this RRS method in the concentration range of 3.75-73.75 nmol/L, with a detection limit of 1.19 nmol/L. The method was applied to the determination of CB in pea shoot and tomato samples. For pea shoot samples, the recoveries were 92.0-103.4% with RSDs of 2.43-7.29%; for tomato samples, the recoveries were 90.9-108.1% with RSDs of 2.11-5.42%. Interference tests including inorganic ions, anions, saccharides, vitamin C, glycyrrhizin, other pesticides, and three carbamate pesticides showed no significant interference within ±10% error, demonstrating the good sensitivity and selectivity of the proposed method for CB. This method provides a new analytical approach for pesticide residue analysis.

items.title: An occupational medicine perspective; lessons from an Arctic research settlement.
items.abstract: This occupational health risk assessment was undertaken in the austere high Arctic Ny Alesund Research Station, the most northerly permanent settlement on the globe, and explores the occupational health impacts seen in this extreme environment. The community hosts researchers from a vast array of subject areas, such as ecology, glaciology, oceanography and astrophysics. This study took the form of a workplace health risk assessment using both qualitative and quantitative assessment methods, such as observational walk-through surveys and environmental measurements, including ambient temperature, wind speed and UV levels. The assessment identified potential circadian rhythm disruption by polar nights and midnight sun, UV-associated skin cancer and sunburn, cataracts, musculoskeletal strain/injury and thermal injury as key health risks. Polar bears, marine life, snowmobile and powerboat use, and climbing and traversing 55% of the glacier cover present a special hazard profile. A focus on communication and relationships, increased exercise levels, reduced screen time, and reduced air pollution may be seen as potential benefits. There are knowledge gaps highlighted which require further study in terms of the long-term health effects of persistent organic pollutants and of repeated cold exposure, as well as how to manage medically vulnerable cold-exposed workers from an occupational health perspective.

items.title: L(2,1)-LABELING ON SEVERAL FAMILIES OF STAR GRAPHS
items.abstract: This research discusses L(2,1) labeling on some families of star graphs, namely planter graphs (R_n), lilly graphs (l_n), and umbrella graphs (U_(m,n)). The L(2,1) labeling is a type of graph labeling that assigns nonnegative integer labels to each vertex of a graph such that two vertices that are one edge apart have labels that differ by at least two, and two vertices that are two edges apart have labels that differ by at least one. This study uses axiomatic descriptive methods and pattern detection in determining the minimum span value of the L(2,1) labeling, denoted as lambda_2,1(G). The results show that lambda_2,1(R_n) = n+3, lambda_2,1(l_n) = 2n+3, and lambda_2,1(U_(m,n)) = m+2. These three graphs were chosen because their L(2,1) labeling is still an open problem and has not been widely studied in previous literature. This research is expected to contribute to the development of graph labeling theory and serve as an initial reference for future researchers. A suggestion for further research is to explore the minimum value of the L(2,1) labeling range in other classes of graphs that have not yet been determined.

items.title: An ALMA sub-kiloparsec test of the Kennicutt--Schmidt relation in a strongly lensed dusty star-forming galaxy at z∼2.78
items.abstract: Star formation is a key process driving galaxy evolution, but understanding how it proceeds within the interstellar medium (ISM) requires observations that resolve the cold molecular gas and dust on sub-kiloparsec (sub-kpc) scales. At z,∼,2--3, near the peak of cosmic star formation, such spatial resolution can generally only be achieved through strong gravitational lensing. We present an ALMA study of SMM:J065837.6-555705, hereafter SMM,J0658, a 20 main-sequence star-forming galaxy at z_̊m CO,=,2.7768,±,0.0002 that is lensed by the Bullet Cluster (1E,0657-56; z,=,0.296) into three images. We used 0 and 0 ALMA Band-3 data to test the Kennicutt--Schmidt (KS) relation at sub-kpc scales at cosmic noon. Using a JWST-based parametric strong-lensing model of the Bullet Cluster, we reconstructed source-plane and rest-frame 803 ̆pmum dust-continuum maps down to physical scales of ∼,200 pc. We derived spatially resolved maps of the intrinsic molecular gas mass surface density (Σ_̊m mol), star formation rate surface density (Σ_̊m SFR), and molecular gas depletion time (τ_̊m dep), and quantified the scale dependence of the CO-to-dust flux ratio over apertures from 200 pc to 3.2 kpc across the reconstructed source. CO(3--2) The 0 ALMA data reveal massive (M_̊m mol,∼,10^9 _⊙) and dense star-forming clumps, with Σ_̊m mol,∼,1.3--2.3 times10^3 ̊m M ̊m M ̊m pc ^ -2 , Σ_̊m SFR,∼,0.5--2.3 $ ̊m M _⊙, ̊m yr ^ -1 , ̊m kpc ^ -2 $, and τ_̊m dep,∼,0.82--2.56 Gyr. The observed CO--dust spatial de-correlation produces a strong scale dependence on τ_̊m dep. We find a KS-relation breakdown scale of 0.8,±,0.1 kpc in SMM,J0658, which is consistent with the resolution of individual regions tracing distinct evolutionary stages of the star formation cycle within the ISM. The ALMA and JWST data also reveal evidence of a lensed galaxy pair at z,∼,2.78, although it remains uncertain whether SMM,J0658 is undergoing an early-stage interaction that could contribute to an enhanced star formation efficiency in localized regions of the ISM. Our results show that the apparent universality of the KS relation breaks down once individual regions of the star formation process are spatially resolved, in line with observations from the local Universe to z,∼,1. We extend this picture to z,∼,2.78, opening a new window onto the resolved properties of the clumpy cold ISM and the star formation cycle at cosmic noon.

items.title: Searching for substellar companion candidates with Gaia. V. M dwarfs within 15,pc studied with absolute astrometry, radial velocities, and direct imaging
items.abstract: In this work, we survey M-type stars within 15,pc observed by Gaia based on their colour, magnitude, and quality of astrometric data. We aim to detect new substellar companions using primarily astrometry and, when available, proper-motion anomaly (PMa) along with radial velocity (RV), and direct imaging (DI) data. Gaia We used the tool to search for bound companions around 582 M dwarfs. We identified all previously known stellar and planetary companions that were consistent with the excess signal. For all newly identified companions, we computed detection limits in the (mass, semi-major axis) parameter space using archival RV and DI data, to rule out the presence of a stellar companion. The joint analysis of the parameter space allowed by astrometry and constrained by RV and DI data provides tight constraints on the nature of the companion. GaiaPMEX Gaia We find that 156 M dwarfs have a bound companion within the sensitivity domain. Of these, the astrometric signals of 37 are attributable to known stellar companions, while those of seven are attributable to known substellar companions. We report 35 new substellar companions, including at least ten giant planets orbiting between 0.2,au and 2,au, with masses close to Gaia M _ Jup . We also report 77 substellar candidates and provide detection limits using astrometric, RV, and DI data for 50 stars with known exoplanets and no significant excess noise. Gaia This work reveals a significant population of new substellar companions to M-type stars, challenging core accretion models. These results provide crucial inputs for estimating occurrence rates and studying the architecture of planetary systems around M dwarfs. Some of the new companions presented here, located beyond the water ice line, are prime targets for DI or coronagraphy observations with JWST or the ELT.

items.title: Observational evidence of the Gaia-Enceladus-Sausage merger's influence on the opposite side of the Galactic center
items.abstract: The Gaia-Enceladus-Sausage (GES) merger event, which occurred approximately 8 -- 11 Gyr ago, is believed to be a key event that shaped the current structure of the Galactic inner halo. Although the remnants of this event have been extensively studied and confirmed to dominate the chemical and dynamical properties of the halo on the near side of the Galactic center (GC; i.e., the side facing the Sun), systematic observational evidence of the far side of the GC (i.e., the side beyond the GC as seen from the Sun) being similarly affected by the GES is lacking. This study is aimed at investigating, using a large sample of red giant stars, whether the far side exhibits signatures of the GES merger event and testing whether the influence of the GES on the Galactic inner halo is global through comparison with the near side. A sample of 14,056 red giant stars was selected from the SkyMapper Southern Survey Fourth Data Release (SMSS DR4) and the Gaia Third Data Release (Gaia DR3) through a series of stringent quality cuts designed to minimize disk contamination. We analyzed and compared the metallicity distributions, velocity-space distributions, velocity dispersions, anisotropy parameters, and action-space characteristics of the near side and the far side. We further demonstrate, through a series of robustness tests, that this global symmetry is not an artifact of measurement uncertainties, residual disk contamination, or incomplete removal of the Sagittarius stream. Observational evidence is found for the influence of the GES merger event on the far side. A chemical-abundance analysis shows that the far side also contains a metal-rich component that peaked at Fe/H ≈ -1.4. A kinematic analysis reveals that the metal-rich population (-1.7 < Fe/H łeq -1.3) on the far side exhibits GES-typical features consistent with the near side, namely a ``sausage''-shaped distribution in velocity space and a velocity anisotropy parameter as high as β ∼ 0.8 -- 0.9. An action-space analysis further shows that 10.86% of stars on the far side bear the dynamical imprint of the GES, which is statistically consistent with 11.56% on the near side. The residual prograde rotation on the far side persists under increasingly aggressive disk-removal cuts, indicating that it reflects a genuine kinematic signal rather than residual disk contamination. These results demonstrate that the GES merger event affected not only the near side but also the global structure of the entire inner halo (r < 28 kpc), with its influence also being evident on the far side, and exhibiting spatial symmetry.

items.title: MAGIC’s interferometric diameters of θ Ophiuchi and β CMa andcomparison with asteroseismic modelling
items.abstract: β Cephei type stars are massive (8-25M_⊙) and known to have several pulsation modes with periods typically of a few hours. Despite a better understanding of their physics since 1992, the inner structure of these stars involves key stellar physics processes that are still uncertain. Asteroseismology offers insights into these variable stars by analysing pulsation modes, helping to probe their inner layers and understand their structure and mixing processes. Building an asteroseismic model that would reliably predict an observable of a β Cephei star would be a significant improvement, thereby reducing the uncertainty on their internal structure (e.g., overshooting parameter α or metallicity). We measure the angular diameter of two β Cephei stars, þeta Oph and β CMa, using the MAGIC Stellar Intensity Interferometer and compare them, together with the Gaia and Hipparcos parallaxes, to the predictions of the asteroseismic model. The latter are based on Levenberg-Marquardt local minimisation of stellar evolution model parameters to fit observed pulsation modes. In the case of þeta Oph, the observed angular diameters are compatible with the asteroseismic model. For β CMa, the radius derived from the angular diameter and the Hipparcos parallax is in tension, at the 2.5σ level, with the asteroseismic prediction. We show that this tension mirrors a pre-existing conflict between independent spectroscopic determinations of the surface gravity of the star, that percent-level systematics of the stellar models are quantitatively insufficient to explain it, and that it most likely points to a bias of the Hipparcos parallax. In the frame of this paper, the statistical uncertainty on the interferometric results is similar to the systematic uncertainty on the parallaxes. With the already implemented addition in early 2024 of the first Large-Sized Telescope of the northern hemisphere array of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO-North LST-1) to the setup, the uncertainty in the angular diameter of these stars is expected to decrease by an order of magnitude, allowing to further constrain stellar evolution models and parallaxes.

items.title: Super-orbital period evolution of Hercules X-1
items.abstract: Hercules X-1 ( is one of the most well-studied X-ray binaries that exhibits super-orbital modulation of its X-ray flux. The origin of the super-orbital periodicity in is still under debate between counter-precessing, twisted--tilted accretion disc and free precession of the neutron star, with no clear consensus. The fluctuations in the super-orbital periodicity in with data obtained during the 1970--1990 period have been reported to be stochastic in nature with no long-term trend. We aim to investigate the long-term trend of the super-orbital modulations in with more recent and uninterrupted data from 1995--2025 to examine the presence of features that may favour or disfavour the proposed mechanisms. The main aim of this study is to test the stability of the super-orbital period using data available from sensitive all-sky instruments. We probed the variation in the super-orbital period in using long-term light curves from five X-ray monitors, namely ̊xte, and along with data available in the literature, together spanning ∼50 yr. We employed multiple timing-analysis tools to trace the long-term evolution of the super-orbital period. In the uninterrupted data of super-orbital modulation for the last 30 years, the super-orbital period in s s is decreasing at the rate of ∼ -5 10^ -5 -1 . The analysis of the diagram showed that the super-orbital period in also has variabilities at shorter time scales on top of an overall decay. Hence, a simple quadratic function cannot explain the variabilities observed in the curve. A positive correlation was found between the mean count rate and super-orbital period obtained at different linear segments of the curve. The modulation of the super-orbital period in from a few to a few tens of super-orbital cycles suggests that there is a restoring mechanism in the system. We discuss the possible mechanisms responsible for the observed long-term decay and short-term variabilities.

items.title: TORNADO study: what impact did the COVID-19 pandemic have on psychotropic drug user profiles? Application of a multichannel sequence analysis based on the French healthcare database.
items.abstract: Since the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic, an increase in the delivery of psychotropic drugs has been observed. However, there are no more precise data to date on the profile of people affected by these changes in consumption. The aim of this study was therefore to assess its impact on the profile of psychotropic drug users. Two historical cohorts, a "COVID cohort" (2020-2021) and a "pre-COVID cohort" (2018-2019), were constituted from the National Health Data System (SNDS) database. Within each of these two cohorts, three distinct subpopulations were defined according to the presence of reimbursements for psychotropic drugs during year n-1 (no previous use population, low previous use population, high previous use population). Then we analyzed reimbursements for psychotropic drugs using a multichannel sequence analysis and performed clustering analysis of sequences. The clusters identified in the three sub-populations of the COVID cohort were broadly similar to the clusters identified in the three sub-populations of the pre-COVID cohort with equivalent proportions. However, the COVID cohort differs in some aspects from the pre-COVID cohort: (1) the loss of a cluster of hypnotic users in the low previous use population, (2) earlier and longer consumption of certain psychotropic drugs (antidepressants, anxiolytics) in some clusters of the no previous use and low previous use populations, (3) a higher proportion of individuals affiliated to a specific insurance plan for low-income patients in some clusters corresponding to psychiatric profiles thought to be more severe in the three sub-populations and (4) a change in the sex ratio in some clusters of the no previous use and low previous use populations. In addition to providing answers to the specific question of the impact of the Covid-19 health crisis on the profile of psychotropic drug users, this study highlights the interest and feasibility of the multichannel sequence analysis method in pharmaco-epidemiology.

items.title: Pseudoganglia of the nerve to teres minor: anatomical and histological study with possible explanation for their existence.
items.abstract: Previous descriptions have identified a pseudoganglion frequently associated with the nerve to teres minor (NTM), a branch of the axillary nerve. This anatomical study was performed to better understand this association and theorize a potential pathomechanism. In the prone position, anatomical dissection of the NTM was carried out on 72 sides adult anatomical donors. The presence of a pseudoganglion was noted, and when it was present, morphometrics were performed. Select pseudoganglia of the NTM were submitted for histological analysis. In specimens with a pseudoganglion of the NTM, its relationships to surrounding tissues were observed with range of motion of the arm. The findings demonstrated that among the cases studied, a pseudoganglion was evident in the NTM in 97.2% of the cases. During abduction (up to 90 degrees) of the arm, all pseudoganglia approached and were compressed by the long head of the triceps brachii. The histological composition observed in sections of the fusiform enlargement corresponded to the cell types typically found in peripheral nerves and sections of the NTM located proximal to the enlargement. Notably, no ganglion (neuronal cell bodies) cells were identified in these selected sections. The NTM was normal histologically proximal, at, and distal to the pseudoganglia. Based on our study, most specimens have a pseudoganglion on the NTM. We believe this adaptation around the NTM is a response to repeated conflict between it and the long head of the triceps brachii during arm abduction.

items.title: Some Fires Leave Life Behind: A Comparative Study of Spatial Burn Patterns in Prescribed Fires and Wildfires.
items.abstract: Prescribed burning is increasingly used in the Brazilian Cerrado to reduce fuel loads and prevent large wildfires, yet how it shapes fine-scale burn mosaics relative to wildfires is poorly known. We sampled 535 transects across 45 fire events (27 prescribed fires, 18 wildfires) in ten protected areas of Minas Gerais, Brazil, recording ground cover every ~1 m as burned vegetation, unburned vegetation, bare soil, or rock. Using mixed-effects models and event-level permutation tests, we compared unburned cover and the number, length, distribution, and composition of unburned sequences. Prescribed fires retained more unburned cover than wildfires (28.0% vs. 17.9%; p = 0.006) and more unburned sequences per transect (6.1 vs. 4.2; p = 0.006), mainly because they rarely left 50-m transects completely burned (0.6% vs. 10.1%). Unburned sequences were more concentrated among transects in wildfires (Morisita's Iδ = 1.65 vs. 1.12; p < 0.001), but sequence length and its variability did not differ, and most sequences were about 1 m long. The strongest contrast was in composition: rock and soil were equally available in both fire types ( ~ 15% of points) and made up nearly all unburned cover after wildfires, whereas unburned vegetation covered 13.6% of points after prescribed fires versus 0.5% after wildfires, accounting for about 90% of the difference. Prescribed fires thus differed from wildfires less in the geometry of the unburned mosaic than in the vegetation retained within it. We present a rapid, low-cost protocol for post-fire patchiness assessment that distinguishes vegetated refugia from ground that cannot burn.

items.title: Psychological distress and mental health service use among Asian New Zealanders: evidence from linked national survey and administrative data.
items.abstract: Aim This study examined psychological distress and mental health service use among Asian New Zealanders, disaggregated into Chinese, Indian, and Other Asian sub-groups, compared with sole Europeans. We also assessed socio-demographic factors and unmet health needs as predictors. Methods We used linked New Zealand Health Survey (2011/2012-2018/2019 pooled) and administrative data from the Integrated Data Infrastructure. Psychological distress was measured using the Kessler Psychological Distress Scale. Mental health service use was identified via publicly funded hospitalisations for mood and anxiety disorders and dispensing of antidepressants and anxiolytics. Weighted Poisson regression estimated relative risks (RRs) comparing Asian sub-groups with sole Europeans and examined predictors within sub-groups. Results There were no meaningful differences in risk of high psychological distress across groups. All Asian sub-groups were less likely to use mental health services compared with sole Europeans (adjusted RRs [aRRs] 0.32-0.59). Unmet need for primary care predicted higher psychological distress (aRRs 2.24-4.53) and greater service use across all sub-groups (aRRs 1.99-2.37). Gender and New Zealand -born patterns varied by sub-group and were obscured in aggregated analyses. Conclusion Asian New Zealanders are not homogeneous in mental health service use. Inequities exist despite comparable psychological distress, highlighting structural and cultural barriers. Disaggregated analyses and improved access to culturally responsive primary care are critical for mental health equity.

items.title: Environmental noise levels in mixed-use urban zones of Kuwait: a zone-level assessment against regulatory and health-based guideline values.
items.abstract: Environmental noise is an undercharacterised public-health concern in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. This study reports an empirical, policy-oriented assessment of environmental noise across six mixed-use urban zones in Kuwait. The field campaign was carried out by a commercial environmental monitoring provider and comprised 15-min measurements at 432 locations during predefined daytime, evening, and nighttime windows, with weekday and weekend replication; the authors analysed the dataset released to them and did not take part in the measurements. The overall site-level mean Leq,day was 64.1 ± 8.7 dB(A), and zone means ranged from 56.4 ± 9.1 dB(A) in Jahra to 71.3 ± 5.2 dB(A) in Shuwaikh, with strong spatial clustering of the measured levels near arterial-industrial interfaces (Moran's I = 0.72, p < 0.001). The measurements were compared period by period with the limits of KEPA Decision No. 8 of 2017, which sets separate daytime, evening, and nighttime values for four categories of receiving area: the daytime mean exceeds the applicable limit in three of the six zones, no zone exceeds its evening limit, and only one zone exceeds at night. Interpreted separately against WHO health-based guidance, the sample-based Lden indicator exceeds 53 dB(A) at 88.2% of locations. That contrast-largely within national limits, largely above the WHO reference-is the central finding. Because each period was represented by a short-term sample, the Lden values are indicative screening estimates rather than strategic long-term exposure indicators, and the regulatory assessment is reported at zone level because the location-level land-use classification was not part of the released dataset.

items.title: Cancer Survivorship in Eastern Europe: Evolving Oncology Care Beyond Treatment.
items.abstract: This narrative review examines how selected cancer rehabilitation approaches are being integrated into survivorship care across Eastern and Central Europe. It focuses on rehabilitation as a practical indicator of whether oncology care is evolving beyond treatment, while acknowledging that comprehensive survivorship care encompasses additional domains. The literature discussed includes supervised and home-based exercise, lymphedema care, cardio-oncology rehabilitation, telerehabilitation, virtual and game-based interventions, and early implementation models. Breast cancer and selected adult long-term survivor populations are most extensively represented, particularly in reports from Poland, the Czech Republic, and Slovakia. Study designs and clinical settings vary, limiting conclusions about implementation across the region. The reviewed studies and practice reports suggest growing attention to cancer rehabilitation, but integration into survivorship pathways remains uneven. Referral processes, workforce roles, care coordination, and participation outcomes warrant further evaluation. Rehabilitation offers a practical entry point for strengthening patient-centered survivorship care, alongside other rehabilitation domains that are not examined in depth in this review.

items.title: Influenza virus and coronavirus: evolution, epidemiology, antiviral drugs and vaccine development.
items.abstract: Influenza viruses and coronaviruses are enveloped, single-stranded RNA viruses that pose persistent and pandemic threats to global public health. Despite belonging to distinct viral families, they share remarkable parallels in modes of transmission, clinical manifestations, and socioeconomic impacts, yet diverge fundamentally in evolutionary mechanisms and epidemiological trajectories. This review compares the history, spread, treatments, and vaccines for these two types of viruses. Influenza viruses possess a segmented genome, which enables antigenic shift and reassortment. In contrast, coronaviruses have large, nonsegmented genomes and rely on recombination, mutation accumulation, and insertions to achieve host switching and immune evasion. Both spread to humans through wildlife (intermediate hosts), live animal markets, intensive agriculture, and global travel. Antiviral strategies have evolved from M2 and neuraminidase inhibitors (NAIs) for influenza to polymerase inhibitors and protease inhibitors for coronavirus, yet drug resistance remains a common challenge. Vaccine platforms, including inactivated, live-attenuated, recombinant, mRNA, and viral vector technologies, have been deployed against both viruses. This review concludes that integrated, platform-based preparedness, encompassing broad-spectrum antivirals, universal vaccines, and proactive ecological surveillance, is essential for building pandemic-resilient public health systems capable of responding to both influenza and coronavirus threats, as well as future emerging respiratory viruses.

items.title: A National Pediatric Primary Care Research Agenda.
items.abstract: Pediatric primary care (PPC) promotes child wellbeing through health supervision, anticipatory guidance, screening, and intervention. Given an evolving PPC landscape, content experts collaborated with the American Academy of Pediatrics Pediatric Research in Office Settings network in an iterative, multiyear process to create a PPC research agenda to advance child health that reflects professional and family priorities. Using an adapted nominal group technique, we identified research areas of focus based on (1) what PPC clinicians said they frequently encounter in practice; (2) the extent of the problem for families nationally; (3) evidence gaps; and (4) areas in which research could have the highest impact on child health. From 2022 to 2024, we synthesized contributor feedback from 8 key content expert sessions. This process resulted in 6 interconnected domains of highest priority for PPC research: (1) child mental health, (2) obesity, (3) communicating science to support families, (4) pediatric workforce, (5) injury prevention, and (6) adolescent health. We identified cross-cutting themes that warrant research in connection with these 6 prioritized domains. Examples of such themes include removing barriers to access and ensuring quality services for all children; under-resourced communities; care coordination and linkages within and outside PPC; supporting parents/caregivers; and technology and social media, which can serve as tools to enhance practice and can be assets or threats to child wellbeing. This manuscript details a vision for a national, coordinated PPC research agenda to inform investigators' and funders' efforts to advance primary health care and the health of all children based on our results.

items.title: Progress on eliminating New Zealand's HIV epidemic by 2030: successes and opportunities.
items.abstract: Aotearoa New Zealand has the tools to end human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) transmission and the strategic framework to deliver it. In this viewpoint, we assess progress on the Government's HIV action plan 2023-2030, combining insights from epidemiological and behavioural surveillance, policy responses and the experiences of affected communities. New HIV diagnoses have declined markedly among gay, bisexual and other men who have sex with men (GBM), echoing an increase in HIV prevention behaviours. HIV diagnoses remain very low in key populations such as sex workers and people who inject drugs. These encouraging results show that investing in prevention-technologies and environments-is working. However, HIV diagnoses are static among Māori and Pacific GBM, and must decrease among heterosexual women and men, indicating that the benefits are uneven. With 5 years left to meet the HIV elimination target, we identify gaps and emerging challenges, highlight opportunities, propose new initiatives and reflect on the conditions for success. More can be done to improve HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) uptake, HIV testing innovations are needed and routine "opt-out" HIV screening is warranted in sentinel settings. HIV stigma needs to be eliminated to improve the lives of people with HIV and remove barriers to prevention.

items.title: Scenario-based analysis of stage distribution and stage-specific survival among Māori diagnosed with lung cancer in Aotearoa New Zealand.
items.abstract: Lung cancer survival in Aotearoa New Zealand differs between Māori and European populations. This study used scenario-based standardisation to compare survival when Māori estimates were standardised to the European stage distribution, stage-specific survival or both. The scenarios aimed to assess which of these differences was associated with the larger change in estimated survival. National cancer registry data were used to identify all primary lung cancers for Māori and European populations diagnosed between 2015 and 2024, with mortality follow-up to December 2025. Survival was modelled using sex-specific Cox regression, including age at diagnosis and diagnosis year, ethnicity, Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) summary stage, and an ethnicity-by-stage interaction. Survival probabilities at 1, 3 and 5 years were estimated. Scenarios were constructed for Māori in which stage distribution, stage-specific survival or both were standardised to those of Europeans. Five-year survival was lower for Māori than for Europeans among males (11.3%, 95% confidence interval [CI] 9.4-13.7 vs 16.8%, 95% CI 15.2-18.7) and females (17.1%, 95% CI 15.0-19.5 vs 24.2%, 95% CI 22.5-26.2). Standardising stage distribution increased estimated 5-year survival to 13.5% (95% CI 11.4-16.2) for Māori males and 20.2% (95% CI 17.9-22.9) for Māori females. Standardising stage-specific survival produced larger increases, to 17.2% (95% CI 15.4-19.3) and 23.4% (95% CI 21.5-25.6), respectively. Estimates were highest when both were standardised, at 19.5% (95% CI 17.7-21.7) and 26.6% (95% CI 24.7-28.8). Differences in both stage distribution and stage-specific survival were associated with lung cancer survival inequities. Standardising stage-specific survival produced a larger change than standardising stage distribution alone.

items.title: Estimating selected screening-related parameters using New Zealand-specific glaucoma prevalence data: optometry visits for glaucoma screening at age 45 years.
items.abstract: Regular eye examinations for glaucoma at age 45 years and every 5 years after have been promoted in the New Zealand setting. We aimed to estimate selected screening-related parameters for optometry visits for glaucoma screening at age 45 years. Selected glaucoma screening parameters were identified from the literature, and data were extracted from a New Zealand longitudinal study (Dunedin Study) on the prevalence of glaucoma in 45-year-olds. Out-of-pocket costs were estimated from New Zealand optometry assessment fees. We estimate that routine screening for glaucoma within a New Zealand cohort of 45-year-olds has a low positive predictive value of 5.4%. That is, for every 100 people who get a positive screening result for glaucoma, around 95 of these diagnoses would be expected to be false positives and only five would truly have glaucoma. The number needed to screen to detect one case of glaucoma was estimated at 177. The out-of-pocket cost per true case of glaucoma detected was around NZ$24,300, equivalent to NZ$5.8 million at the national level to detect 241 true cases per year (assuming 70% uptake). However, there would be many other additional costs likely with any formal screening programme encompassing the full clinical pathway. These New Zealand-specific findings for selected screening parameters align with recommendations from international agencies showing that there is a lack of evidence in favour of population screening for glaucoma. Future research could focus on evaluating more targeted screening or risk-based screening, e.g., using artificial intelligence-assisted fundus imaging.

items.title: General practitioners' experiences with pathology laboratory services and service disruptions in Aotearoa New Zealand: a qualitative study.
items.abstract: The aim of this study was to assess general practitioners' (GPs) knowledge about the medical laboratory landscape: how do they use laboratory services and what are their views on the strikes and current system? Sixth year medical students conducted open-ended interviews with a convenience sample of 17 GPs using a protocol developed from the literature and discussion with a laboratory scientist. Interviews were recorded and transcribed. Transcripts were abductively coded. Four themes were identified: GPs were satisfied with their local laboratory service; there was variation in GP knowledge about laboratory structures; affected GPs struggled with the impact of the strikes but questioned whether there was significant public awareness of the strikes in among the various challenges in the healthcare system; laboratory service processes varied and GPs had many improvement suggestions. GPs work closely with laboratories and value the relationships they have with skilled laboratory scientists. Current systems put pressure on laboratories' ability to function effectively, which poses risks to equity, transparency and system resilience.

items.title: Artificial intelligence, environmental pollution, and environmental justice: opportunities, challenges, and emerging public health risks.
items.abstract: Environmental pollution remains a major contributor to global disease burden and premature mortality, with persistent exposure inequalities affecting vulnerable populations worldwide. In turn, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful tool for analyzing complex datasets, identifying environmental patterns, predicting pollution trends, and supporting evidence-based decision-making. Consequently, AI is increasingly applied in environmental monitoring, exposure assessment, epidemiology, climate science, toxicology, and governance. This narrative review critically examines the interplay between AI, environmental pollution, public health, and environmental justice. AI offers substantial benefits such as improved air- and water-quality monitoring, enhanced risk assessment, advanced remote sensing, and better identification of environmental inequalities. However, it also presents emerging environmental and health challenges. Growing evidence indicates that AI systems , particularly large-scale generative models and their data-center infrastructure, require significant energy, water, and material resources, contributing to greenhouse gas emissions, water consumption, demand for critical minerals, and electronic waste. These burdens may disproportionately affect already disadvantaged communities. AI has the potential to support more equitable environmental policies by improving detection of pollution hotspots and strengthening community-level monitoring. However, its environmental footprint raises important concerns regarding sustainability and justice. Therefore, AI should be considered both a tool for advancing environmental protection and a source of environmental pressures requiring careful evaluation. Integrating principles of sustainability, transparency, public health, and environmental justice into AI development and deployment is essential to maximize benefits while minimizing unintended harm.

items.title: VEGABrain: a Visualizer of Enriched Gene Analysis for the developing human brain
items.abstract: RNA sequencing datasets are widely reused resources in developmental neuroscience, yet inspecting them spatially remains unclear and difficult. Here, we present VEGABrain, an openly accessible web tool that renders bulk RNA-seq onto brain cortical and subcortical atlas surfaces across five human developmental windows spanning the first trimester to adulthood. Beyond single-gene maps, VEGABrain contributes a composite per-region enrichment layer using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA) scores precomputed for ∼19,000 gene sets drawn from Gene Ontology, Reactome, KEGG, BioCarta, the Human Phenotype Ontology and the MSigDB hallmark collection, and aggregated to a score for every gene set, developmental window and brain region. Furthermore, VEGABrain allows users to submit a custom gene list and obtain its ssGSEA map across development, computed on demand. VEGABrain is open source and requires no installation, offering easy-to-query expression throughout development and brain areas.

items.title: Dynamic Temporal and Tactile Cueing in Cantonese-English Bilingual Children With Childhood Apraxia of Speech: An Exploratory Randomized Crossover Design.
items.abstract: Purpose This exploratory randomized crossover study examined the effects of Dynamic Temporal and Tactile Cueing (DTTC) delivered in Cantonese (DTTC-Cantonese) and English (DTTC-English) to Cantonese-English bilingual children with childhood apraxia of speech (CAS). The study assessed (a) treatment and generalization effects within each language, (b) cross-linguistic generalization between Cantonese and English, and (c) the influence of language dominance and treatment order on treatment outcomes. Method Three bilingual children aged 4;6 to 5;11 (years;months) with confirmed CAS in both languages completed two 6-week treatment phases in a counterbalanced sequence. Probe data across 15 sessions per child were analyzed for phoneme accuracy, tone/stress accuracy, and intelligibility in trained, untrained, and generalization words. Nonparametric effect sizes (Tau- U ) were calculated comparing baselines with each treatment and posttreatment phase. Results Treatment-related gains were observed across participants, with the largest and most stable improvements generally occurring in trained words following direct treatment. Modest within-language generalization to untrained words was observed, whereas generalization to a shared probe word list was limited. Cross-linguistic generalization across segmental and prosodic domains was generally minimal, although small and inconsistent changes were occasionally observed. Treatment response patterns varied across participants, with individual differences observed in how language dominance and treatment order shaped gains and temporary changes in the nontreated language. Conclusions DTTC is feasible and effective for improving speech accuracy and intelligibility in bilingual Cantonese-English children with CAS. Improvements were generally observed following direct treatment, although treatment response pattern varied across participants and languages. Limited cross-linguistic generalization suggests that treatment in both languages remains necessary.

items.title: Misdiagnosis of Trigeminal Neuralgia and Inappropriate Prescribing of Carbamazepine and Its Derivatives in Headache Disorders.
items.abstract: Objectives We aimed to determine the rate of facial pain misdiagnosis leading to the use of CBZ, OXC or eslicarbazepine (ESL), along with the associated clinical features. Methods We conducted a service evaluation of patients seen in a single tertiary-care headache centre to identify patients with any exposure to CBZ, OXC, or ESL from June 2014 to April 2024. Final diagnoses were reviewed and patients with inappropriate usage or previous misdiagnosis of trigeminal neuralgia were characterized. Results Of the 226 patients prescribed CBZ/OXC/ESL, 190 had headache or neuralgia indications. Crucially, only 65 patients (34%) were appropriately prescribed for trigeminal neuralgia, SUNHA or other neuralgias. Eight patients misdiagnosed with trigeminal neuralgia and not exposed to CBZ/OXC/ESL were identified. Of those either inappropriately treated with CBZ/OXC/ESL or potentially-misdiagnosed-as-trigeminal neuralgia (n=133), migraine was among the most common (79%; 44% migraine only) final diagnosis. The main clinical features in those misdiagnosed were facial involvement of pain (75%), unilateral pain (69%), throbbing (55%), stabbing (34%), sharp pain (33%) and allodynia (66%). Adverse effects were seen in 59% on carbamazepine and 55% on oxcarbazepine. Discussion In patients referred to a tertiary headache clinic, trigeminal neuralgia is over diagnosed and inappropriately treated with CBZ and its derivatives resulting in no useful clinical outcome and substantial side effects. Migraine with lateralised facial involvement is a common presentation resulting in this misdiagnosis.

items.title: Enduring DNA Methylation Marks of Blast and Trauma Exposures in Warfighters.
items.abstract: Introduction Service members (SMs) in high-risk military occupational specialties can sustain hundreds to thousands of career blast and psychological trauma exposures, yet objective biomarkers capturing effects of these exposures remain elusive. Data included demographics, medical and combat exposure history, and blood samples collected during training. Neurocognitive performance was evaluated pre- and post-training in breachers using the Defense Automated Neurobehavioral Assessment (DANA). Results EAA significantly correlated with military service duration, CF1-blast, and CF2-trauma (all P Conclusions DNA methylation signatures of career blast and trauma exposures were associated with epigenetic age acceleration and diminished neurocognitive performance in SMs engaged in tactical operations, supporting the utility of epigenetic biomarkers for objective exposure assessment and operational readiness.

items.title: Dopaminergic modulation of cognitive control in forced and voluntary task switching.
items.abstract: Rationale Cognitive control relies on a delicate balance between cognitive stability and flexibility, enabling individuals to maintain task goals while adapting to changing task demands. Dopamine is considered a key neuromodulator of this balance, with D1 and D2 receptors differentially supporting stable versus flexible control modes. Objectives This study investigated D1 and D2 receptor contributions to dopaminergic modulation of behavioural performance in forced and voluntary task switching. Methods Participants ( N = 64) completed a hybrid task-switching paradigm including forced and voluntary task switches. Both tasks were performed under placebo or one of four dopaminergic conditions: L-Dopa (general dopaminergic enhancement), bromocriptine (selective D2 receptor enhancement), sulpiride (D2 receptor reduction) and a combination of L-Dopa and sulpiride (D1 receptor enhancement). Results Under placebo, robust switch costs in reaction times were observed, larger for forced-choice than free-choice trials. The voluntary switch rate was negatively associated with switch costs, indicating greater flexibility in individuals with a higher tendency to switch. There was no evidence for dopaminergic substances affecting overall switch costs in reaction times or error rates, nor overall error rates at the group level. However, D1 receptor enhancement selectively slowed free-choice relative to forced-choice responses, suggesting increased effort during self-initiated task selection. Exploratory analyses revealed that D2 receptor block reduced voluntary switching in individuals with a high baseline tendency to switch, and this reduction was associated with increased error rates in free-choice trials. Conclusions Overall, dopaminergic effects on cognitive control depended on task demands and individual control profiles. Rather than directly affecting cognitive flexibility, receptor-specific dopaminergic activity seems to modulate higher-level decision processes underlying voluntary task selection.

items.title: Sex Differences in the Late Positive Potential During Emotional Reappraisal: A Sham-Controlled tDCS Study.
items.abstract: BackgroundTranscranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) has been investigated as a potential means of modulating dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC)-mediated emotion regulation. We investigated late positive potential (LPP) responses, a neural index sensitive to the appraisal of emotional content, during cognitive up-regulation, down-regulation, and passive viewing of negative images following anodal, cathodal, and sham tDCS over the left DLPFC.MethodsThirty healthy adults (16 women; 19-38 years) completed three counterbalanced sessions in a within-subject, randomized, double-blind design. Each session involved 20 min of tDCS (anodal, cathodal, or sham) over the left DLPFC, followed by EEG recording during a cognitive reappraisal task. Participants up-regulated, down-regulated, or passively viewed negative images, and passively viewed neutral images, rating each for valence and arousal.ResultsNegative images elicited larger LPP amplitudes than neutral images, alongside higher arousal, more negative valence, and slower responses. Females exhibited larger LPP amplitudes across conditions and greater arousal to negative images than males. Among negative-image conditions, exploratory follow-up analyses indicated greater early LPP amplitude during up-regulation than negative maintain; however, down-regulation did not reliably reduce LPP amplitude relative to negative maintain after correction for multiple comparisons. Single-session tDCS yielded no reliable group-level effects on LPP amplitude or behavioural ratings, although exploratory partial correlations revealed condition-specific neural-behavioural associations.ConclusionFindings support LPP sensitivity to emotional salience and regulation, and highlight sex differences in neural and subjective responses. In contrast, acute left-DLPFC tDCS did not reliably alter mean LPP amplitude or behavioural indices of cognitive reappraisal.

items.title: Frontal Low-Frequency Electroencephalographic Coherence in Bipolar Disorder: A Covariate-Controlled Secondary Analysis of a Public Resting-State EEG Feature Dataset.
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo test whether bipolar disorder (BD) is associated with predefined frontal/frontopolar low-frequency scalp electroencephalography (EEG) coherence differences relative to healthy controls (HC), depressive disorder (DD), and schizophrenia (SZ) in a covariate-controlled reanalysis of a public resting-state EEG feature dataset.MethodsThe covariate-complete sample included 472 participants (93 HC, 66 BD, 196 DD, and 117 SZ). Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) models adjusted for age, sex, education, and intelligence quotient (IQ). Primary outcomes were predefined frontal/frontopolar delta, theta, and combined delta-theta coherence means. Electrode-pair, regional, all-frequency, distributional, global-reference, frontopolar, and age sensitivity analyses assessed robustness.ResultsBD had higher adjusted coherence than all comparison groups across the three primary measures (partial η 2 = .037-.040); Holm-adjusted BD-HC, BD-DD, and BD-SZ contrasts were significant for each measure. Features surviving false discovery rate correction were concentrated in the delta and theta bands. Findings were robust to distributional, outlier, and global-coherence analyses, but effects were strongest in frontopolar pairs and attenuated as anterior electrodes were excluded.ConclusionsBD showed higher covariate-adjusted frontal/frontopolar low-frequency scalp coherence than HC within this dataset. Differences from DD and SZ were smaller and concentrated in frontopolar pairs susceptible to ocular artifacts. Because only scalp-level coherence features were available and participant-level artifact-rejection data were unavailable, the findings do not establish a diagnostic biomarker, diagnostic specificity, or source-level mechanism. Artifact-controlled replication is required.

items.title: Diclofenac and Ibuprofen Suppress TRPM2 Novel Agonist (Arachidonic Acid)-Induced Mitochondrial Oxidative Neurotoxicity and Apoptosis.
items.abstract: Mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mROS) and increased Ca 2+ influx mediated by transient receptor potential (TRP) melastatin 2 (TRPM2) channel activation have been closely linked to neurodegenerative disorders. While antioxidants, 2-aminoethoxydiphenyl borate (2APB), and N-(p-amylcinnamoyl)anthranilic acid (ACA) suppress TRPM2, oxidative stress and ADP-ribose (ADPR) activate it. The most specific non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medications that have antioxidant properties are diclofenac (DIF) and ibuprofen (IBU). Arachidonic acid (ARA) has been shown to stimulate Ca 2+ in neuronal cells by TRP vanilloid 4 (TRPV4) and TRP ankyrin 1 (TRPA1) activations, but not TRPM2 stimulation. By blocking TRPM2, we evaluated the protective effects of DIF and IBU on ARA-induced oxidative neurotoxicity in human SH-SY5Y neuronal cells. Eight groups as control, DIF, IBU, ACA, ARA, ARA + DIF, ARA + IBU, and ARA + ACA were induced in the SH-SY5Y cells. ARA exposure and TRPM2 agonist (ADPR and H 2 O 2 )-induced TRPM2 currents and Ca 2+ influx were downregulated by the treatments of ACA, 2APB, IBU, DIF, and PLA2 inhibitor (bromoenol lactone). The treatments also reduced the ARA-induced increases of lipid peroxidation, apoptosis, mitochondrial membrane dysfunction, mROS, intracellular ROS, Zn 2+ , Fe 2+ , cell death, and caspase values by increasing cell viability, glutathione (GSH), and glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px). In conclusion, IBU and DIF treatments modify ARA-mediated increases in mROS, apoptosis, oxidative damage, Fe 2+ , Zn 2+ , and Ca 2+ influx by TRPM2 inhibition but GSH level/GSH-Px activation. The results of the novel TRPM2 antagonists (IBU and DIF) may offer protection against the mROS neuronal damage caused by the novel TRPM2 agonist (ARA), which is linked to increased apoptosis.

items.title: Ramping-up hippocampal ripples and their neocortical coupling support human visual short-term memory.
items.abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that the hippocampus contributes to visual short-term memory (VSTM). However, the neural mechanisms through which hippocampal activity supports the maintenance of VSTM representations remain largely unknown. Here, using intracranial EEG recordings from human participants performing a delayed match-to-sample task for naturalistic objects, we investigated the role of hippocampal ripple activity-brief high-frequency oscillations associated with memory replay-in VSTM maintenance and hippocampal-neocortical communication. We found that hippocampal ripple rates progressively ramped up during the maintenance period and supported successful VSTM. More critically, hippocampal ripples were temporally coupled with the ripples in the lateral temporal lobe (LTL), and these coupled ripples were associated with memory reactivation in the LTL. These findings provide direct evidence that hippocampal-neocortical interaction via coupled ripples supports VSTM, extending the role of hippocampal ripples from long-term consolidation to short-term mnemonic processes and offering new insights into the dynamic coding mechanisms of working memory.

items.title: Prefrontal mechanisms of threat-context integration in facial emotion recognition: the role of trait anxiety.
items.abstract: Background Social communication requires accurate recognition of facial expressions, which is strongly influenced by environmental context. In threatening situations, individuals typically identify danger-related signals more readily than safety-related cues. Although such threat-detection biases can be adaptive, exaggerated biases may contribute to anxious psychopathology. Here, we examined individual differences in threat perception and tested whether threat-related perceptual biases can be modified through threat-safety reversal learning. Methods Using whole-head magnetoencephalography, 81 participants (58 female, 23 male) with low or high trait anxiety completed an emotion recognition task involving subtly expressive fearful and happy faces presented in either an instructed threat-of-shock or safety context. Results Verbal instructions reliably established threat and safety contexts and, as predicted, planned contrasts show enhanced recognition accuracy for ambiguous facial expressions in a context-congruent manner, particularly in high-anxiety participants. Also consistent with preregistered hypotheses, processing of affectively incongruent face-context combinations was associated with mid-latency prefrontal activation. However, at later processing stages, high-anxiety individuals showed blunted prefrontal differentiation, suggesting reduced sensitivity to contextual deviance.During threat-safety reversal learning, early prefrontal activity indicated flexible differentiation between threat and safety in low-anxiety participants, whereas this effect was absent in high-anxiety individuals, pointing to difficulties in updating previously learned threat associations. Conclusion Together, these findings suggest that high levels of trait anxiety disrupt prefrontal mechanisms supporting flexible integration of contextual and facial information, resulting in rigid emotion recognition and reduced adaptability in updating threat-safety associations - processes that may contribute to persistent fear and maladaptive emotional responses.

items.title: Depressive symptoms moderate daily anticipated and momentary emotion dynamics and associate with complex brain network topology: Resting-state EEG and ecological momentary assessment evidence.
items.abstract: Background The dynamic linkage between anticipated and momentary emotion is a core daily regulatory process, yet the psychopathological and neurophysiological mechanisms disrupting this linkage in depression remain unclear. By bridging macroscopic neural topology with microscopic behavioral dynamics, this study investigated the within-person dynamics of these emotions and their cross-level associations with depressive symptoms and brain network topology. Methods Integrating resting-state electroencephalography (rs-EEG) with a 14-day ecological momentary assessment (EMA; 3 assessments/day), we recruited 96 young adults. Minimum spanning tree (MST) analysis was applied to characterize baseline brain network topology across multiple frequency bands. Dynamic structural equation modeling (DSEM) was employed to examine within-person dynamics and cross-level statistical moderation. Results Anticipated emotion prospectively predicted subsequent momentary positive emotion ( β = .191) and inversely predicted momentary negative emotion ( β = -.125). However, baseline depressive symptoms significantly moderated this prospective affective dynamic: Johnson-Neyman analyses identified empirical transition ranges (PHQ-9 scores 5.7-9.7; mild symptom range) beyond which the prospective emotional link attenuated to non-significance. Furthermore, topological metrics in the theta and delta bands exhibited indirect statistical associations with daily emotional dynamics via their cross-sectional relationship with baseline depressive symptoms. Conclusions An attenuated prospective association between positive anticipation and subsequent momentary emotional experience represents a key affective alteration in depressive distress. This daily emotional attenuation co-occurs with elevated depressive distress and is indirectly associated with a centralized topological organization in low-frequency resting-state brain networks. These findings provide novel neurophysiological indicators and highlight the critical window for ecological interventions before symptom severity reaches the moderate range.

items.title: Harmonised approaches to cognitive impairment assessment in systemic lupus erythematosus: Challenges and future directions.
items.abstract: Cognitive impairment (CI) is a significant problem in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), but multicentre validated studies are limited. An inaugural international meeting brought together 37 researchers from four continents to address challenges, knowledge gaps, and research harmonisation. Two breakout groups focused on clinical/psychological aspects and neuroimaging. Discussions covered a core outcome set for CI in SLE, defining a "gold standard" measure, subjective versus objective assessments, confounding variables, and neuroimaging methodologies. Instead of a universal CI measure, researchers suggested selecting cognitive domains relevant to SLE. Both objective and subjective assessments are crucial, alongside measures of daily functioning, resilience, and social determinants. Imaging discussions highlighted scanner variability and the need for harmonised acquisition and analysis techniques. To advance research, an international collaboration will align protocols and develop a finalised core dataset, reducing variability and complexity in CI studies in SLE.

items.title: Cue reactivity and product choice among young adult dual users of combustible and electronic cigarettes: Evidence from the lab and natural environment.
items.abstract: Aims The aim of this study was to characterize same-product and cross-product cue-reactivity for cigarettes and e-cigarettes and the impact of cueing on choice across laboratory and real-world settings among those who regularly use both cigarettes and e-cigarettes. Design Two-session laboratory experimental design followed by a 28-day ecological momentary assessment (EMA). Setting Rhode Island, USA. Participants N = 70 young adults (age 21-34) who regularly use cigarettes and e-cigarettes. Measurement In each laboratory session, we measured craving on a 0 to 100 scale for cigarettes and e-cigarettes prior to cueing, after a neutral cue and after a substance cue. Choice to use cigarettes vs. e-cigarettes was measured across 10 trials and indexed as: (#ENDS choices - #cigarette choices) / (total #ENDS+cigarette choices); scores thus ranged from -1 (cigarette only) to 1 [Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems (ENDS) only]. In the EMA, we measured craving during random reports and self-initiated cue surveys using the same 0-100 scale. We also measured past-hour cue-exposure retrospectively when cigarette or e-cigarette use was reported. Results In the laboratory, cue exposure increased craving for the cued substance relative to the pre-cue craving level [cigarette urge: unstandardized coefficient (b)= 14.83, 95% confidence interval (95% CI) = 11.24-18.41; cigarette desire: b = 11.46, 95% CI = 7.76-15.17; e-cigarettes urge: b = 7.64, 95% CI = 3.65-11.63; e-cigarette desire: b = 6.84, 95% CI = 2.92-10.76]. E-cigarette cues statistically significantly increased cigarette desire relative to the pre-cue craving level (b = 3.81, 95% CI = 0.33-7.29) but not urge (b = 2.75, 95% CI =[-0.66 to 6.16). Cigarette cues did not statistically significantly alter e-cigarette craving relative to the pre-cue craving level (urge: b = 1.78, 95% CI = -1.12 to 4.69; desires: b = 0.33, 95% CI = -2.71 to 3.37). Cue exposure did not statistically significantly alter product choice (b = -0.05, 95% CI = -0.19 to 0.10) beyond stated preference (b = 0.33, 95% CI = 0.18-0.49). In the natural environment, cue exposure was associated with increased craving relative to the random report for the cued product (cigarettes: b = 9.57, 95% CI =[7.61-11.53; e-cigarettes: b = 8.70, 95% CI = 6.80-10.61) but decreased craving for the non-cued product (smoking cues: b = -4.54, 95% CI = -6.37 to -2.71; vaping cues: b = -2.12, 95% CI = -4.16 to -0.08). Past-hour smoking cue exposure was associated with increased odds of reporting smoking (reference group = vaping) [odds ratio (OR) = 8.11, 95% CI = 3.73-17.63) whereas past-hour vaping cue exposure was associated with decreased odds of reporting smoking (OR = 0.06, 95% CI = 0.02-0.17). Summary Same-product cue reactivity effects for cigarettes and e-cigarettes appear to converge across laboratory and naturalistic settings, but cross-product effects do not.

items.title: Resection of Posterior Temporomesial Long-Term Epilepsy-Associated Tumors Through the Supracerebellar Transtentorial Approach: A Report of 2 Cases.
items.abstract: Background and importance Surgical resection of epileptogenic lesions involving the posterior temporomesial (PTM) region is challenging due to approach-related risks to functional temporal-occipital structures. Stereotactic ablation techniques, while excellent alternatives, are associated with incomplete ablation and lower efficacy in larger lesions. Success of the supracerebellar transtentorial (SCTT) approach, which avoids approach-related injury to overlying functional networks, relies on developing a good supracerebellar corridor and cerebellar bridging vein preservation, both typically reliant on cerebral relaxation through a semisitting position and favoring a paramedian rather than a more lateral hemispheric approach, respectively. We report 2 case reports to demonstrate that the SCTT approach (1) can be carried out in the park bench and prone positions and (2) is feasible even in the presence of a dominant developmental venous anomaly (DVA) involving a paravermian cerebellar bridging vein. Clinical presentation Two pediatric patients with long-term epilepsy-associated tumors (LEATs) of the PTM region, including a right calcified posterior temporo-occipital and a left posterior fusiform gyrus LEAT adjacent to a dominant paravermian cerebellar bridging DVA, were resected using the SCTT approach in the lateral park bench position and prone position, respectively. Both cases have remained seizure-free (Engel Class IA) at 60 and 30 months of postoperative follow-up, respectively. Conclusion The SCTT approach offers an excellent alternative to both standard open surgeries and stereotactic ablation techniques for children with LEATs in the PTM region. This approach can be used in both the lateral park bench and prone positions even in the presence of dominant paravermian cerebellar bridging DVA.

items.title: Management of Non-Dental Biofilm-Induced Gingival Diseases and Conditions and Gingival Enlargement: The EFP S2k-Level Clinical Practice Guideline.
items.abstract: Background Following the 2018 Classification, the European Federation of Periodontology (EFP) developed Clinical Practice Guidelines (CPGs) for the management of periodontitis and peri-implant diseases. To date, no clinical practice guidelines have been developed for non-dental biofilm-induced gingival diseases (NBIGDs) and conditions or for gingival enlargement. While these conditions are less common/rare, they present in general and specialist practice settings and there is therefore a need to develop such a set of guidelines. Aim To develop an S2k-level CPG for the management of NBIGDs and conditions and gingival enlargement. Methods This S2k-level CPG was developed by the EFP, following methodological guidance from the Association of Scientific Medical Societies in Germany and, where applicable, the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) process. A rigorous and transparent process included the following: synthesis of relevant research in two specifically commissioned systematic reviews; evaluation of the quality and strength of evidence; formulation of specific recommendations; and a structured consensus process involving leading experts and broadly based stakeholders. Recommendations were based on the best available evidence, combined with structured expert consensus, particularly in areas where direct evidence remains scarce. Results The S2k-level CPG for management of NBIGDs demonstrates that, because of their rarity, heterogeneity and complexity, and of the paucity of randomised controlled trials, NBIGDs should be managed within specialist centres, with urgent/immediate referral for suspected malignancies. Treating biofilm-induced inflammation is beneficial in most cases. Management of gingival enlargement is context-dependent and should be medical in nature, with surgery reserved for non-responsive cases. Conclusion The present S2k-level CPG informs clinical practice, health systems, policymakers and indirectly the public on the most effective interventions in the management of NBIGDs and gingival enlargement.
