items.title: AutoMeta: LLM Agent-based Automated Meta-Analysis in Public Health
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Meta-analysis supports public health decision-making, yet conducting and updating reviews remain time- and labour-intensive. Although large language model (LLM) agent systems have been proposed to automate literature reviews, heterogeneous exposure definitions, effect measures and covariate-adjustment models pose challenges for public health evidence synthesis. Methods: We present AutoMeta, an LLM-based agentic workflow for public health meta-analysis that uses stage-specific instructions to guide planning and tool use across literature search, screening, data extraction and statistical synthesis, with structured outputs linking each stage. To address the heterogeneity of public health evidence, it expands exposure terminology, structures eligibility assessments, links extracted estimates to their analytical context, and uses tested functions for effect-size transformation and synthesis. For systematic evaluation, we constructed AutoMetaBench from 27 systematic reviews spanning environmental health, nutrition and health behaviours, encompassing 421 included-study records, 4164 data fields and 95 effect units. We used this benchmark to assess performance at each stage and end to end. Results: AutoMeta improved evidence coverage and synthesis accuracy while supporting rapid end-to-end execution. In stage-specific evaluations, it outperformed the respective comparators across all four stages, achieving 93.1% search recall, 94.8% recall among the top 50 ranked records, and 93.6% data extraction accuracy. Agreement with reference pooled effects and 95% confidence intervals reached 96.8% and 95.8%, respectively. Across 27 end-to-end tasks, AutoMeta reproduced reference pooled effects and both 95% confidence interval bounds within 5% relative error in 85.2% of tasks, compared with 7.4% for the single-agent comparator, while taking an average of only 26 minutes per task. Conclusions: AutoMeta demonstrates substantial advantages in evidence synthesis and statistical analysis for public health meta-analysis. Its LLM-based agentic workflow improves synthesis efficiency and accuracy, while AutoMetaBench provides a dedicated benchmark for the systematic evaluation of automated methods. These contributions advance automated public health evidence synthesis and support timely evidence updates.

items.title: Effectiveness of Husband-Involved Maternity Education on Skilled Delivery Service Utilization in Rural Communities of Central Ethiopia: A Cluster-Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: In low-income countries, skilled delivery service utilization remains disproportionately low among rural women, resulting in a high rate of preventable maternal and neonatal mortality. Poor husband involvement in maternity care is one of the major contributing factors in Ethiopia. Hence, the purpose of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of husband-involved maternity education on skilled delivery service utilization in rural communities of central Ethiopia. A two-arm parallel-group cluster-randomized controlled trial was carried out among couples in the rural community of Central Ethiopia. The intervention group received group maternity education and individual home visits. A total of 496 couples from 16 clusters were randomly assigned to either the intervention (n=248) or the control group (n=248). A generalized estimating equation analysis was done to evaluate the intervention effectiveness. At the end line, 97.9% of the couples in the intervention group and 98.7% of the couples in the control group were available for analysis. There were no significant differences in baseline characteristics between the control and intervention groups. SDSU was significantly higher among pregnant women who received HIME intervention than those who did not receive the interventions, with a net effect of 21% (95% CI 18.7% - 23.2%, p < 0.001). In the GEE model, the SDSU was a 2-fold increase compared to the control group (AOR: 2.435, 95% CI 1.531, 3.874). This research indicates that involving husbands in the maternity education has a great effect on improving skilled delivery service utilization among pregnant women.

items.title: Dietary anthocyanidin intake and incident autoimmune hypothyroidism: prospective and multi-omic analyses in UK Biobank.
items.abstract: Anthocyanidins have antioxidant and immunomodulatory properties, but prospective evidence linking dietary intake to autoimmune hypothyroidism remains limited. We examined this association in 118 724 UK Biobank adults with at least two valid 24 h dietary recalls. Follow-up began at the last recall; 2350 events occurred over a median of 13.28 years. In sex-stratified multivariable Cox models, participants in the highest intake category had a lower hazard than those consuming ≤1 mg d -1 (HR 0.75; 95% CI 0.65-0.87; P for trend P for trend = 0.005). For nonalcoholic-source intake, the highest-category HR was 0.95 (95% CI 0.83-1.08; P for trend = 0.216). Among 247 nuclear magnetic resonance biomarkers measured after dietary assessment, five fatty-acid measures and two small-LDL lipid-composition measures met the FDR criterion after adjustment for recruitment biomarker values and ethanol dose. Among 73 807 genetically eligible participants, neither thyroid polygenic score showed evidence of interaction with intake. Higher anthocyanidin intake was associated with a lower hazard of autoimmune hypothyroidism and subsequent lipid-related biomarker differences. Residual confounding and uncertainty about nonalcoholic sources limit causal interpretation.

items.title: More Than a Tobacco Problem: Cigarette Smoking as a Marker of Poorer Cardiovascular Health Among Emergency Medical Services Clinicians.
items.abstract: Objectives Emergency medical services (EMS) work demands physical capacity, sustained alertness, and performance under stress, making cardiovascular health a workforce concern, not only a personal one. Cigarette smoking persists in portions of the EMS workforce, but whether it signals cardiovascular risk beyond tobacco exposure itself is unknown. We examined whether cigarette smoking was associated with poorer cardiovascular health across the non-tobacco domains of the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) framework among nationally certified EMS clinicians. Methods We conducted an observational study and cross-sectional secondary analysis of a voluntary survey offered to nationally certified emergency medical technicians (EMTs), advanced EMTs, and paramedics upon completion of recertification (October 2023-April 2024). To isolate associations beyond tobacco exposure, the primary outcome was a modified composite score (mLE7) averaging the seven non-nicotine LE8 domains (0-100 scale). Ideal cardiovascular health was defined as mLE7 ≥ 80. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models adjusted for demographic, educational, occupational, and organizational characteristics. Results Among 36,436 survey respondents, 7,703 had complete data for smoking status and all seven non-nicotine domains. Of these, 48.8% had never smoked, 45.2% formerly smoked, and 6.0% currently smoked. Mean mLE7 scores were 59.2 among never smokers, 56.9 among former smokers, and 51.5 among current smokers. Compared with never smokers, current smokers had lower adjusted mLE7 scores (β, -6.02; 95% CI, -7.63 to -4.41) and lower odds of ideal cardiovascular health (aOR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.23 to 0.61). Former smokers had intermediate results (β, -1.62; 95% CI, -2.37 to -0.87; aOR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.62 to 0.86). Current smoking was associated with poorer scores across diet, physical activity, sleep, blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood glucose domains (p Conclusions Among EMS clinicians, current cigarette smoking was associated with poorer cardiovascular health across nearly every non-tobacco domain, suggesting that smoking may serve as a readily identifiable marker of broader cardiovascular risk in this workforce. Agencies may consider pairing cessation support with broader cardiovascular health initiatives for clinicians who smoke. Sensitivity analyses addressing missing data yielded consistent results.

items.title: A Pathway Analysis of Factors Associated With Community-Based Home Palliative Care Needs Among Older Adults.
items.abstract: BackgroundCommunity-based home palliative care may improve end-of-life quality for older adults, yet evidence from Chinese primary care settings remains limited.ObjectiveTo examine factors associated with community-based home palliative care needs among older adults and explore their direct and indirect associations using path analysis.MethodsA cross-sectional survey was conducted among 550 older adults from 11 communities in Chongqing where public primary healthcare institutions provided palliative care services. Data were collected using demographic and elder-care questionnaires, a self-developed palliative care needs questionnaire, and the Brief Health Literacy Assessment Scale. Univariate analyses, regression, and path analysis were performed.ResultsEducational attainment, household income, medical insurance type, self-rated health, and health literacy were directly associated with palliative care needs. Education was also indirectly associated with needs through health literacy, income, and insurance participation. Findings highlight the need to strengthen health literacy, insurance support, and primary care capacity.

items.title: Relationship of Psychosocial Factors and Physical Health Indicators With Mental Health in Elementary School-Aged Children.
items.abstract: PurposeThis study examined (1) associations of social emotional learning (SEL) skills, resilience, vitality, cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF), in-school physical activity (PA), and out-of-school PA with mental health in fourth- and fifth-grade students, and (2) whether these associations differed by gender.DesignCross-sectional study.SettingThis study was conducted at eleven public elementary schools in one of the Mid-West States.Sample815 students in 4th-5th grades voluntarily participate in this study.MeasuresParticipants completed the PACER test for assessing CRF and Qualtrics surveys measuring mental health, SEL skills, resilience, vitality, and PA.AnalysisMultiple linear regression analyses were conducted for the total sample and by gender.ResultsSEL, resilience, vitality, CRF, and both in-school and out-of-school PA were significantly associated with mental health in the total sample (F = 36.89, P 2 = 0.317), boys (F = 19.35, P 2 = 0.317), and girls (F = 18.26, P 2 = 0.334). Key predictors included SEL self-management and relationship skills, vitality, and CRF. Gender differences showed mental health in boys was linked to SEL, vitality, resilience, and out-of-school PA, whereas in girls it was associated with SEL self-awareness and self-management, vitality, and CRF.ConclusionsMental health in children is influenced by social-emotional, psychological, and physical factors, supporting school-based interventions that consider gender differences.

items.title: Changes in Past 30-Day Smoked, Vaped, and Edible Cannabis Use Among Young Adults in Texas, 2022-2026.
items.abstract: Background Little is known about recent trends in cannabis use among young adults residing in states where recreational cannabis remains prohibited. We examined trends in the prevalence of past 30-day cannabis use overall and by mode among Texas college students from 2022-2026. Methods Participants were 48,860 18-25-year-olds attending 11 Texas colleges/universities who completed annual cross-sectional surveys between 2022-2026; and were predominantly female (60.2%) and Hispanic/Latino (41.5%). Generalized linear mixed-effects regressions examined trends in past 30-day any cannabis, smoked, vaped, and edible cannabis use. Models adjusted for sociodemographics, tobacco use, depression, and anxiety. Results Across all outcomes, prevalence increased from 2022-2024, peaked in 2024, and subsequently declined from 2025-2026. The adjusted prevalence of any past 30-day cannabis use more than doubled from 17.4% in 2022 to 39.2% in 2024 before declining to 17.0% in 2026. Similar patterns were observed for smoked, vaped, and edible cannabis. Past 30-day tobacco use and depression were associated with greater odds of cannabis use; associations with age, sex, race/ethnicity, and anxiety varied by outcome. Conclusions Cannabis use among Texas college students varied substantially between 2022-2026. Continued surveillance is needed to understand temporal changes in cannabis use within evolving cannabis policy environments.

items.title: Data quality assessment of maternal and newborn indicators from District Health Information Software 2 in five African countries for the period 2014-2023.
items.abstract: Background Tracking progress of sustainable development goal (SDG) targets requires robust monitoring systems, yet data quality remains challenging across sub-Saharan Africa. Most countries rely on aggregated data from District Health Information Software 2 (DHIS2) or surveys to track maternal, newborn and child health (MNCH) indicators. We evaluated MNCH data quality in DHIS2 across Ghana, Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zimbabwe (2014-2023). Methods We analysed 16 ENAP-aligned indicators and their 29 corresponding data elements captured in DHIS2 across health facility levels. We applied the WHO Data Quality Review framework to assess availability, reporting completeness, internal consistency (ratio-based validation metrics and temporal trends), and external consistency (comparison with UN Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation (UN IGME), Maternal Mortality Estimation Inter-Agency Group (MMEIG), and World Health Organization Global Health Observatory data). Results Of 29 data elements, Uganda had highest availability (72-76% during 2020-2023), followed by Kenya (62-66%), Tanzania (52%), and Ghana and Zimbabwe (41% each). Reporting completeness varied substantially: Tanzania achieved >95% facility reporting across all levels, while other countries showed disparities between hospitals and lower-level facilities. Internal consistency revealed problematic patterns for mortality-related ratios in Ghana (stillbirth-to-neonatal mortality ratios reaching 5.0-12.5) and Kenya (KMC-to-low birthweight ratios >2.0). After adjusting DHIS2 estimates for facility birth coverage, stillbirth rates generally exceeded or matched UN IGME estimates, whereas maternal mortality ratios showed substantial underreporting relative to MMEIG estimates. Ghana showed the closest MMR alignment and Kenya the largest discrepancy. Neonatal mortality was underreported in Ghana and Uganda but appeared higher than UN IGME estimates in Tanzania, a finding sensitive to aggregation method. Conclusions DHIS2 data quality varies substantially across countries, with country-specific challenges in availability, completeness and consistency. Strengthening facility-level data capture and developing an MNCH data quality module are crucial for improving data reliability.

items.title: The associations of outdoor and indoor air pollution with cognitive function among older adults in China.
items.abstract: Background Air pollution exposure has been associated with cognitive decline, but evidence remains limited regarding outdoor and household air pollution, different cognitive domains, and urban-rural differences. This study examined the longitudinal associations of outdoor particulate matter and household solid fuel use with cognitive function among older Chinese adults. Methods We used nationally representative data from 8,806 participants aged ≥60 years in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study from 2013 to 2020. Outdoor air pollution was assessed using annual mean PM1, PM2.5, and PM10 concentrations, and household air pollution was assessed by solid fuel use for cooking and heating. Cognitive function included global cognition, memory, and mental status. Linear mixed-effects models were used to examine the associations of air pollution exposure with subsequent cognitive function. Stratified analyses were conducted by urban-rural residence. Results Higher outdoor particulate matter exposure was generally associated with poorer subsequent global cognition and memory. PM2.5 exposure in 2013 was inversely associated with global cognition in both 2015 and 2018. Solid fuel use for cooking in 2013 was associated with lower global cognition (β = -0.57; 95% confidence interval (CI) = -0.93, -0.22), memory (β = -0.53; 95% CI = -0.77, -0.31), and mental status (β = -0.23; 95% CI = -0.40, -0.06) in 2018, while solid fuel use for heating was associated with lower global cognition (β = -0.42; 95% CI = -0.79, -0.05) and memory (β = -0.67; 95% CI = -0.92, -0.41). In stratified analyses, inverse associations appeared more evident among rural participants. Conclusions Outdoor particulate matter exposure and household solid fuel use were associated with poorer subsequent cognitive function among older adults in China, particularly global cognition and memory. These findings suggest that ambient and household air pollution may be relevant to cognitive ageing.

items.title: Phage therapy reduces bacterial burden and inflammation in a neutropenic murine sepsis model caused by hyperinvasive carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
items.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae is an emerging opportunistic pathogen associated with severe clinical outcomes, and carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae (CRKP) has become a critical threat requiring alternative therapeutic strategies. Phage therapy has recently gained attention as a promising alternative to combat antimicrobial resistance. However, its efficacy alone and in combination with antibiotics in immunocompromised hosts remains understudied. Here, we established a cyclophosphamide-induced neutropenic murine sepsis model due to a hyperinvasive CRKP strain carrying multiple virulence factors. In vitro , ceftazidime-avibactam (CAZ-AVI) at 8/4 μg/mL was required to suppress growth of this strain for 48 h, and this concentration was slightly reduced to 4/4 μg/mL when combined with a cocktail of three taxonomically distinct phages (P24, P39, and P49). In vivo , a single dose of the phage cocktail (9 × 10 8 plaque-forming units/mouse), administered intravenously or intraperitoneally following bacterial challenge, achieved 2.5-5.1 log 10 reductions of bacterial burdens across multiple tissues and organs. Correspondingly, serum tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-6, and interleukin-1β levels decreased significantly, and histopathological analysis revealed markedly mitigated inflammatory infiltration and tissue damage in the lung and liver. Both administration routes achieved comparable outcomes. Furthermore, in a delayed-treatment survival experiment, treatment with the phage cocktail combined with CAZ-AVI, initiated 2 h after lethal challenge, resulted in an 83.3% survival over the 28-day observation period. In contrast, all untreated mice succumbed within 2 days, and phage cocktail alone resulted in only 8.3% survival. Collectively, these findings provide in vivo evidence supporting the combination of phage cocktail and CAZ-AVI against CRKP infection in immunocompromised hosts. Importance Carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae (CRKP) has emerged as a critical threat to global public health, causing life-threatening infections, disproportionately affecting immunocompromised patients who often fail to respond to conventional antibiotic therapy and experience high mortality rates. However, the efficacy of phage therapy in this vulnerable population and the comparative performance of different administration routes remain largely unexplored. Here, we established a cyclophosphamide-induced neutropenic murine sepsis model to evaluate the therapeutic potential of a phage cocktail against CRKP. We demonstrate that both intravenous and intraperitoneal phage administration achieve substantial bacterial load reduction and significant attenuation of systemic inflammation, revealing that phage therapy retains a robust positive response even in the absence of a fully functional host immune system. These findings underscore the clinical translational potential of phage as a viable alternative to antibiotics for combating CRKP infections in immunocompromised patients and provide critical evidence supporting intravenous phage delivery as a feasible administration route.

items.title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 1 Transmission Risk During Commercial Air Travel, 2000-2025.
items.abstract: Objectives Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 1 (SARS-CoV-1) have the potential for global translocation and transmission through infected travelers. This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed transmission of these viruses during commercial air travel. Methods We searched 8 databases for studies published during 2000-2025 of MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV-1 transmission during air travel. We included studies describing contact investigation(s) and outcome(s) of MERS-CoV or SARS-CoV-1 exposures on aircraft. We completed title and abstract screening, full-text review, and data extraction in Covidence. We assessed risk of bias using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. We classified contacts of index cases as close contacts according to study-defined contact definitions. We calculated attack rates for close contacts, non-close contacts, and passengers (and/or crew) on the whole plane. We used a random-effects meta-analysis to estimate pooled attack rates (PARs) and pooled risk differences (PRDs). A leave-one-out sensitivity analysis assessed the robustness of pooled estimates. Results Nineteen studies met inclusion criteria. No secondary cases were identified from 11 MERS-CoV studies. Among 5 SARS-CoV-1 studies reporting whole-plane data, the PAR was 1.2% (95% CI, 0.3%-4.3%). Sensitivity analyses indicated that this estimate was robust. Among 4 studies reporting outcomes for close contacts, the PAR was 3.4% (95% CI, 1.0%-11.1%), while 2 studies of non-close contacts yielded a PAR of 0.3% (95% CI, 0.1%-1.3%). The PRD comparing close and non-close contacts was 0.8% (95% CI, -5.5% to 7.1%). Conclusions Although both viruses are capable of person-to-person transmission, evidence of transmission during air travel was identified only for SARS-CoV-1. The findings support an evidence- and risk-based, pathogen-specific approach to aircraft contact investigations rather than a uniform strategy for all emerging respiratory viruses.

items.title: Use of mHealth interventions in the management of chemotherapy-related adverse drug reactions.
items.abstract: BackgroundChemotherapy remains a cornerstone of cancer treatment but carries a substantial burden of adverse drug reactions (ADRs), poorly managed after patients leave hospital. mHealth technologies offer a scalable way to remotely monitor, report, prevent, and manage ADRs. No review has mapped mHealth functionality for chemotherapy-related ADR management across cancer types.ObjectivesTo map existing evidence on mHealth interventions used for monitoring, reporting, preventing, or managing chemotherapy-related ADRs among cancer patients, and to identify gaps for future research.MethodsThis review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) framework and Population-Concept-Context approach. A systematic search of PubMed and Scopus identified studies evaluating mHealth interventions (apps, SMS systems, telemonitoring platforms, or wearables) for chemotherapy-related ADRs in cancer patients of any age or setting. Data were charted on study characteristics, intervention functionality, and outcomes, then synthesized narratively.Results7 studies (one RCT, one non-randomized trial, two systematic reviews, one with meta-analysis, two observational studies, one non-randomized study) met inclusion criteria, mostly in breast cancer (71%) and delivered via smartphone apps (86%). Monitoring was universal (100%); reporting and management were each present in 71% of studies; prevention was weakest (29%, always secondary). Benefit tracked with pairing monitoring to active management: severe ADR incidence fell from 50.0% to 20.2%, quality of life improved significantly (SMD = 0.31, p < 0.0001), and alerts showed 72% positive predictive value. Monitoring-only platforms improved usability without clinical gains.ConclusionmHealth interventions show promise for chemotherapy ADR management, but benefits depend on linking monitoring to reporting and management rather than monitoring alone; prevention remains a key gap.

items.title: Quantum analogue-to-digital converter for phase estimation
items.abstract: Traditional quantum metrology assesses precision using the figures of merit of continuous-valued parameter estimation. Recently, quantum digital estimation was introduced: it evaluates the performance information-theoretically by quantifying the number of significant bits of the parameter, redefining key benchmarks like the Heisenberg bound. Here we report the first experimental realization of a quantum analogue-to-digital converter for quantum metrology, which takes a continuous parameter as the input and outputs a bit string, using an advanced photonic platform comprising a fully reconfigurable integrated circuit and a quantum dot source of highly indistinguishable photons. We implement a protocol for digital phase estimation that is capable of surpassing classical strategies in terms of mutual information between the output bit string and the unknown parameter, through the simultaneous use of different entangled state resources. We tackle experimental imperfections by using machine learning techniques for noise deconvolution and estimation process refinement. Our protocol is experimentally benchmarked against classical strategies via the number of recoverable bits of the unknown parameter. Our results open new perspectives for future implementation of quantum digital estimation strategies.

items.title: Robust and cost-effective quantum network using Kramers-Kronig receiver
items.abstract: The quantum internet holds the potential to facilitate applications that are fundamentally inaccessible to the classical internet. Among its most prominent applications is quantum key distribution (QKD) networks, which connect two distant nodes to establish a secure key based on the principles of quantum mechanics. However, the subsequent extensive reliance on interferences in existing QKD protocols leads to the weak robustness of the system and the corresponding network. In this work, we propose a robust and cost-effective quantum network using the Kramers-Kronig receiver. We first propose a continuous-variable QKD protocol based on direct detection without interference, which achieves the recovery of quadrature components through the Kramers-Kronig relation. Subsequently, we have extended this protocol to continuous-variable quantum access networks, further highlighting the robustness and cost advantages of interference-free detection. The experimental results show that each user can achieve an asymptotic secret key rate of 50 kbit/s within the access network range using only one photodetector without optical interference structures. This scheme opens up new possibilities in establishing a robust and cost-effective quantum network, serving as a foundational element in the progress toward establishing a large-scale quantum internet.

items.title: Review and detailed analysis of the Plio-Quaternary tectono-stratigraphic architecture and evolution of the Sicily Channel (Central Mediterranean)
items.abstract: The regions outward the leading edge of the orogenic wedges and external to the associated foredeep basin, i.e. , the foreland areas, are often perceived as stable zones. Nevertheless the Sicily Channel—situated in the central Mediterranean between Sicily and Tunisia and regarded as the continental foreland of the Sicilian Maghrebian chain—reveals significant tectonic complexity. It comprises three major tectonic troughs (Pantelleria, Malta, and Linosa grabens) formed by the ongoing extension of Africa. This area includes a foreland-foredeep-mountain chain system encompassing the Pelagian foreland, the Gela Foredeep Basin, and the offshore section of the Neogene-Quaternary Sicilian-Maghrebian chain. Based on an extensive review of available literature, including previously published multichannel seismic reflection profiles and structural maps, we provide a detailed analysis of the stratigraphic architecture and key tectonic features in the Sicily Channel during the Plio-Quaternary. Furthermore, we assess the timing of major tectonic events to gain a comprehensive understanding of the region’s Plio-Quaternary structural evolution. Our findings demonstrate that the Sicily Channel is not merely a simple rifted foreland zone but is characterized by recurrent extensional and compressional phases during the late Neogene/Plio-Quaternary. This evidence indicates that distinct tectonic regimes can spatially and temporally coexist within a foreland area, reinforcing the idea that foreland zones actively record dynamic processes driving lithospheric deformation and are prone to tectonic reactivation.

items.title: Efficient Long-Time Simulations of Dissipative Multiscale Systems via High-Order Numerical Homogenization
items.abstract: By a high-order numerical homogenization method, a heterogeneous multiscale scheme was developed in [Z. Jin and R. Li, Multiscale Model. Simul., 20 (2022), pp. 583–617] for evolving differential equations containing two time scales. In this paper, we further explore the technique to propose an efficient algorithm able to carry out simulations up to a long time, which was prohibitive before. The new algorithm is a multigrid-in-time method which combines coarse-grid high-order approximations with fine-grid low-order evaluations. The high efficiency is attained by minimizing the computational cost while the approximation accuracy is guaranteed. A priori error estimates are rigorously established and validated by numerical examples.

items.title: Reaching for the Edge. II. Stellar Halos out to Large Radii as a Tracer of Dark Matter Halo Mass
items.abstract: The diffuse outskirts of brightest cluster galaxies (BCGs) encode valuable information about the assembly history and mass of their host dark matter halos. However, the low surface brightness of these stellar halos has historically made them difficult to observe. Recent deep imaging, particularly with Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC), has shown that the stellar mass within large projected annuli, such as 50 and 100 kpc, is a promising proxy for halo mass. However, the optimal radial definition of this “outskirt mass” remains uncertain. We construct an HSC-like mock observing pipeline to measure stellar mass density profiles of BCGs in the IllustrisTNG simulations. The resulting profiles reproduce HSC profiles across 6 orders of magnitude in surface density. We then measure stellar masses within different annuli and how tightly they connect to halo mass. Stellar masses measured within simple apertures exhibit more scatter in the stellar mass–halo mass relation than those measured within projected ellipsoidal annuli. We identify an optimal range, with inner radii of ∼60–300 kpc and outer radii of ∼250–500 kpc. We also introduce two halo-mass-dependent Sérsic models for average stellar halo profiles. The first depends only on halo mass, M vir , and has a median error of 0.19 dex (∼54%). Adding the central stellar mass of the BCG as a second parameter reduces this to 0.15 dex (∼39%). Together, these results provide fitting functions for BCG stellar halos that can be applied to future wide-field surveys to infer halo masses from deep imaging data.

items.title: Direct torque detection of crystal chirality
items.abstract: Chirality governs phenomena ranging from chemical reactions to the topology of quasiparticle charge carriers. However, a direct macroscopic probe for crystal chirality remains a significant challenge, especially in time reversal symmetric systems with weak circular dichroism signal. Here, we propose the ``Chiralometer'', a mechanical detection method that probes chirality by driving angular momentum carriers out of equilibrium. Using first-principles calculations and semiclassical transport theory, we demonstrate that a temperature gradient in insulators or an electric field in metals induces uncompensated angular momentum in phonons and electrons, respectively. This imbalance generates a macroscopic mechanical torque ($τ\sim 10^{-11} N \cdot m$) well within the sensitivity of modern torque magnetometry and cantilever-based sensors. We identify robust signatures in chiral crystals such as Te, SiO$_2$, and the topological semimetal CoSi. Our work establishes mechanical torque as a fundamental order parameter for chirality, offering a transformative tool for orbitronics and chiral quantum materials.

items.title: Anisotropic field suppression of charge order reveals orbital-selective Kondo hybridization in UTe 2
items.abstract: UTe 2 is a rare correlated quantum material where unconventional density-wave orders, Kondo physics, spin-triplet pairing, and reentrant superconductivity coexist. Because superconductivity emerges from a strongly correlated normal state, identifying and controlling intertwined normal-state orders are essential for understanding the electronic landscape where superconductivity arises. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy in a vector magnetic field, we uncover a staggered charge density wave (CDW) in high-quality UTe 2 crystals. This CDW exhibits a strong directional field response: It is completely quenched by a modest 1.7-tesla magnetic field along the quasi–one-dimensional uranium-chain direction while remaining robust against fields along other crystallographic axes. This anisotropy suggests an orbital-driven field-tuned quantum phase transition. Unexpectedly, the same field orientation concurrently suppresses the 5f Kondo resonance. Modeling indicates a switch in the dominant hybridization channel from Te 5 p- U 5 f to U 6 d- U 5 f coupling, suggesting an intimate interplay between CDW and the Kondo effect.

items.title: Inspiral test of the Kerr hypothesis beyond the quadrupole with GW241011
items.abstract: All multipole moments of a Kerr black hole are uniquely determined by its mass and spin. Gravitational wave observations can test this prediction by measuring spin-induced multipole moments imprinted on the inspiral phase of compact binary mergers. In this Letter, we show that the recently reported compact binary coalescence GW241011 enables a simultaneous test of deviations in the spin-induced quadrupole and octupole moments of the binary components from their black hole values. We find no evidence for deviations from the Kerr prediction and place the first constraints on spin-induced octupole moments of the compact binary. This approach complements tests of the Kerr nature of compact binary merger remnants based on quasinormal mode measurements in the ringdown phase.

items.title: EP250302a: Violent Shell Collision in a Soft-X-Ray-selected Gamma-Ray-burst-like Transient
items.abstract: The Einstein Probe (EP) opens a previously unexplored soft X-ray window onto gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), filling a critical observational gap in the soft X-ray coverage of their prompt emission. In this Letter, we present EP250302a, a soft-X-ray-selected, GRB-like transient at z = 1.131 detected by the EP. Follow-up observations from X-ray to radio reveal a narrow X-ray flare at ∼1.1 ks and subsequent achromatic optical and X-ray rebrightening. These features challenge a standard single-component afterglow model and indicate the need for multiple ejecta components. A violent collision between a late relativistic shell and the decelerated leading blast wave provides a plausible interpretation: the flare arises from internal dissipation of the late ejecta, while the rebrightening is powered by the shocked emission produced in the collision. Quantitative modeling constrains the kinetic energy ratio between the late shell and the initial ejecta to E k,iso,2 / E k,iso,1 ∼ 5 (with E k,iso,2 ∼ 10 53 erg and E k,iso,1 ∼ 2 × 10 52 erg), as well as the Lorentz factor contrast to Γ 2,0 /Γ 1,0 ≈ 0.98–2.27, required to reproduce the observed flare luminosity and rebrightening amplitude. Such an energetic late shell can be launched in a radiatively inefficient second episode of central-engine activity. Thanks to the well-sampled, early-time multiband coverage facilitated by the EP trigger, EP250302a provides a valuable case to test the physical connection between central-engine activity and shell collisions.

items.title: Are Nucleosynthetic Yields Universal? Interpreting the Multielemental Abundances of Quiescent Galaxies over Cosmic Time Using Milky Way Stars
items.abstract: The detailed abundance patterns of quiescent galaxies offer powerful constraints on their formation and evolution. Yet physical insight remains elusive, as nucleosynthetic yields are notoriously uncertain. We introduce a framework that circumvents this problem by using Milky Way abundance trends as empirical proxies for initial mass function (IMF)-averaged yields. Applied to quiescent galaxies from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey ( z ∼ 0), LEGA-C ( z ∼ 0.7), and JWST/SUSPENSE ( z ∼ 2), our approach recovers the α - and Fe-peak abundances with a median offset of ∼0.05 dex across 10 elements, compared to ∼0.23 dex for theoretical yields. Systematic residuals of up to ∼0.1–0.2 dex remain for some elements in galaxies with the highest velocity dispersions. The largest discrepancies arise in N, Sr, Ba, and (at z ∼ 2) C, all of which depend on asymptotic giant branch enrichment, a channel we do not explicitly model. We explore the impact of a top-heavy IMF and find that it can shift the IMF-averaged core-collapse supernova yields by ∼0.05–0.2 dex in a direction that reduces the systematic residuals. Surprisingly, the predictions succeed without modeling the full chemical-evolution history of a galaxy: Mg and Fe alone are sufficient to predict the remaining α - and Fe-peak elements. Combined with previous results in dwarf galaxies and the Milky Way disk, this success suggests that the IMF-averaged nucleosynthetic yields of α - and Fe-peak elements are largely universal. This predictability makes the empirical yields immediately useful: embedding them in stellar population synthesis models will improve inferences on stellar populations and star formation histories, while incorporating them into cosmological simulations will produce more observationally motivated predictions.

items.title: Assessing the imprint of eccentricity in GW signatures using two independent waveform models
items.abstract: The gravitational wave signal from merging compact binaries encodes information about their orbital and intrinsic properties. Over the last few years, state-of-the-art waveform models have begun to incorporate the effects of orbital eccentricity into their estimated signal. Over a similar period, many groups have applied these waveforms to characterize whether the imprint of eccentricity is present and, if so, measure this time-evolving property (at a suitably-defined reference point). In this work, we present a comprehensive analysis of 162 confident sources identified in the O3 and O4a observing runs of the International Gravitational Wave Network (LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA). Using the RIFT parameter inference engine, we employ two independently implemented waveform models (SEOBNRv5EHM and TEOBResumS-Dali) which account for orbital eccentricity and the effects of aligned compact object spins. Using these two waveforms, we find consistent conclusions that disfavor the eccentric hypothesis. Unlike previous work, among binary black hole candidates, we find potential evidence for eccentricity in three events: GW200129, GW231001, and GW231123. For the latter two events, the evidence for eccentricity is ambiguous, with different degrees of support from different waveforms. Consistent with previous work, we find conclusions obtained about GW200129 can be sensitive to analysis settings, as expected, given the nonstationary noise present.

items.title: Reconstruction of Reionization Histories from 21 cm Power-spectrum Evolution with Artificial Neural Networks
items.abstract: We investigate whether the redshift evolution of the fixed- k dimensionless 21 cm power spectrum, Δ 21 2 ( k , z ) , contains sufficient information to reconstruct reionization histories x HI ( z ) with artificial neural networks. Using semi-numerical realizations generated within a restricted three-parameter 21cmFAST model family, we train a compact feed-forward network to learn the inverse mapping from power-spectrum trajectories to the neutral-fraction history on a 97-point redshift grid spanning 6 ≤ z ≤ 15. For k = 0.1, 0.5, and 1.0 h Mpc −1 , representative tests on an independent test set show that the midpoint redshift z 50 is recovered more accurately than the duration Δ z = z 75 − z 25 in terms of dimensionless relative errors: z 50 is reconstructed with MAE = 0.0046 and RMSE = 0.0100, whereas Δ z yields MAE = 0.0302 and RMSE = 0.0378. This result indicates that fixed- k power-spectrum evolution carries stronger information about the timing of reionization than about the detailed width of the transition within the adopted prior. We further test an idealized foreground-free SKA1-Low-like thermal-plus-sample-variance noise model and find that the reconstruction remains stable in the favorable signal-to-noise regime considered here. These results demonstrate that neural networks can serve as prior-dependent inverse mapping for reconstructing reionization histories from 21 cm power-spectrum evolution.

items.title: A framework for modelling Population III stars in cosmological simulations
items.abstract: Population III (Pop III) stars are the first generation of stars to form in the universe, emerging from primordial gas composed mainly of hydrogen and helium. In this work, we present a comprehensive framework for modelling Pop III stars in cosmological simulations. This includes: (1) an enhanced thermochemical network that tracks the equilibrium abundances of $\rm {H_2^+}$ and $\rm {H^-}$ which catalyses $\rm H_2$ formation in primordial gas; (2) detailed stellar spectra of Pop III stars computed from MESA evolutionary tracks and TLUSTY NLTE atmosphere models; and (3) comprehensive supernova feedback, including both Core-Collapse and Pair-Instability supernovae, with detailed elemental yields. We implement these improvements in AREPO-RT and test them using cosmological zoom-in simulations of a 1.07 × 1010M⊙ halo at z = 3 with varying Pop III IMF. Our results show that Pop III stars form at z > 13 and are under 1 percent of new stars by z ∼ 5. Their Lyman-Werner radiation raises the local LW flux by two orders of magnitude at z ≈ 16, and their feedback lowers the star formation rate at z > 5.5. The new chemistry more than doubles the mass fraction of cool, dense pristine gas, while Pop III feedback creates photo-heated diffuse gas and drives distinct metal enrichment patterns at 10 20 Å) comparable with JWST observations from a galaxy at z ∼ 11.

items.title: Density fluctuations in pseudo-streamer and helmet streamer: Generation, propagation and comparison with Metis observations
items.abstract: Recent white-light observations from the Metis coronagraph on board Solar Orbiter have shown the presence of propagating density fluctuations with a period of ∼5 minutes, particularly in the observationally bright regions of helmet streamers and pseudo-streamers. These density fluctuations have been shown to originate from magnetohydrodynamic wave modes – slow and fast modes can directly compress the plasma, whereas AlfvÃ©n waves generate density fluctuations via a non-linear coupling with the slow and fast modes. In general, in low plasma β regions, slow modes contribute more towards the generation of density fluctuations, whereas in high β regions, there are significant contributions from both slow and fast waves. In this work, we investigate the propagation of (non-linear) AlfvÃ©n waves and the associated density fluctuations using a 2.5D axisymmetric global solar wind model that includes two distinct magnetic field topologies – a helmet streamer and a pseudo-streamer. Key differences in these magnetic configurations give rise to differences in the wave behaviour due to, for example, the presence of a current sheet in the helmet streamer and an X-type null point in the pseudo-streamer, and the structure of the β = 1 layer in both magnetic field configurations. This leads to the possible creation of prominent interference patterns along the helmet streamer axis, which do not appear along the pseudo-streamer axis. Unlike in the streamer region, we also find that along the pseudo-streamer axis, the contribution to the density fluctuations is due to the fast waves only, despite being in a low β plasma.

items.title: Primordial black holes from vector-induced curvature perturbations sourced by primordial magnetic fields
items.abstract: Generating an appreciable abundance of primordial black holes (PBHs) requires a substantial enhancement of primordial curvature perturbations on small scales. In this Letter, we propose a new post-inflationary mechanism in which such an enhancement arises during a stiff, or kination, epoch. The mechanism is driven by metric vector perturbations sourced by the vector component of the electromagnetic stress-energy tensor associated with primordial magnetic fields (PMFs). Since these first-order vector modes remain approximately constant during kination, they act as persistent nonlinear sources for second-order scalar perturbations. We show that the resulting vector-induced curvature perturbations are amplified toward the infrared cutoff of the kination band and exhibit the characteristic scaling PR(k) k^{-5}. As a concrete realization, we consider PMFs generated in a Ratra-type magnetogenesis scenario and find that the induced curvature perturbations can produce PBHs with an abundance large enough to constitute a substantial fraction of the dark matter.

items.title: Multiparameter two-photon polarimetry approaching the quantum limit
items.abstract: Photonic quantum metrology has demonstrated advantages in precision and resource efficiency for a wide range of applications, with several schemes approaching the fundamental quantum Cramér-Rao precision bound (QCRB). However, the intrinsic incompatibility of quantum measurements represents a hurdle in extending these advantages to the simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters. In this paper, we present an experimental protocol approaching the QCRB simultaneously in two polarisation parameters, across a wide range of the parameter space, with as few as $\sim 200$ photon pairs, offering advantages for polarimetric sensing for dim sources such as in X-ray astronomy or photosensitive samples.

items.title: Design and Performance of the Carruthers Geocoronal Imager
items.abstract: The GeoCoronal Imager (GCI) onboard the Carruthers Geocorona Observatory is the primary scientific instrument of the mission. It is designed to measure far ultraviolet light at 121.6 nm Lyman- $\alpha $ α (Ly- $\alpha $ α ) emitted by hydrogen (H) atoms in Earth’s exosphere with the sensitivity, accuracy and precision to meet the mission’s scientific objectives regarding the nature of terrestrial exospheric structure and dynamics on both global and regional scales. The GCI is comprised of two co-aligned UV imaging systems. The Narrow Field Imager (NFI) acquires nearly continuous images of exospheric Ly- $\alpha $ α radiance near and above the Earth’s limb at relatively high spatial and temporal resolution, while the Wide Field Imager (WFI) uses relatively higher optical sensitivity and a wider field of view to detect faint Ly- $\alpha $ α emission from the exosphere’s outermost extent. Both imaging channels feature identical active pixel sensor cameras, gain-intensifiers, and 6-position optical filter wheels. This paper outlines the instrument design requirements, informed by mission science goals, as well as its performance as measured in the vacuum ultraviolet laboratory test and calibration.

items.title: Combining gravitational wave search pipelines to find subthreshold signals in GWTC-5.0
items.abstract: The detection of transient gravitational wave signals relies on independent search algorithms that analyse detector data and assign significance measures to candidate events. However, varying performance complicates their interpretation. We use supervised machine learning combined with conformal prediction, a framework to quantify uncertainties, to merge multi-pipeline information into well-calibrated confidence scores. We demonstrate that this approach is robust across different classifier architectures and remains stable when trained on different simulated datasets. When applied to events across the GWTC catalogue up to and including the second part of the fourth observing run, the framework identifies several subthreshold candidates with elevated confidence, including the binary neutron star candidate GW200311_103121. We examine the reliability of these up-rankings, finding evidence that high-confidence predictions correspond to signal-like events. This framework enables simplified systematic candidate assessment for gravitational wave catalogues and real-time alerts by providing a single, well-calibrated confidence measure per candidate.

items.title: Hidden Drowsiness in Wakefulness: Differences in Resting-State EEG Profiles in Natural Short Sleepers Versus Recommended Length Sleepers.
items.abstract: Chronic insufficient sleep affects cardiovascular, endocrine, immune and nervous systems and is linked to cognitive decline and increased mortality. Among habitual short sleepers, a subgroup known as natural short sleepers (NSS) report sleeping ≤ 6 h per night without experiencing subjective daytime dysfunction. However, discrepancies between subjective and objective markers of alertness raise questions about their true cognitive state. NSS have been described as high in behavioural activation, a phenotype overlapping with ADHD and mania in which dysregulation of resting-state brain arousal has been well documented. Despite these parallels, few studies have investigated the neurophysiological features of NSS. The current study examined resting-state EEG in NSS and recommended-length sleepers (RLS) during eyes-open conditions. Results showed that NSS exhibited significantly higher global alpha power and regionally steeper aperiodic exponents, particularly in occipital areas, both markers of increased drowsiness. Although global exponent values did not differ significantly, a significant Group × Region interaction was observed and NSS showed a trend toward increasing aperiodic exponents over time, suggesting less stable wakefulness under low-stimulation conditions. These findings point to subtle neurophysiological differences in NSS, raising the possibility that their perceived resilience to short sleep may mask underlying drowsiness.

items.title: A two-platform blueprint for modeling human brain development.
items.abstract: No single experimental system spans human neural-plate induction through late-stage circuit maturation. Brain organoids have transformed human developmental neuroscience, yet a decade of progress has clarified their intrinsic limitations: they cannot fully recapitulate neural induction driven by embryo-scale developmental signals, nor achieve the degree of circuit maturation that requires an in vivo physiological context. Stem cell-based embryo models are positioned to provide mechanistic access to peri-gastrulation and early neurulation, whereas interspecies chimeras provide the physiological milieu to study myelination, pruning and circuit-level function. Here we propose a two-platform roadmap that integrates stem cell-based embryo models to decode developmental logic with interspecies chimeras to study functional maturation. We outline reproducibility and reporting standards, including rigorous benchmarks for neural-tube formation and closure, and present a milestone-based oversight framework anchored to verifiable developmental landmarks. Together, these complementary platforms enable causal interrogation of human neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disease while remaining responsive to ethical and technical constraints.

items.title: Dynamic visualization of cell adhesion molecule interactions using reversible split-HaloTag labeling in living cells.
items.abstract: Critical for diverse cellular functions, cell adhesion molecules (CAMs) interact to transduce information from the external environment to drive coordinated intracellular responses. However, direct visualization of CAM interactions in living cells and organisms remains a major challenge. Recent developments in split-HaloTag technology present a promising strategy for chemical labeling of protein-protein interactions. Here, we apply this method to dynamically monitor CAM interactions in living HEK293T cells using split-HaloTag-CAM fusion proteins. With high specificity, we visualized trans-cellular interactions between known adhesion pairs natively found in neuronal and immunological synapses. To expand the system's versatility, we adapted a modified split-HaloTag component (cpHaloΔ N272H ) that enables reversible dye exchange and facilitates rapid time-lapse imaging of CAM interactions. Leveraging fluorogenic HaloTag dyes, split-HaloTag-CAMs measured the real-time disassembly and reassembly of Ca 2+ -dependent CAM junctions in live cells. These tools enabled imaging long-term changes in surface contacts mediated by CAM binding, thus providing a robust platform for dissecting the spatiotemporal dynamics of CAM interactions in cellular and organismal contexts.

items.title: Ketamine promotes strategic and efficient approach-avoidance conflict resolution.
items.abstract: Adaptive behavior requires flexibly balancing approach and avoidance in risky or threatening environments, a flexibility disrupted in depression and other disorders marked by excessive avoidance. Benzodiazepines such as lorazepam broadly dampen neural excitability and synaptic plasticity, whereas ketamine may enhance both. We therefore asked whether ketamine promotes more strategic and efficient motivational behavior. In this completed randomized crossover study, 34 healthy participants with no lifetime neurological or psychiatric disorders and no regular medication use were assessed at the University Medical Center Freiburg (DRKS00025471). Participants completed three visits separated by seven days: a control visit without medication, followed by intranasal ketamine (50 mg) and oral lorazepam (1 mg) in randomized, counterbalanced order. Threat probability and loss magnitude were varied independently in a dynamic approach-avoidance conflict task conducted after ketamine's acute dissociative phase. Reported behavioral outcomes were net token gain, approach behavior, and approach and withdrawal latencies. Behavioral assessors were blinded to condition; participants and physicians were not. Mixed-effects models were used. All 34 randomized participants completed each condition and were analyzed. Ketamine yielded 57% higher token gains than control (β = 0.09, 95% confidence interval 0.05 to 0.13; p < 0.001) and 33% higher gains than lorazepam (β = 0.05, 0.01 to 0.09; p = 0.009). Behavior following ketamine was more strongly guided by outcome value than threat probability and showed faster approach and withdrawal responses. Lorazepam produced a less selective increase in approach behavior. No unexpected adverse events occurred. In healthy participants, ketamine was associated with more efficient and value-sensitive approach-avoidance behavior than control and lorazepam.

items.title: Dopamine dynamics in a mouse model of temporal lobe seizures with impaired consciousness.
items.abstract: Objective Focal temporal lobe seizures often lead to impaired consciousness. Recent work has shown depressed cortical arousal, with slow waves and decreased cortical acetylcholine as a possible mechanism for impaired consciousness in focal seizures. However, the role of other key subcortical arousal systems such as dopamine is largely unknown. We aimed to address this gap by investigating dopamine dynamics in a mouse model of focal limbic seizures with impaired behavioral responsiveness. Methods We induced focal limbic seizures by brief electrical hippocampal stimulation in awake head-fixed mice with hippocampal and cortical local field potential recordings. Behavior was assessed by a conditioned auditory response task. We measured cortical dopamine with a genetically encoded fluorescent sensor via fiber photometry. Activity of dopaminergic neurons in the ventral tegmental area (VTA) was recorded by calcium measurements. Results Focal hippocampal seizures were associated with altered cortical electrophysiological activity and impaired behavioral responsiveness. During seizures, we found sustained increases in dopamine in both medial prefrontal and orbital frontal cortex. We also found increased dopaminergic neuronal activity in the VTA during seizures. Despite these sustained increases, transient task-evoked dopaminergic increases in both cortex and VTA were reduced during seizures. Behavioral responses during seizures were reduced, and auditory stimuli without behavioral responses elicited smaller transient VTA dopaminergic signals compared to stimuli with preserved responses. Significance Together, those results reveal distinct dysregulation of dopamine dynamics across sustained and fast time scales during focal limbic seizures. The sustained increases in dopamine suggest that the altered cortical function and impaired consciousness in focal limbic seizures may more closely resemble encephalopathy or delirium than deep sleep. Depressed transient dopamine release with sensory stimuli could also contribute to impaired behavioral responsiveness during seizures. Further work on the role of dopamine could have important therapeutic implications for altered cognition and behavior in people with epilepsy.

items.title: Integrating behavioral and molecular biomarkers reveals neurotoxic effects of common insecticide in big brown bats.
items.abstract: While foraging in croplands, bats are exposed to pesticides that can be neurotoxic even at low concentrations, affecting their physiology and behavior. These sublethal effects are often assessed using molecular biomarkers in isolation, with limited insights into ecological consequences. Here, we used an integrative approach to assess the sublethal effects of chlorpyrifos, a common neurotoxic insecticide, on big brown bats (Eptesicus fuscus). We combined behavioral experiments with molecular biomarkers that could reveal the mechanisms underlying observed changes. We orally exposed bats to chlorpyrifos and evaluated their associative memory in a crawling Y-maze, and their stereotyped flight trajectories. To understand the mechanisms behind these behavioral changes, we quantified brain cholinesterase (ChE) activity and used non-targeted proteomics to identify cellular and molecular biomarkers of neurotoxicity. Exposed bats did not change their flight consistency, but were less explorative, had a slower reflex response, and made more incorrect choices in the Y-maze. Exposed bats had a significant reduction in their ChE activity and showed dysregulation of proteins involved in neurological processes like memory, learning, and sound perception. Our results not only provide a comprehensive understanding of the different ways in which pesticides affect individual performance, they also provide a broad description of the underlying cellular and molecular processes, increasing our mechanistic understanding of these effects. Moreover, our results support the sensitivity of behavior as an ecologically relevant biomarker of toxicity and the importance of considering multiple levels of organization to elucidate the mechanisms underlying altered behavior in wildlife due to human activities.

items.title: The relationship between regularity of nighttime rest behavior and depressive symptoms in everyday home-life using smartphone-based sensor data.
items.abstract: Background Depression is associated with disruptions in circadian and behavioral rhythms. Beyond sleep duration, temporal consistency of sleep-related behavior may represent a relevant aspect of behavioral rhythms. We examine nighttime rest regularity derived from passive smartphone activity data and its association with depressive symptom severity. Methods Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) scores and self-reported sleep duration were collected via smartphones from 234 individuals with major depressive disorder (MDD; n = 95) or healthy controls (HC; n = 139). Step counts from a 15-day window surrounding BDI assessment were analysed for nighttime intervals (10 pm-8 am), requiring at least seven valid nights. Group differences and associations between nighttime rest regularity, sleep duration, and depressive symptom severity were examined. Results No significant MDD-HC differences in rest regularity emerged (all p ≥ .058), although estimates descriptively suggested lower nighttime consistency (NCI: β = -0.083) and greater rest-duration variability (LRI-SD: β = 0.118) in MDD. Within MDD, lower regularity corresponded descriptively to higher BDI scores, but no associations survived correction (all p-BH ≥ 0.154). LRI-SD showed the largest positive estimate (β = 0.086, p-BH = 0.154). Self-reported sleep duration was not significantly associated with BDI scores in MDD (β = 0.045, p = .662) or rest regularity variables (|β| ≤ 0.043, all p ≥ .236). Conclusion Smartphone step count data enable multi-day characterization of nighttime rest regularity. No significant associations with self-reported sleep duration emerged, suggesting distinct behavioral characteristics. Associations with depressive symptom severity showed small descriptive tendencies but remained nonsignificant after correction, warranting investigation.

items.title: Longitudinal contributions of mother-toddler neural synchrony and maternal depression to children's neural reward response.
items.abstract: Background Healthy reward processing during early childhood is important for emotional development. Identifying factors that promote the development of reward processing is clinically important, given its relation to risk for depression. Parent-toddler dyadic interactions may support the development of healthy reward function in the prefrontal cortex, a region involved in reward processing, which is accessible during naturalistic social tasks via functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). Method The current study aimed to evaluate whether mother-toddler prefrontal synchrony during dyadic play and the presence of maternal depression may predict child reward function. At baseline, 63 toddlers (49% female; M age =30.6 months) and their biological mothers (21 with depression) engaged in a dyadic play task while undergoing fNIRS hyperscanning. One year later, child prefrontal response to reward was assessed via fNIRS. Results Greater mother-toddler left prefrontal oxyhemoglobin synchrony during positive dyadic play at baseline was associated with greater child left and right prefrontal oxyhemoglobin response to winning reward one year later. Children with a maternal history of depression had greater left prefrontal deoxyhemoglobin response to reward (i.e., greater prefrontal deactivation) when compared with children without this maternal history, although this finding did not hold after controlling for maternal antidepressant use. Conclusions Our findings suggest that positive mother-toddler dyadic interactions may support, via co-regulation of prefrontal reward regions, the emergence of children's own prefrontal reward response during the preschool years. Further, our findings demonstrate that clinically observable maternal depression may be related to greater prefrontal deactivation in response to reward as early as age three.

items.title: Brain variation underlying genetic factors linked to psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders.
items.abstract: Background Psychiatric and neurodegenerative conditions have both shared and distinct symptomatology, but the brain mechanisms underlying diagnostic similarities and differences remain unclear. Methods Using genome-wide association data, we analyzed 12 psychiatric disorders and four neurodegenerative diseases, assessing polygenic overlap, shared loci, and genetic causal relationships linking their genetic latent factors with 3,935 brain imaging-derived phenotypes (IDP). Results Using genomic structural equation modeling, we identified an internalizing factor (F1), an addiction factor (F2), a factor related to schizophrenia and bipolar disorder (F3), a neurodevelopmental factor (F4), and a factor related to Alzheimer's disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (F5). These showed shared transcriptomic enrichments for frontal and anterior cingulate cortical regions, while F1-specific depletion in substantia nigra and F3-specific enrichment in nucleus accumbens appeared to be specific. Fine-mapping identified 99 variants, including shared loci (e.g., VRK2: F1, F2, F3; TSHZ3: F1, F2; TCF4: F1, F3) and factor-specific loci (e.g., DRD2-F2; SCN2A-F3; FOXP2-F4; TNIP1-F5). The brain-wide analysis of fine-mapped loci identified 1,480 IDP associations (false discovery rate q 400 brain IDPs (mostly related to cortical area, cortical grey-white contrast, cortical thickness, and regional and tissue volume). Similarly, MOBP rs1768190 related to F5 was associated with >200 brain IDPs, with about half of them related to cortical thickness. Conclusions The present study provides new insights into cross-diagnostic mechanisms linking genetic variation and molecular changes to the brain structural and functional variation across psychiatric and neurodegenerative conditions.

items.title: The Association between Physical Activity and Higher Corticolimbic Synaptic Density is Independent of Body Mass Index.
items.abstract: Background Regular physical exercise has been linked to biomarkers of slowed biological aging, including brain aging, though the neurobiological mechanisms underlying this relationship remain unclear. Exercise may enhance neuroplasticity and attenuate synaptic decline; however, evidence supporting these effects has largely been limited to animal and postmortem studies. Whether physical activity is associated with synaptic density in the living human brain remains unknown. Methods We used positron emission tomography (PET) with the radiotracer [ 18 F]SynVesT-1 to quantify synaptic density in vivo in 51 individuals (61% female). Participants were classified as physically active or insufficiently active, and group differences in synaptic density across corticolimbic regions were examined. Additional regression and mediation analyses assessed associations among physical activity, synaptic density, body mass index (BMI), and depressive symptom severity. Results Physically active individuals exhibited significantly higher synaptic density across corticolimbic regions compared to insufficiently active individuals (F 6,44 =2.41, p=0.042). These effects remained marginally significant after adjusting for BMI and depressive symptom severity (F 6,42 =2.33, p=0.050). Region-specific regression analyses further demonstrated positive associations between physical activity and synaptic density. Mediation analyses indicated that BMI did not account for the observed relationships. Conclusions These findings provide the first known in vivo evidence that physical activity is associated with higher synaptic density in the living human brain, particularly within prefrontal circuits. Results suggest that exercise may support synaptic integrity through mechanisms partially independent of BMI. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine causality, characterize temporal dynamics, and evaluate whether physical activity may serve as a scalable intervention to preserve synaptic health.

items.title: Flow-induced endothelial lipid dysregulation in ischemic stroke: from mechanotransduction to therapeutic implications.
items.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) induces significant and sustained alterations in cerebral hemodynamics, which extend beyond the acute phase and actively contribute to post-stroke cerebrovascular remodeling. Accumulating evidence suggests that endothelial cholesterol and neutral-lipid homeostasis is a critical determinant of vascular integrity, whereas its dysregulation may promote endothelial inflammation, and vascular remodeling. Abnormal shear stress, particularly low and oscillatory shear stress, may connect post-stroke hemodynamic changes to endothelial lipid dysregulation by regulating lipid uptake, intracellular lipid processing, cholesterol efflux, and lipid storage through mechanotransduction pathways. Although direct evidence demonstrating that altered shear stress drives endothelial lipid accumulation in the cerebral vasculature remains limited, findings from endothelial studies and mechanobiology suggest a functional "flow-lipid axis" implicated in post-stroke vascular pathology. In this review, we summarize the hemodynamic alterations following IS and how abnormal shear stress may regulate endothelial cholesterol and neutral-lipid homeostasis through mechanosensors and downstream pathways, including AMPK, mTOR, SREBP, and lipophagy. We further identify the existing gap in causal evidence connecting post-stroke hemodynamics to cerebral endothelial lipid accumulation, and propose targeted translational research avenues aimed at facilitating the development of hemodynamic- and metabolism-based therapeutic strategies for IS.

items.title: Brain-Computer Interfaces for Traumatic Brain Injury and Spinal Cord Injury: Lesion-Pattern Matching, Functional Restoration, and Clinical Translation.
items.abstract: Background Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are increasingly being developed for clinically relevant assessment, communication, rehabilitation, and functional restoration after central nervous system injury. However, their clinical roles differ substantially across injury types. This narrative review examines BCI applications in traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) using an injury-pattern-guided framework that links residual neural architecture with clinical tasks, interface selection, and outcome assessment. Main body In SCI, motor intention and cortical activity may remain accessible despite disruption of descending pathways, supporting motor-intention decoding, brain-controlled functional electrical stimulation, neuroprosthetic control, and brain-spine interfaces. In TBI, diffuse and heterogeneous network dysfunction shifts the clinical emphasis toward detection of covert consciousness, assisted communication, neurofeedback, and multimodal rehabilitation. We compare non-invasive, endovascular, electrocorticographic, and intracortical recording approaches; summarize evoked-response, motor-imagery, and continuous decoding paradigms; and distinguish functional substitution from closed-loop restoration of an individual's own movements. Recent invasive systems have supported the restoration of grasping, standing, and walking in selected individuals with SCI, whereas evidence in TBI remains concentrated on brain-state assessment and low-bandwidth communication. Conclusion Clinical translation will require careful candidate selection, stable long-term recordings, effective bidirectional feedback, clinically meaningful real-world outcomes, ethical oversight, and sustained technical support. Disease-specific translational pathways, rather than a universal BCI model, are likely to provide the most practical route to routine clinical use after central nervous system injury.

items.title: Reactive, subjective and executive agents: How survival circuits underlie the expansion of subjective experience and felt motivation in humans and other vertebrates.
items.abstract: We review the evolution of agency in vertebrates from the Cambrian explosion to humans. Active locomotion sparked evolution of efficient decision-making in arthropods, vertebrates and later in cephalopods. Isolated neural pathways-ancient control architectures for fitness-effective action-became interconnected survival circuits: evolutionarily conserved, functionally integrated neural pathways responding to specific classes of stimuli and that compete for control, with their own set of specific responses. Computational complexity was reduced by constraining inputs, processing and outputs. We hypothesize that three evolutionary transitions deepened the subjective experience by extending the survival circuits: (i) Associative and social learning implied non-genetic information acquisition; (ii) A simulated reality where episodic-like memory and internal simulation resulted in prediction-based action-selection; (iii) Setting and executing one's own wellbeing goals based on future expectations produced a felt experience of short-term personal goals. This subjective agency in vertebrates and some arthropods and cephalopods evolved from reactive agency. Key to this transition was the mighty quadruple-subjective experience, social learning, simulation-based prediction and felt goals-paving the way for nonverbal rationality and consciousness, again reinforcing each other. The emergence of culture, social bonding and the beginning of friendship started in early vertebrates. In humans and partly in some other lineages, the mighty quadruple coevolved with language-based culture under adaptation to social games into executive agency, enhancing the capacities for friendship and sociability and the impact of personalised and conscious norms, values and purpose in the survival circuits, further strengthening the feeling of free will.

items.title: Transdiagnostic effects of medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS): A systematic review and meta-analysis of sham-controlled trials.
items.abstract: Background There is a growing body of evidence to support the role of the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) as having a central role in a variety of psychiatric disorders. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) has been investigated over the mPFC in multiple recent sham-controlled trials. However, no meta-analysis of transdiagnostic symptoms across psychiatric disorders has been undertaken. Objectives This systematic review and meta-analysis (CRD42022354346) examined the transdiagnostic symptoms of rTMS to the mPFC for a number of psychiatric diagnoses. Methods The analysis included randomised, sham-controlled trials of rTMS to the mPFC for psychiatric disorders. The key outcomes were change in clinical symptoms, quality of life, and cognition measures from pre- to post- treatment, in symptom domains including depression, anxiety, obsessive compulsive symptoms, negative symptoms, craving, and consumption. Findings We retrieved 3,901 records, 176 were screened at full text, and 30 were included. Seventeen symptom domains and 1,083 participants were analysed. rTMS to the mPFC produced moderate to large effects for obsessive compulsive symptoms, moderate effects for negative symptoms and craving, and small effects for depressive symptoms. Effects for anxiety, cognition, consumption and impulsivity were non-significant. Interpretation was limited by the overall small number of studies, high heterogeneity in findings and some concerns of risk of bias. Conclusion This systematic review and meta-analysis suggests that rTMS over the mPFC may have therapeutic potential for obsessive-compulsive symptoms, negative symptoms, and craving, with modest effects for depressive symptoms. Further high-quality, adequately-powered trials are needed to confirm effects and clarify optimal stimulation protocols.

items.title: Something's gotta give: Reward-induced effort modulation in task-switching reveals a flexibility-stability trade-off.
items.abstract: Everyday behavior requires balancing two control modes: flexibility, for switching between tasks, and stability, for maintaining goals in the face of interference. One influential account posits that these modes trade off, such that increased flexibility comes at the cost of reduced stability. However, empirical support for this trade-off remains equivocal. We propose that it arises from reward-induced effortful control modulations during tasks that require both modes simultaneously. Across two experiments (N = 80 and N = 87), participants completed a task-switching paradigm in which cued reward incentives were manipulated over varying timescales. Large rewards increased flexibility, evinced by reduced task switch costs, but reduced stability, evinced by increased incongruence costs. In Experiment 1, this trade-off also emerged across blocks, with fluctuations in stability and flexibility inversely related under reward. Overall, these findings provide evidence for a reward-driven flexibility-stability trade-off, in which higher incentives promote flexibility at the cost of stability.
