items.title: Transplantation of Lhx8/KDM7A/FGF4-induced OM-MSCs-derived neuron-like cells improves neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment in Aβ1-42-induced mouse model.
items.abstract: Cell-based therapies have emerged as a promising therapeutic avenue for Alzheimer's disease (AD). Prior studies have demonstrated the beneficial effects of neuronal-like cells differentiated from human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) in mitigating AD pathology. This study investigates the therapeutic efficacy and molecular mechanisms of neuronal-like cells derived from olfactory mucosa MSCs (OM-MSCs) in Aβ1-42-induced acute neurotoxicity. Neuronal differentiation of OM-MSCs was induced using tricyclodecan-9-yl-xanthogenate (D609). An in vivo model was constructed by intrahippocampal injection of Aβ1-42 and treated by transplantation of OM-MSC-derived neuronal cells (OM-MSCs-NCs). In this study, we demonstrated that LIM homeobox protein 8 (Lhx8) expression was upregulated during OM-MSCs-NCs neuronal differentiation. Functional analyses revealed that Lhx8 overexpression enhanced neuronal differentiation of OM-MSCs, whereas Lhx8 knockdown impaired this process. In Aβ1-42-induced mouse models, transplantation of OM-MSCs-NCs ameliorated cognitive deficits, and neuroinflammation while promoting M2-like microglial polarization. Notably, Lhx8-overexpressing OM-MSCs-NCs exhibited amplified therapeutic efficacy, whereas Lhx8-knockdown cells showed diminished effects. Mechanistically, Lhx8 transcriptionally activates lysine demethylase 7 A (KDM7A) by binding to its promoter, thereby regulating the KDM7A/fibroblast growth factor 4 (FGF4) axis. Knockdown of either KDM7A or FGF4 abolished both the pro-differentiation effects of Lhx8 overexpression in vitro and its therapeutic benefits in an Aβ1-42-induced acute toxicity model. In conclusion, Lhx8 promotes neuronal-like differentiation of OM-MSCs by activating the KDM7A/FGF4 axis, thereby alleviating neuroinflammation and cognitive deficits in an Aβ1-42-induced mouse model.

items.title: A nonsense variant in KCNH7 (c.1324 C>T) is associated with a variable phenotypic spectrum of epilepsy.
items.abstract: KCNH7 is a voltage-gated potassium (K+) channel (Kv) that regulates membrane excitability and K+ flux across tissues. Studies using mouse models have suggested that Kcnh7 may play an important role in epilepsy susceptibility and pathogenesis. However, clinical and experimental evidence implicating KCNH7 variants in human epilepsy, as well as the genotype-phenotype association, remains unclear. Here, we aimed to refine the clinical, genetic, and functional electrophysiological features of a p.R442* variant identified in three individuals to elucidate potential genotype-phenotype association that may guide anticipatory management. We generated Kcnh7 mutants​ using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing. Heterozygous mutants exhibited increased neuronal hyperexcitability and increased seizure susceptibility due to reduced Kcnh7-encoded protein levels. Functional analyses established the KCNH7 p.R442* variant as a loss-of-function allele, with haploinsufficiency identified as a primary pathogenic mechanism. Our results underscore the significance of functional characterization for the KCNH7 p.R442* variant within the context of clinical interpretation, although larger cohorts are required to further validate these observations.

items.title: Global threats and conservation strategies for temporary ponds based on expert opinion and scientific evidence.
items.abstract: Temporary ponds are dynamic aquatic habitats found in all global biomes. Because they seasonally or intermittently dry out, they often support specialist flora and fauna including many endemic species. Although numerous studies report their decline, there is little consensus on their primary threats or effective mitigation strategies. Through a literature review and a global questionnaire survey of 137 pond experts, we identified agricultural intensification and urbanization as the leading threats, followed by habitat modification and climate change. The limited regulation of ecologically damaging human activities such as resource extraction or pollution and weak enforcement of conservation laws were also seen as significant barriers to effective protection. Although pond creation for ecological restoration emerged as the most common intervention, achieving desired conservation outcomes was found to be challenging because new ponds often are too permanent or too ephemeral to support many temporary pond specialists. We therefore identified the key challenges, considerations, and emerging guidelines needed to improve pond creation outcomes. A widespread lack of awareness among policymakers, researchers, land managers, and the general public was cited by most experts as a key driver of neglect. Our findings highlight the need to raise awareness and engage a broader range of stakeholders in the conservation of these ecologically valuable, yet often overlooked, habitats.

items.title: Using resource selection functions (RSFs) to model the movement ecology of invasive predators in the last remaining habitat of the endangered Atlantic whitefish.
items.abstract: Aquatic invasive species are among the top threats to freshwater fishes globally, causing declines in freshwater biodiversity and altering ecosystem functioning. Within Nova Scotia, Canada, invasive chain pickerel (Esox niger) and smallmouth bass (Micropterus dolomieu) have been found to reduce the abundance and diversity of native fishes. The invasive range of both species threatens and overlaps with the critical habitat of one of Canada's most endangered fishes, the Atlantic whitefish (Coregonus huntsmani). Here, we examine the seasonal space and depth use of adult chain pickerel and smallmouth bass using acoustic telemetry in Milipsigate Lake, Nova Scotia. High-resolution positions were calculated and analyzed using resource selection functions (RSFs) and generalized additive models (GAMs) to determine the relative space use and predicted depth of both species within the lake. Areas with the highest relative probability of use (>0.7) differed between species, and seasonal changes in space use were only significant for smallmouth bass (p < 0.001). Chain pickerel had the highest relative probability of space use in shallow areas of Milipsigate Lake (<4 m), whereas areas with the highest relative probability of space use for smallmouth bass were concentrated around four distinct overwintering sites. Chain pickerel were predicted to occupy a narrow range (~2 m) of relatively shallow depths year-round. Smallmouth bass were predicted to occupy depths that were on average three times deeper than chain pickerel, including a broad range of depths from spring to fall (0-15 m) that contracted during the winter months (2-6 m). Here, we showed that the combined occupancy of the lake by both species is extensive, with limited overlap in space or depth use year-round. Ultimately, the methodologies and results presented in this study could help inform the development of management strategies for invasive freshwater fish species.

items.title: Lanthanide-dependent methanotroph thrives on radioactive promethium.
items.abstract: Lanthanides serve as essential cofactors in the methanol dehydrogenases of methylotrophic bacteria. While biological function has been characterized for the naturally occurring members of the series, promethium, the only lanthanide existing as exclusively radioactive isotopes and virtually absent from nature, has remained unexplored. Here, the acidophilic methanotroph Methylacidiphilum fumariolicum SolV grows on β⁻-emitting Pm-147 as its sole lanthanide source, removing 98% of the isotope from the medium over 60 h despite a calculated radiation dose of 3.6 Gy. Reconstituted methanol dehydrogenase of the type XoxF-MDH displays Pm-dependent activity precisely between the neodymium and samarium variants. Bacterial lanthanide metabolism thus incorporates a naturally absent and radioactive member of the lanthanide series.

items.title: Migration strategy and colonization: the disproportionate role of partial migration.
items.abstract: Colonization drives diversification and determines how species shift their ranges, making it central to ecology and evolution. As both seasonal migration and dispersal depend on locomotor capacity, migration could be a major yet overlooked route to colonization. Here, we present evidence that partially migratory species are disproportionately successful in founding new populations, whereas strict migrants establish more rarely despite routinely reaching potentially suitable habitat in novel areas. Building on the threshold model of migration, we propose that partial migrants' liability to migrate lies closer to the threshold and/or is more environmentally sensitive, allowing displaced individuals to settle. This mechanism can help explain species distributions and diversification and predict which species might colonize newly suitable areas under global environmental change.

items.title: Microbial hazards and contamination dynamics in warm marine seafood supply chains: From detection to predictive risk management.
items.abstract: Warm marine seafood systems face distinctive microbial safety challenges arising from elevated environmental temperatures, climate-sensitive Vibrio ecology, cold-chain vulnerability, and heterogeneous supply chains. This review critically examines how environmental drivers of indigenous marine pathogens interact with post-harvest contamination and microbial amplification from harvest to retail, and evaluates the implications for HACCP verification, microbial risk assessment (MRA), molecular surveillance, traceability, and preventive control. The evidence indicates that seafood microbial risk is cumulative and stage-dependent: environmental baseline hazards are modified by time-temperature history, water and ice quality, sanitation, handling, processing, and cross-contamination. Reliance on endpoint and predominantly qualitative microbiological sampling limits source attribution, obscures contamination and amplification points, and constrains quantitative exposure assessment. We therefore propose an integrated environment-to-consumer framework linking stage-specific quantitative microbiology with environmental monitoring, predictive microbiology, molecular source attribution, HACCP verification, traceability, and quantitative MRA. Particular emphasis is placed on pathogenic Vibrio spp. as climate-sensitive hazards and on the complementary roles of culture-based and genomic methods in determining viable hazards and contamination pathways. Oman and the Gulf Cooperation Council are considered as a regional case within the broader context of tropical and subtropical seafood systems. The central priority is a transition from endpoint pathogen detection toward longitudinal, quantitative, and predictive microbial risk management capable of identifying where hazards originate, where they are amplified, and which interventions most effectively reduce consumer exposure.

items.title: Genome-resolved multi-omics reveals microbiome reorganization and carbon-flow regulation driven by functional bioaugmentation in thermophilic anaerobic digestion.
items.abstract: Bioaugmentation has emerged as a promising strategy for manipulating complex microbial ecosystems. However, the ecological mechanisms determining whether introduced microorganisms can functionally integrate into indigenous communities remain poorly understood. Here, genome-resolved metagenomics and metabolomics were combined to investigate how B. thermoamylovorans Y25 influenced microbial succession and ecosystem-level carbon transformation. Y25 successfully established within the thermophilic anaerobic microbiome and promoted a 12.69% (472.00 ± 27.69 NmL g -1 VS, p < 0.05) increase in cumulative methane yield without compromising reactor stability. This improvement occurred without significant changes in methanogenesis-related genes. Instead, Y25 bioaugmentation induced pronounced shifts in microorganisms associated with hydrolysis and fermentation and enhanced pathways related to substrate transport and intermediate carbon metabolism, accompanied by coordinated metabolite changes. These findings support a transition from strain-centered bioaugmentation strategies toward an ecosystem-level perspective, highlighting that successful microbial engineering depends on ecological integration and functional coordination within indigenous microbial networks.

items.title: Combined effects of sulfoxaflor, microplastics, and Nosema ceranae on honeybee physiology and midgut transcriptomics.
items.abstract: Honeybees in agricultural ecosystems frequently encounter pesticides, microplastics (MPs), and pathogens, yet the combined effects of these stressors remain poorly understood. Here, honeybees (Apis mellifera L.) were exposed to sulfoxaflor (SFX, 10 μg/L), polystyrene nano- and microplastics (PS-NMPs, 0.08 μm and 5 μm, 25 mg/L), and Nosema ceranae (Nc, 1×10 6 spores/mL), either alone or in combination. Survival rate, sucrose consumption, midgut weight, histological structure, midgut transcriptomics, stress-related gene expression, and enzyme activities were assessed. Among the single stressors, SFX caused the strongest reduction in survival, whereas Nc more prominently reduced sucrose consumption and induced midgut epithelial thickening. In contrast, SFX and PS-NMPs were more strongly associated with reductions in midgut weight and epithelial thickness. Although combined exposure did not consistently increase mortality relative to single stressor exposure, it induced marked transcriptomic disturbances. Lysosome pathway changes were observed across most treatment groups, whereas combined exposure involving Nc showed the strongest transcriptomic perturbation, characterized by suppression of ribosome and oxidative phosphorylation pathways. Representative gene expressions and enzyme activities further revealed stressor-specific immune, detoxification, and lysosome associated responses. These findings provide new insights into the complex interactions among multiple stressors in honeybees and highlight the potential ecological risks associated with multi-stressor exposure in honeybees.

items.title: Mineral-microbe interactions in stratified dam reservoirs.
items.abstract: Mineral-microbe interactions are core interfacial processes regulating elemental cycling in aquatic sediments. Dam construction converts free-flowing rivers into sediment-retaining and often stratified reservoirs, thereby altering hydrodynamic energy, particle sorting, residence time, oxygen delivery and redox zonation at the sediment-water interface. Although extensive studies have documented dam effects on hydrology, sediment delivery, water quality and greenhouse gas emissions, less attention has been given to how reservoir formation reorganizes established mineral-microbe processes at oxygen-limited interfaces that persist during periods of stable thermal stratification. Here, we synthesize recent progress on mineral-microbe interactions in stratified dam reservoirs. We first examine how flow attenuation and sediment trapping create fine-grained, organic-rich depositional zones, and how thermal stratification promotes hypolimnetic anoxia, redox gradients and reactive sediment-water interfaces. Against this environmental background, we focus on three closely related modes of mineral-microbe coupling: microbial colonization on mineral surfaces, electron transfer between microorganisms and redox-active phases, and microbially mediated mineral transformation. We then summarize how these mechanisms operate in natural aquatic systems, including extracellular polymeric substances (EPS)-mediated colonization, direct and shuttle-mediated electron transfer, and microbial mineral dissolution, precipitation and transformation. Building on this baseline, we discuss how reservoir stratification and redox conditions reorganize these same processes and their consequences for Fe/Mn mineral cycling, organic matter stabilization, nutrient release, pollutant mobility and greenhouse gas production. Because stratification, anoxia and early diagenetic redox reactions also occur in natural deep lakes, we distinguish these shared limnological and diagenetic mechanisms from dam-specific controls, including sediment retention, regulated residence time, water-level fluctuation, selective withdrawal and downstream sediment discontinuity. This review provides a focused conceptual framework for linking dam-induced environmental transition with mineral-microbe coupling, and highlights implications for reservoir water-quality management, internal loading control, contaminant risk and carbon-cycle regulation.

items.title: Drivers of biodiversity in mineral extraction sites - a cross-taxa analysis with implications for management and restoration.
items.abstract: Extraction sites are often considered sources of environmental damage. However, in intensively used and nutrient-enriched landscapes they may also provide exceptional secondary habitats, shaped by disturbance and nutrient depletion. Their contribution to biodiversity across taxonomic groups remains insufficiently understood, and integrated guidelines for managing biodiversity during active extraction are needed. We examined terrestrial and aquatic biodiversity across twelve active German extraction sites of limestone, gypsum, sand and gravel. Data on vascular plants, soil parameters and six insect groups were collected via vegetation relevés, soil samples, DNA metabarcoding from trap samples and transect walks on 103 terrestrial plots. Aquatic diversity (Amphibia and Odonata) was assessed at 75 water bodies using transect walks and eDNA metabarcoding. Across all sites, we recorded 2054 species, including 168 threatened in Germany. Species composition varied strongly across substrate types and between plots. Terrestrial insect diversity increased with plant species richness, while higher latitude, which was correlated with sampling year, and the proportion of shrubs had negative effects. The respective insect groups showed group-specific responses to plot age, the proportions of open soil, active extraction area and surrounding grassland. To maximise conservation value, particularly for terrestrial insects, site management should promote habitat heterogeneity and allow the formation of temporary habitats through natural succession. Increasing vascular plant richness boosts local insect diversity. Embedding biodiversity management into the regional context can create networks of valuable secondary habitats. Extraction sites thus bear a high but so far underused potential to advance restoration targets beyond existing protected areas.

items.title: Effects of sampling methods on recovery of introduced emerald ash borer parasitoids: a Bayesian integrated nested Laplace approximation analysis of the mapBioControl dataset.
items.abstract: Since 2007 and 2015, respectively, the parasitoids Tetrastichus planipennisi Yang (Hymenoptera: Eulophidae) and Spathius galinae Belokobylskij and Strazanac (Hymenoptera: Braconidae) have been introduced to the United States for biological control of the emerald ash borer Agrilus planipennis Fairmaire (Coleoptera: Buprestidae). A web-enabled geospatial database, mapBioControl, has also been developed to support monitoring, management, and evaluation of these biological control efforts. We applied Bayesian binomial models and discrete-time hazard models to mapBioControl data to assess how sampling method, sampling effort, and release year influenced recovery probabilities for T. planipennisi and S. galinae across the United States and Canada. For both species, best-fit Bayesian binomial models indicated that recovery method was an important predictor of parasitoid detection, although method-specific patterns differed between species. Discrete-time hazard models indicated higher first-detection hazards for targeted recovery methods relative to yellow pan traps, including tree debarking for S. galinae (HR = 3.48 [95% CrI: 1.88 to 6.47]) and T. planipennisi (HR = 9.81 [95% CrI: 5.42 to 17.76]). Detection probabilities also increased with a greater number of sampling days for targeted recovery methods. While little evidence of residual spatial autocorrelation for T. planipennisi was detected, there were strong indications of spatial autocorrelation for S. galinae. Our results indicate that post-release monitoring is influenced by sampling method and sampling effort, and targeted recovery methods like tree debarking and larval sentinel logs may provide higher probabilities of parasitoid detection. When resources are limited, trade-offs among cost, labor, and monitoring objectives should guide the choice of sampling method.

items.title: Widespread marine mammal and seabird reductions are unlikely to benefit salmon due to indirect ecosystem effects.
items.abstract: Pacific salmon are depleted due to anthropogenic impacts, and populations have failed to recover despite management interventions. Predation on salmon by pinnipeds and seabirds has been suggested as a barrier to recovery, leading to calls for predator culls by some. However, no studies have evaluated the whole-ecosystem impact of removing these predators nor estimated the direct and indirect effects of these culls on salmon. We use an end-to-end ecosystem model to assess the efficacy of widespread culls in marine environments. We find that culls are unlikely to benefit salmon due to the indirect food web effects of predator reduction and the low biomass of top predator groups. Instead, more abundant fish predators, northward-expanding competitors, and temperature-sensitive prey have larger effects on salmon in the ocean.

items.title: Absence of hydraulic segmentation in tropical and subtropical woody plants.
items.abstract: The stem-leaf segmentation hypothesis proposes that leaves act as safety valves to protect stem hydraulic function under drought, which involves two specific mechanisms, i.e., hydraulic segmentation hypothesis (HSH; higher hydraulic resistance in leaves than in stems) and vulnerability segmentation hypothesis (VSH; lower embolism resistance in leaves than in stems). However, relative to the VSH, the HSH remains poorly understood. In this study, we measured sapwood specific hydraulic conductivity (ks), leaf hydraulic conductance (${K}_{\mathrm{leaf}}^{\mathrm{max}}$), embolism resistance (P50), and maximum stomatal conductance (gs) of 118 woody species from six tropical and subtropical forests. To test the HSH, we examined the relationships between stem and leaf hydraulic conductivity, and between hydraulic function and gas exchange. It is hypothesized that these tropical-subtropical species exhibiting distinct hydraulic segmentation (leaves as a hydraulic bottleneck) showed negative ks-${K}_{\mathrm{leaf}}^{\mathrm{max}}$ relationship and stronger ${K}_{\mathrm{leaf}}^{\mathrm{max}}$-gs relationship (than ks-gs). We found that there were no significant ks-${K}_{\mathrm{leaf}}^{\mathrm{max}}$ relationships across all the studied species and in any forest type or functional group. In addition, gs was positively related with ks, but not with ${K}_{\mathrm{leaf}}^{\mathrm{max}}$. Our results thus did not support HSH in tropical-subtropical woody species. Furthermore, we analyzed ks-${K}_{\mathrm{leaf}}^{\mathrm{max}}$ relationship under different degree of vulnerability segmentation (the difference in P50 between stem and leaf; P50leaf-stem). Specifically, the ks-${K}_{\mathrm{leaf}}^{\mathrm{max}}$ relationship was absent under weak P50leaf-stem ( 2 MPa), revealing that the degree of P50leaf-stem influences the stem-leaf hydraulic relationship. This study deepens our understanding of the stem-leaf hydraulic framework coping with drought stress.

items.title: Deep longitudinal phenotyping of a single individual enables host-microbiome metabolic modeling over 3.6 years.
items.abstract: This study examines a single subject (LS) experiencing severe episodic colonic inflammation and associated gut microbiome dysbiosis. Metagenomic sequencing of LS's stool samples at 51 time points over 3.6 years provided a time series of gut microbial species' relative abundances, from which we generated time-point specific microbiome models. Flux balance analysis was used to predict metabolic phenotypes across the time series. The microbial abundances and predicted fluxes were compared with clinical inflammation biomarkers [serum C-reactive protein (CRP); stool lactoferrin, calprotectin, lysozyme, and secretory immunoglobulin A]. Each of these 51 microbiome models were integrated with a time-point specific male whole-body metabolic model personalized based on LS's weight, blood glucose, and cholesterol. A healthy average (HeAve) community model from 34 individuals provided a reference. Our models predicted methane overproduction from high Methanobrevibacter smithii levels, coinciding with peak CRP and calprotectin. We found that Escherichia coli plays a central role in shaping the predicted metabolome and may promote inflammation through trimethylamine N-oxide and formaldehyde production, out-competing Desulfovibrio piger and Akkermansia muciniphila via active methyl and sulfur cycles. At a later time point, LS experienced a major shift in gut Proteobacteria ecology: E. coli, over-abundant at 675 × HeAve, dropped nearly 80-fold in one month, while Morganella morganii rose by nearly eight times, which coincided with a spike in LS's lactoferrin and lysozyme, a rise in species including Klebsiella pneumoniae and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, a change in predicted metabolic profile, and increased alpha diversity. We also noted a correlation between postulated inflammation periods and predicted lithocholic acid levels. This work extends two previous studies of 7 and 27 of these time points. Our analysis demonstrates the value of pairing multi-omics time-series data with systems biology approaches in an n-of-1 design, resolving how microbiome composition dynamics shape host-microbiome metabolism and inflammation.

items.title: Tracking the trajectory of individual conjugative plasmids in bacterial communities using CRISPR acquisition-based recording
items.abstract: Horizontal gene transfer mediated by conjugative plasmids is a primary driver of bacterial evolution and the spread of adaptive traits, including antibiotic resistance determinants. Tracking how these plasmids disseminate through complex microbial communities remains a major challenge. Current methodologies often yield static, endpoint snapshots of host identity, overlooking transient transfer events and plasmid encounters with the co-resident mobilome. To overcome these limitations, we introduce SPacer Integration (SPI) plasmids, which turn the mobile element itself into a recorder of its own transfer history. We engineered conjugative and mobilizable plasmids to carry a CRISPR-Cas adaptation cassette (cas1-cas2 and a minimal CRISPR array) and maintain tight repression of cas1-cas2 expression in the donor cell, so that upon transfer they capture spacers from the chromosome and plasmids of new hosts and store them permanently in their own array. Subsequent PCR amplification and sequencing of these expanded arrays provide a molecular record of both the bacterial hosts and the co-resident plasmids encountered. We created SPI plasmids using the backbones of well-characterized mobilizable and conjugative plasmids RSF1010, RP4, F, and R100-1. We tested SPI plasmids in defined laboratory matings and in complex wastewater communities. The analysis of the acquired spacers successfully mapped permissive host ranges and profiled the co-resident plasmids in situ. Requiring only standard cloning, PCR and sequencing, this accessible and cost-effective strategy establishes a new framework for studying plasmid ecology. Because spacers are integrated chronologically, it further offers the potential to reconstruct multi-step transfer trajectories across natural microbial networks.

items.title: Terminological variation in ecological connectivity terms in Europe
items.abstract: Abstract Ecological connectivity has become a major policy concern in Europe, but the language used to describe connected green–blue interventions is still fragmented. We analysed 3,868 articles with first authors based in Europe, published between 1956 and 2025, to examine how 15 related terms have been used across time, contexts, disciplines and keyword networks. Green infrastructure clearly dominates the literature, followed by ecological network, while corridor-, belt- and pathway-related terms occupy a smaller but diverse space. Since the early 2000s, the field has moved away from a mainly conservation-focused vocabulary towards broader concepts linked to urban planning, climate adaptation and ecosystem services. We show that broad terms connect debates across planning, ecology and climate, whereas more specific terms remain narrowly used. To improve comparable monitoring and policy alignment, we propose a pragmatic ‘umbrella + mechanism + scale’ heuristic for naming connected green-blue interventions.

items.title: Community perspectives on the health information ecosystem
items.abstract: Abstract The COVID-19 infodemic highlighted how misinformation, inconsistent guidance, and barriers to reliable information undermined vaccine confidence, particularly in underserved communities. This qualitative study examined barriers to vaccination, as well as communication and information challenges experienced by community residents and stakeholders in areas of high social vulnerability in a mid-sized Midwestern city. Focus groups and interviews with community residents, community leaders, and healthcare providers (N = 31) were thematically analysed and interpreted through the Social Ecology of Health Beliefs and Misinformation Framework. Findings identified two primary themes: (1) barriers to vaccination and (2) communication and information challenges, including language barriers and a lack of reliable information. These challenges emerged across individual, interpersonal, community, and structural/systemic levels. Community-informed solutions included micro-communication through trusted community messengers, culturally congruent communication, and partnerships with faith organisations. Importantly, these findings have implications for future public health crises, highlighting the need for coordinated strategies that operate across ecological levels and emphasise clear, culturally relevant, and trusted health messaging. Strengthening trusted messenger networks, fostering community partnerships, and implementing policies that address inequities may improve preparedness for future public health crises.

items.title: The mOTUs-db in 2027: linking taxonomy, genome-encoded function, and biogeography across environments.
items.abstract: A molecular understanding of microbial communities requires linking taxonomic composition to the genome-resolved functional potential of member taxa. However, this integration remains challenging since representative genomes from cultivated strains are unavailable. Here, we present a new release of the mOTUs database, which extends genome coverage of underexplored environments and enriches its 3.9 million genome collection with functional annotations. Samples are annotated with a new hierarchical environmental ontology and geographic coordinates, supporting customizable sample grouping and biogeographic analyses, while links to MicrobeAtlas provide further insight into global taxon distributions. The web interface has new features for interactive exploration of samples, studies, and taxon abundances on a map. The integrated mOTUs command-line tool enables taxonomic profiling of metagenomes, comparison of user genomes with marker gene-based operational species-level taxonomic units (mOTUs) represented in the database, and retrieval of genomes based on identifiers, taxonomic labels, and functional annotations. A new API enables high-throughput programmatic retrieval of user-tailored subsets. Taken together, mOTUs provides a foundation for advancing microbial ecology through systematic integration of taxonomic composition, functional potential, and environmental distribution of taxa within one framework. The database is available at https://motus-db.org.

items.title: Chromosome-level assembly and population-scale genomics in an intensively monitored wild bird, the Seychelles warbler.
items.abstract: Understanding evolutionary processes is greatly facilitated by high-quality data on genetic variation. We report the development of a genomic toolkit for a recently bottlenecked, long-term studied species, the Seychelles warbler (Ptimerl dezil; Acrocephalus sechellensis). This toolkit comprises a reference genome assembled into 31 chromosomes, together with functional annotations and reference-panel-free imputation of whole-genome sequences from 1,935 individuals. The genomic data have been used to assign the sequenced individuals into a genetic pedigree. Individual genomic data are associated with a suite of phenotypic metadata, amassed from three decades of fieldwork in this closed, long-term monitored population. We compared sex and parentage assigned using the genomic data with the previously recorded sex and parentage metadata to identify and correct 41 sample DNA samples labelled with the wrong identity. This population resource enables a wide range of analyses, that include, but are not limited to phylogenetics, metabarcoding, recombination rates, linkage patterns, adaptation, heritability, demographic history, selection, and inbreeding estimates. We wish to encourage interest from researchers seeking to collaborate on future analyses and data collection. Overall, our methods demonstrate the potential of next generation sequencing and statistical tools to provide dense genomic datasets at large sample sizes for wild populations.

items.title: How Indigenous Psychologies Resemble Mathematics: The Epistemic Role of Conceptual Innovation.
items.abstract: This paper argues that indigenous psychologies and mathematics share an important methodological feature: both advance understanding by refining conceptual systems and terminology. Throughout the history of mathematics, the reformulation of concepts has often enabled mathematicians to solve problems that had remained unresolved for centuries. Similarly, indigenous psychologies emerged from the recognition that the concepts of mainstream psychology do not always adequately capture the psychological realities of indigenous populations. They therefore develop culturally grounded concepts and terminology that improve the understanding of psychological phenomena within specific cultural contexts. Most indigenous psychology concepts belong to the field of social psychology. If the primary goal of social psychology is to understand human social behavior and experience, then indigenous psychologies pursue this goal through conceptual innovation in much the same way that mathematics advances through the refinement of its own conceptual framework. The paper also identifies important limits to this analogy: unlike mathematical concepts, the usefulness of indigenous psychological concepts may be difficult to appreciate without experience of the relevant cultural environment. The paper therefore discusses cultural experience and social success as possible ways of assessing the value of indigenous psychological concepts.

items.title: Natural environments and sleep during pregnancy: Associations of green and blue spaces with prenatal sleep outcomes in a Canadian cohort.
items.abstract: Objectives Sleep quality during pregnancy is critical for maternal and child health, yet environmental determinants of prenatal sleep remain understudied. Green and blue spaces have demonstrated positive effects on mental health, which is robustly associated with sleep, but direct impacts of green and blue spaces on sleep among pregnant individuals are unclear. This study examined associations between green and blue spaces and sleep duration, disturbance, and impairment during pregnancy. Methods Data from the pan-Canadian Pregnancy during the Covid-19 Pandemic (PdP, n = 8583) were linked with green (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), tree canopy) and blue space (distance from the nearest water body) data from Canadian Urban Environmental Health Research Consortium (CANUE). Sleep outcomes included self-reported sleep duration, disturbance, and impairment. Multiple linear regression models adjusted for age, ethnicity, neighborhood deprivation, socioeconomic status, population density, COVID-19 restriction severity, season, physical activity, and trimester. Results Greater tree canopy cover and NDVI were significantly associated with longer sleep duration. Contrary to our hypothesis, greater distance from water bodies was also associated with longer sleep duration and lower sleep disturbance. After additional adjustments, only the associations with sleep duration remained significant. No associations were observed for sleep-related impairment. Conclusions Green spaces, particularly tree canopy, may positively influence prenatal sleep duration, whereas the effects of blue spaces may depend more on the type of interaction with these environments and additional contextual factors. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating environmental factors, particularly tree-rich environment, into maternal health strategies and urban planning to support perinatal well-being.

items.title: Weekly intensive longitudinal assessment as a therapeutic adjunct for adolescent suicide risk: An observational study.
items.abstract: Adolescent suicide is a leading cause of death, highlighting the need for scalable prevention strategies. Intensive longitudinal assessment (ILA) is commonly used in suicide research to track fluctuations in suicidal thoughts and behaviors (STB), though its therapeutic potential remains unclear. This study examined whether weekly app-based ILA engagement during outpatient treatment was associated with improved STB outcomes among high-risk adolescents and explored possible psychological mechanisms underlying these effects. Participants were 362 adolescents receiving outpatient care for STB (M age = 14.80 years, SD = 1.85) who were followed for 6 months. Adolescents were grouped by treatment condition (brief interpersonal psychotherapy-based suicide crisis intervention [IPT-A-SCI] vs. active control) and ILA engagement (ILA vs. no ILA). ILA participants completed one app-based assessment per week concerning the preceding week. STB were assessed using clinician-administered and self-report measures at baseline and follow-up. An ILA × Time × Treatment interaction indicated that the association between ILA and reduced SI presence was significantly stronger among adolescents receiving IPT-A-SCI than among those in the active control condition at one-month follow-up. Within the IPT-A-SCI arm, ILA engagement was also associated with greater reductions in SI severity over time. ILA was associated with reduced suicidal behavior at six-month follow-up in the active control arm. Mediation analyses showed that perceived connectedness and emotional awareness were associated with STB outcomes, though neither significantly mediated the relationship between ILA and STB. Findings suggest that weekly ILA paired with clinician-monitored safety follow-up may serve as an adjunct to outpatient care for high-risk adolescents.

items.title: Closing the evidence gap: a life course and neurodiversity-informed participatory scoping review of healthy ageing randomised controlled trials in adults with developmental disabilities.
items.abstract: Adults aged 18 years and older with developmental disabilities experience disproportionate adverse health outcomes across the life course and shortened life expectancy. We conducted a participatory scoping review of randomised controlled trials of healthy ageing interventions for adults with developmental disabilities, informed by the WHO life course framework and neurodiversity principles. We searched Ovid MEDLINE and Web of Science Core Collection on June 25, 2024, and April 10, 2025, and charted study characteristics and framework alignment. We included 79 trials with 8221 participants. Although 77 (97%) of 79 studies addressed at least one functional ability, only 25 (32%) targeted life course transitions, 28 (35%) targeted multiple ecosystem levels, 22 (28%) used participatory approaches, and 20 (25%) used strengths-based approaches. Life course and neurodiversity principles were incompletely integrated into intervention research, indicating opportunities to address developmental transitions, multiple ecosystem levels, social and community participation, and strengths across the life course.

items.title: Psychological, lifestyle, and self-management profiles among Indonesian adults with diabetes in the fifth wave of the Indonesia family life survey.
items.abstract: Diabetes mellitus requires continued psychological adjustment, healthy lifestyle behaviors, and ongoing disease management. This study examined heterogeneity in psychological functioning, well-being, lifestyle behaviors, and diabetes care indicators among adults with diabetes in the fifth wave of the Indonesia Family Life Survey (IFLS-5). The analysis included 685 respondents with a self-reported diagnosis of diabetes by a health professional and 14 binary indicators in six domains: psychological distress (depressive symptoms, sleep disturbance, neuroticism), subjective well-being (life satisfaction, general happiness), lifestyle behaviors (smoking behavior, physical activity, sweet food consumption), diabetes self-management (medication use, health monitoring), comorbidity and functional burden (comorbid chronic conditions, functional limitation), and healthcare service utilization (outpatient health service utilization, inpatient hospitalization history). A three-class solution was retained because BIC and CAIC were lowest at three classes, the Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin test did not support a fourth class, the smallest class comprised 16.2% of the sample, and the classes were interpretable; class separation was moderate (entropy = 0.719). The classes were Low-Distress Low-Engagement (61.1%), with low distress, high well-being, and comparatively low medication use and monitoring; High-Engagement High-Comorbidity (22.7%), with a high probability of current medication use and health monitoring and the heaviest comorbidity and functional burden; and High-Distress Low-Engagement (16.2%), with elevated depressive symptoms, lower well-being, and the lowest probabilities of medication use and monitoring. The three-class structure was reproduced when seven indicators kept their original scales, although membership in the distress class was less stable. The same three classes were obtained without the Neuroticism indicator, whose internal consistency was low, and adjusting the standard errors for household and enumeration-area clustering changed them only slightly. These co-occurring patterns require longitudinal and external validation.

items.title: Why purpose matters for first-year psychology students: Examining an autonomy-based pathway to study-related positive affect and intellectual risk taking.
items.abstract: The transition to higher education often challenges students' motivation and wellbeing. Drawing on Self-Determination Theory and the Dualistic Model of Passion, this research examined whether academic self-concordance and harmonious passion (HP) statistically mediated the association between purpose in life (PIL) and two outcomes central to first-year adjustment: study-related positive affect (Study 1) and intellectual risk taking (IRT; Study 2). Two cross-sectional studies were conducted with independent cohorts of first-semester psychology students from a university in the Netherlands, with each cohort recruited in a consecutive academic year. In both studies, serial mediation analyses using PROCESS Model 6 (Hayes, 2022) showed that higher PIL was associated with greater academic self-concordance, which was, in turn, associated with higher HP for study. In Study 1, the indirect association between PIL and study-related positive affect through academic self-concordance and HP was significant. In Study 2, the same indirect association was significant for IRT. Overall, these findings are consistent with the proposed theoretical model linking purpose in life with more autonomous, value-aligned academic motivation and adaptive academic outcomes during the transition to university.

items.title: Public evaluation of environmentalinformationdisclosure materials for waste-to-energy incineration facilities: Effects of information quantity and comprehensibility support.
items.abstract: Environmental information disclosure is an important governance tool for reducing controversy and improving communication during the siting and operation of waste-to-energy incineration facilities. Drawing on cognitive load theory, this study examines whether key design features of disclosure materials affect the public's evaluations of the quality of these materials. Using environmental impact assessment reports as representative disclosure materials, the study conducts a survey experiment with nearby residents (N = 577), develops five experimental versions that vary in information quantity and the presence of comprehensibility support, and tests the effects using one-way and two-way ANOVA. The results show significant differences in evaluations across information quantity conditions, with the medium quantity version receiving the highest ratings. Adding comprehensibility support significantly improves public evaluation, with a significant interaction between information quantity and comprehensibility support. These findings contribute to environmental psychology research by deepening our understanding of public responses to environmental information disclosure, while offering practical guidance for government agencies and project developers seeking to improve environmental information disclosure and risk communication.

items.title: Downstream effects of emotion regulation tactics and acceptance in younger and older adults.
items.abstract: Older adults report higher emotional wellbeing than younger adults and report using more emotion regulation tactics that approach positive elements of a stimulus and acceptance. However, it remains unclear what drives these age differences in regulation behaviour. Are particular regulation behaviours preferred due to their downstream consequences (i.e. their immediate affect and later memory for the eliciting stimulus)? Little prior work has examined the affective and cognitive outcomes of different emotion regulation tactics across age groups. In the present study, younger (N = 77; ages 18-25) and older adults (N = 62, ages 55+) viewed negative images while implementing Valence × Direction emotion regulation tactics (classified by approaching or avoiding positive/negative elements of a stimulus, yielding: positive-approaching, negative-approaching and negative-receding) and acceptance. Participants also reported their subjective valence and arousal after each regulation attempt. Afterwards, they completed an incidental memory task. Positive-approaching was associated with the most positive self-reported valence and lowest arousal. Negative-receding was associated with the poorest memory performance, whereas positive-approaching was associated with the best. Age group did not significantly interact with tactic type for affective or memory outcomes. Overall, these results suggest that some forms of emotion regulation may simultaneously support emotional wellbeing and information processing.

items.title: Men's Engagement in and Enjoyment of Sex Toy Use with Female Partners: Exploring Differences in Masculinity, Sexism, Male Genital Image, and Sexual Esteem.
items.abstract: Despite growing prevalence of partnered sex toy use, limited research has examined the psychological factors that shape men's engagement with and enjoyment of sex toys. The present study investigated whether conformity to masculine norms, precarious manhood beliefs, hostile and benevolent sexism, male genital self-image, and sexual esteem differentiate men who use sex toys with female partners from those who do not, and men who enjoy such use from those who do not. Male-identified participants (N = 828; Mage = 39.63; SDage = 15.29) who had ever had at least one female sexual partner completed an online survey. Multivariate and discriminant function analyses revealed that sex toy users demonstrated less conformity to masculine norms, fewer precarious manhood beliefs, lower sexism, and greater genital self-image and sexual esteem than non-users. Among users, enjoyers exhibited lower masculine conformity, precarious manhood beliefs, and sexism, alongside greater sexual esteem, compared to non-enjoyers; genital self-image did not differ significantly between groups. Hierarchical logistic regressions further indicated that sexual esteem - but not genital self-image - predicted use of phallic-style toys. Findings suggest that masculine ideology and traditional sexual scripts may pose meaningful barriers to partnered sex toy engagement among men who have sex with women, with possible implications for sexual health education.

items.title: Multivariate cortical thickness-cognition covariance supports the criterion validity of the Riga Cognitive Screening Task.
items.abstract: There is a predicted increase in the prevalence of older adults presenting with mild to severe cognitive impairment. Screening tools with high sensitivity are the first frontier in identifying a cognitive pathology; however, to ensure that they are measuring the intended concept or criterion, thorough psychometric procedures should be followed. In this study, concurrent criterion validity of Riga Cognitive Screening Task was measured, using cortical thickness of regions of interest as the criterion. 106 older adults (Mage = 70.49, SD = 8.08, 35.8% male) with varying levels of cognitive functioning were involved in the study. All participants underwent cognitive assessment with the screening task and a 3T MRI. Cortical thickness of selected temporal and parietal regions was used as a brain measure. Behavioural Partial Least Squares Correlation was conducted and one latent variable was extracted. The results confirmed that Riga Cognitive Screening Task shows good criterion validity, suggesting successful use for screening.

items.title: Genetic and Epigenetic Determinants of Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviors: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: A better understanding of the determinants of physical activity (PA) and sedentary behavior (SB) is needed to counter increasing inactivity. Twin and family studies indicate that these behaviors are shaped by biological factors, including genetic and epigenetic mechanisms. The number of genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and epigenome-wide association studies (EWAS) on PA and SB that try to elucidate these mechanisms has been increasing, motivating a review on whether their findings point to overlapping or distinct biological mechanisms. In this preregistered systematic review, we synthesize GWAS and EWAS findings on PA and SB and identify replicated loci across studies. We included nine GWAS reporting 414 unique lead SNPs and seven EWAS reporting 437 significant CpG sites associated with PA and/or SB. Across all findings, 51 genomic loci and 93 SNPs met our replication criteria, defined as support from at least two different GWAS or EWAS studies. Five genomic loci (1p36.23, 1p13.3, 1q21.3, 6p22.2, and 6p21.31) including six lead SNPs (rs301799, rs8450, rs4845364, rs2393593, rs10947452, and rs6457816), showed convergence between PA/SB-associated GWAS variants and mQTLs for PA/SB-associated CpG sites, highlighting candidate regions for future functional follow-up. Functional annotation indicated that these loci are mostly enriched in genic and transcript-associated regions. Gene mapping and enrichment analyses highlighted biological pathways across neurobiological systems involved in motivation and exercise liking, as well as peripheral systems related to movement, exercise capacity, energy metabolism, and cardiometabolic functioning. PA/SB-associated SNPs also overlapped with variants linked to body composition, cardiometabolic markers, educational attainment, cognitive ability, and brain-size traits. Overall, PA and SB appear to be influenced by a complex, highly polygenic architecture, with consistent genetic influences but limited convergence yet in epigenetic influences. Further large-scale, multi-ancestry studies integrating genomic and epigenomic data with harmonized PA/SB measures are needed to inform functional genetic studies.

items.title: Morally motivated crimes are less sensitive to punishment.
items.abstract: Modern western legal and criminal justice theories assume that punishment should deter criminalized behavior by introducing costs that reduce its expected utility, but, empirically, punishment often has weak effects on rates of crime and recidivism. Here, we hypothesize that when people are motivated to engage in criminalized behavior for moral reasons, they show diminished sensitivity to punishment. We demonstrate our hypothesis across 10 correlational, experimental, and economic game studies with participants drawn from the general population as well as participants with criminal backgrounds. Studies 1 to 3 draw on federal data of over 30,000 offenders and find that participants' estimates of moral motives for crime predict higher recidivism while estimates of material motives predict the opposite. Studies 4 to 8 use judgment studies and find that morally motivated crimes are less sensitive to punishment across a diversity of crime types, when motives are manipulated but actions are kept constant, persist for different types of consequences, and are unique to moral motivation. Studies 9 and 10 employ economic games and find that when players take money from others for moral reasons, they are less deterred by the imposition of fines. Implications for systems of punishment, offender psychology, and restorative justice approaches are discussed.

items.title: Immersive Virtual Nature to Promote Mental Health and Nature Connectedness in Youth: Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Mental health disorders are increasing among adolescents and young adults. While contact with real nature provides mental health benefits, access to natural environments is not always possible. Immersive virtual nature (IVN) represents a potential alternative to promote mental health and nature connectedness. This scoping review aims to map and synthesize how IVN has been used to promote mental health and nature connectedness among adolescents and young adults (<24 years). A systematic search was conducted across 6 databases (PubMed, Scopus, PsycINFO, Embase, Cochrane Library, and CINAHL) in November 2025 and updated in August 2026, supplemented by citation tracking and expert consultation. Inclusion criteria encompassed quantitative and qualitative studies examining IVN interventions with mental health and/or nature connectedness outcomes. Sixty-one studies were included (4630 participants). The majority involved young adults (n=55), almost all university students, while only 6 studies included adolescents. Overall, included studies reported improvements in mental health and nature connectedness outcomes following IVN. Single-session IVN studies (n=26) reported immediate improvements, multisession IVN interventions (n=11) reported short-term benefits, and environments characteristics comparisons (n=30) compared different virtual environments. This last category indicated that visual characteristics (brightness and vegetation density), auditory stimuli, and interactivity substantially influence outcomes. IVN shows promising potential to support mental health in youth populations. However, current evidence is limited by methodological heterogeneity, the predominance of laboratory-based single-session interventions, and the scarcity of research in adolescents. Future research should prioritize rigorous multisession interventions in younger and more clinically diverse populations, while also exploring personalization strategies based on environmental characteristics.

items.title: Medication Management Strategies for People with Multiple Long-Term Conditions Approaching End of Life: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Despite the challenges of managing medication for people with multiple long-term conditions approaching end of life, guidance remains limited. The review aim was to evaluate the effectiveness of medication management strategies in this population and identify research gaps. Eligible studies examined medication management strategies in adults ages ≥ 50 years with multiple long-term conditions approaching end of life. Studies focusing on a single condition, early-stage multimorbidity, or non-pharmacological palliative care interventions were excluded. MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, Scopus, and PsycINFO were searched from inception to September 2025. Study quality was assessed independently by two reviewers using recognized appraisal tools, with risk of bias rated as high, fair, or low. A narrative synthesis was conducted. From 14,945 records, six studies met inclusion criteria. All focused on deprescribing potentially inappropriate medications, with mixed effects on polypharmacy, regimen complexity, and clinical outcomes. The limited number of studies, all conducted in Europe, and the presence of high risk of bias in half of them, restrict generalizability. Findings suggest that deprescribing, supported by multidisciplinary and patient-centered approaches, is central to optimizing medication management at end of life in multimorbid populations. Further research is needed on broader strategies, including symptom control and anticipatory prescribing beyond deprescribing.

items.title: Who do children turn to for help regulating their emotions? Intrinsic interpersonal emotion regulation in late childhood.
items.abstract: Children often regulate their emotions with help from multiple people within their social networks, including parents, peers, and teachers. In late childhood, children are increasingly expected to take an active role in managing their emotions, making it important to understand how they seek interpersonal emotion regulation support. The present study examined who children turn to for emotion regulation support and whether the way this support is organized is linked to their emotion regulation strategies and emotional functioning. Participants included 180 children aged 9-12 years (M = 10.72, SD = 1.06; 57% female; 75% White) who nominated specific people they would turn to for help regulating sadness, nervousness, and excitement and reported characteristics of these relationships. Children also reported their use of cognitive reappraisal, expressive suppression, and generalized anxiety symptoms. Parents reported children's self-management skills. Children's emotion regulation support was organized primarily around family members and peers and embedded in close, long-standing relationships. Support across a wider range of emotions and reliance on different helpers for different emotion regulation goals were associated with greater cognitive reappraisal, even after accounting for the number and closeness of helpers. Greater relationship-type diversity was associated with lower parent-rated self-management. The organization of children's emotion regulation support was unrelated to expressive suppression and generalized anxiety symptoms. These findings provide an initial picture of children's interpersonal emotion regulation support across relationships in late childhood and suggest that some features may be relevant to specific aspects of children's emotion functioning. items.title: Remote delivery of problem management plus by nonclinicians for adults with psychological distress in New York City: A pilot feasibility study.
items.abstract: A single-arm trial was conducted to assess the feasibility, acceptability, and perceived utility of remotely delivered Problem Management Plus (PM+) in New York City. Two settings were used to evaluate these parameters: a graduate psychology training clinic and community-based organizations (CBOs) with staff without clinical training. Participants (N = 45) received five sessions of PM+ delivered via Zoom. Primary clinical outcomes were distress related to client-generated problems (Psychological Outcomes Profile), depression symptoms (Patient Health Questionnaire-9), and anxiety symptoms (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7) administered at baseline and 1 week postintervention. Semistructured interviews were conducted with a subsample of participants and providers. Twenty-four helpers were trained in PM+: 15 students from the university training clinic and nine staff from two CBOs. Twenty-seven clients received PM+ from graduate students, and 18 clients received PM+ from CBO staff. Most clients (92.6% university clinic, 88.9% CBOs) completed all five PM+ sessions. Change from baseline to end line showed a medium to large effect across primary outcome measures in both settings. Qualitative interviews further supported the feasibility and acceptability of remote PM+. Remotely delivered PM+ appears to be feasible, acceptable, and safe, which supports its potential to expand the mental health workforce. Additional research is warranted to evaluate the effectiveness of remotely delivered PM+. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: "Stifled" child psychology research in wartime China: I. Huang and the Experimental Nursery School at National Chekiang University, 1935-1944.
items.abstract: This article examines the Experimental Nursery School established by the Department of Education at National Chekiang University and later directed by the Chinese child psychologist I. Huang. It reconstructs the school's history from its founding in 1935 and wartime closure in 1937 through the continuation of related work in child psychology to 1944. Drawing on Huang's writings, institutional records, recollections by colleagues and students, and materials from Huang's bequest held by the Pan Shuh Library of the Institute of Psychology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, the article situates the Experimental Nursery School within the transnational circulation of the mental hygiene movement and the introduction of Arnold Gesell's Yale Guidance Nursery model into China. It argues that Huang did not simply reproduce the Yale model. Working through Chekiang University's Department of Education, he brought together naturalistic observation, child guidance, psychological research, case study, and the professional training of education students. The school consequently functioned as an early childhood education institution, a site for observing and studying children, and a practicum base for students. Huang's child-guidance work encouraged educators to move from moral judgment and disciplinary correction toward investigating the psychological causes of children's behavior and linked individual differences to individual guidance through sustained observation and case study. Although the school closed after the full-scale outbreak of the Second Sino-Japanese War, its research orientation continued in Huang's wartime research, teaching, and writing and later entered historical accounts of Chinese child psychology. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: From close noticing to structural competency: A guide to historical interpretation as a psychological humanities methodology.
items.abstract: Recent years have seen renewed interest in the psychological humanities as a means of studying human subjectivity and experience. What practicing the psychological humanities entails remains unclear. This article provides an introductory guide to one psychological humanities methodology: the craft of historical interpretation. The article opens by explaining the kinds of evidence on which psychologist-historians rely, where this documentation is typically found, and how the scholar can collect and process it. The article then describes three approaches to "close noticing" telling details that serve as potential interpretive clues. These approaches are drawn from literary criticism, historiography, and the analysis of material objects. These close noticing skills are also tied to certain epistemic virtues that help orient the researcher toward a truthful reading of texts and documents. Next, "thick description," the narrative form that some of the best contemporary social and cultural historians use to convey the results of their research, is described along with certain criteria used to evaluate the success of this mode of interpretation. Finally, the article addresses the ultimate aim of much historical research: the situating or contextualizing of phenomena within deep social and cultural structures. This interpretative gesture is related to the notion of cultivating "structural competency" as well as the end goals of other forms of psychological inquiry. items.title: The hangover of oppression: An ecological momentary assessment study of oppression-based stressors and daily alcohol use and hazardous drinking outcomes among sexual and gender minoritized young adults.
items.abstract: Sexual and gender minoritized (SGM) young adults are at greater risk for hazardous drinking and alcohol use disorder (AUD) than their heterosexual and cisgender counterparts. These inequities are often explained with oppression frameworks, which posit that oppression-based stressors (i.e., discrimination) contribute to hazardous drinking and the development of AUD. However, research examining the daily and within-person associations between oppression-based stressors and alcohol use among SGM young adults is nascent and equivocal. We conducted a 30-day ecological momentary assessment of daily within- and between-person oppression-based stressors and same-day alcohol use outcomes (i.e., alcohol use, quantity of drinks, heavy drinking, alcohol-related consequences, hangover symptoms) among 98 SGM young adults who engaged in heavy drinking (71.4% met criteria for AUD). We also examined multiple person-level moderators (e.g., sociodemographics, addiction severity, stress exposure and sensitivity) to identify for whom oppression-based stressors confer risk for hazardous drinking. Results indicated that on days participants experienced more oppression-based stressors than their average, they reported greater odds of daily heavy drinking. Participants who experienced greater oppression-based stressors overall reported more daily negative and positive alcohol-related consequences and hangovers. The within-person associations between oppression-based stressors and some of the hazardous drinking outcomes were moderated by AUD symptoms, a family history of alcohol problems, greater lifetime exposure to cisheterosexism, and identification as plurisexual (e.g., bisexual). Our findings provide support for oppression and addiction frameworks and further highlight risks that plurisexual young adults experience. The results underscore the need to target oppression to reduce hazardous drinking among SGM young adults. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

items.title: Association Between Nutritional Supplements Use During Pregnancy and Postpartum Depressive Symptoms Among Jordanian Women: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Postpartum depression is a common mental health condition affecting women during the postpartum period and represents a significant public health concern. Maternal nutritional status during pregnancy, including the use of dietary supplements has been proposed as a potentially modifiable factor associated with postpartum mental health outcomes. However, the evidence from Middle Eastern populations and Jordan mainly remains limited. To examine the association between nutritional supplement use during pregnancy and postpartum depressive symptoms among Jordanian women. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among Jordanian postpartum women. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire covering sociodemographic, obstetric, psychosocial, and nutritional characteristics, alongside the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) to assess depressive symptoms. Appropriate statistical analyses were used to evaluate associations between supplements use, reported nutritional deficiencies, and postpartum depressive symptoms. A significant proportion of participants exhibited postpartum depressive symptoms (44.3%). No statistically significant associations were found between postpartum depressive symptoms and the most commonly used prenatal supplements. In contrast, vitamin D and zinc deficiencies were significantly more prevalent among women experiencing postpartum depressive symptoms. Furthermore, zinc and magnesium supplementation during pregnancy was associated with lower scores on the Postpartum Depression Scale (EPDS). Poor family support and obesity were also significantly associated with higher depressive symptom scores. Postpartum depression was common among this group and was associated with specific nutritional deficiencies, the use of certain supplements, and psychosocial factors. These findings emphasize the need for an integrated approach to maternal mental health that considers both nutritional status and social support and highlight the importance of further research in similar settings.

items.title: Extrachromosomal circular DNA in human cancer: from biogenesis mechanisms to therapeutic vulnerabilities.
items.abstract: Extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA) is an essential type of circular DNA that is mainly characterized by independence from chromosomes and a broad size distribution. Increasing evidence suggests that the distinctive genomic distribution of eccDNA establishes it as a clinical biomarker. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying its biogenesis and function in tumorigenesis have not been fully elucidated. Thus, in this review, we summarize the emerging insights into the biogenesis mechanisms of eccDNA, with particular emphasis on the recently described single-strand break driven internal loop (i-loop) model. We also discuss its critical roles in oncogenesis, including oncogene amplification, tumor heterogeneity, cell death, tumor immunity and drug resistance. We further outline current detection methods for eccDNA and evaluate its potential as a promising diagnostic, prognostic and predictive biomarker for human cancers, as well as a therapeutic vulnerability with implications for chemotherapy, radiotherapy, immunotherapy and nanotherapy.

items.title: Parental leave benefits and fathers' postpartum mental health in Sweden.
items.abstract: Mental health conditions in the postpartum period are common. Generous parental leave has been shown to protect against poorer postpartum mental health among mothers; however, evidence for fathers remains limited. We examine whether levels of paid parental leave benefits are associated with fathers' mental health in the first year after childbirth in Sweden. Using national population registers, we include 210,285 first-time fathers whose children were born between 2007 and 2011. Fathers receiving basic benefits have higher odds of receiving any mental healthcare, being prescribed antidepressants or anxiolytics, and using specialist outpatient care than those receiving higher-level earnings-related benefits. The results are robust after adjusting for mental health history, income and employment status, though associations are attenuated. Fathers who do not take parental leave during the first year are more likely to receive any mental healthcare, specialist outpatient care or hospitalisation. Overall, fathers with access to more generous paid parental leave benefits experience better postpartum mental health. These findings suggest that well-compensated parental leave may benefit fathers' mental health and promote gender equality in caregiving. However, further efforts are needed to determine whether parental leave systems mitigate or reproduce health inequalities given that parental leave benefit levels are contingent on labour market conditions.

items.title: Intravaginal tobacco use among women in The Gambia: A qualitative study on the motivators, dependence and health risks.
items.abstract: Intravaginal insertion of smokeless tobacco (taba) is an emerging, little-researched method of tobacco use practiced in several countries in sub-Saharan Africa. This study aimed to characterise patterns of intravaginal taba use and the motivations, perceived benefits, adverse effects and dependence associated with this practice among women in The Gambia and examined whether this practice represents an unrecognised nicotine exposure pathway. Qualitative study using in-depth semi-structured interviews with current and former users of taba recruited through the Medical Research Council Unit The Gambia Pregnancy Care Integrating Translational Science Everywhere (PRECISE) and Mothers Health Foundation databases and supplemented by snowball sampling. Data were analysed thematically. Urban and rural communities across four health regions of The Gambia. Forty-two women aged 18-49 years who were current (n = 31) or former (n = 11) users of taba, recruited through community networks and health research programmes. Interviews explored initiation, patterns of use, composition and preparation of taba, perceived benefits and harms, risk perceptions and indicators of dependence. We translated, transcribed and analysed the data using a deductive-inductive thematic approach. Women commonly initiated taba use for perceived therapeutic purposes, particularly treatment of vaginal infections, pain and reproductive health concerns. Social networks strongly influenced initiation, and early adverse physiological reactions, such as burning, vomiting and dizziness, were frequently normalised as evidence of effectiveness. Its continued use was reinforced by perceived sexual, health and emotional benefits, including vaginal tightening, enhanced pleasure and relief from loneliness or unmet sexual needs. Participants indicated that products often contain potentially toxic additives (caustic soda, ashes, battery acid). Many reported symptoms consistent with nicotine toxicity and described progression to habitual use, characterised by cravings, withdrawal symptoms and difficulty quitting despite recognised harms, including suspected cancer and reproductive complications. Secrecy and stigma surrounding use were common. In The Gambia, intravaginal smokeless tobacco (taba) use appears to be initiated for perceived therapeutic and sexual health benefits, but users report experiences consistent with nicotine dependence and exposure to harmful additives in taba products, highlighting a previously unrecognised form of tobacco exposure among women.

items.title: Variations in Scheduled Non-Lunch Recess and Withholding: Preliminary Findings from the U.S. Education and Physical Activity Policy Study Physical.
items.abstract: Recess provides a critical school-based venue for student physical activity. However, recess provision and withholding practices remain inconsistently documented. This exploratory study described variability in daily scheduled non-lunch recess minutes, and recess withholding practices among U.S. elementary schools participating in a national physical education teacher questionnaire. This cross-sectional exploratory study used schoolyear 2022-2024 data from the U.S. Physical Education and Physical Activity Policy (US-PEPAP) questionnaire. Physical education teachers reported frequency and duration of scheduled non-lunch recess and whether their school withheld recess. After exclusions for ineligible settings, incomplete data, and multiple same-school responses, the analytic sample included 1,416 elementary, K-8, or K-12 schools across 51 jurisdictions (50 states, plus Washington D.C.). An exploratory composite recess practice score (range: 0-3) was constructed based on provision of the recommended at least 20-minutes/day of recess and whether recess was withheld. Unweighted school-level summaries were calculated overall and by jurisdiction. Mean scheduled non-lunch recess was 16.21-minutes/day (SD=8.84). The mean exploratory composite recess practice score was 1.24 (SD=1.13). Among participating schools, 230 (16.2%) reported the recommended 20-minutes/day and did not withhold, while 421 (29.7%) schools provided recommended 20-minutes/day, but practiced withholding. A total of 221 (15.6%) reported less than 20-minutes/day without withholding, and 544 (38.4%) reported less than the recommended 20-minutes/day and practiced withholding. Scheduled non-lunch recess and withholding varied among participating schools. These preliminary findings provide a current overview of school practices across the nation, and indicate a need for follow-up studies using representative sampling techniques to assess jurisdiction estimates.

items.title: Early Life Interventions in IgE-mediated Food Allergy Prevention and Management.
items.abstract: Food allergy has become a major public health concern. Over the past decade, advances in understanding early immune development have transformed approaches to both prevention and treatment of IgE-mediated food allergy. Landmark trials demonstrated that early and sustained introduction of allergenic foods, particularly peanut and egg, significantly reduces the risk of food allergy. This lead to a paradigm shift from allergen avoidance to proactive early introduction. For children who develop food allergy, emerging evidence indicates that early intervention may offer unique advantages, possibly due to heightened immune plasticity. Oral, epicutaneous, and sublingual immunotherapy have shown efficacy in increasing allergen tolerance, with studies suggesting improved outcomes and greater likelihood of remission when initiated in early childhood. Mechanistic studies indicate that these therapies modify allergic immune responses through suppression of effector cells, induction of regulatory pathways, and increased production of protective allergen-specific antibodies. In addition, omalizumab has become the first biologic approved in the United States for food allergy in individuals aged ≥1 year. Despite substantial progress, important knowledge gaps remain. Continued integration of mechanistic discoveries, clinical trials, and real-world evidence will be essential to refine precision approaches that maximize prevention, improve treatment outcomes, and reduce the lifelong burden of food allergy.
