items.title: Soft Mixture of Quantum Experts for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Learning
items.abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has attracted increasing interest as a possible route to construct feature representations that are difficult to reproduce with classical models. However, near-term QML architectures based on trainable parametrized quantum circuits remain affected by limited hardware resources, noise, and severe optimization difficulties such as barren plateaus. In this work we propose Soft-MoQE, a Soft Mixture of Quantum Experts architecture that replaces variational quantum training with the input-dependent selection and combination of fixed quantum feature maps. The model is composed of a heterogeneous pool of non-trainable quantum circuits, each defining a distinct embedding, and a classical gating network that learns how to weight these embeddings for each data point. We benchmark Soft-MoQE on three PCA-reduced tasks: MNIST parity, MNIST 10-class, and FashionMNIST. Soft-MoQE outperforms the single best expert, the uniform average of all experts and a linear baseline, achieving task-dependent performance comparable to that of a trainable quantum neural network, without optimizing any quantum parameter and with a quantum training cost that is lower by orders of magnitude. The analysis of the class- conditioned expert usage shows that the learned routing combines a few experts for each input, with a selection that depends on the class. These results support the learned routing among fixed quantum circuits as a trainability-aware design principle for hybrid QML.

items.title: Towards Transparent Computational Agents for Air Traffic Control: Explainability, Interpretability and Trust
items.abstract: We report preliminary findings from an ongoing investigation into transparency techniques for computational Air Traffic Control agents. Air Traffic Controller Officers (ATCOs) observed two types of agent in simulated air traffic controlling exercises. ATCOs found the chosen transparency techniques helpful to some extent: revealing how agents were making controlling decisions was an essential foundation for trust. However, the ATCOs' trust depended on whether they could be made sense of in a live, operational context and the agents' actions where judged to be professionally competent.

items.title: Interpersonal trust, institutional trust and trust in technology in Air Traffic Control
items.abstract: Air traffic control (ATC), the safe, orderly and efficient management of planes through controlled airspace is a complex task. In this article, we explore the roles that different kinds of trust play in ATC. Our study provides the essential foundations for examining the conditions that need to be satisfied if Air Traffic Controllers are to establish and sustain trust relationships with technical innovations, such as agent-based systems, and so ensure their safe and dependable embedding within ATC work.

items.title: Negotiating Control and Accountability among Stakeholders in High-Risk AI Use Cases: Development and Evaluation of the Method ALIGN
items.abstract: Characteristics of Artificial Intelligence (AI) severely restrict human control. This creates new challenges for socio-technical systems design especially in safety-critical domains, where control over risks is essential along with the accountability for any harm caused. Drawing from human factors and AI governance literature, expert interviews and participant observation in a complex high-risk AI use case from the railways, we developed ALIGN, a scenario-based method that supports the governance of and stakeholder involvement in AI development and implementation in three ways: raising awareness for potential accountability-control misalignments in socio-technical systems and their negative consequences, offering a structured approach to assessing the alignment between accountability and control for stakeholders in a given use case, and supporting effective design decisions to mitigate AI risks. We describe the iterative development and evaluation of ALIGN and discuss how this method promotes AI governance by highlighting the relevance of control-accountability alignment throughout the AI life cycle.

items.title: Inferring Neural Activity Changes under Recording Uncertainty with Transformers and Variational Inference
items.abstract: A difference in recorded firing rate across days may reflect a change in neuronal activity, missed spikes or recording a different neuron. We present a statistical approach that combines neuron tracking with Bayesian estimates of stationary mean recorded firing rates. Bounds under assumed differences in spike detection connect recorded rates to biological rate changes. We assess recording loss and uncertainty in rate changes in simulations, and count-model fit in recordings. We also compare two transformer estimators with Gaussian and flow variational inference under a shared temporal negative-binomial model. Flow variational inference agrees most closely with reference posteriors, while predictive performance varies across mice. Rate-change intervals contain true simulated changes less often than intended. In UnitMatch recordings from five mice, some inferred changes remain supported when spike detection is allowed to differ between days; others depend on equal detection. These interpretations require a correct neuron match. The approach identifies which inferred rate changes remain supported under specified recording assumptions and where uncertainty limits interpretation.

items.title: A structure-based model of the bacterial chemosensory array reveals how the scaffolding protein CheW tunes sensory responses
items.abstract: We introduce a structure-based Ising model of the bacterial chemosensory array to investigate how the scaffolding protein CheW tunes signaling responses. The model couples the activity states of core signaling units and of CheW subunits within hexameric rings on a lattice with the structure observed in cryoEM experiments. Recent experiments show that increasing CheW participation in hexameric rings raises response cooperativity in non-adapting cells and sensitivity in adaptation-proficient cells. Our lattice model quantitatively reproduces both effects, while mean-field theory shows that CheW increases the effective coupling between core units, sharpening the response in both cell types. The statistics of CheW placement (complete hexameric rings versus random distribution) substantially alter how responses vary with CheW abundance. Moreover, different coupling strengths can yield the same static response yet markedly different activity fluctuations and dynamics. CheW abundance further controls a crossover from relaxational to oscillatory fluctuations, whose location depends on the spatial distribution of CheW. These dynamical signatures, including oscillations predicted near native CheW levels, are testable by single-cell dynamics measurements. Combined with CheW titration and our modeling results, these measurements can probe the array's assembly dynamics and allosteric couplings. Beyond the chemosensory array, our approach can generalize to other large protein complexes, providing a framework to study the functional role of scaffolding proteins and allosteric interfaces in signal processing.

items.title: A Dual-SOM Learner Model of Instructional Efficiency within Cognitive Load Theory
items.abstract: This paper presents a novel methodological framework, integrating a dual self-organising map (SOM) neural network architecture with Cognitive Load Theory (CLT), for assessing instructional efficiency within learning environments. By representing curriculum content as a directed acyclic graph of topic dependencies, the proposed model captures collective learning behaviour across two core dimensions: academic performance and subjective/introspective mental effort. During SOM training, representative data sets of successful learner trajectories are compressed into two topologically ordered, identically structured neural networks: PSOM (performance space) and ESOM (mental effort space). By pairing these behavioural maps, the model serves as a decision-support tool that enables instructors to simultaneously pinpoint structural instructional design defects, such as hidden topic prerequisites, and evaluate collective cognitive load profiles. The implementation and performance of the PSOM component (and, by extension, its symmetrical twin, ESOM) is linked to an earlier modelling study employing a SOM with identical structure and encoding semantics situated in the same domain (i.e., a learning environment). This paper combines the study of behavioural phenomena with theoretical work on human cognitive architecture via SOM neurocomputational cognitive behavioural modelling.

items.title: Discovery of a Massive Outer Companion to the TOI-178 Resonant Chain
items.abstract: We report the discovery of a massive outer companion around TOI-178, a known planetary system with six inner small planets within 0.15 AU, five of which are in a 2:4:6:9:12 resonant chain. We analyse the astrometric anomalies in the combined Gaia DR2/DR3 - Hipparcos catalogue (G23H) and literature radial velocities, revealing strong evidence for a massive outer companion at several AU. We combine the resulting orbital fit posterior with archival high-contrast imaging to constrain the properties of the corresponding massive outer companion, TOI-178 h. We also study the dynamical stability of the inner resonant chain in the presence of this previously unknown outer companion via both heuristic and N-body simulations. We find that the inner system appears to be robust to the perturbing influence of TOI-178\,h, in line with the systems several Gyr age. Our analysis results in a final posterior solution for TOI-178\,h with a semi-major axis of $6.9^{+12.3}_{-3.3}$ AU, a mass of $21^{+47}_{-11} M_J$, and eccentricity of $0.76^{+0.18}_{-0.35}$, likely corresponding to an eccentric brown dwarf. TOI-178 is currently the only known system that has maintained a high-multiplicity resonant chain whilst in the dynamical presence of a massive outer companion, showcasing a unique outcome of planet formation.

items.title: A Homogeneous Benchmark of Exoplanet Mass-Radius Relations
items.abstract: The mass-radius ($M$-$R$) relation is fundamental to inferring the bulk composition and internal structure of exoplanets. However, published relations remain difficult to compare directly because studies adopt different planetary samples, fitting procedures, and evaluation metrics. We construct a homogeneous, quality-controlled benchmark of 963 exoplanets with dynamically measured masses and transit radii from the NASA Exoplanet Archive. We compare empirical power laws, probabilistic models, and machine-learning (ML) regressors using point accuracy, interval coverage, and probabilistic calibration. On the full test set, a multi-feature random forest has the lowest root-mean-square error, 0.329~dex in $\log_{10} M$ versus 0.368~dex for a fitted two-parameter power law ($p = 0.007$ unadjusted; $p = 0.059$ after Holm correction across 13 comparisons). Radius-only ML models perform comparably to the single power law. In three ranges of the measured radius, several methods improve on the power law below 1.6 $R_\oplus$, but none does between 1.6 and 4 $R_\oplus$. Including stellar and orbital covariates significantly improves predictions only for low-mass planets ($M < 4.4\,M_\oplus$), although this result is sensitive to missing covariate data and weakens when the training and test sets are separated by host star. Within their calibrated radius domains, the published empirical and probabilistic relations remain highly competitive. Finally, a first-order variance decomposition shows that formal measurement uncertainties account for only $\sim$3\% of the residual variance (0.067 of 0.401~dex), and the remaining $\sim$0.396~dex arises from compositional diversity, selection effects, and model approximation error.

items.title: Potential spectral markers of intrinsic magnetic fields of hot exoplanets in the UV range
items.abstract: A method for detecting the intrinsic magnetic fields of exoplanets, based on the effect of atomic alignment (the redistribution of populations among magnetic sublevels under the action of anisotropic radiation from the host star), has been adapted for observations with the Spektr-UV space telescope. A procedure for selecting sensitive transitions is proposed, and triplet absorption lines in the UV range that are sensitive to alignment are identified. On the basis of three-dimensional aeronomic models of the hot Jupiters KELT-20 b and HAT-P-32 b, absorption spectra in these lines are calculated for cases with and without intrinsic magnetic fields of the exoplanets. Using the Spektr-UV exposure-time calculator, the observability of the effect is assessed, and an observing program is proposed, specifying the optimal duration of individual exposures and the number of transits required to detect the signal.

items.title: Polycentrality in Urban Socioecological Systems: A Multilayer Analysis of Social Infrastructure in Iztapalapa, Mexico City
items.abstract: The spatial distribution of infrastructure and activities, along with the networks and interactions that connect them, is key to understanding the relationship between urban form, function, and sustainability from a complex systems perspective. Within this dynamic relationship, the extent to which localized social infrastructure can reinforce existing functional centralities or create conditions for the emergence of new ones remains insufficiently understood. This study examines these relationships through the UTOPÍAS program in Iztapalapa, Mexico City, where 15 public social facilities have been established across a historically underserved urban territory. We develop a multilayer network framework integrating pedestrian infrastructure, GTFS-based public transport services, and UTOPÍAS as a target layer to assess multimodal connectivity, travel-time accessibility, and spatial coverage. These conditions are examined alongside indicators of local economic centrality (PCI and wPCI) to investigate how infrastructure interdependencies relate to the functional organization of urban space. The analysis reveals spatial heterogeneity in multimodal accessibility and differences in the integration of UTOPÍAS with existing transport networks. By relating these patterns to pre-existing economic centralities, we examine whether distributed social infrastructure may reinforce established functional centers or create conditions favorable to emerging centralities, without assuming that spatial decentralization necessarily produces polycentrality. The findings contribute a relational, data-driven approach to understanding how social infrastructure and mobility shape urban functions, emphasizing accessibility and territorial integration as critical conditions for more equitable and sustainable urban development.

items.title: The Structural Number of Parties: An Electoral-Outcome-Independent Baseline for Comparing Party-System Scale
items.abstract: How many parties can a country structurally sustain? Standard measures such as the effective number of parties (ENP) cannot answer this question. They are descriptive and post hoc: they summarize competition only after an election, and they depend on electoral returns that are often missing, interrupted, or unreliable in many developing democracies, particularly in Africa. They also offer no common scale for comparing the size of party registers with realized electoral fragmentation. We introduce the Structural Number of Parties (SNP), an outcome-independent baseline derived from two universally available quantities: population size and territorial area. Building on the logic of the seat product model and the cube-root law of assembly size, the SNP gives an ex ante benchmark that can be computed for any country and year, including where electoral data are absent. Applied to African states, the SNP enables a structural gap diagnosis that distinguishes under-fragmented systems, marked by hegemonic-party dominance, from over-fragmented ones, marked by excessive atomization. The framework thus provides a transparent and reproducible tool to inform institutional reform and the rationalization of party systems across the continent.

items.title: Modelling population distribution across cities on spatial networks using the kinetic theory of multi-agent systems
items.abstract: We investigate the urban population distribution of the Italian region of Sardinia through the kinetic theory of multi-agent systems on spatial networks, interpreting cities both as agents and vertices of a graph, and representing interurban links as edges. We consider various emigration rules to model the interactions between agents, obtaining two main results: the bimodal lognormal fit of the total population distribution among cities and the Pareto fit of the tail. Overall, our model provides results consistent with the actual distribution derived from ISTAT data of Sardinia; furthermore, the bimodal lognormal fit generally follows the distribution tail more accurately than the Pareto one, although the two coincide in the first half.

items.title: Thermodynamics of gas giants accreting via shocks: the role of molecular hydrogen dissociation
items.abstract: Within the core-accretion framework, gas giants acquire most of their mass through accretion shocks during runaway gas accretion. The shock thermodynamics---governed by radiative cooling, accretion history, and equation of state (EoS)---sets the post-shock gas entropy and initial thermal state, strongly influencing both observables and subsequent evolution. We aim to build a coupled evolutionary model predicting the initial thermodynamic conditions, intrinsic luminosities, and upper limits on magnetic field strengths of gas giants across diverse accretion histories. We couple radiation hydrodynamics and $\mathrm{H_2}$ dissociation to long-term planetary interior evolution by training a physics-informed neural network (PINN) predictor on 1000 first-principles simulations resolving the shock physics. This PINN provides post-shock outer boundary conditions for MESA to evolve the planetary envelope beyond runaway accretion. The PINN predicts higher post-shock temperatures than the canonical cold-start model, with the discrepancy widening with planetary mass, while post-shock entropy jumps sharply when $\mathrm{H_2}$ dissociates at $\sim 2000$ K. Gas giants evolved with PINN-derived boundary conditions achieve intrinsic luminosities 4--10 times higher than cold-start models. Under optimistic assumptions, the maximum magnetic field strength at $2 R_{\mathrm{J}}$ reaches a few gauss for a $0.3 M_{\mathrm{J}}$ planet, $\sim 100$ G for $1 M_{\mathrm{J}}$, and $\sim 500$ G for $3 M_{\mathrm{J}}$. Incorporating detailed radiation hydrodynamics and realistic thermodynamics into accretion shock models yields higher initial entropies, brighter intrinsic luminosities, and stronger magnetic fields, providing improved constraints on the masses and accretion rates of directly imaged exoplanets.

items.title: Analytical formulae for planet-planet or moon-moon tides
items.abstract: Almost negligible among the solar system planets, mutual tides raised by a secondary on another secondary orbiting the same primary may gain increased importance in tightly packed systems, e.g., between the components of close-in exoplanetary systems or between the moons of gas giants. In this work, we derive an analytical formula for the planet-planet tidal potential and for the effect of mutual tides on the rotational and orbital evolution of moons or planets in a coplanar configuration. The procedure follows closely the steps of W. M. Kaula (1961), and the resulting potential and derived quantities are presented in the form of an expansion into modes of different frequencies (in the temporal domain) and spherical harmonic components (in the spatial domain). The analytical formulae are implemented into a code and compared with an independent numerical solution.

items.title: Asgard/NOTT: L-band nulling interferometry at the VLTI IV. Prospects for characterising hot exozodiacal dust
items.abstract: Near-infrared interferometric surveys have revealed extended emission around the photosphere of $\approx 40$ main-sequence stars, attributed to the presence of hot exozodiacal dust (HEZD). A promising technique for investigating this phenomenon is nulling interferometry. The Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) nulling interferometer NOTT (Nulling Observations of exoplaneTs and dusT) is designed to characterise exoplanets and HEZD in the $L'$ band ($3.5-4.0\,μ$m). We aim to assess NOTT's potential for the detection and characterisation of HEZD with various instrumental and model parameter configurations. We model the HEZD as an optically thin dust ring, using the nearby Sun-like star $τ$ Ceti with HEZD as a reference model. Applying the end-to-end nulling tool SCIFYsim to model the instrumental response of NOTT to simulated HEZD brightness distributions, we evaluate how variations in HEZD and instrumental parameters affect NOTT's key observables: the photon flux rate and the null depth. We demonstrate that NOTT is capable of disentangling stellar and dust contributions to the signal and detecting HEZD. The null depth and photon flux rate are sensitive to the HEZD geometry, with inclination, position angle, and ring location having the strongest impact on the signal. Although the detailed temporal signatures are target-specific, the results can be generalised to other systems. NOTT has the potential to deliver unprecedented sensitivity for HEZD observations, granting access to detailed information through spectral dispersion, beam-combination schemes, and exploitation of sky rotation. This enables more sensitive HEZD detections than is possible with current instruments, and improved spatial constraints on the dust, as well as variability studies.

items.title: Localized active phase in the coevolving voter model with fixed links
items.abstract: The coevolving voter model (CVM) describes the evolution of node states and network topology through copying and rewiring dynamics. It traditionally assumes that all ties can be rewired, overlooking unbreakable real-world relationships like family or close friendships. To address this, we introduce fixed links that cannot be rewired and study how these structural constraints modify the collective dynamics of the CVM. In addition to the active and frozen phases of the CVM, we find a new localized active phase in which activity is sustained, beyond a percolation transition, by a giant component of fixed links. The existence of this new phase is predicted by a moment-closure approximation that goes beyond the standard pair approximation. The finite-size manifestation of this phase is an asymmetric fragmented phase. In addition, the active-frozen transition of the CVM, manifested as a fragmentation transition for finite systems, is delayed by the existence of fixed links to larger values of the rewiring rate.

items.title: MAIC-2 v2.3: A Fortran program for simulating the surface temperature, atmospheric water transport and surface glaciation of the planet Mars
items.abstract: The Mars Atmosphere-Ice Coupler MAIC-2 is a computationally efficient, zonally-averaged model designed to simulate Martian surface temperature, atmospheric water transport and surface glaciation over timescales of 10^5 to 10^7 years. While sophisticated General Circulation Models (GCMs) provide high-resolution simulations of the Martian atmosphere, their high computational cost makes them largely unsuitable for studies covering millions of years of orbital evolution. MAIC-2 addresses this gap by utilizing physically-based, zonally-averaged parameterizations, including a Local Insolation Temperature (LIT) scheme and a mass balance engine driven by free-convection and instantaneous mixing physics. Version 2.3 introduces a fully modularized Fortran architecture that improves maintainability and ensures that the software remains entirely self-contained, requiring no external numerical libraries or specialized data formats for execution. Demonstrated through a 20-million-year transient simulation, the model successfully reproduces the primary characteristics of the Martian polar layered deposits. MAIC-2 provides the planetary science community with a versatile, open-source tool for investigating the long-term climatic impacts of orbital variations on the Martian surface.

items.title: LUC3D: Multi-animal 3D pose tracking in the browser
items.abstract: Animal behavior unfolds in three dimensions over time, yet accessible scientific tools for analyzing it in its natural form remain limited. Uncertainty from popular 2D pose methods can be refined with multi-camera approaches to produce more accurate 3D estimates. This paper presents LUC3D (Label Unification and Correspondence in 3D Annotation GUI), a browser-based 3D GUI for reducing the amount of manual labor required for labeling, proofreading, and multi-camera multi-animal tracking while requiring no installation to maximize accessibility. As proof-of-concept we present two datasets of proofread multi-camera 3D triangulated pose data of mouse social behavior, a protocol for generating 3D consistent labels, and a cross-view re-identification tracking algorithm for multi-animal multi-camera pose data. This tool allows for the widespread adoption of 3D pose estimation techniques for studying social behavior while reducing the cost of entry for neuroscience labs across the world.

items.title: Spectral and complexity-based signatures of advanced concentration absorption meditation: A high-density EEG study of jhana
items.abstract: Advanced meditation provides structured and reproducible alterations of consciousness that are increasingly used as model states for the neuroscience of consciousness. Jhana-type advanced concentration absorption meditation (ACAM-J) consists of eight progressively deepening absorption states (ACAM-J1-8) in which sensory and self-referential content gradually attenuate. We applied high-density EEG and a comprehensive multidimensional battery of spectral and complexity measures to characterize each ACAM-J state individually in 20 advanced meditators, together with phenomenological ratings. ACAM-J produced widespread posterior-central reductions in oscillatory and aperiodic power, posterior aperiodic flattening across all eight states, and convergent increases in entropy-based complexity over the posterior cortex, with power effects strengthening with phenomenological depth. Crucially, neural complexity remained elevated even in the late, most minimal and unified states, in opposition to the prevailing account that links higher neural entropy to richer phenomenal content. Between practitioners, lower power and higher entropy accompanied more visual and auditory but less bodily content, a redistribution rather than an enrichment of experience; within practitioners, only reduced low-frequency power tracked wider attention and less narrative thought. ACAM-J thus emerges as a non-pharmacological model state at the high-complexity end of the spectrum of altered consciousness, and reveals a previously unquantified dissociation between neural complexity and experiential richness for specific ACAM-J states.

items.title: Perceptual glimpses are locally accumulated and globally maintained at distinct processing levels.
items.abstract: Making decisions often requires the integration of multiple pieces of information. An extensive body of research has investigated the neural architecture underpinning evidence accumulation in perceptual tasks where information is continuously present, but less is known about how this neural architecture operates in situations affording only intermittent glimpses of an evidence source. In two electroencephalography experiments, human participants judged the direction of up to two pulses of motion evidence separated by gaps of varying duration. Our behavioural analysis found that participants used both pulses but underutilised the second and showed no systematic decrease in accuracy as a function of gap duration. At the neural level, motor beta lateralisation tracked cumulative evidence across pulses, maintaining a sustained representation of the decision variable through the gap and until response. In contrast, the centroparietal positivity (CPP), a previously characterised signature of evidence accumulation, built up transiently to a peak that scaled with each pulse's contribution to the decision variable (i.e. the absolute belief update it produced), falling back to baseline in between pulses. These patterns were recapitulated in a model where pulse-information transiently integrated at the CPP level is fed to and maintained at a bounded motor level. In this model, the evidence in the second pulse is only integrated to the extent that the evidence in the first pulse falls short of the bound, or not integrated at all if a bound has already been hit.

items.title: Silent Teachers in Anatomical Education: A Historical Review of Paradigm Shifts in Human Cadaver Procurement Since Ancient Persia.
items.abstract: Human cadaveric dissection has played an important role in the development of anatomical knowledge and remains an established component of medical education. The availability of human bodies for anatomical study has varied across historical periods, reflecting changes in educational institutions, procurement practices, and ethical and sociocultural considerations. This narrative review examines the historical development of human dissection and cadaver procurement, with particular emphasis on Iran. Relevant literature was identified through searches of MEDLINE via PubMed and supplemented by historical publications, scholarly sources, locally sourced literature and contextual information, reference-list screening, and citation tracking. The literature was synthesized chronologically and thematically to examine the development of anatomical knowledge, the emergence of modern anatomy education in Iran, and reported changes in cadaver procurement practices. The historical literature documents a long tradition of medical scholarship and anatomical knowledge in Iran, followed by the gradual development of formal anatomy education through modern medical institutions. Reported sources of cadavers for anatomical education in Iran have included unclaimed bodies, imported cadavers, and voluntary body donation. However, the available evidence is insufficient to establish a comprehensive chronology of these practices or to determine their relative contributions across institutions and historical periods. The increasing recognition of voluntary body donation represents an important development in contemporary anatomical education, alongside continuing ethical and sociocultural considerations concerning informed consent, respect for human remains, and public acceptance. Cadaveric dissection continues to be used alongside alternative teaching approaches, including anatomical models and digital technologies. The historical development of cadaver procurement in Iran reflects broader changes in anatomical education and institutional practice. Further research based on historical records and institutional documentation is needed to clarify the chronology of procurement practices and their implications for contemporary anatomical education and ethical governance.

items.title: Aortic stiffness and brain perfusion: a population-based study.
items.abstract: ObjectivesThe objective was to examine the association of aortic stiffness and age with brain perfusion, brain structure, and cognitive function in a population-based sample.DesignThe sample included randomly selected descendants from a large community study. Aortic stiffness was assessed using carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (CFPWV) measured by applanation tonometry. Brain perfusion and structural brain measures were obtained using magnetic resonance imaging, and cognitive performance was evaluated using standardized neuropsychological tests. Participants were stratified by the median CFPWV ( ≤ or >8.6 m/s) for comparison and associations were examined in multivariable regression analyses adjusted for age, sex, heart rate, mean arterial pressure, use of antihypertensive medication and CFPWV.ResultsThe study included 269 subjects, average age 62 years. Participants with higher aortic stiffness (>8.6 m/s) were older, had higher heart rate, blood pressure, and more frequently used antihypertensive medication. Total brain, grey matter, and white matter perfusion were significantly lower in those with higher aortic stiffness. Relative brain volume was lower, and white matter hyperintensity (WMH) burden higher in unadjusted analyses, whereas cognitive performance did not differ. In multivariable models, increased aortic stiffness was independently associated with lower total brain perfusion, while chronological age was independently associated with lower brain volumes and greater WMH burden.ConclusionsThese findings indicate that aortic stiffness and aging represent related but distinct contributors to brain health. Aortic stiffness was independently associated with reduced brain perfusion, whereas age was the dominant determinant of structural brain changes.

items.title: Imaging fast neural circuit activity in brain and nerve with electrical impedance tomography (fnEIT): review, method and engineering aspects.
items.abstract: Fast neural electrical impedance tomography (fnEIT) is a technique for imaging neural activity in the brain or nerves, with a resolution of milliseconds and millimetres, using a probing applied current and boundary or depth voltage measurement. Proof of principle has been demonstrated in animal studies, but it is yet to be adopted into common use. Objective. The purpose of this review is to provide an introduction and overview of the method and technical aspects of fnEIT research and its place in the biomedical sciences. Topics covered include the bioimpedance of action potentials, fnEIT studies to date, similar EIT methods and technical innovations. Approach. A methodical critical review of the fnEIT literature has been performed. Promising areas of future work and their applications are highlighted, including challenges that must be overcome. Main results. It is shown that the fields of nerve imaging and neuromodulation, cognitive neuroscience in animals and humans, and epileptic seizure localisation could benefit from the ability of fnEIT to image millisecond scale neuronal depolarization throughout brain or nerve. This is achievable with existing methods but with current limitations of the need for implanted cranial or nerve electrodes and averaging to a repeated stimulus. Current approaches to overcome this include CMOS integrated active electrodes, frequency division multiplexing for parallel signal acquisition, and recording with atomic magnetometers. With these, it is a realistic possibility to achieve non-invasive imaging of fast neural activity in real-time with an electrode-atomic magnetometer helmet in human subjects with a resolution of mm and msec. Significance . This review serves as a general guide for those working in related fields or those considering the use of EIT. With the above advances, it is a realistic possibility to achieve non-invasive imaging of fast neural activity in real-time with an electrode-atomic magnetometer helmet in human subjects with a resolution of mm and msec.

items.title: A unifying framework for structured population dynamics in modern coexistence theory
items.abstract: Variation within populations is ubiquitous in nature, yet many models and frameworks in community ecology assume that all individuals within a population interact with the community identically. Modern coexistence theory is no exception; however, several subfields of ecology have independently been integrating coexistence theory, each asking the same underlying question: how do structured population dynamics shape coexistence outcomes? Here, I propose a unifying framework for integrating population variation into modern coexistence theory that is applicable across all fields of ecology. The application of this framework is presented in three case studies: niche overlap and fitness differences between influenza substrains, mutual invasibility between competing perennial plants, and fluctuation-dependent invasion outcomes in apparently competing prey with a foraging-predation risk tradeoff. Together, these examples illustrate the framework's broad applicability, power to resolve the interaction between population and community level processes, and its potential to reveal novel ecological phenomena.

items.title: Genetic Variability and Yield Determinants of Upland Rice Genotypes in Akungba Akoko Agro-Ecology
items.abstract: Abstract Background Rice is one of the world's most important cereal crops and a major source of food and income for millions of people, especially Nigeria, which has almost reach her self-sufficient production capacity. However, genetic variability significantly influences yield component traits in rice for stability and adaptability. Therefore, this study assessed the genetic variability and trait associations influencing grain yield in upland rice genotypes evaluated under the Akungba Akoko agro-ecology. Methods Fourteen genotypes were tested under field conditions in a randomized complete block design at the experimental field of the department of Plant Science and Biotechnology, and data were collected on yield and related agronomic traits, analyzed using GLM models of SPSS version 27. Result The analysis of variance revealed highly significant differences among genotypes, confirming the presence of considerable genetic diversity. Plant height, number of tillers, effective tillers, flag leaf length, panicle length, panicle weight, number of grains per panicle, number of spikelets, thousand grain weight, grain length and width, days to panicle initiation, days to maturity, and grain yield per hill all vary significantly among the genotypes. These significant differences suggest considerable genetic variability within the tested genotypes, which is favorable for selection and breeding. Coefficient of variation (CV) provides a measure of experimental precision and variability relative to the mean. Most traits have CV values below 20%, with some lower than 10%, which suggests good experimental consistency. For example: Plant height CV 5.8% (high precision). Number of tillers CV 16.4%. Grain yield CV 25.8%, which is typical for yield traits due to their inherent variability. Estimates of genotypic and phenotypic coefficients of variation indicated that while some traits were strongly under genetic control, others were more sensitive to environmental influence. Grain yield showed positive and significant correlations with key yield components, particularly productive tillers, panicle weight, number of grains per panicle, and thousand-grain weight, highlighting their value as indirect selection criteria. Genetic parameter estimates further demonstrated high heritability (> 90%) for traits such as plant height, number of tillers, panicle weight, and maturity, coupled with high genetic advance values, suggesting strong additive gene action and effective selection potential. Conversely, traits like panicle length exhibited lower heritability, reflecting greater environmental influence. Conclusion The study shows good genetic variability and heritability for most important yield and agronomic traits in upland rice genotypes from this agro-ecology, indicating strong potential for selection and breeding improvements. Traits like panicle weight, grain yield, and tiller number are particularly promising targets for breeders.

items.title: A minimal pangenome graph for Salminus brasiliensis, a freshwater migratory Neotropical flagship species: it takes two to tango
items.abstract: Abstract Two chromosome-level, reference-guided consensus genomes of Salminus brasiliensis are presented for an Upper Paraná Basin specimen (Brazil), representing a potentially distinct lineage from the Vertebrate Genomes Project reference specimen, from Argentina. These resources allow for a genomic variation framework, including the minimal reference pangenome graph. Short reads mapped against the VGP reference assemblies yielded two ~ 1.07–1.08 Gb pseudohaplotypes (N 50 =38.9–40.8 Mb), with union k-mer completeness of 94%, Q V ~33 each. BUSCO completeness scores are 97.8% for the principal genome and 97.4% for the lifted annotation proteome. The reference pangenome graph for S. brasiliensis was obtained from four chromosome-level haploid sets, using minigraph. It is 1.1 Gb, comprising 288,788 segments (average length 3,826 bp), 404,621 links (809,242 arcs), with average node degree 1.4 (maximum 3). Additional read-to-graph alignments (GAM/GAF) and other accompanying genomic datasets, such as gene annotation, are also provided. The bioinformatics datasets made available for this model Neotropical migratory freshwater species—relevant for conservation, fisheries and aquaculture—can be applied in fields such as ecology, evolution and biotechnology.

items.title: A comprehensive review of craniomandibular morphometric indices in carnivora: Anatomical basis, functional significance, and comparative applications.
items.abstract: The skull of carnivorans represents a highly integrated anatomical structure shaped by selective pressures associated with feeding ecology, sensory specialization, locomotion, and phylogenetic history. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of craniomandibular morphometric indices in the order Carnivora, integrating their anatomical definitions, morphometric foundations, and functional significance. Standardized cranial and mandibular measurements are reviewed together with 11 widely used proportional indices, including the Cranial Index (CI), Skull Index (SI), Facial Index (FI), Facial Length Index (FLI), Cranial Length Index (CLI), Cranial Height Index (CHI), Orbital Index (OI), Palatal Index (PI), Foramen Magnum Index (FMI), Mandibular Body Index (MBI), and Mandibular Ramus Index (MRI). The review highlights the biomechanical and evolutionary relevance of these indices by examining their relationships with bite performance, craniofacial organization, sensory adaptations, feeding ecology, and morphological diversification among carnivoran families. In addition to summarizing published morphometric indices, several proportional indices that have rarely been reported as independent variables are derived from previously published linear craniometric measurements, providing standardized quantitative descriptors for comparative analyses across species. By compiling anatomical landmarks, measurement protocols, functional interpretations, and comparative data within a unified framework, this review identifies current knowledge gaps and promotes greater methodological consistency in future studies. Although some proportional indices were calculated from published measurements rather than directly reported in the original literature, they provide valuable complementary metrics for evaluating cranial and mandibular morphology. Overall, the integration of these 11 morphometric indices offers a comprehensive approach for investigating craniofacial evolution, functional morphology, feeding adaptations, and taxonomic diversity in both extant and fossil carnivorans. This review provides a practical reference for researchers in comparative anatomy, evolutionary biology, paleontology, and veterinary morphology.

items.title: Bidirectional Interplay Between the Skin Microbiota and the Host: An EAACI Task Force Report.
items.abstract: The skin microbiome is a diverse community of bacteria, fungi, archaea, and viruses colonizing the human skin and is thought to play an important role in skin health. Skin homeostasis and immunity are influenced by a dynamic interplay between the host immune system, the skin microbiome, and other host factors. Disruption of the skin microbiome well-functioning by environmental, lifestyle, and host-related factors can lead to dysbiosis, which has been associated to some pathological skin conditions, resulting in skin inflammation and an impaired barrier function. Building on the previous work from the EAACI Task Force that emphasized how environmental and lifestyle factors impact host resilience through the skin microbiome, the present review focuses on intrinsic host factors. We provide a comprehensive discussion on how the skin composition differs at different anatomical locations and is influenced by age, gender, hormones, immune system activity, and how the host "multi-omes" (genome, transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome) interact with the skin microbiome. Additionally, we review current strategies to modify skin microbiome functions, including the role of diseases and medication, as well as topical microbiome-targeting biotic and bacteriophage therapies. Overall, this review highlights current knowledge and key research gaps, offering insights to guide future investigations and therapeutic innovations in skin health.

items.title: [The law of muscular fatigue across history and species].
items.abstract: Since the earliest anatomical descriptions, comparative studies of muscle tissue have revealed a common architecture within the animal kingdom. This structural invariance implies that the fundamental laws governing muscle function are also universal. The law of fatigue represents a typical case: during exertion, a critical intensity exists below which the muscle can work indefinitely without fatigue onset, and above which fatigue sets in abruptly, inevitably leading to exhaustion. This fatigability threshold is critical, for it delineates sustainable effort from that which is not. Overcoming what has historically been a limited permeability between disciplines, research in human physiology and animal ecology now converge to test this law in free-ranging animals. This approach shows that there can be considerable value in moving beyond classical experimental models, so as to explore muscle tissue more broadly across the immense diversity of the animal kingdom. Moreover, by revealing a method applicable to species in the wild, hitherto inaccessible to study, this approach paves the way for its transfer to preclinical and clinical research. By relying on spontaneous activity so as not to disturb the animals concerned, it addresses important ethical considerations, facilitating both the non-invasive longitudinal monitoring of mice and the assessment of patients for whom the evaluation of physical capacity also remains a delicate matter.

items.title: A change in sex chromosomes caused by allopolyploidy in a willow lineage triggered new evolutionary changes in descendant species.
items.abstract: Polyploidization through hybridization between species with different sex chromosomes is evolutionarily surprising. To understand stable sex-determining systems in such hybrids, we studied a dioecious allotetraploid (4n) willow lineage that arose by hybridization between Salix species from the Salix and Vetrix clades. We generated chromosome-level assemblies for three allotetraploids and one related diploid, characterized their sex-linked regions (SLRs) to infer their evolutionary history, and analyzed mRNA and small RNA (sRNA) expression profiles of candidate sex-determining genes. Female genome assemblies confirmed that the same two subgenomes contributed to all allotetraploids studied. Both progenitor species have male heterogamety (XY systems), with SLRs on different chromosomes (7 and 15), whereas the allotetraploids have female heterogamety (ZW systems). Three 4n species, Salix babylonica, Salix matsudana, and Salix chienii, retained Z-SLRs in the former chromosome 15Y pericentromeric location, which carry male-determining partial duplications of the ARR17 gene, and an inversion between the SLRs arose adjacent to these duplications in their common ancestor. Another 4n species, Salix pentandra, split before these 4n species diversified, and the ARR17 partial duplications are in the chromosome's pseudo-autosomal (recombining) region. We identify a W-linked ARR22-like gene and propose it as a candidate sex-determining factor in this species, pending functional testing.

items.title: Comparative genomics reveals contrasting candidate adaptive signatures in two ecologically similar plateau fishes.
items.abstract: Plateau aquatic environments expose fishes to chronic cold, hypoxia, ultraviolet radiation and low productivity, providing natural systems for studying genomic features associated with environmental adaptation. Whether related fishes inhabiting similar cold-water plateau environments exhibit comparable or divergent genomic responses remains unclear. We compared two plateau cypriniform fishes, Aspiorhynchus laticeps and Diptychus maculatus , within a 12-species phylogenomic framework, integrating orthogroup inference, gene-family turnover, coding-sequence divergence, chromosome-scale synteny and duplicated gene-pair divergence profiling. The strongest contrasts occurred in species-specific orthogroups and gene-family turnover. Aspiorhynchus laticeps had a larger set of apparent species-specific orthogroups, enriched mainly in oocyte and reproductive processes, and its expanded families and elevated- ω orthogroups were associated with immune, receptor-mediated and membrane-associated functions. By contrast, D. maculatus had fewer species-specific orthogroups enriched for neural and synaptic processes and a contraction-dominated gene-family profile involving host defence, mucosal immunity and chromatin-related processes. The focal contrast did not exceed empirical background variation, and expansion-related computational analysis of gene family evolution (CAFE) estimates were associated with assembly continuity and input-gene properties. These findings indicate that ecologically similar plateau fishes may exhibit different combinations of candidate genomic features, highlighting the joint influence of ecological adaptation and genome history.

items.title: Evolutionary selection pressures give rise to risky preferences in value-based decision-making.
items.abstract: We are living in a dynamically changing world, where optimal decision-making under uncertainty is linked to the survival of species. However, evolutionary selection pressures that shape value-based decision-making (VBDM, i.e. choosing between available options based on their expected value) under uncertainty have received only limited attention. The current work demonstrates that fitness associated with different VBDM preferences is influenced by the value properties of the environment, as well as the characteristics and the density of competitors in the population. Computational model-based analysis shows that, when there are an increasingly large number of discrete strategies competing for fitness, risk-seeking tendencies can eventually dominate the population. We demonstrate that the strength of these strategies was minimizing suboptimal decisions by tracking the expected value difference between available options more precisely. We discuss the broad implications of our finding across behavioural ecology, behavioural economics and also in relation to the evolutionary basis of vulnerability to psychiatric conditions such as gambling addiction.

items.title: Maximum threshold of eco-geological suitability evaluated with geodiversity of a region: the natural ecological potential applied as a quantitative baseline for ecological status assessment.
items.abstract: Quantitatively assessing the correspondence between ecological status and natural ecological potential is important for ecological protection and sustainable development in ecologically fragile areas. However, most conventional ecological assessments lack a quantitative baseline of natural ecological potential. Thus, it is difficult to determine whether and to what extent ecological restoration is needed, increasing the risk of excessive or insufficient restoration. To address this gap, eco-geological suitability (EGS) was introduced to quantify natural ecological potential by integrating key geodiversity-related indicators. Zhangbei, China, was selected as a case study to evaluate EGS in an ecologically fragile area. Nine eco-geological indicators were integrated using the entropy-weighted Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (EW-TOPSIS) model to quantify EGS. Soil thickness, soil texture, and soil parent material contributed most to EGS. The quantitative identification of areas with relatively high or low EGS provides a baseline for evaluating ecological status. Ecological status was characterized using the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI). Ecological status and potential correspondence assessment (ESPCA) was conducted using normalized RSEI and EGS values. RSEI was substantially lower than EGS in central and northern Zhangbei, mainly associated with intensive agriculture. RSEI was substantially higher than EGS in the low-potential southern and eastern hills under extensive afforestation. ESPCA enabled the first quantitative identification of potential ecological overload areas associated with excessive afforestation. This study establishes a transferable framework for assessing ecological status and potential correspondence in fragile regions, helping to avoid land degradation risks from inappropriate intervention.

items.title: Habitat preference in two European fireflies is reflected in their colour vision.
items.abstract: Colour vision has so far been demonstrated in only a single firefly species, the European Lampyris noctiluca. Lamprohiza splendidula is another widespread European species that often co-occurs with L. noctiluca. First, in field surveys, we quantitatively demonstrated that the former species prefers open habitats, while the latter shows a stronger preference for densely vegetated areas. Second, by measuring compound eye spectral sensitivity with electroretinography and assuming dichromatic colour vision, we used a basic psychophysical colour space model to quantify the physiological experience sensed by L. splendidula and L. noctiluca males viewing the females' bioluminescent signal with eyes adapted to spectral conditions of densely vegetated areas and open areas illuminated by the late twilight sky, when the activity of these fireflies is maximal. Dark-adapted eyes of both species were mostly sensitive to the yellowish green spectral region (559-568 nm), well matching the bioluminescence peak wavelength of the females (556 nm). Recordings on green-adapted eye preparations revealed the presence of a second, blue-sensitive photoreceptor (423-456 nm). We also found that the spectral separation between the blue- and green-sensitive receptors was greater in L. splendidula than in L. noctiluca. According to our colour vision modelling, differences in the spectral sensitivities of the two species' visual systems may help maintain colour vision performance and facilitate female detection in their respective preferred habitats.

items.title: Volatile dialogues between plants and microorganisms.
items.abstract: Covering: up to 2026Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are key mediators of long-distance communication in biological systems. While their roles in plant-insect interactions are well established, emerging evidence highlights their importance in plant-microbe interactions. In this highlight, we discuss the biosynthesis and ecological functions of plant VOCs (pVOCs) and their impact on microbiome assembly and function. We examine how constitutive and stress-induced pVOCs shape microbial community composition and how microbial VOCs (mVOCs) influence plant growth and defense by modulating hormonal and metabolic pathways. We further address the bidirectional nature of volatile-mediated interactions and the challenges associated with studying complex VOC blends in natural environments. Understanding these dynamic volatile dialogues provides new opportunities for microbiome engineering and sustainable crop production.

items.title: The Unified Model Graph: Drawing the Statistical Models of Psychology
items.abstract: Psychologists describe their statistical models with diagrams. The conventions in use, path diagrams, multilevel panels, plate notation, and causal graphs, each grew inside one modeling tradition, and they disagree on basic symbols. As a result, one figure can stand for two different models. An ellipse with three arrows can show a factor model or a latent profile model. A labeled arrow can show a fixed slope or a person-varying slope. A mediation triangle can show a regression decomposition or a causal claim. This article introduces the Unified Model Graph (UMG), a notation built so that the figure identifies the model that was fitted. Three visual cues type every quantity: fill for observed versus latent, shape for continuous versus categorical, and outline for inferential role. Four edge types separate regression, covariance, deterministic, and mixture relations. Plates mark replication, and a badge states whether the figure makes a causal claim. Every well-formed UMG corresponds to exactly one family of distributions, and path diagrams, plate notation, and causal graphs are special cases; the formal results and proofs are in the supplemental material. The accompanying R package \pkg{} builds diagrams from code or from fitted lavaan, lme4, mirt, and brms objects, validates them, translates them to and from lavaan syntax, checks necessary identification conditions, derives testable implications, and generates model-implied data displays. A benchmark of eight R diagramming packages on ten representational features and ten operations locates what the notation adds. All materials, scripts, and outputs are openly archived.

items.title: Trust miscalibration across cultures and social classes
items.abstract: Do people accurately judge how trustworthy others are? Trust in strangers underpins modern societies, yet people sometimes misjudge others’ trustworthiness, with potentially detrimental implications for social cohesion and public well-being. In pre-registered studies across 23 countries (N = 9,758), we quantify the trust gap: the discrepancy between people’s belief about how many people would return a wallet lost in the street and how many people actually do return it. In line with prior research, people in Western, high-income countries underestimated others’ trustworthiness. However, people in non-Western, low- and middle-income countries overestimated trustworthiness. As anticipated, the trust gap varied with socio-economic status within countries: People of lower socio-economic status were more likely to underestimate others’ trustworthiness than people of higher socio-economic status, consistent with exploitation being more costly for people with fewer resources. Finally, a randomized controlled trial showed that informing participants about actual wallet return rates reduces trust miscalibration. Information provision led those who had underestimated others’ trustworthiness to increase their generalized trust, and those who had overestimated others’ trustworthiness to decrease their generalized trust. These findings demonstrate the value of studying the psychology of trust beyond high-income individuals and societies; and of providing accurate information about everyday cooperation to reduce miscalibrations in how people trust one another.

items.title: Avoiding the worst leaders is more important than getting the best
items.abstract: Society and organizations invest heavily in selecting the best leaders 1, and existing research shows a positivity bias by focusing on the bright side of leadership 2–4. Yet, according to Popper 5, the central question of institutional design is not who should rule, but how to prevent bad leaders from doing too much damage. This raises the question of which approach is more consistent with human psychology: Aim for the best leaders, or avoid the worst? We provide robust evidence for an “avoid-the-worst” principle in human leadership preferences. Although text analyses indicated that the top 100 business schools emphasize good leadership far more than the prevention of bad leadership, actual employee experiences from 9.9 million Glassdoor reviews show that people mentioned their leader 70% more often in the negative than positive section, and negative leader mentions predicted company ratings 1.5 times more strongly. Providing causal evidence, five high-powered experiments across 40 countries (N = 51,433) revealed that people were more willing to sacrifice time and money to avoid a bad leader than obtaining a good leader—across morality and competence, hypothetical and incentivized choice, ideology and culture. People care more about avoiding the worst leaders than getting the best.

items.title: Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-III (ACE-III): Preliminary psychometric properties, normative data, and normative thresholds for functionally independent French older adults.
items.abstract: The Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-III (ACE-III) has demonstrated good psychometric properties across different languages and populations. However, psychometric evidence and normative data for the French version remain limited. Therefore, this study aimed to examine the psychometric properties of the ACE-III in functionally independent French older adults and to establish normative data. A total of 103 community-dwelling, functionally independent older adults living in France completed a semistructured interview, the ACE-III, Fried Frailty Phenotype, Geriatric Depression Scale, and University of California Los Angeles Loneliness Scale. Internal consistency, construct validity, and concurrent criterion validity were examined. Regression-based normative equations, normative trajectories, and individualized normative thresholds were developed using age and education. The ACE-III demonstrated good internal consistency (Cronbach's α = .81) and satisfactory construct and concurrent criterion validity evidenced by strong correlations between the global score and subdomains (r = .67 to .92). Age significantly predicted ACE-III performance. Education was retained in the normative models following a theory-driven approach. Regression-based normative equations, normative trajectories, and individualized normative thresholds were established for the total score and each neurocognitive domain. These findings support the use of ACE-III for neurocognitive screening in French older adults. Longitudinal and process-based studies are warranted to further establish its clinical utility.

items.title: Gender differences in perceptions, use, and treatment outcomes of self-guided internet-delivered cognitive behavioural therapy among public safety personnel.
items.abstract: Mental health concerns are prevalent among public safety personnel (PSP), particularly among PSP women, but the role of gender in PSP mental health is not yet well understood. Internet-delivered cognitive behavioural therapy (ICBT) is an effective treatment for various mental health concerns. The current study assessed for gender differences in PSP's perceptions of, use of, and response to ICBT. In this longitudinal single-group open trial, 267 Canadian PSP (53.9% women) participated in self-guided ICBT tailored for PSP. Clients completed questionnaire measures at pre-treatment and 8 weeks post-enrollment. We assessed gender differences using ANCOVAs, independent-samples t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, and chi-square tests. Women and men did not differ in posttreatment symptoms of depression, anxiety, or post‑traumatic stress after accounting for pre‑treatment symptoms (all p 's ≥ .26); number of lessons accessed within the ICBT course ( p = .75); or treatment satisfaction (all p 's ≥ .36). Women had more favourable pre-treatment attitudes toward ICBT (all p 's ≤ .002) and were more likely to report prior mental healthcare ( p < .001). These findings support prior literature demonstrating no significant differences in ICBT treatment outcomes between women and men PSP despite more favorable perceptions of it among women PSP.

items.title: Personality traits shape emotion regulation strategies in children with developmental language disorder.
items.abstract: Children with Developmental Language Disorder (DLD) often face socio-emotional challenges beyond language needs, yet the role of personality traits in shaping their emotion regulation (ER) remains underexplored. This study compared ER strategies between children with DLD and typically developing (TD) peers, examined personality predictors of ER and explored the associations between these ER strategies and psychosocial adjustment. Sixty-eight children (DLD = 27; TD = 41), aged 8-12 years, completed self-report measures of personality, ER strategies, including Cognitive Reappraisal (CR) and Expressive Suppression (ES), and psychosocial adjustment. Children with DLD reported higher ES use, whereas no group differences emerged for CR. In the DLD group, higher Extraversion predicted greater use of both CR and ES, Neuroticism predicted lower CR and Agreeableness predicted lower ES. Regarding adjustment, higher ES predicted poorer psychosocial adjustment across both groups. Findings highlight personality influences on ER in children with DLD, with implications for socio-emotional assessment.

items.title: Adverse Event Reporting in Trials of Digital Eating Disorder Interventions: A Systematic Review of Current Practice and Recommendations for the Field.
items.abstract: Objective Balancing the benefits and risks of digital eating disorder interventions is essential for informed decisions regarding their implementation, yet remarkably little is known about the adverse events associated with their use. This systematic review aimed to characterise the frequency, extent, and nature of adverse event reporting in randomized trials of digital eating disorder interventions. Method Databases were searched for randomized trials of digital eating disorder interventions that reported on adverse events. Data on adverse event definitions, assessment, monitoring, management, and reporting were extracted and synthesised qualitatively. Results Only 16 of 53 identified digital intervention trials reported on adverse events. Considerable heterogeneity was observed in adverse event definitions, assessment methods, monitoring procedures, and reporting practices. Reported events from 11 trials ranged from psychological harms to physical complaints, but it was often unclear whether these events were attributable to the intervention. Few trials reported safety procedures, and 10 of the 11 trials that identified adverse events did not describe how these events were managed. Conclusion Adverse event reporting in digital eating disorder trials remains uncommon and highly heterogeneous. We propose a series of recommendations to improve the monitoring, management, and reporting of adverse events in future digital intervention trials.

items.title: Development of the Sexual Experiences Survey-Victimization-Short Forms (SES-V-SF) and a Psychometric Evaluation of SES-V Standard and Short Forms.
items.abstract: The Sexual Experiences Survey-Victimization (SES-V) was substantially revised in 2024 to broaden the range of sexual exploitation victimization assessed. Although the revised SES-V offers important advantages, its length may limit its usefulness in some research and applied contexts. The purpose of this study was to develop a short form of the SES-V and to evaluate the psychometric performance of both the short-form and the standard-form SES-V. Using a predefined process, we selected two to four items from each SES-V module. These items captured 89% to 96% of the victimization reported within each module in a national dataset. We then recruited 1,103 adults through CloudResearch, oversampling groups previously underrepresented in SES-V research. Participants were randomized to complete the standard-form SES-V or one of two short-form versions along with measures to assess convergent validity. A subsample of participants ( n = 640) completed the same SES-V form again two weeks later to assess test-retest reliability. The short forms performed well and were comparable to the standard form in convergent validity and test-retest reliability. Endorsement rates on the short forms were similar to the standard form across three of four modules, and the short forms required less than half the administration time (i.e. a median of under five minutes). Findings were generally consistent across demographic subgroups. This study provides psychometric support for the short forms and additional psychometric evidence for the standard form. Future research should further examine whether the short forms capture the full range of victimization across diverse populations.

items.title: Psychological Assets and Cardiovascular Health in Adulthood: A Mixed Methods Investigation.
items.abstract: Background Psychological risk factors like depression increase risk for poor cardiovascular outcomes but psychological assets like purpose in life are protective and linked to reduced risk of cardiovascular events. However, most assets are investigated individually, and not all have been explored in relation to cardiovascular health (CVH). This study used mixed methods to assess multiple psychological assets and evaluate associations with CVH 12 years later. Methods Data came from 2092 participants in the National Child Development Study. At age 50 years, participants wrote open-ended responses describing their futures. Two trained researchers qualitatively coded each response by rating them for 7 commonly assessed psychological assets (1=not at all; 7=very): optimism, purpose, satisfaction, personal growth, agency, enjoyment, and overall positivity. At age 62, CVH behavioral factors (exercise, smoking status, sleep) were self-reported; CVH clinical factors (blood pressure, lipids, glucose, body weight) were measured during nurse visits. Following Life's Essential 8 guidelines, CVH components were combined into total CVH scores. Linear regressions examined associations between each age 50 asset and age 62 CVH scores, adjusting for age 50 confounders. Results All age 50 assets were positively associated with better CVH scores 12 years later, accounting for sociodemographic characteristics and word counts ( p ≤0.05). Purpose (b=0.81 [95% CI, 0.33-1.29]) and personal growth (b=0.82 [95% CI, 0.34-1.20]) showed the strongest associations with CVH in fully adjusted models. Conclusions Higher levels of most midlife psychological assets were linked with better CVH over time, suggesting multiple paths to health protection. These findings highlight assets that could be prevention targets.

items.title: The Stockholm Declaration advocates a broad approach for reformation of science publishing in a complex stakeholder world.
items.abstract: Because integrity and trustworthiness of science rely on the attitude and behaviour of scientists and publishers, the recent flood of fake publishing and rising publishing costs motivated us to propose an extensive reformation of science publishing. Our Stockholm Declaration suggested 34 concrete actions to counter this unhealthy development, with a call to action for science and educational institutions, science academies and organizations, funders and publishers to unite in an effort to achieve fundamental changes. However, Csaba Szabo argued in a comment that the Stockholm Declaration 'fundamentally misdiagnosed' this science crisis and that a 'true reform' would require the publishing infrastructure to be rebuilt as a public utility with open access and post-publication review. Open access is certainly a desired goal for the future because science and science communication are a public good. However, post-publication reviews are problematic, leaving many poor studies unquestioned. By contrast, the Stockholm Declaration proposes to gradually transform publishing systems in a complex landscape of academic disciplines and publishers with different publishing models in a fast-moving AI world. Such a complex ecosystem requires a broad range of actions to be implemented as quickly as possible, especially independent integrity screening of scientific manuscripts and publications and adjustment of academia's assessment systems of scientific achievements.

items.title: A systematic review of the challenges experienced by parents of multiples.
items.abstract: Background In recent years, growing attention has been directed towards the postnatal challenges experienced by parents of multiples. However, no systematic review has synthesised these challenges comprehensively across multiple domains (psychological, physical, financial and healthcare-related challenges). Aim This review aimed to systematically identify, explore and synthesise the postnatal challenges experienced by parents of multiples within the UK. Methods The review was conducted in accordance with the 2024 Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) guidelines and followed the PRISMA framework for study identification, screening, inclusion and exclusion. A quality appraisal of included studies was also undertaken. Results Nine studies with varied methodological designs met the inclusion criteria. Thematic synthesis revealed a range of postnatal challenges, which were categorised into four domains: psychological (e.g. stress, guilt), physical (e.g. exhaustion, feeding difficulties), healthcare (e.g. lack of specialist support) and financial (e.g. increased childcare costs). Conclusion These findings highlight the complex and cumulative nature of parenting multiples. They demonstrate the need for tailored psychological interventions, enhanced professional training and revised postnatal guidance that better reflects the lived realities of families with multiples. Future research should support this by addressing gaps in evidence, particularly around daily accessibility challenges and the perspectives of healthcare professionals.

items.title: Common early-life exposure of the colorectal epithelium to the microbiome-derived mutagen colibactin
items.abstract: Colibactin is a mutagen produced by bacterial strains in the colorectal microbiomes of some healthy people. It generates somatic mutations characterised by the mutational signatures SBS88 and ID18 in normal human colorectal epithelial cells in vivo. Increasing prevalence of colibactin mutagenesis during the 20th century is hypothesised to have caused recent international increases in early-onset colorectal cancer incidence. Here, we establish the early-life prevalence, timing, mutation burdens and distribution through the colon of colibactin mutagenesis by sequencing normal colorectal epithelial cell genomes to detect SBS88 and ID18 in 90 healthy and inflammatory bowel disease affected children and adolescents. Colibactin-induced mutagenesis was present in ~43%, with or without inflammatory bowel disease. It usually begins shortly after birth and ceases by age five years. Mutation burdens are higher in the left than right colon and show substantial variation, with some children displaying mutation burdens comparable to those of healthy non-exposed individuals greater than 60 years of age. The future public health implications of this common early life mutagen exposure will depend on clarification of its role in colorectal cancer causation.

items.title: “A slippery slope, then this pushed it off the edge": The Psychological Impact of the UK Supreme Court ruling on the Meaning of Sex in the Equality Act for Trans and Gender Diverse People
items.abstract: Background: Following the UK Supreme Court's For Women Scotland (FWS) ruling, concerns have emerged regarding its implications for the health and wellbeing of transgender and gender-diverse (TGD) people. Although structural stigma is increasingly recognised as a determinant of health inequalities among marginalised populations, little is known about how major legal and policy changes influence psychological wellbeing within TGD communities. This study examined perceptions of structural stigma following the FWS ruling and investigated its association with mental health, suicidality, loneliness, social gender-role recognition, and community resilience. Method: Two convergent studies were conducted. Study 1 involved a qualitative analysis of asynchronous audio interviews with UK-based TGD adults exploring experiences and perceptions of the FWS ruling. Reflexive thematic analysis was used to identify key themes. Study 2 utilised a cross-sectional survey of UK TGD adults to examine associations between perceived structural stigma, loneliness, mental health, suicidality, social gender-role recognition, and community resilience. Structural equation modelling was used to test loneliness as a mediating mechanism and community resilience as a moderating factor. Results: Across both studies, participants perceived the FWS ruling as contributing to structural stigma by undermining social recognition, belonging, and feelings of citizenship. Qualitative findings suggested that participants responded to these experiences through heightened vigilance, changes to public self-presentation, and withdrawal from social environments. Quantitative analyses indicated that greater perceived structural stigma was associated with poorer mental health, higher suicidality, lower social gender-role recognition, and greater loneliness. Loneliness emerged as a significant mediator of these relationships. Although community resilience did not moderate associations between loneliness and mental health, greater levels of community resilience were associated with lower loneliness and suicidality. Conclusions: Findings provide the first empirical evidence that the FWS ruling may function as a form of structural stigma with important implications for the wellbeing of TGD people in the UK. Loneliness appears to be a key mechanism through which structural stigma influences psychological outcomes, while connection to LGBTQ+ communities may serve as an important psychosocial resource. The findings highlight the need for continued monitoring of the mental health impacts of legal and policy changes affecting TGD populations and for interventions that strengthen belonging, social connection, and community support.
